item:chok-sul-s-head.text: Chok'sul's Head. Chok'sul's Head serves as gruesome physical proof of the death of the Mo'grosh ogre chieftain. Brought to Magistrate Bluntnose in Thelsamar, it secures a formal bounty placed by local dwarven authorities. The ogres of Mo'grosh Stronghold pose a persistent menace to the settlements of Loch Modan, orchestrating assaults against Thelsamar, the excavation sites, and the vital Stonewrought Dam. Magistrate Bluntnose placed a bounty on the brute presumed to be coordinating these attacks: Chok'sul. Given the chaos of the northeastern hills, the magistrate demands undeniable evidence before releasing township funds. The severed head of the ogre chieftain provides the grotesque certainty the dwarven council needs to mark the contract fulfilled.

item:clarice-s-pendant.text: Clarice's Pendant. Clarice's Pendant is a small keepsake belonging to Clarice Foster, an undead resident of the Pools of Vision in Thunder Bluff. Once a token from her former husband, Yuriv, the jewelry now serves only as a bitter reminder of abandoned family and misplaced devotion to the Light. Clarice's Pendant represents the fractured human past common to many of the Forsaken. Before the Third War consumed Lordaeron, Clarice's husband Yuriv abandoned her and their children to join the fight against the undead, proclaiming that devotion to the Holy Light took precedence over all else. Instead of saving his home, Yuriv perished, leaving his family behind to ultimately succumb to the very Scourge he set out to fight. For Clarice, the pendant is not a cherished memento, but an insulting trinket symbolizing a lifetime spent coming second to zealotry and duty.

item:claw-key.text: Claw Key. The Claw Key is one of three druidic keys hidden within the Talon Den atop Stonetalon Peak. Alongside the Barrow Key and Sleepers' Key, it is required to unlock the enchanted Talon Den Hoard. The night elf druids established the Talon Den high upon Stonetalon Peak as a sanctuary and repository for powerful relics. To ensure these treasures remained safe from trespassers, they hid them behind a layered security system. The hoard itself is sealed by three distinct enchanted locks: the Barrow Key, the Sleepers' Key, and the Claw Key. Each key is concealed inside a specialized druidic cache resembling a torch within the winding tunnels of the barrow den. The druids did not leave the keys unguarded or freely accessible. Opening the cache that holds the Claw Key requires first acquiring the Gatekeeper's Key, which is tucked away near the barrow entrance. Once retrieved, the Claw Key serves as a vital component in breaking the druids' seal and claiming the riches hidden deep within the mountain.

item:cliffspring-river-sample.text: Cliffspring River Sample. In Darkshore, foul water gathers at the base of the Cliffspring River waterfall. Drawn for Thundris Windweaver in Auberdine, the vial shows that corruption is moving toward the coast. The Cliffspring River runs from Darkshore's eastern heights, past ancient stone bridges, and into the sea at Mist's Edge. Its clear waters have turned foul and visibly corrupted. Thundris Windweaver, a night elf in Auberdine, fears the tainted flow will reach the settlement's shore and water supply. He sent travelers to draw water from the pool beneath the river's lower waterfall. The sample confirms that unnatural rot is moving downstream toward the coast.

item:cloth-request.text: Cloth Request. At the Canal Tailor and Fit Shop, Rema Schneider receives Harlan Bagley's request for fresh cloth and knitted goods. His shelves are emptying quickly. Harlan Bagley asks Rema Schneider for a fresh supply of knitted garments and cloth. Bagley notes a sudden and unsettling surge in trade: citizens and travelers are buying armor and sturdy clothing as if bracing for a brutal season. The rush leaves Rema puzzled and wary. The House of Nobles has announced no open war, so Rema wonders why city folk are quietly armoring themselves and whether the crown's leaders are hiding unrest.

item:cloven-hoof.text: Cloven Hoof. The Cloven Hoof is a mysterious relic guarded deep within Thousand Needles by the Galak centaur tribe. Preserved inside an ancient sacred flame at Splithoof Hold, it emanates an uncharacteristic supernatural energy that tauren scholars are keen to understand. Held within an ancient brazier at the deepest recess of Splithoof Hold, the Cloven Hoof is one of the most treasured relics of the Galak centaur. The artifact is continually enveloped in a magical flame, requiring blessed water to briefly quench the blaze so it can be handled. Centaur society is notoriously brutal and splintered into violent clans, but their reverence for the brazier suggests ritual significance tied directly to their origins. Tauren observers like Rau Cliffrunner at Freewind Post believe the strange aura radiating from the hoof could reveal critical insight into the race that has plagued Kalimdor's plains for generations.

item:comar-s-heart.text: Comar's Heart. Comar's Heart is a macabre ritual component carved from Comar Villard, a faithful human wanderer searching the marshes of the Wetlands for his lost wife. Forsaken warlocks in the Undercity seek out this relic of pure devotion to feed the summoning rites of a succubus. To bind a creature as capricious and predatory as a succubus, warlocks must bait the demon with true purity and devotion. Carendin Halgar's disciples in the Undercity identify Comar Villard as one of the few men possessing such unblemished fidelity. While his wife was lost amidst the turmoil sweeping the Eastern Kingdoms, Comar stubbornly wanders the sodden roads of the Wetlands, refusing to abandon his search. It is precisely this unwavering love that marks him for slaughter, turning his still-beating heart into the ideal lure for a demonic servant.

item:consecrated-rune.text: Consecrated Rune. A Consecrated Rune is an inscribed sacred item passed to fledgling dwarven paladins training in Coldridge Valley. It serves as an introductory summons from Bromos Grummner, directing initiates to report to Anvilmar and begin their formal duties as Knights of the Silver Hand. Novice dwarven paladins proving themselves in Coldridge Valley are handed a Consecrated Rune once they have shown basic martial competence. Inscribed with sacred words and blessed by the Holy Light, the rune originates from Bromos Grummner, the paladin trainer residing inside Anvilmar. Dwarves hold immense respect for the traditions of the Holy Light introduced to them by their human allies. Reading the rune serves as both an official summons and a symbolic rite of passage, confirming the novice's place among the Knights of the Silver Hand.

item:console-key.text: Console Key. At the Venture Company digsite in the Barrens, Tinkerer Sniggles holds the Console Key. It unlocks the main control terminal and lets the samophlange be removed once the apparatus is shut down. The Venture Company runs an industrial outpost in the northern Barrens. Its steam-driven machinery depends on a device called a samophlange. The console is locked against unauthorized hands, and only Tinkerer Sniggles, the chief technician on site, carries the Console Key. The key opens the terminal casing so the rig can be powered down.

item:control-console-operating-manual.text: Control Console Operating Manual. At the Venture Company site southwest of Sludge Fen, the Control Console Operating Manual guides workers through the machinery. It explains how to close the valves and disengage the samophlange. Southwest of Sludge Fen, the Venture Company runs a drilling and research site in the northern Barrens. Its machinery links gauges, pressurized valves, and mechanisms to a device called a samophlange. Without the right instructions, working the volatile controls can cause a dangerous failure or lock the system. The manual gives the valve sequence for disengaging the core apparatus without triggering an explosive failure.

item:corroded-shrapnel.text: Corroded Shrapnel. Corroded Shrapnel consists of jagged metal fragments lodged deep within the corrupted treants of the Stonetalon Mountains. Recovered from fallen protectors like Charred and Blackened Ancients, this debris provides physical evidence of the foul weaponry used by the Venture Company during their retreat. When the Venture Company was driven back from the groves of Stonetalon, the goblins unleashed brutal, reckless munitions to cover their escape. Shrapnel from these explosive weapons tore into the valley's defending treants, embedding jagged metal deep within their bark and core. Rather than healing, the ancient guardians slowly fell to corruption, their wood blackening and their fury turning upon anyone who stepped into the vale. The rusted, tainted fragments recovered from these wounded protectors are sought by Kaela Shadowspear so the gnome Gaxim Rustfizzle can analyze the exact mechanisms of the corruption.

item:corrupt-manifestation-s-bracers.text: Corrupt Manifestation's Bracers. Tainted bracers lie on the coast of Silverpine Forest, remnants of a corrupted water elemental. Shaman initiates recover them during the Call of Water and cast them into the Brazier of Everfount with pure water to cleanse the shrine and summon a pure water spirit. The Scourge's plague reached the spirits of Lordaeron. Along Silverpine Forest's misty coast, west of the Sepulcher, a sacred water shrine fell to corruption. Its water manifestation became an aggressive shade. Shaman initiates must defeat it and recover its bracers. At the Brazier of Everfount, they cast the bindings into the flame with pure water, lifting the corruption and calling forth an unblemished water spirit.

item:corrupted-brain-stem.text: Corrupted Brain Stem. Corrupted Brain Stems are biological specimens harvested from the twisted naga and satyrs inhabiting Blackfathom Deeps and the Ashenvale coastline. Gershala Nightwhisper of Auberdine seeks them to study the physical deformities wrought by reckless magical corruption. By examining these brains, night elf scholars hope to understand and potentially prevent a similar fate from befalling the blood elves. The satyrs and naga of Kalimdor stand as living testaments to the warping power of forbidden magic and demonic pacts. Long ago, reckless kaldorei highborne were irrevocably transformed into serpent-like aquatic beasts and demonic horned fiends. The brain stems harvested from these creatures exhibit heavy physical mutation, providing direct anatomical proof of how deep corruptive energies burrow into the nervous systems of once-elven beings. In the coastal settlement of Auberdine, the night elf Gershala Nightwhisper observes the troubling rumors surrounding the blood elves of the Eastern Kingdoms. Fearing that their flirtation with demonic sorcery will spawn yet another generation of monsters on Azeroth, Gershala tasks adventurers with venturing into Blackfathom Deeps. By dissecting both naga and satyr tissues, the researcher hopes to map the path of magical degeneration before another elven culture is lost.

item:corrupted-kor-gem.text: Corrupted Kor Gem. Around Blackfathom Deeps, naga rites leave Kor gems corrupted. Spellcasters prize the stones for holding arcane force, but this taint must be cleansed before a gem can be used in righteous smithing. Kor gems can capture and hold great stores of magic, making them prized by sorcerers and enchanted smiths. Near the ruins of Blackfathom Deeps, naga oracles and tide priestesses claim the stones for their shadowy rites. Their foul enchantments warp each gem with corruption from the sea. The taint does not drain the stone's latent power, so those who need a potent focus still seek gems among the naga.

item:cougar-claws.text: Cougar Claws. Cougar Claws are harvested from flatland cougars that roam the central plains of Mulgore. They serve as a vital material in tauren ritual craft, embodying the untamed balance and natural ferocity of the wild predators. The flatland cougar is one of the apex hunters of Mulgore's sprawling grasslands, stalking prey with instinctual grace. In tauren tradition, taking the claws of such a predator is not an act of casual slaughter or trophy hunting, but a way to harness the natural spirit of the beast. When goblin operations begin defiling the ancestral waters of the plains, Mull Thunderhorn calls upon young hunters to gather these claws alongside those of prairie stalkers. The tauren believe that the pure, uncorrupted predatory instincts of native beasts can be woven into a ritual totem capable of scouring unnatural toxins and foul sorcery from the poisoned Thunderhorn Water Well.

item:courser-eye.text: Courser Eye. Courser Eyes are biological reagents harvested from the antlered coursers roaming the highlands of Stonetalon Mountains. Witch Doctor Jin'Zil in Malaka'jin seeks a large quantity of them to prepare a concoction he mockingly refers to as forest magic.

item:covert-ops-pack.text: Covert Ops Pack. The Covert Ops Pack is a kit of specialized demolitions gear and operational schematics assembled for Alliance espionage in the Stonetalon Mountains. Designed to dismantle the Venture Company's rapacious presence in Windshear Crag, the satchel equips agents to trigger coordinated sabotage while securing high-value technical intelligence. Issued for clandestine strikes deep within Venture Company territory, the Covert Ops Pack pairs brute destructive power with tactical precision. Inside are color-coded NG-5 explosives matched to remote triggers, alongside thorough instructions designated Plan Alpha and Plan Beta. The strategy relies on triggering high-yield distractions at key infrastructure nodes—namely the Cragpool Lake lumber mill and the eastern mine. While goblins scramble to extinguish blazes and assess mechanical failures, an infiltrator slips past the chaos to pilfer critical documents and schematics. The contents of the pack serve a dual purpose for the Alliance in Stonetalon. For the night elf Sentinels, the detonations and theft disrupt the merciless clear-cutting and gouging of the sacred mountainside. For Alliance tinkers, the primary reward lies in the documents themselves. Recovering Venture Company engineering schematics offers rare insights into goblin heavy machinery, revealing mechanical weak points to exploit and allowing Alliance engineers to adapt industrial innovations into their own designs.

item:crate-of-crash-helmets.text: Crate of Crash Helmets. A heavy supply shipment of dwarven Siege Engine headgear destined for the Shimmering Flats in Thousand Needles. The sturdy helmets are urgently required by the Brassbolts brothers to protect test drivers from concussions caused by their experimental rocket cars. Out across the blinding white expanse of the Shimmering Flats, gnome engineers test the absolute limits of mechanical propulsion. Unfortunately for the test pilots, the experimental rocket cars designed by the Brassbolts brothers move far faster than their steering can reliably handle. With drivers routinely suffering violent crashes and head trauma, ordinary leather caps no longer suffice. To prevent their roster of willing daredevils from vanishing entirely, heavy-duty dwarven Siege Engine helmets are packed and dispatched across the sea to keep drivers conscious—and alive.

item:crate-of-horseshoes.text: Crate of Horseshoes. In Elwynn, fifty iron horseshoes are bound for Lakeshire. Smith Argus forged fifty fresh horseshoes in Goldshire, then packed the crate and hammered it shut. Verner Osgood commissioned them for Lakeshire, where constant pressure from gnolls and orcs leaves local craftsmen reliant on Elwynn for essential metal goods. The delivery answers Verner's desperate need for equipment, and Argus includes a stern bill of sale so the Redridge craftsman knows frontier survival comes at a steep price.

item:crate-of-inn-supplies.text: Crate of Inn Supplies. The Crate of Inn Supplies is a parcel packed in Coldridge Valley destined for the Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos. With the mountain pass overrun by troggs, regular supply routes are cut, leaving the inn dependent on passing travelers to carry goods through. Ordinarily, goods flow smoothly between the quiet training grounds of Anvilmar and the bustling towns of Dun Morogh. However, recent trogg incursions have severed Coldridge Pass, cutting off civilian couriers until armed Mountaineer escorts can clear the roads. Packed by Hands Springsprocket, this heavy crate holds essential tavern provisions that Tannok Frosthammer in Kharanos has been waiting on anxiously amid the disruption.

item:crate-of-lightforge-ingots.text: Crate of Lightforge Ingots. In Duskwood, the Crate of Lightforge Ingots carries hope against Morbent Fel. The rare consecrated metal is bound for the Dwarven District in Stormwind. Duskwood's hope rests in this crate of lightforge iron. The rare metal can channel holy power against dark entities, while Morbent Fel's protections turn aside ordinary steel. Only an artisan who knows its temper and honors its sacred nature can work it.

item:crate-with-holes.text: Crate With Holes. A portable transport container provided by the goblin entrepreneur Mebok Mizzyrix in Ratchet. Pierced with air vents, it safely houses a trained Snufflenose Gopher used to track down subterranean culinary delicacies within the quilboar stronghold of Razorfen Kraul. To acquire rare Blueleaf Tubers from the thorny depths of Razorfen Kraul, goblin merchant Mebok Mizzyrix relies on trained Snufflenose Gophers rather than blind digging. Because gophers cannot simply follow an adventurer across the dusty trails of the Barrens on foot, Mebok packs each critter into a well-ventilated wooden crate. Once brought into the humid, root-choked corridors of the quilboar lair, the crate is unlatched, allowing the beast within to follow its keen sense of smell toward buried tubers.

item:crawler-leg.text: Crawler Leg. Along Darkshore’s misty coast, crabs lose legs that most travelers have no use for. Their tough limbs can help keep a gnome’s communication device working. Darkshore’s crabs leave sturdy limbs along the shore, from pygmy tide crawlers to reef crawlers. Night elf sentinels pay them little mind, but the gnome engineer Wizbang Cranktoggle has found a use for them. Working from Auberdine, Wizbang designed his prototype long-distance communication devices, called buzzboxes, to run on improvised local components. Crawler legs’ segmented joints and durable chitin provide the friction and leverage needed to repair Buzzbox 827, along the shoreline just south of town.

item:creeper-ichor.text: Creeper Ichor. Creeper Ichor is a rare, virulent fluid harvested from the moss creepers lurking throughout the forests of the Hillsbrad Foothills. It is sought by the Royal Apothecary Society in Tarren Mill as a potent biological agent for formulating novel plagues against the living. In Tarren Mill, Apothecary Lydon conducts experiments to craft deadly new toxins, seeking to eradicate the surrounding human population. Despising the clean air and vibrant life of the foothills, Lydon searches for natural toxins and biological catalysts native to the local wildlife. The venomous fluids of the forest's giant arachnids, particularly the elusive ichor found within mature moss creepers, serve as an ideal base for his Elixir of Suffering. Mixed with other reagents like gray bear tongues, this fluid aids the Forsaken in perfecting their craft of lethal alchemy.

item:crocolisk-skin-classic.text: Crocolisk Skin (Classic). Crocolisk skins are harvested from the tough hides of the crocolisks inhabiting the islands and waters of the Loch in Loch Modan. Prized by merchants and leatherworkers for their durability, they fetch a respectable price despite the danger involved in securing them. The cold waters of the Loch teem with aggressive crocolisks that make their dens along the lake's islands and shores. Hunting them is no simple task, as these ferocious beasts possess razor-sharp teeth and thick, resilient scales capable of turning away careless blades. Despite the hazards, hunters operating out of Farstrider Lodge frequently harvest the creatures. Tailors, leatherworkers, and distant merchants continually seek out the skins to craft durable garments and protective armor, making a bundle of undamaged hides a valuable trade commodity in the region.

item:crocolisk-tear-classic.text: Crocolisk Tear (Classic). A Crocolisk Tear is a curious alchemical reagent gathered from the crocolisks inhabiting the waters of Loch Modan. It is sought by Chief Engineer Hinderweir to synthesize a neutralizing mixture capable of disarming Dark Iron explosives. Loch crocolisks are hardy reptiles native to the temperate waters of Loch Modan. While hunters often prize their skins and meat, Chief Engineer Hinderweir discovered an unexpected utility in their secretions. Combined with potent spider venom and resonant ogre minerals, the tear of a crocolisk provides the specific chemical properties needed to counteract volatile Dark Iron demolition charges threatening the Stonewrought Dam.

item:crossroads-supply-crate.text: Crossroads Supply Crate. Stolen provisions for the Crossroads lie scattered among Razormane camps in the Barrens. A raided caravan left the settlement short of food, tools, and necessities. Razormane quilboar raided a caravan carrying supplies to the Crossroads. The crates were dragged into nearby camps among the underbrush and dirt dens. Thork, the settlement's commander, seeks their return before the outpost runs dangerously low on food, tools, and necessities.

item:crude-flint.text: Crude Flint. Crude Flint pieces are rough fire-starting stones carried by the Mosshide gnolls throughout the Wetlands. The gnolls use them to kindle blazes from freshly hewn marsh timber, an act that deeply enrages the local protector, Rethiel the Greenwarden. While crude and unworked, these simple striking flints provide the Mosshide gnolls with their primary means of generating heat and cooking meat amidst the damp bogs of the Wetlands. Unfortunately for the marsh's ecosystem, the Mosshides fell living timber to feed their hearths and bonfires. This reckless harvesting and combustion of living boughs caught the ire of Rethiel the Greenwarden, who perceives each spark struck as an assault against the natural balance. Determined to stop the slaughter of the marsh's trees, Rethiel tasks passing adventurers with systematically stripping the Mosshide pack of their firestones. Rather than repurposing the scavenged flint, the guardian plans to smash every retrieved piece to dust and cast the fragments into the sea, ensuring the gnolls can no longer burn the Wetlands' living wood.

item:crystal-kelp-frond.text: Crystal Kelp Frond. Murlocs carry Crystal Kelp Fronds from the ocean to Crystal Lake in Elwynn Forest. William Pestle in Goldshire seeks them for an invisibility liquor. Crystal Kelp Fronds come from saltwater oceans, so their presence in Elwynn Forest’s fresh water is unusual. Murloc tribes along Crystal Lake’s shores gather and keep the fronds for reasons of their own. Alchemists value their strange power to distort sight. William Pestle in Goldshire uses them as the chief ingredient in an invisibility liquor, meant to help sweethearts slip past watchful family eyes.

item:crystal-phial.text: Crystal Phial. In Shadowglen, Tenaron Stormgrip entrusts young night elves with a Crystal Phial. They carry it to a nearby moonwell to draw sacred water for rites honoring and nourishing Teldrassil. Young night elves receive a Crystal Phial atop Aldrassil. Tenaron Stormgrip sends them to the moonwell just north of the bough to gather its glowing waters. The delicate vessel holds water touched by the sacred legacy of the Well of Eternity. Returning with a Filled Crystal Phial begins the Crown of the Earth pilgrimage, teaching the young kaldorei about the balance of magic, history, and nature in their new island home.

item:crystalized-scales.text: Crystalized Scales. Crystalized Scales are the hardened, mineralized hides harvested from basilisks dwelling in harsh Kalimdor environments such as the Charred Vale and Thousand Needles. When ground into a fine powder, these unusual scales serve as an exotic magical reagent coveted by spellcasters in Stormwind. Basilisks that endure extreme environmental heat and ash—particularly those dwelling within Stonetalon's Charred Vale or the shimmering salt flats of Thousand Needles—develop rigid, crystal-encrusted hides. These crystalized scales possess latent arcane resonance, making them exceptionally valuable to scholarly wizards across the Great Sea who experiment with rare spellcraft. In the human kingdom of Stormwind, the mage Collin Mauren actively seeks out adventurers journeying into the Kalimdor frontier to secure these scales. By pulverizing the crystalline mineral layers into dust, Mauren utilizes the particulate material as a vital reagent for newly conceived spells and personal arcane research.

item:curative-animal-salve.text: Curative Animal Salve. Across Darkshore and the Barrens, druids use Curative Animal Salve to treat sick wildlife. Herbalists prepare it in both lands, while the Cenarion Circle sees the animals’ afflictions as signs of a wider blight. Druids use Curative Animal Salve to ease sick wildlife in Darkshore and the Barrens. Alanndarian Nightsong directs young druids to treat sick deer between the Cliffspring River and the borders of Ashenvale. In the Barrens, Tonga Runetotem brews the same remedy for sick gazelles grazing north of the Crossroads. Each herbalist prepares the salve from locally gathered herbs in batches of ten doses. Field practitioners apply it directly to the animals, while both herbalists work with local authorities to produce larger supplies. The salve eases an animal’s suffering, but the Cenarion Circle sees the afflictions as signs of a wider disturbance. In Moonglade, Dendrite Starblaze observes that the afflicted deer on the coast and the suffering gazelles on the savannah are no random casualties. They are unwitting victims of a blight spreading across Kalimdor from multiple directions. For initiates, treating the animals tests their dedication to protecting nature and their skill in cleansing poison.

item:daffodil-bouquet.text: Daffodil Bouquet. The Daffodil Bouquet is a fresh bundle of bright flowers gathered by the herbalist Martie Jainrose in Lakeshire. Intended as a romantic token of appreciation from Guard Parker to Darcy, the gift inadvertently stokes local gossip and petty rivalry. When Guard Parker wishes to express his gratitude to Darcy at the Lakeshire inn for packing his daily lunch, he arranges a gesture through the town's herbalist, Martie Jainrose. Martie prepares a bouquet of daffodils, noting they are her personal favorite. However, when delivered to Darcy, the bright blooms immediately raise suspicions: Darcy recognizes the selection as Martie's signature flower and suspects petty jealousy from the other woman, half-joking that Martie might have poisoned the stems out of spite.

item:daggerspine-scale.text: Daggerspine Scale. A Daggerspine Scale is a tough reptilian scale harvested from the Daggerspine naga prowling the southern shores of the Hillsbrad Foothills. Sought after by the Royal Apothecary Society, these scales serve as a crucial catalyst to activate virulent brews in the Forsaken's ongoing plague experiments. The Royal Apothecary Society constantly seeks biological reagents to enhance their toxins, plagues, and concoctions. When refining the experimental brew known as the Elixir of Agony, the apothecaries discovered that scales taken from the local Daggerspine naga possessed unique reactive properties. When combined with troll regenerative elixirs and murloc organs, the scales help chemically activate dormant contaminating agents suspended in raw mixtures. Procuring them requires hunting along the rocky coastline east of Southshore, braving both the vicious naga tribe and nearby Alliance forces.

item:dal-bloodclaw-s-skull.text: Dal Bloodclaw's Skull. Dal Bloodclaw's Skull is taken from the chieftain of the Thistlefur furbolg in northern Ashenvale. Brought to Raene Wolfrunner in Astranaar, it serves as tangible proof that an imminent attack on the night elf settlement has been averted. The Thistlefur furbolgs residing north of Astranaar have grown rapidly in number and aggression, corrupted alongside much of Ashenvale's ancient forests. Fearing that the growing tribe would soon amass the courage to march directly on Astranaar, the night elf sentinel Raene Wolfrunner ordered the culling of their ranks and the death of their leader, Dal Bloodclaw. Claiming Dal Bloodclaw's Skull serves not as a trophy of petty vengeance, but as grim and undeniable evidence that the tribe's leadership has been shattered, buying the defenders of Astranaar precious time.

item:dalaran-mana-gem.text: Dalaran Mana Gem. Dalaran Mana Gems are crystallized arcane reserves carried by Kirin Tor personnel operating in Silverpine Forest. Forsaken spellcasters covet these gems as potent raw components for crafting enchanted vestments like spellfire robes. The mages, conjurors, and guards of the Kirin Tor stationed around Ambermill in Silverpine Forest carry specialized mana gems to focus and replenish their arcane energies. For the Forsaken practitioners in the Magic Quarter of the Undercity, these crystalline conduits represent an accessible source of concentrated magical essence. Although some undead mages acknowledge a shared academic heritage with Dalaran, pragmatic necessity and a philosophy of survival dictate that unyielding rivals are fair game to be stripped of their magical resources. When harvested from fallen Kirin Tor operatives, these gems are brought to tailors like Josef Gregorian in the Undercity alongside bundles of simple linen. While ordinary craftsmen cannot directly channel arcane power, skilled tailors can bind the mana gems into the weave of the cloth. This infusion transforms common thread into enchanted garments capable of bolstering a fledgling spellcaster's connection to the arcane.

item:dalaran-pendant.text: Dalaran Pendant. Dalaran Pendants are magical talismans carried by the Kirin Tor wizards stationed at the village of Ambermill in Silverpine Forest. The Forsaken seek to collect these pendants to disrupt the magi's arcane workings and trace the source of their power. In the village of Ambermill, Kirin Tor sorcerers, conjurers, and protectors actively weave formidable arcane spells threatening Forsaken control over southern Silverpine Forest. Each operative carries an attuned Dalaran Pendant. At the Sepulcher, Shadow Priest Allister tasks Forsaken operatives with recovering these pendants to slow down the mages' efforts and uncover who is guiding their magical weave.

item:dalaran-status-report.text: Dalaran Status Report. The Dalaran Status Report is a cache of sensitive intelligence compiled by the Kirin Tor wizards stationed at Ambermill in Silverpine Forest. It details the current state of the rebuilding city of Dalaran, making it a prized document for the Forsaken and the Deathstalkers of Undercity. The Scourge sacked Dalaran and Archimonde brought down its towering spires during the Third War. Its surviving magi removed its protective shield early in the reconstruction and are rebuilding the city in the open. The Kirin Tor also maintains enclaves such as Ambermill in southeastern Silverpine Forest. The Dalaran Status Report contains intelligence about the state of Dalaran sought by the Deathstalkers.

item:dalin-s-heart.text: Dalin's Heart. Dalin's Heart is a macabre ritual component carved from Dalin Forgewright, an honorable man patrolling near the Greymane Wall in Silverpine Forest. Undercity warlocks seek it out as an offering of unblemished purity, intended to lure and bind a succubus to their service. To summon and subjugate a succubus, Undercity warlocks require rare bait: the physical hearts of truly virtuous mortals. Dalin Forgewright earned his dark fate through selfless devotion, spending his days defending desperate Lordaeron refugees barred from safety at the sealed Greymane Wall. His unstinting altruism marks him as an emblem of goodness in a fallen land, making his heart an irresistible prize for demonic seduction rites conducted within the Temple of the Damned.

item:darkhound-blood.text: Darkhound Blood. Darkhound Blood is a foul bodily fluid harvested from the tainted canine beasts roaming the fields and forests of Tirisfal Glades. Gathered at the behest of the Royal Apothecary Society, it serves as an early reagent in their dark experiments to engineer a lethal new plague. Under the command of Lady Sylvanas Windrunner, the Royal Apothecary Society strives to develop a virulent contagion capable of wiping out Arthas and his Scourge. Stationed in Brill, Apothecary Johaan theorizes that local beasts, corrupted by dark energies and resilient to the surrounding decay, possess unusual biological properties. By distilling the blood of wild darkhounds, Johaan aims to uncover biological compounds that can resist or propagate virulent necrotic strains.

item:darkshore-grouper.text: Darkshore Grouper. Along Darkshore, grouper are a familiar catch, though murloc attacks have driven fishermen from their boats. The fish is prized for food and sport, and a good haul is harder to find. Darkshore Grouper are a welcome catch in the cold waters off Darkshore. Anglers around Auberdine value them for the simple dishes they make, and travelers and residents alike enjoy those meals. A fishing line and basic gear are enough to bring one in. For many fishermen, the pleasure of catching a grouper matches the pleasure of eating it. Fishermen such as Gubber Blump once took small boats into deeper waters and brought back grouper by the dozen. Coastal murlocs have grown more aggressive, grounding most boats around Auberdine. Anglers now fish from shore and dock, where locals suspect the murlocs are eating the grouper. A good haul takes patience.

item:darksoul-shackle.text: Darksoul Shackle. A Darksoul Shackle is an enchanted fetter worn by the Moonrage Darksoul worgen stalking Silverpine Forest. Crafted under the direction of Archmage Arugal, these implements are sought by Forsaken mages at the Sepulcher seeking to unravel the feral magic gripping the region. When Archmage Arugal unleashed the worgen upon Silverpine Forest, his own arcane mastery proved insufficient to fully direct and sustain the otherworldly beasts. To compensate for his shortcomings, he bound enchanted implements, such as Darksoul Shackles, to his creations. These fetters channel external sorcery into the Moonrage Darksouls, reinforcing their supernatural strength and anchoring the curse that keeps them thrall to Shadowfang Keep.

item:darnassus-marzipan.text: Darnassus Marzipan. At Hallow's End, Darnassus innkeepers hand out festive marzipan to visitors who dance for it. Crafted in the night elven capital for the autumn celebration, this sweet is one of four treats Jesper needs. During Hallow's End, Alliance capitals share a tradition of lighthearted trick-or-treating. Dwarves offer sharp mints, Stormwind makes chewy nougat, and Darnassus innkeepers prepare delicate marzipan for visitors. To receive a piece, you must show some festive spirit and dance when the innkeeper asks. The sweet is one of four regional treats sought by Jesper, a sick orphan in Stormwind's Cathedral Square who cannot go out to collect sweets himself.

item:darthalia-s-sealed-commendation.text: Darthalia's Sealed Commendation. Darthalia's Sealed Commendation is an official dispatch penned by the Forsaken battle commander in Tarren Mill. It praises a soldier's relentless campaign against the humans of Hillsbrad and delivers word of those victories directly to Undercity's high command. Following the brutal clashes across the Hillsbrad Foothills, High Executor Darthalia drafted this sealed dispatch to officially record victories against Hillsbrad's human defenders and the devastation wrought upon human positions. Sealed to preserve the commander's appraisal from prying eyes, the document is addressed to Varimathras, dreadlord advisor to Lady Sylvanas Windrunner. For the Forsaken leadership in the Royal Quarter, such missives offer tangible proof that Alliance enclaves south of Lordaeron can be broken, freeing northern garrisons to focus on the relentless threat of the Scourge.

item:deadmire-s-tooth.text: Deadmire's Tooth. Deadmire's Tooth is a trophy taken from the ancient crocolisk known as Deadmire, who stalks the murky waters of Dustwallow Marsh. Bringing it to the hunter Melor Stonehoof atop Thunder Bluff proves that the aging predator has been granted a merciful and honorable death. In the traditions of the tauren hunters on Hunter Rise, tracking wild beasts is not merely a test of martial prowess or mindless bloodsport. It is a spiritual covenant of balance, reverence, and occasionally, mercy. Deadmire was once one of the most magnificent crocolisks in Dustwallow Marsh, but his great age turned his final years into excruciating torment. Despite possessing the unyielding spirit and terrifying ferocity of his prime, his massive bones and failing body became a prison of endless pain. Claiming Deadmire's Tooth serves as physical proof to Melor Stonehoof that the beast's prolonged suffering has finally been brought to an end through an honorable hunt.

item:death-cap.text: Death Cap. In Darkshore, Death Cap grows in the cave behind Cliffspring Falls. Night elf herbalists seek the scarce fungus, but the Grove of the Ancients warns against approaching the falls. Death Cap grows in the damp cave behind Cliffspring Falls, along Darkshore's northeastern mountain ridges. Scaber stalks carpet the cavern floor, but Death Cap is scarce. Night elf herbalists such as Barithras Moonshade value it for experimental brewing. Finding even one means entering a cavern the Grove of the Ancients warns against, where corruption is taking root.

item:deathstalker-report.text: Deathstalker Report. The Deathstalker Report is a written dispatch penned by Deathstalker Rane Yorick detailing military reconnaissance in Silverpine Forest. It contains critical tactical intelligence intended for High Executor Hadrec at the Sepulcher regarding local Scourge movements and the state of the Forsaken's forward scouts. Reconnaissance in northern Silverpine Forest is a lethal duty, even for the undead. After finding themselves ambushed and pinned down by Scourge prowling the pine woods, Deathstalkers Rane Yorick and Quinn Yorick had to consolidate their findings into this hurried dispatch. The report summarizes unexpected levels of Scourge resistance threatening Forsaken territorial ambitions in the region. Because Quinn suffered grievous injuries during their mission, the document is entrusted to passing allies to ensure High Executor Hadrec receives word at the Sepulcher without delay.

item:deepfury-s-orders.text: Deepfury's Orders. Deepfury's Orders is a crumpled parchment recovered from the body of Ol' Rustlocke beneath the Thandol Span. It contains grim instructions belonging to the Dark Iron dwarves who ambushed the scouting dwarven defender. While scouting the foundations of the Thandol Span, the dwarven bridge defender Ol' Rustlocke was cornered and slain in a sudden Dark Iron ambush. Clasped beside the scout's clenched fist lay these orders, drafted by the enemy leader, Deepfury. The document serves as direct proof of a coordinated plot targeting the bridge that connects the Wetlands to the Arathi Highlands.

item:deepmoss-egg.text: Deepmoss Egg. In the Stonetalon Mountains, Deepmoss Eggs draw goblin merchants from Ratchet. Deepmoss spiders lay clustered clutches in the crags and canyons, and Booty Bay pirates prize them for omelettes. Deepmoss spiders nest across the Stonetalon Mountains, especially in Sishir Canyon and beneath the surviving trees of Windshear Crag. They leave clustered clutches of viable eggs in thick webbed sacks, sheltered by damp mountain moss. Most travelers have little use for them, but goblin traders see a chance to profit. Booty Bay has taken to spider egg omelettes, an eccentric culinary fad among wealthy pirates and adventurous diners. Local supplies cannot satisfy their appetite, so Mebok Mizzyrix of Ratchet arranges shipments through Wharfmaster Dizzywig. Collectors brave Stonetalon's venomous broods for fresh clutches, which become valuable cargo.

item:defias-docket.text: Defias Docket. Defias operatives have hidden their orders at Addle's Stead in western Duskwood. The docket gives Stormwind's search for its missing emissary a lead into the Brotherhood's plans. Master Elling Trias points investigators toward Duskwood as they follow leads on the kingdom's missing diplomat. Watcher Backus has noted unusual Defias movements converging on Addle's Stead, the derelict farm south of the road from Westfall. A strongbox on the property holds the Defias Docket. Its records track the Brotherhood's movements, revealing work that reaches beyond highway robbery and local banditry.

item:defias-tower-key.text: Defias Tower Key. At Klaven's Tower in Westfall, the Defias Tower Key proves an infiltrator reached the guarded perimeter. Stormwind operatives seek it from the malformed drones outside. Klaven's Tower stands on the Westfall coast as a Defias Brotherhood stronghold. Recent shipments from Duskwood brought new guards to its perimeter: malformed Defias drones, undead and covered in spikes. SI:7 operatives watch the grounds and direct field agents to pick the pockets of these sentries. Fighting them head-on is not the way to prove the perimeter has been breached. The key shows an infiltrator got through without raising an alarm.

item:deliah-s-ring.text: Deliah's Ring. Deliah's Ring is an engraved piece of jewelry recovered from a corpse pile amassed by the Rot Hide gnolls in Silverpine Forest. Bearing the inscription 'For Deliah', the keepsake offers a grim trail tracing back to a plague victim stolen from Tirisfal's mass graves. Discovered upon the pockmarked, relatively fresh hand of a corpse among gnoll mounds in Silverpine Forest, the ring is inscribed simply: 'For Deliah'. The discovery reveals that the local Rot Hide gnolls are not merely scavenging battlefields—they are actively raiding the mass graves of Tirisfal Glades and ferrying human and Forsaken corpses south to Fenris Isle for their own vile purposes.

item:delivery-to-mathias.text: Delivery to Mathias. Keryn Sylvius sends a sealed parcel from Goldshire to Master Mathias Shaw in Stormwind. The delivery gives a promising rogue entry into SI:7's inner workings. A parcel from the Lion's Pride Inn to the Stormwind Barracks may look like ordinary courier work. For a budding rogue, it is an audition for Stormwind Intelligence. Local trainer Keryn Sylvius entrusts the package to novice cutpurses, giving them a direct introduction to Master Mathias Shaw. The delivery tests whether they can cross the capital quietly, keep a low profile, and follow discreet orders without asking questions. The handoff brings an operative into SI:7 headquarters in Old Town. Mathias Shaw uses such deliveries to separate pretenders from true talents. Those who present the parcel without faltering receive high-stakes field assignments, beginning with covert reconnaissance and infiltration against Defias smuggling networks in Elwynn Forest.

item:deviate-hide.text: Deviate Hide. Deviate Hides are the mutated skins stripped from the beasts dwelling within the Wailing Caverns. Warped by the corrupting dream of the druid Naralex, these otherworldly pelts are sought by druids looking to repurpose the nightmare's taint into durable leather goods. When the night elf druid Naralex entered his deep slumber beneath the Barrens, his dream turned into an Emerald Nightmare that warped the local cavern ecology. The beasts lurking in the depths transformed into unnatural deviate predators with tough, mutated hides. While inherently touched by evil, these pelts possess unusual, supple resilience that makes them uniquely suited for leathercrafting. Nalpak, perched high above the cavern mouth in the skull-shaped rock formation, collects these hides to study their properties and fashion them into sturdy utility packs.

item:devlin-s-remains.text: Devlin's Remains. Devlin's Remains are the collected skeletal bones of Devlin Agamand, the younger son of the wealthy family who owned the Agamand Mills. Stalking the roads near his ruined ancestral estate as a mindless Scourge thrall, he was struck down to deliver his bones to a vengeful survivor in Brill. In life, Devlin Agamand stood in the shadow of his elder brother Thurman. Where Thurman was gentle and tall, Devlin was remembered as physically frail and viciously sharp-tongued. When the Plague of Undeath swept through northern Tirisfal Glades, the Agamand family failed to protect their lands and laborers. Devlin was among the first to fall, reanimated as a ravenous Scourge ghoul whose frantic, mad chattering haunted the roadside leading up to Agamand Mills. Coleman Farthing, a Forsaken residing in Brill, holds a deep and abiding grudge against the entire Agamand bloodline. Holding them directly responsible for failing his family when the plague arrived, Farthing tasked travelers with laying Devlin to rest and collecting his remains. Farthing sought to display Devlin's bones upon his mantle, savoring the knowledge that his former masters have been reduced to dust and shattered fragments under his heel.

item:dirt-caked-pendant.text: Dirt-Caked Pendant. In the Barrens, a captive orc gives up the Dirt-Caked Pendant he carried. The keepsake reaches Gan'rul Bloodeye in Orgrimmar, where it is used to draw a succubus.

item:disarming-colloid.text: Disarming Colloid. Disarming Colloid is a specialized chemical agent formulated to counter the volatility of Seaforium explosive powder. Provided by the dwarf Ashlan Stonesmirk in the Wetlands, it serves as the crucial stabilizing component in a neutralizing mixture meant to prevent a catastrophic demolition of the Stonewrought Dam. When Ashlan Stonesmirk analyzed the unusual blasting powder left by Dark Iron sappers at the Stonewrought Dam in Loch Modan, he recognized it immediately by its distinct scent and fine silver crystals: Seaforium. While harmless when completely dry, Seaforium becomes immensely destructive upon contact with moisture, making it an existential threat to the waterlogged Stonewrought Dam. To halt this reaction before a detonation occurs, Stonesmirk provided a disarming colloid. When combined with three specific local reagents—lurker venom, crushed Mo'grosh crystal, and a crocolisk tear—this colloid effectively neutralizes the explosive properties of the Seaforium compound.

item:disarming-mixture.text: Disarming Mixture. Disarming Mixture is a specialized chemical concoction prepared by Chief Engineer Hinderweir at the Stonewrought Dam. Created to neutralize volatile Seaforium explosives, it is used to prevent Dark Iron saboteurs from destroying the massive dwarven structure holding back the waters of Loch Modan. When Dark Iron saboteurs planted a heavy Seaforium charge beneath the foundation of the Stonewrought Dam, standard methods of defusal were far too risky. Lacking immediate Mountaineer support, Chief Engineer Hinderweir combined the Disarming Mixture from ingredients named by the explosives expert Ashlan Stonesmirk to rapidly neutralize the underwater explosive. When stirred directly into the planted powder keg, the solution neutralizes the reactive compounds, reducing a catastrophic explosion to a harmless, fizzling ruin.

item:divined-scroll.text: Divined Scroll. The Divined Scroll is an enchanted parchment used by the night elves of Silverwind Refuge to unmask the source of Ashenvale's disturbed waters. By channeling the residual magic within intact water elemental bracers, the scroll reveals the identity of the rogue spellcaster summoning them. The tainted waters of Mystral Lake have long troubled the Sentinels guarding Ashenvale. To pinpoint who is manipulating the water elementals infesting the lake, Sentinel Velene Starstrike provides travelers with an uncharged divining scroll. By gathering intact bracers directly from the slain elementals and using them as an arcane reagent, the latent bindings within the metal bleed into the parchment. The resulting Divined Scroll exposes the magical signature of the rogue wizard behind the infestation.

item:divining-scroll.text: Divining Scroll. The Divining Scroll is an enchanted parchment provided by Sentinel Velene Starstrike at Silverwind Refuge. Its magic allows investigators to trace the magical signature of the unnatural water elementals infesting Ashenvale back to their creator. When corrupt water elementals began rising from the pristine pools of Ashenvale, the Sentinels knew the disturbance was not a natural emergence. Sentinel Velene Starstrike acquired this divination scroll to identify the person responsible. By channeling the scroll's magic through intact elemental bracers as a focusing reagent, the user extracts the summoner's signature, transforming the blank parchment into a Divined Scroll that names the guilty party.

item:dogran-s-pendant.text: Dogran's Pendant. Dogran's Pendant draws a succubus toward the warlocks of Orgrimmar. Dogran, a wounded orc, carries it while separated from his mate, Zankaja. In the Cleft of Shadow, warlocks turn the sorrow bound to it into a lure. Dogran's Pendant carries the sorrow of an orc separated from Zankaja. Captivity and crippling wounds have overshadowed their love. The warlocks of the Cleft of Shadow know that demons such as succubi prey on love, yearning, and vulnerability. They use the pendant's grief to draw a succubus across the Twisting Nether and into Neeru Fireblade's summoning circle.

item:dolanaar-delivery.text: Dolanaar Delivery. In Shadowglen, young travelers carry harvested herbs south to Dolanaar. Porthannius entrusts them with the bundle for Innkeeper Keldamyr. Fresh herbs from Aldrassil are bound for Dolanaar. Porthannius is occupied with matters among the druids of Shadowglen, so he entrusts the bundle to young travelers heading south along the road. They carry it to Innkeeper Keldamyr. The parcel brings you to Dolanaar's inn, where Keldamyr receives it with gratitude. The inn offers weary travelers rest, peace of mind, and sanctuary before they venture deeper into Teldrassil.

item:dragonmaw-war-banner.text: Dragonmaw War Banner. Dragonmaw War Banners are rallying standards carried by the Dragonmaw orcs entrenched in the Wetlands. Stamped with the iconography of their clan, they serve as proof of battle for the dwarven defenders of Menethil Harbor seeking to quell the rising orcish threat. Following the Second War, the Dragonmaw clan was shattered after losing control of their enslaved red dragons. The enraged drakes turned on their captors, driving the survivors out of Grim Batol and into the eastern hills. In recent times, the remaining orcs have begun gathering strength once more under Chieftain Nek'rosh, raising their war banners over encampments northeast of Menethil Harbor. These crude, imposing standards represent both their lingering defiance and a direct menace to the marshland settlements. Captain Stoutfist, stationed at Menethil Harbor, tasks Alliance adventurers with striking into the marsh encampments to bring back these banners. Trophies stripped from raiders, centurions, and bone-warders, the banners confirm to the dwarven garrison that the Dragonmaw encampments are being systematically broken before the clan can launch coordinated raids.

item:dried-seeds.text: Dried Seeds. At the Crossroads, Tonga Runetotem gives travelers Dried Seeds to test the life-giving power beneath the Barrens' waters.

item:durnan-s-scalding-mornbrew.text: Durnan's Scalding Mornbrew. Durnan's Scalding Mornbrew is a freshly poured, piping-hot dwarven beverage intended for Durnan Furcutter in Coldridge Valley. Because the drink quickly loses its heat in the frigid mountain air, it must be rushed directly to Anvilmar before it goes cold. In the biting chill of Coldridge Valley, few comforts rival a mug of fresh mornbrew served piping hot. When a courier gets delayed delivering a round to Grelin Whitebeard, the fresh cup meant for Durnan Furcutter inside Anvilmar risks freezing over. Durnan specifically expects his brew scalding, leaving only a short window of a few minutes to carry the steaming mug up the snowy path into the mountain hall before it cools completely.

item:durotar-tiger-fur.text: Durotar Tiger Fur. Across the Echo Isles off Durotar's southeastern coast, tigers supply fur for the Darkspear, whose refugee population keeps growing. The trolls use the pelts for blankets, tents, and armor. In Sen'jin Village, the Darkspear must make scarce supplies last. They let the local tigers thrive until their growing needs call for a cull. Trolls cure the thick hides into goods their settlement needs, including protective armor and warm blankets for changing seasonal weather. The Echo Isles lie south of Durotar, across open water. The Darkspear once called the archipelago home, until the witch doctor Zalazane drove them out. Hunters face dangers from Zalazane's thralls and from tigers waiting among the thick foliage. Experienced hunters such as Vel'rin Fang speak of spending entire days motionless in the jungle brush to secure a single clean kill.

item:duskbat-wing.text: Duskbat Wing. A Duskbat Wing is a raw material harvested from the leather-winged bats flitting through the gloom around Deathknell. In the resource-starved Forsaken settlement, these leathery appendages are salvaged and repurposed by local tailors into sturdy makeshift armor for newly risen soldiers. When new undead claw their way from the soil of Deathknell, they emerge bearing little more than rags and brittle bones. Surrounded by the lingering Scourge mindless and hostile wildlife, the fledgling Forsaken must scrape together whatever protective gear they can find. Novice Elreth, assistant to Shadow Priest Sarvis, collects Duskbat Wings alongside wolf paws to piece together and reinforce clothing and armor for freshly raised warriors before they are sent into the wilderness to fight.

item:dusky-crab-cakes.text: Dusky Crab Cakes. Dusky Crab Cakes are a savory dish prepared by Chef Grual in Darkshire to satisfy the desperate hunger of Jitters. The local delicacy has a tangy flavor, and a famished Jitters considers it an exquisite meal.

item:dust-devil-debris.text: Dust Devil Debris. Across Westfall, Dust Devils leave charged grit in their wake. Mages value this debris as a reagent for enchanting parchment and binding messaging spells into scrolls. Dust Devils sweep across Westfall’s plains as violent whirlwinds. When one is struck down, the living storm collapses into charged dust and grit called Dust Devil Debris. A faint trace of the elemental vortex remains in the residue. In Stormwind, arcane practitioners such as Collin Mauren prize it for specialized sorcery. Infused into enchanted ink and parchment, the grit helps a wizard bind an airy messaging spell to a scroll, carrying words across the kingdom.

item:dwarven-tinder.text: Dwarven Tinder. Dwarven Tinder is a specially prepared flammable substance used by Alliance forces in the Wetlands. It was distributed to saboteurs tasked with incinerating the Dragonmaw clan's siege engines before they could be brought against Menethil Harbor. When Alliance scouts discovered that Chieftain Nek'rosh had constructed heavy catapults within the Dragonmaw encampment, Menethil Harbor faced an imminent crisis. Cut off from southern reinforcements by intense fighting in Dun Algaz, the defenders could not survive a prolonged siege. The solution was preemptive sabotage. Provided to volunteers advancing into orcish territory, Dwarven Tinder catches quickly from a struck spark, producing flames intense enough to consume reinforced wooden siege engines in minutes.

item:ear-of-balgaras.text: Ear of Balgaras. The Ear of Balgaras serves as grim proof of the death of Balgaras the Foul, a Dark Iron warlock who led the assault on Dun Modr. Recovered from the cowardly commander's corpse, it brings closure to the Ironforge mountaineers defending the northern Wetlands. Dun Modr fell into ruins when Dark Iron invaders sabotaged the Thandol Span and wiped out the local dwarven garrison. Their commander in the field was Balgaras the Foul, a scheming warlock who directed his troops from the shadows while shying away from personal combat. For Longbraid the Grim, the mountain king's officer stationed outside the ruined outpost, justice demanded tangible evidence of the ringleader's fall. Severing Balgaras's ear provides absolute verification that the warlock's reign of terror at the northern border has ended. The loss of Dun Modr cost Longbraid his brother along with dozens of stout soldiers who perished during the collapse of the West Bridge. Presenting the warlock's ear does not mend the shattered span or revive the fallen, but it destabilizes the surviving Dark Iron forces scattered through the northern Wetlands. Without Balgaras to direct them, the remaining raiders become far easier for Ironforge's scouts to contain before another commander is sent from the south.

item:ebonlocke-s-response-to-solomon.text: Ebonlocke's Response to Solomon. Ebonlocke's Response to Solomon is an official letter penned by Lord Ello Ebonlocke, the mayor of Darkshire. Carried back to Lakeshire, it flatly rejects Redridge's desperate plea for military assistance from the Night Watch. Facing blackrock orc incursions, Magistrate Solomon of Lakeshire sought reinforcements from Duskwood after Stormwind ignored his petitions. Lord Ello Ebonlocke's reply is scathing and uncompromising. Ebonlocke points out that the Night Watch exists only because Stormwind abandoned Darkshire when corrupting magic first gripped the woods. Stripping the town of its defenders to aid Redridge would leave Duskwood defenceless, ensuring it fell to evil before the militia even reached the forest's edge.

item:echeyakee-s-hide.text: Echeyakee's Hide. At the Crossroads, Sergra Darkthorn awaits the pale hide of Whitemist, the legendary white lion of the Barrens. Tauren honor the beast as an embodiment of mercy and death, while hunters bring the pelt as proof of their prowess. Echeyakee means Whitemist in the Taur-ahe tongue. The lion earned that name among the savannah's predators for his stealthy white coat and swift kills, ending prey's lives before fear or pain could take hold. A hunter summons the elusive cat near the giant kodo bones northeast of the Crossroads with a ceremonial horn, then claims his pelt. Bringing it to Sergra Darkthorn proves martial skill and honors Whitemist's silent, merciful end.

item:egalin-s-grimoire.text: Egalin's Grimoire. Egalin's Grimoire is a prized arcane tome detailing the foundational rites required to summon and command a voidwalker. Penned by a master warlock, it serves as an essential teaching text within the Undercity's Temple of the Damned. Written by the master summoner Egalin, this grimoire details the delicate and dangerous process of pulling a being of chaos from the Nether. Egalin was renowned among practitioners for his effortless command over summoned voidwalkers, an ability passed down to his students, including Carendin Halgar. Without the specific formulas and channeling methods recorded in the text, an unprepared summoner risks being torn apart by the very entity they call forth.

item:electropeller.text: Electropeller. In Darkshore, Wizbang Cranktoggle's electropellers lie scattered in freshwater rivers after a failed night outing. Wizbang Cranktoggle built the electropeller to propel an experimental exploding duck decoy. The gnome inventor works out of Auberdine. While scouting Darkshore's waterways after too many drinks, he blacked out. Hours later, he woke with singed hair and an empty pack. His electropellers had tumbled into Darkshore's freshwater currents, where they remain scattered through rivers and lakes until patient anglers recover them.

item:elixir-of-pain.text: Elixir of Pain. The Elixir of Pain is an experimental alchemical concoction brewed by Forsaken apothecaries stationed in Tarren Mill. Distilled using blood harvested across the foothills, the mixture is designed to test biological agents intended to serve Lady Sylvanas's darker ambitions. The Royal Apothecary Society relentlessly pursues new formulas to bolster the Forsaken's position against their mortal neighbors and the Scourge. The Elixir of Pain represents one such trial, blended from freshly harvested ingredients collected around the Hillsbrad Foothills. Concocted with little regard for the living, the potion serves as a proof of concept for volatile substances intended to aid the Dark Lady.

item:elixir-of-suffering.text: Elixir of Suffering. The Elixir of Suffering is an alchemical concoction brewed by Apothecary Lydon in Tarren Mill. Developed under the orders of the Royal Apothecary Society, the draught is an experimental step toward a virulent plague intended to eradicate both living humans and the Scourge. Within the ruined hamlet of Tarren Mill, Apothecary Lydon tirelessly combines raw reagents gathered from the surrounding wilderness into toxic draughts. The Elixir of Suffering represents an early milestone in the Royal Apothecary Society's overarching mandate: formulating a new plague designed to exterminate the living and dead alike. Lydon tests the lethal brew on his unfortunate assistant, a frog named Umpi, to ensure its potency.

item:elune-s-tear.text: Elune's Tear. Elune's Tear is a rare, luminous mineral found on the central island of Iris Lake in Ashenvale. Revering it as a sacred blessing of the Moon Goddess, night elf herbalists and healers seek the stone for its potent ability to cleanse magical corruption and deadly sickness. Found secluded upon the small islet in Iris Lake east of Astranaar, Elune's Tear is a mystical stone believed to carry the purity of the Moon Goddess herself. The lake itself has not escaped the forest's corruption: its waters have turned a sickly green, and twisted bog beasts roam its shores. The stone is famous among local night elf herbalists and healers—such as Orendil Broadleaf—as an emergency remedy capable of washing away deep-seated corruption when ordinary woodland poultices fail.

item:embalming-ichor.text: Embalming Ichor. Embalming Ichor is an unnatural preserving fluid harvested from the bodies of Rot Hide gnolls in northern Tirisfal Glades. It sustains the gnolls' animated existence and has drawn the close interest of the Forsaken Apothecaries, who seek to analyze its properties to counter the Scourge. The Rot Hide gnolls infesting Garren's Haunt and the nearby mass graves are not typical wild beasts; they are rotting, preserved thralls deployed by the Scourge to dig up plague victims. Flowing through their decayed veins is Embalming Ichor, a foul fluid that artificially preserves their flesh and grants them enduring unlife. For Magistrate Sevren in Brill, recovering vials of this ichor serves a dual purpose: it confirms the destruction of these graverobbers and provides Royal Apothecary Society researchers with fresh specimens to dissect, study, and weaponize against the Lich King's minions.

item:emerald-dreamcatcher.text: Emerald Dreamcatcher. In Starbreeze Village, the Emerald Dreamcatcher lies forgotten after the Gnarlpine furbolgs drove out its people. Druids of Ban’ethil Barrow Den gave it to Tallonkai Swiftroot, hoping it would draw vigor from the Emerald Dream. Gaerolas Talvethren, the druidic warden of Ban’ethil Barrow Den, oversaw the making of the Emerald Dreamcatcher. The druids gave the enchanted amulet to only a chosen few. It draws ambient energy from the Emerald Dream, bringing fortune and protection to whoever carries it. When the maddened Gnarlpine furbolgs overran Starbreeze Village, the amulet remained inside a dresser, stranded in hostile, corrupted territory.

item:empty-blue-waterskin.text: Empty Blue Waterskin. Brine sends the Empty Blue Waterskin north from the Barrens to gather sacred water. The liquid will help her prepare the draught needed to summon and appease the water spirit. Brine gives the Empty Blue Waterskin to a shaman initiate at her hilltop hut in the southern Barrens. The vessel marks the final and most perilous gathering task of early training. To commune with the spirit of water, the initiate must seek pure, undisturbed sources across Kalimdor. The waterskin is meant for a secluded fountain deep within the Ruins of Stardust, along Ashenvale's contested borderlands. The initiate must leave the safety of Horde territory and travel into ancient groves guarded by nature beasts and night elves. At a fountain in the ruined sanctuary deep within the Ruins of Stardust, the waterskin is filled and becomes a Filled Blue Waterskin. With water samples from the Barrens and Tarren Mill, its contents let Brine brew the draught needed to summon and appease the elemental spirit of water.

item:empty-brown-waterskin.text: Empty Brown Waterskin. In the Barrens, Brine gives an empty waterskin to a shaman initiate. Brine gives a shaman initiate an empty leather skin for the opening trial of the Call of Water. The initiate must carry it to the watering hole beneath her dwelling and return with it full. The pool is guarded by local quilboar, who prize its water. In the Barrens, where water is scarce, even a small oasis can sustain life and spark violence.

item:empty-cleansing-bowl.text: Empty Cleansing Bowl. At Auberdine, the Empty Cleansing Bowl carries moonwell water against the Blackwood corruption. Mixed with food samples, the water makes a meal that briefly breaks the satyrs’ demonic sway over the furbolgs. Thundris Windweaver gives the Empty Cleansing Bowl to adventurers in Auberdine to carry sacred water from the local moonwell. The night elves have learned that satyrs use enchanted talismans to drive the northern Blackwood furbolgs into demonic madness. Dip the bowl into the moonwell, then mix the water with nuts, grains, and fruits gathered from the furbolgs. The blessed meal briefly restores the afflicted creatures’ sanity and reveals the satyr overseer responsible.

item:empty-cliffspring-falls-sampler.text: Empty Cliffspring Falls Sampler. At Cliffspring Falls in Darkshore, young druids gather water to investigate a poison killing local wildlife. The Cenarion Circle gives them empty samplers for water from the cave mouth. Cliffspring Falls feeds northern Darkshore, so trouble in its headwaters threatens the local wildlife. When a wasting poison began killing the region’s deer, Dendrite Starblaze of the Cenarion Circle gave empty samplers to young druids sent from Moonglade. They must reach the cliffs by the falls and gather water at a cave entrance overrun by hostile naga.

item:empty-dreadmist-peak-sampler.text: Empty Dreadmist Peak Sampler. At Dreadmist Peak, druids seek tainted water in an empty Cenarion vessel. The sample may help diagnose and cure the blight spreading among wildlife in the northern Barrens. Dendrite Starblaze suspects the pools atop Dreadmist Peak are at the heart of a sickness afflicting gazelles and unsettling the northern Barrens. The pools influence the weather, and the druid fears they are tied to the spreading blight. He sends druid initiates with empty samplers to brave the mountain heights and draw water from the peak. The Burning Blade, a demon-worshipping cult, now infests the mountain.

item:empty-leaden-collection-phial.text: Empty Leaden Collection Phial. The Empty Leaden Collection Phial is a shielded container designed by gnome tinkerers to harvest radioactive fallout from the ruins of Gnomeregan. Crafted from lead to protect the bearer from lethal contamination, it is used by adventurers assisting Ozzie Togglevolt in Kharanos. Ozzie hopes the captured glow might yield a cure for their afflicted kin—or at least an extraordinarily potent beverage. When the vents of Gnomeregan flooded the subterranean city with toxic radiation to purge the trogg menace, it instead warped the surviving defenders into leper gnomes and irradiated the invading beasts. Seeking to study and reverse the fallout, Ozzie Togglevolt crafted the Empty Leaden Collection Phial. Made of heavy lead to shield handlers from the ambient danger, the specialized vial draws in the noxious green glow lingering on the bodies of Irradiated Invaders and Pillagers that prowl the ruins. Once sealed, the resulting Full Leaden Collection Phial provides the raw, dangerous matter needed for experimental remedies.

item:empty-red-waterskin.text: Empty Red Waterskin. In Tarren Mill, an empty red waterskin is bound for a well untouched by blight. Brine gives it to shaman initiates for their elemental trials. Brine gives shaman initiates this plain red skin for the Call of Water trials. They carry it across the sea to Tarren Mill in the Hillsbrad Foothills. The Forsaken occupy the town, but its central well still draws fresh spring water. The filled skin brings a sample to Brine, who blends the water into a vial of purest water for the initiate’s trial.

item:empty-sampling-tube.text: Empty Sampling Tube. Thundris Windweaver gives an Empty Sampling Tube in Auberdine to gather water from the Cliffspring River. Night elf scholars study the taint threatening Darkshore. Darkshore's waterways are turning foul as blight spreads through the wilderness. Thundris Windweaver, an investigator in Auberdine, gives you an empty glass tube to collect water from the Cliffspring River. Take the sample from the pool beneath the first waterfall north of town. Night elf naturalists examine it to learn about the corruption flowing toward Mist's Edge.

item:empty-water-tube.text: Empty Water Tube. In Auberdine, the Empty Water Tube is ready to gather sacred moonwell water for the red crystal on Darkshore’s eastern cliffs. Sentinels and scholars seek pure lunar essence to study the mysterious red crystal along Darkshore’s eastern ridge. Ordinary glass or flasks can contaminate consecrated water, so investigators visiting Auberdine’s moonwell receive this sealed vial for the work. They carry its filled contents up the mountain slopes to learn how the alien mineral responds to Elune’s magic.

item:enchanted-gaea-seeds.text: Enchanted Gaea Seeds. Enchanted Gaea Seeds are specially prepared botanical seeds meant to bring revitalization to the ravaged landscapes of Kalimdor. Empowered through druidic magic and gathered at Sun Rock Retreat, they are planted directly into the ash-choked soil of the Charred Vale to counteract devastation and rekindle natural growth. The Enchanted Gaea Seeds represent the Horde's druidic efforts to mend the deep scars left across Stonetalon Mountains. After raw Gaea Seeds are gathered and ritually enchanted by Tammra Windfield at Sun Rock Retreat, they carry sufficient resilience to overcome pervasive corruption and elemental blight. When pressed into the fertile dirt mounds that still survive beneath the soot of the Charred Vale, these seeds take root against the harsh conditions, anchoring new life in a landscape dominated by hostile fire elementals and invasive harpies. The goal of planting these enchanted seeds extends beyond simple gardening; it is an active effort to turn the tide in the struggle for Stonetalon's future. The magic woven into the husks allows them to resist lingering corruption and establish a foothold for native flora. As they flourish, the restored vegetation is intended to soothe the agitated fire elementals, crowd out feral harpies, and counter the rampant deforestation driven by the Venture Company's relentless logging operations.

item:enchanted-resonite-crystal.text: Enchanted Resonite Crystal. The Enchanted Resonite Crystal is an alchemically altered mineral infused with shamanic magic by Mor'rogal in the Stonetalon Mountains. It is crafted specifically to shatter the Resonite cask binding a slumbering, ancient Earthen named Goggeroc. Raw resonite crystals gathered from the deep caverns of the Stonetalon Mountains possess unusual harmonic and earthen properties. Recognizing the danger slumbering within a sealed subterranean cask, the shaman Mor'rogal altered the raw minerals using his elemental powers. The resulting Enchanted Resonite Crystal serves as a precise tool: when struck against the reinforced Resonite cask, it disrupts the housing and forcibly rouses the giant Earthen Goggeroc while he is still disoriented from his long sleep.

item:encrypted-memorandum.text: Encrypted Memorandum. The Encrypted Memorandum is a coded missive handed to novice rogues starting out in Coldridge Valley. Though disguised as official communication, it is actually a clandestine invitation from the local rogue trainer, Solm Hargrin, calling for solidarity among scoundrels in exile. In the bustling dwarven refuge of Anvilmar, rogues must maintain a low profile. Rather than approaching recruits in plain view, the trainer Solm Hargrin uses the Encrypted Memorandum to establish contact. Masked as an official directive from distant superiors, the coded parchment ensures that fledgling rogues know where to find mentorship without drawing unwanted attention from the local guards or suspicious townsfolk.

item:encrypted-parchment.text: Encrypted Parchment. In the Valley of Trials, Encrypted Parchment guides young orc rogues toward the Den. Gornek hands it to recruits who show promise, and its cipher points them to Rwag, the hidden trainer. Young orcs prove their strength in the Valley of Trials under the open sun. Those who show a gift for stealth, deception, and bladecraft draw different notice. After facing the local wildlife, promising orc rogues receive Encrypted Parchment from Gornek. Its coded words call to those who can read a message meant to stay hidden. The cipher leads a novice into the Den, past the other clan trainers, to find Rwag. The recruit learns there that the Shattered Hand arranged the summons. The order works within the Horde's covert network, and answering the call begins a rogue's training in espionage and shadowcraft.

item:encrypted-rune.text: Encrypted Rune. An Encrypted Rune is a coded summoning message handed to promising new rogues in Coldridge Valley. Delivered covertly, it bids the bearer to decipher its contents and seek out the rogue trainer Solm Hargrin inside Anvilmar. In the sheltered snowy basin of Coldridge Valley, overt recruitment is rarely the style of the local scoundrels and scouts. Instead, novitiates showing a knack for stealth and cunning are slipped an Encrypted Rune. Marked with subtle ciphers, the inscribed stone carries a discreet invitation from Solm Hargrin, the rogue mentor quartered in Anvilmar. It serves as both a private test of literacy in thieves' cant and an introduction to the shadowy craft needed to survive Dun Morogh's harsh wilderness. Deciphering the rune directs new rogues to Solm, who looks to bolster the valley's covert ranks amidst rising local tensions. Beyond basic bladecraft and stealth techniques, Solm emphasizes vigilance and camaraderie, reminding incoming rogues that in this time of strained peace it is all the more important for their kind to stick together.

item:encrypted-scroll.text: Encrypted Scroll. The Encrypted Scroll is a discreet parchment delivered to promising newly risen rogues in Deathknell. Bearing the seal of David Trias, it directs the recipient to introduce themselves for formal training among the Forsaken's covert operatives. When a freshly awakened Forsaken shows an aptitude for stealth and subterfuge, they do not remain unnoticed for long. The Encrypted Scroll is handed over in Deathknell once a scout proves capable against the mindless Scourge roaming the nearby graveyard. Bearing the personal seal of the rogue trainer David Trias, the scroll instructs the bearer to seek him out in the local inn. It serves as an initial vetting process, pointing fledgling operatives toward the discipline required to serve the Dark Lady rather than wasting their second chance at life as mere pickpockets. The message itself is brief, directing the rogue to establish contact within Deathknell before venturing deeper into Tirisfal Glades. Trias keeps tabs on up-and-coming talent on behalf of the Shadowstalkers, the covert arm of the Forsaken. To survive in Lordaeron, the Forsaken rely heavily on silent blades and cunning scouts to counter the Scarlet Crusade, surviving Alliance enclaves, and leftover Scourge filth. Answering this ciphered summons is the first step toward joining that covert network.

item:encrypted-sigil.text: Encrypted Sigil. In Shadowglen, the Encrypted Sigil carries a summons to newly awakened night elf rogues. Frahun Shadewhisper calls them to begin training as dangers gather around Teldrassil. New night elf scouts and infiltrators in Shadowglen receive the Encrypted Sigil through discreet means. A quiet messenger delivers it on behalf of Frahun Shadewhisper. Its contents are hidden instructions that tell the initiate to report to Frahun near Aldrassil. Reading and delivering the token shows Frahun that an initiate can follow subtle directions and handle covert messages. Frahun uses the summons to explain why rogues matter in an unsettled world. Tensions simmer between the night elves and the distant Horde, but open warfare is not the only danger facing their people. Rogues must gather intelligence across Teldrassil as the Kaldorei’s unseen eyes and blades, and learn to strike before threats take root in the World Tree’s boughs.

item:encrypted-tablet.text: Encrypted Tablet. In the Valley of Trials, the Encrypted Tablet sends novice troll rogues to Rwag. The rogue trainer inscribes its coded message and keeps his post inside the Den. Novice troll rogues receive the Encrypted Tablet when they arrive in the Valley of Trials. Its ciphered words direct them to Rwag, an orc trainer who lives in the Den’s shaded caves. The slate keeps the local shadow operatives’ business discreet while testing whether new recruits can understand its message. Deciphering the tablet brings recruits into contact with the Horde’s wider shadow network. When they report to Rwag, scouts learn that syndicates such as the Shattered Hand watch their progress. The syndicates rely on valley trainers to judge whether prospective cutpurses, spies, and assassins are sharp enough to serve the new nation.

item:essence-of-nightlash.text: Essence of Nightlash. The Essence of Nightlash is the lingering magical remnant collected from the defeated banshee Nightlash at the Dead Fields. It serves as irrefutable proof for High Executor Hadrec that the Scourge force bolstering the local rot hide gnolls has been broken. At an abandoned farmstead in northern Silverpine known as the Dead Fields, packs of undead rot hide gnolls have entrenched themselves under Scourge command. Initial Forsaken assaults were repeatedly broken not by the feral gnolls, but by their spectral commander: the banshee Nightlash. Calling upon wailing magics, she reinforced the gnoll lines and routed the forces sent from the Sepulcher. Slaying her dissolves her incorporeal form into dust, leaving behind a crystalline, magical essence that represents her permanent dissolution. Because banshees leave behind no corporeal corpse, the Essence of Nightlash is the only physical evidence that the malevolent spirit has been destroyed.
