High Executor Hadrec at the Sepulcher requires this essence to verify that the Scourge's local foothold has collapsed, allowing the Forsaken to finally secure their northern perimeter and suppress the rot hide threat.

item:essential-artificial.text: Essential Artificial. An Essential Artificial is a versatile, standardized mechanical component vital to gnomish tinkers and engineers. Left behind in stockpiles during the frantic evacuation of Gnomeregan, these parts are highly sought after by gnomes seeking to rebuild their technological efforts from exile in Ironforge. Before the fall of Gnomeregan, the essential artificial served as a cornerstone of day-to-day gnomish engineering. Described by tinkers as a nigh-universal component, it was integrated into countless contraptions, clockwork wonders, and heavy machinery throughout the subterranean halls. Its standardized nature made it indispensable to smiths and machinists seeking reliable, interchangeable modular parts. When the trogg invasion and subsequent radiation disaster forced the gnomes into a desperate, panicked exodus, massive reserves of these components were abandoned where they sat. They remain stored inside heavy, steam-powered dispensers known as artificial extrapolators scattered across the deeper passages of Gnomeregan. In Tinker Town, master craftsman Klockmort Spannerspan actively recruits daring adventurers to venture back into the contaminated ruins and salvage these parts so research and invention can continue.

item:etched-note.text: Etched Note. The Etched Note is a formal summons delivered to promising young tauren hunters resting at Camp Narache. Penned by the camp's hunter trainer, Lanka Farshot, the message welcomes the novice into the traditions of the hunt and calls them forward for their initial instruction. Within the safe confines of Camp Narache, young shu'halo are recognized early for their natural inclinations and family lineages. The Etched Note is delivered by a runner on behalf of Lanka Farshot, the resident hunter mentor. It names the hunter as the heart of the tribe while serving as a stern reminder that raw instinct must be tempered through rigorous instruction and a deep reverence for the wilderness of Mulgore. For the tauren, hunting is far more than a practical method of survival—it is an honored, sacred discipline woven into tribal society. The note reminds the reader that hunters blend the roles of warriors, shamans and druids, and that the tribe will look to them for guidance and protection. By presenting the letter to Lanka, the student takes their first official steps into learning weaponcraft, understanding beasts, and fulfilling their duty to defend and sustain the tribes.

item:etched-parchment.text: Etched Parchment. Gornek gives hunters in the Valley of Trials a summons from Jen'shan. The Etched Parchment points them toward their first lessons in Durotar. Young orcs and Darkspear trolls begin their rites in the Valley of Trials. As recruits prove themselves against the local vermin, Gornek guides them toward their calling. He gives the Etched Parchment to those who will wield bow, gun, and fang. Its message comes from Jen'shan, a skilled hunter trainer seeking fresh eyes and steady hands. Taking the parchment to Jen'shan begins a hunter's training in Durotar. She teaches that the wild path takes dedication: mastering the beasts of the desert demands as much effort as an arcanist's magic or a shaman's work with the spirits. Her summons brings new hunters to lessons in marksmanship and wilderness survival.

item:etched-rune.text: Etched Rune. The Etched Rune is a carved stone tablet given to aspiring dwarven hunters in Coldridge Valley. It serves as an invitation from the hunter trainer Thorgas Grimson, directing fledglings to seek him out within Anvilmar to begin their formal wilderness instruction. Carved with specific dwarven runes, this small stone tablet is passed along to novices who demonstrate potential out in the snowdrifts of Coldridge Valley. Sent by the mountaineer and hunter trainer Thorgas Grimson, the rune encourages fledgling trackers to pause their outdoor tasks and report to Anvilmar. Reading the stone marks a hunter's first step away from basic survival and toward understanding the deeper craft of the wild—learning to respect the beasts of Dun Morogh, track mountain predators, care for ranged weaponry, and endure the brutal elements.

item:etched-sigil.text: Etched Sigil. In Shadowglen, the Etched Sigil calls new night elf hunters to their trainer. Newly awakened night elf hunters receive the Etched Sigil as they enter Shadowglen. Its carved marks of the hunt carry a welcome and summons from Ayanna Everstride, the hunter trainer who lives high in Aldrassil’s hollowed boughs. The token sends each novice to seek her out and begin instruction in archery, wilderness tracking, and the night elf bond between stalker and beast.

item:explosive-stick-of-gann.text: Explosive Stick of Gann. In the southern Barrens, Gann Stonespire turns stolen dwarven plans against Bael Modan. He built the charge to sabotage the dwarves’ flying machine. When Prospector Khazgorm led the Ironforge excavation into southern Kalimdor, the dwarves drove the Stonespire tauren from their ancestral village and razed their sacred grounds to build Bael Modan. Gann Stonespire reclaimed Khazgorm’s blueprints to avenge his displaced and fallen kin. He studied the plans and assembled a charge with enough force to wreck heavy machinery.

item:faded-shadowhide-pendant.text: Faded Shadowhide Pendant. A tarnished talisman once worn by the Shadowhide gnolls of Redridge, enchanted to serve as a conduit for dark orders. To the astonishment of whoever holds it, the pendant also carries a delayed magical message cast by the wizard Theocritus. The Shadowhide gnolls roaming the Redridge Mountains answer to a sinister master named Morganth, coordinating their movements through enchanted pendants. While investigating these talismans from his sanctuary at Tower Azora, the High Mage Theocritus devised an experimental spell to breach their mystical frequency. Though his magical broadcast took weeks to manifest, this faded pendant proved that the gnolls' communication line can be hijacked, opening a path to disrupt their dark master's reach.

item:fallen-moonstone.text: Fallen Moonstone. A Fallen Moonstone is a luminous, magically charged stone gathered from the tranquil waters of Fallen Sky Lake in Ashenvale. Imbued with sacred lunar energy, these stones possess potent restorative properties capable of renewing vitality and curing severe frailty. Fallen Moonstones were once gathered in abundance along the shores and shallows of Fallen Sky Lake, southeast of Astranaar. Highly treasured by the night elves for their restorative magic and lunar blessing, they were often sought out to aid in recovery when ordinary remedies proved insufficient. However, harvesting them became treacherous when corrupt Shadethicket bog beasts overran the lake. Their leader, a Shadethicket Oracle, hoarded every stone it could find on a small central island, cutting off the local Kaldorei from a vital source of healing.

item:fandral-s-message.text: Fandral's Message. In Darnassus, Fandral Staghelm sends a message across the sea to Onu in Darkshore. The sealed dispatch carries news about Oracle Glade in Teldrassil. Arch Druid Fandral Staghelm writes from the Cenarion Enclave in Darnassus. His sealed dispatch is addressed to Onu, the Ancient of Lore who dwells in the Grove of the Ancients. Reports have reached Fandral about the state of Oracle Glade in Teldrassil, and he sends a courier south of Auberdine with word for Onu. The journey crosses the waters to Darkshore, carrying a message from the heart of the new World Tree to Kalimdor’s older, shadowed mainland.

item:fang-of-vagash.text: Fang of Vagash. The Fang of Vagash is a massive predator tooth taken from the notorious beast Vagash in the snowy crags of Dun Morogh. It serves as tangible proof for local breeders that the marauding monster threatening their prized rams has finally been slain. Dun Morogh's high crags are home to bitter cold and ferocious predators, but none have plagued the local ranches quite like Vagash. Looming in the ridges above the Amberstill Ranch, this savage beast frequently stalks downhill under cover of darkness to slaughter prized rams. With Ironforge's troops already stretched thin, the local herdsmen cannot count on the city guard for protection. Slaying the beast and carving away one of its vicious fangs offers indisputable evidence that the pasturelands are safe once more.

item:fangore-s-paw.text: Fangore's Paw. Fangore's Paw is the severed hand of Lieutenant Fangore, a commanding officer among the Shadowhide gnolls in the Redridge Mountains. It serves as gruesome proof of the gnoll chieftain's demise for Magistrate Solomon in Lakeshire. The grim bounty was placed to dismantle the warlord's threat against the besieged township. Lieutenant Fangore acts as a primary field commander for the Shadowhide gnolls encroaching across the Redridge Mountains. Operating in direct service to the renegade mage Morganth, Fangore directs violent assaults against trade roads, outlying farms, and the defenses around Lake Everstill. Because gnoll raiders do not leave traditional uniforms, official seals, or banners to confirm their casualties, the township authorities rely on grim physical evidence. Magistrate Solomon specifically demanded Fangore's paw as unmistakable proof of his execution, allowing the town of Lakeshire to breathe slightly easier amid mounting surrounding perils.

item:farren-s-report.text: Farren's Report. Farren's Report is an official dispatch drafted by Lieutenant Farren Orinelle in Southshore detailing his investigations into the local naga. Farren uses this document to appeal to his former mentor, Major Samuelson in Stormwind Keep, hoping to secure a reassignment back to the capital. Stationed on the embattled coast of Hillsbrad Foothills, Lieutenant Farren Orinelle grew weary of local leadership and the remote frontier. After tasking adventurers with hunting the Daggerspine naga to gather proof of their threat, Orinelle compiled his findings into a formal report. Rather than submitting it to his commanding officer, Marshal Redpath, Farren aimed to send it directly to Major Samuelson, the captain of the guard in Stormwind Keep. Having trained under Samuelson, Farren hoped the document would demonstrate his competence and justify an immediate transfer back to the comforts of Stormwind City.

item:fathom-core.text: Fathom Core. The Fathom Core is a specialized relic recovered from a submerged fathom stone in the depths of Blackfathom Deeps. When deciphered, it provides a comprehensive record of elemental activity in the surrounding region. The Earthen Ring seeks this artifact to discern what dark rituals the Twilight's Hammer cult is conducting beneath Ashenvale. Resting within an ancient fathom stone submerged among the Moonshrine Ruins, the Fathom Core serves as a historical record for elemental phenomena. It registers and preserves shifts, disruptions, and surges in the elements over time. For the shaman of the Earthen Ring stationed at Zoram'gar Outpost, acquiring the core is essential for understanding how the Twilight's Hammer cultists are manipulating the regional elements to serve their own ends.

item:feather-charm.text: Feather Charm. Feather Charms are crude magical trinkets carried by Frostmane troll novices in the snow-swept valleys of Coldridge Valley. Though fashioned from simple materials, they harbor an innate sorcerous resonance that catches the eye of local warlock mentors. The Frostmane trolls inhabiting the snowy caverns southwest of Anvilmar are known mostly for territorial savagery, but their novices dabble in primitive spellcraft. The feather charms carried by these young trolls hold a faint yet unmistakable magical power. In Anvilmar, warlock instructor Alamar Grimm considers them an intriguing subject of study—surprising for crude trollcraft—and uses them as a proving ground for fledgling warlocks seeking to master the binding of their first imp.

item:fel-cone.text: Fel Cone. Beneath Teldrassil's boughs, Fel Cones carry corruption into the forest. Night elf defenders put the pods to use against nearby tricksters. Beneath Teldrassil's boughs, Fel Cones show that corruption has reached the young tree. Gnarled and fallen, the pine cones billow foul green smoke. They lie scattered just east of Dolanaar. Tainted magic has warped the surrounding flora, and the pods are dangerous to touch or eat without caution.

item:fel-moss.text: Fel Moss. Fel Moss spreads through Teldrassil’s forests, its insidious corruptive energies carried by hostile grell and grellkin. The taint threatens the World Tree’s wildlife and native furbolg tribes. Corruption has reached Teldrassil’s boughs, though the World Tree was planted to restore the night elves’ immortality and heal the natural world. Fel Moss is one clear sign of that decay. Impish grell and grellkin infest Shadowglen, with the unnatural, wicked magic of the moss clinging to them and radiating from their growth. The dryad Tarindrella gathers samples to measure how deeply the rot has entered the sacred woodland canopy.

item:felix-s-box.text: Felix's Box. Felix's Box is a small container of personal belongings belonging to Felix Whindlebolt, a refugee who fled the fall of Gnomeregan. Lost during the frantic evacuation into Dun Morogh, the box was looted by local Frostmane trolls and carried off to their camps southwest of Anvilmar. When radiation flooded Gnomeregan during the failed attempt to purge the trogg menace, Felix Whindlebolt joined the frantic exodus of gnomes into Coldridge Valley. In his desperation to escape the radioactive fumes, Felix dropped his most prized personal possessions and crafting gear along the snowy road. Before he could recover them, indigenous Frostmane trolls plundered the roadside remnants and dragged his box, along with his chest and bucket of bolts, back to their crude settlements southwest of Anvilmar. Unaccustomed to physical violence and ill-suited for the harsh wilderness of Dun Morogh, Felix was forced to seek the help of passing adventurers in Anvilmar to recover his belongings. Retrieving Felix's Box represents more than just returning a modest container; it restores a piece of normalcy and livelihood to a displaced artisan who lost everything in the catastrophe that consumed his underground homeland.

item:felix-s-bucket-of-bolts.text: Felix's Bucket of Bolts. Felix's Bucket of Bolts is a container of spare hardware and tools owned by Felix Whindlebolt, a gnome refugee who fled the fall of Gnomeregan. During his escape into Dun Morogh, the bucket was snatched by local Frostmane trolls and dragged into their nearby camps. When radiation flooded Gnomeregan following the disaster against the troggs, thousands of gnomes fled into the freezing wilds of Dun Morogh with whatever they could carry. Felix Whindlebolt managed to escape with his vital equipment, but in the chaos of his flight toward Anvilmar, he was ambushed by the Frostmane trolls who inhabit the crags southwest of town. The trolls plundered his belongings, including this bucket full of bolts and parts, leaving the artisan stranded without the essential materials needed to ply his craft in exile.

item:felix-s-chest.text: Felix's Chest. Felix's Chest is a container of personal belongings lost by the exiled gnome Felix Whindlebolt during the flight from Gnomeregan. Carried away by Frostmane trolls lurking near Coldridge Valley, it sits abandoned within one of their primitive mountain camps. When the subterranean techno-city of Gnomeregan fell to trogg incursions and toxic radioactive fallout, thousands of gnomes fled toward the snowy surface of Dun Morogh with whatever possessions they could carry. Felix Whindlebolt managed to escape the irradiated ruins, but amidst the panic of the evacuation, native Frostmane trolls scavenged the roads and overtook the scattered survivors. Felix lost his primary toolkits and belongings, with his sturdy chest hauled off to the crude camps the trolls maintain in the crags southwest of Anvilmar.

item:felstalker-hoof.text: Felstalker Hoof. In Durotar's Valley of Trials, young shaman face demonic felstalkers as a test of readiness. Their hooves are brought to Canaga Earthcaller before they learn to commune with the earth spirits. Canaga Earthcaller sends young shaman against the demonic taint threatening Durotar. The Burning Blade Coven lies north in the Valley of Trials, where felstalkers roam among the coven's vile familiars. Taking a felstalker's hoof tests a shaman's endurance, resolve, and spirit. Those who subdue the beasts prove ready to receive the secrets of the earth and prepare the ceremonial sapta for communing with elemental spirits.

item:fenwick-s-head.text: Fenwick's Head. Fenwick's Head is the grisly proof of execution taken from Fenwick Thatros on the shores of Lordamere Lake. It is claimed by Forsaken rogues operating on direct orders passed down through Lord Varimathras. Within the Rogues' Quarter of the Undercity, Mennet Carkad acts on urgent intelligence routed directly from dreadlord Varimathras. A hostile undead leader named Fenwick Thatros has established a foothold near the decaying docks along Lordamere Lake in Silverpine Forest. To prevent this threat from rallying hostile undead against the Forsaken, Carkad dispatches promising Deathstalkers to locate Thatros, eliminate him, and sever his head as undeniable proof of the kill. Returning Fenwick's Head to Carkad is more than a simple bounty collection; it serves as a crucial trial for Deathstalker operatives. Presenting the severed trophy validates the rogue's competence in infiltration and assassination, opening the door to deeper, more specialized instruction in the shadow arts from the Forsaken masters.

item:fey-dragon-scale.text: Fey Dragon Scale. A Fey Dragon Scale is a shimmering woodland relic harvested from the elusive faerie dragons living around Stonetalon Peak. It is sought after by the Darkspear witch doctor Jin'Zil, who uses it as an exotic reagent in an alchemical brew mocking night elven nature magic. Faerie dragons are mysterious, elusive creatures tied closely to the wild groves of Kalimdor, particularly the untouched forests around Stonetalon Peak. Their scales carry a natural magical luster reminiscent of the deep woods they guard. While revered by the night elves as harmless woodland spirits and allies, outsiders view them as an untamed source of rare magical ingredients.

item:filled-amethyst-phial.text: Filled Amethyst Phial. In Teldrassil, water from the Oracle Tree's moonwell fills an amethyst phial. Corithras Moonrage receives it for the Cenarion druids to study the World Tree's troubled growth. The Oracle Glade lies in northwest Teldrassil, where the oldest and most potent moonwell rests beneath the Oracle Tree. Other moonwells across the boughs meet the night elves' daily needs, but the water here carries the raw essence of Elune's grace. Druids who watch over the World Tree's health collect it in amethyst phials, preserving it for testing and ritual cleansing.

item:filled-blue-waterskin.text: Filled Blue Waterskin. Shamans gather water for their trials at the Ruins of Stardust in Ashenvale. The Filled Blue Waterskin carries a pristine sample from the ancient fountain. Call of Water initiates cross north from the Barrens into Ashenvale's dense forests. Beyond Lake Mystral, the Ruins of Stardust lie against the mountains dividing Ashenvale from Stonetalon. Fierce forest beasts guard the secluded elven sanctuary. At the center of its lake, an untouched fountain holds water untainted by corruption or drought. A blue waterskin filled from its basin carries the sample sought by shaman masters for ritual attunement. Brine, a hermit and water expert, lives on a hill in the southern Barrens and needs this final sample. He combines it with water from contrasting wells and springs, then distills the pure essence into an offering. The offering can manifest and soothe the elemental spirits of water, completing an initiate's trial.

item:filled-brown-waterskin.text: Filled Brown Waterskin. In the Barrens, the Filled Brown Waterskin carries fresh water from the pond below Brine's hut. Aspiring shaman bring it to her to begin brewing sapta, used to commune with water spirits. The pond beneath Brine's hut is a rare source of fresh water in the Barrens. Nearby quilboar fight fiercely over it, and a novice shaman sees how scarce water can drive creatures to defend what sustains them.

item:filled-cliffspring-falls-sampler.text: Filled Cliffspring Falls Sampler. Near Cliffspring Falls in Darkshore, the Filled Cliffspring Falls Sampler holds foul water drawn from the headwaters. The Cenarion Circle needs it to study the sickness striking local deer. Cliffspring Falls feeds much of Darkshore with water from the eastern highlands. Local deer have recently fallen ill with an unnatural sickness. At Dendrite Starblaze’s request in Moonglade, druidic initiates draw water from a cave mouth where hostile naga dwell. The liquid in the vial is visibly foul, showing that the fresh water supply is tainted.

item:filled-containment-coffer.text: Filled Containment Coffer. A Filled Containment Coffer is an enchanted receptacle used by Forsaken spellcasters to trap erratic magical entities. By deploying a Cantation of Manifestation to reveal and weaken rift spawn in the Apothecarium, mages can trap the anomalies inside these reinforced boxes for safe examination. When unexplained magical disturbances manifested within Algernon's shop in the Apothecarium, the Forsaken mage Anastasia Hartwell commissioned practitioners of the arcane to capture the entities responsible. Because the rift creatures exist purely as living magical energy and wander unseen, ordinary cages are useless. Instead, spellcasters reveal the entities with a Cantation of Manifestation, defeat them in combat, and snap these specially prepared containment coffers shut around them. The sealed boxes shield the carrier from volatile magical backlashes while keeping the specimens intact for magical dissection. The presence of living mana creatures in the Undercity poses a serious threat. Once sealed into containment coffers, the captive beasts are transported back to Anastasia Hartwell and the city's scholars. The primary concern among the Forsaken mages is determining whether these intrusions are natural rifts in Azeroth's magical fabric or the preliminary probes of a calculated magical assault aimed at the kingdom.

item:filled-crystal-phial.text: Filled Crystal Phial. In Shadowglen, the Filled Crystal Phial holds water drawn from the moonwell north of Aldrassil. Tenaron Stormgrip asks young night elves to gather it as a first lesson in Teldrassil’s sacred power. Tenaron Stormgrip sends young night elves to gather moonwell water before they venture into the wider world. The moonwell lies in Shadowglen, and its waters hold more than spring water: they carry energies traced to the ancient Well of Eternity. Sentinels honor moonwells as shrines of Elune, while druids use their restorative power to tend nature. The arcane sorcery of old remains forbidden. Gathering the water begins a lesson in the sacrifice at Mount Hyjal and the care needed to nurture Teldrassil.

item:filled-cursed-ooze-jar.text: Filled Cursed Ooze Jar. A Filled Cursed Ooze Jar contains the noxious remains of a cursed ooze collected from the corrupted forests of Felwood. It is gathered on behalf of Laris Geardawdle, a gnome scholar in Ironforge seeking to uncover the primordial origins of slimes across Azeroth. While most adventurers avoid the vile puddles and caustic slimes crawling across Kalimdor, the gnomish researcher Laris Geardawdle sees them as a biological mystery. Noticing that slimes appear in diverse environments and observing Forsaken apothecaries diligently harvesting them, Geardawdle developed a controversial theory: oozes might be primordial secretions tied directly to Azeroth's creation. Gathering a sample requires braving Felwood's blighted woods, defeating a cursed ooze, and scooping the acidic matter into an empty jar before it completely dissolves. Securing these pungent samples serves a dual purpose for Geardawdle. Beyond the pursuit of natural science, he hopes a major discovery will cement his reputation within the dwarven-led Explorers' League. In the wake of Gnomeregan's devastating fall, many gnome refugees in Ironforge feel an intense pressure to prove their worth to their dwarven hosts, and Geardawdle believes that unlocking the ancient secrets of ooze will show everyone that welcoming gnomes was no mistake.

item:filled-dreadmist-peak-sampler.text: Filled Dreadmist Peak Sampler. At Dreadmist Peak, a filled sampler holds water gathered by Horde druids from the summit pools. The Cenarion Circle studies the sample to learn what is poisoning wildlife in the northern Barrens. Dreadmist Peak’s high crags hold pools whose mists shape weather and rainfall across the northern Barrens. The Burning Blade, who worship demons, made their coven atop the summit, and the water soon soured. Cenarion druids suspect demonic rites poisoned the vapors that feed the surrounding savanna. They send initiates to collect a sample in a special sampler. The foul liquid confirms their fears: its corruption can sicken the herds below.

item:filled-etched-phial.text: Filled Etched Phial. A Filled Etched Phial is an ornate dryad vessel laden with consecrated water drawn directly from a night elf moonwell in Ashenvale. Requested by the tauren of Thunder Bluff, this sanctified water possesses the rare spiritual potency required to quench the eternal flame shielding a sacred centaur relic. Obtaining this phial demands infiltrating night elf territory deep within Ashenvale. The empty vessel must first be claimed from the dryads around Raynewood Retreat, whose delicate containers are crafted to hold pure restorative draughts. Filled subsequently at a sacred moonwell near the western bank of the Falfarren River, the phial captures water brimming with celestial, nature-bound power. To the night elves, taking this water uninvited is an act of blatant desecration, but the tauren see it as a vital necessity for addressing a regional threat further south.

item:filled-jade-phial.text: Filled Jade Phial. In Dolanaar, the Filled Jade Phial is carried back with sacred water from Starbreeze Village. The water helps replenish the central wells while young night elves learn their people's history. Druids in Darnassus draw sacred moonwell water from across Teldrassil to replenish their central wells. Corithras Moonrage entrusts young travelers in Dolanaar with a jade phial made to hold the pure water safely. The moonwell outside Starbreeze Village lies east of Dolanaar. Initiates collect its water as they tend the World Tree. When you bring the Filled Jade Phial back to Dolanaar, Corithras Moonrage shares another chapter of kaldorei history. He tells of the years after the Third War, when Nordrassil burned, night elves lost their immortality, the Betrayer was released, and Shan'do Malfurion Stormrage disappeared.

item:filled-pure-sample-jar.text: Filled Pure Sample Jar. A Filled Pure Sample Jar contains an uncorrupted specimen of primordial ooze gathered from the remote wilds. It serves as crucial baseline data for the gnome scholar Laris Geardawdle in Ironforge, who is studying how environmental corruption alters living matter. In his study of oozes across Azeroth, the gnomish researcher Laris Geardawdle discovered a troubling phenomenon: these amorphous creatures absorb and reflect the magical and environmental corruption of their habitats. After cataloging the tainted slimes of Felwood, Laris determined that deciphering the nature of the rot required a control group. A Filled Pure Sample Jar holds ooze harvested from pristine, untainted wilderness—such as the primordial ecology of Un'Goro Crater—offering scholars an unaltered specimen to compare against diseased and corrupted strains. Because oozes are extraordinarily malleable organisms, true 'pure' samples cannot be collected near modern civilization, demonic blights, or necromantic fallout. The glutinous oozes inhabiting the untamed basin of Un'Goro Crater remain relatively isolated from outside corruption, making them an ideal scientific standard for Ironforge's inquiring minds.

item:filled-red-waterskin.text: Filled Red Waterskin. In Tarren Mill, a well gives clear spring water for a shaman’s trial. The Filled Red Waterskin carries water drawn from the village well, amid ruins held by the Forsaken. Brine, a hermit in the Barrens, sends shaman initiates to Tarren Mill for water training. The journey leads to the Hillsbrad Foothills, where decay and the dead surround the town. Yet the central well still draws clear spring water. Brine sees this pure water as a sign of endurance in an unhallowed land. She compares the uncorrupted spring with Warchief Thrall’s resolve through hardship. Gathering the water tests an initiate’s respect for its purity, even in hostile surroundings.

item:filled-tainted-ooze-jar.text: Filled Tainted Ooze Jar. A Filled Tainted Ooze Jar contains viscous, tainted ooze scooped directly from the remains of oozes wandering the corrupted forests of Felwood. Secured in specialized containment jars, these samples are brought to Ironforge to support radical theories regarding the origin of life on Azeroth. The tainted oozes roaming northern Kalimdor carry the deep, lingering corruption of Felwood. Harvesting them requires careful containment using jars provided by gnomish researchers. While most travelers avoid the noxious creatures entirely, collecting these samples provides rare material for natural philosophy and biological study far from the blighted forests. The samples are gathered on behalf of Laris Geardawdle, an ambitious gnome scholar stationed with the Explorers' League in Ironforge. Geardawdle is fascinated by the ubiquitous nature of slimes and noticed that the Forsaken's Royal Apothecary Society has also been taking an active interest in them. Defying popular academic skepticism, he theorizes that slimes and oozes may be primal secretions tied to the very creation of Azeroth itself. Securing these samples is his attempt to prove his standing among dwarven scholars following the tragic fall of Gnomeregan.

item:filled-tourmaline-phial.text: Filled Tourmaline Phial. At the Pools of Arlithrien, the Filled Tourmaline Phial carries moonwell water for Corithras Moonrage. Its waters help him watch the health and balance of the growing World Tree. The Filled Tourmaline Phial draws water from a moonwell southeast of the road to Darnassus, on the shores of the Pools of Arlithrien. Reaching the shrine has grown dangerous as the Gnarlpine furbolgs, once peaceful neighbors, turn violently mad. Corithras Moonrage asks travelers to brave the hostile groves and bring back the water. He hopes it will help him find the deepening corruption unsettling the land.

item:filled-vessel.text: Filled Vessel. At Dolanaar, Corithras Moonrage gathers sacred waters for Fandral Staghelm in Darnassus. The Filled Vessel carries samples from Teldrassil’s moonwells to aid his study of the World Tree’s ailments. Night elf acolytes gather water from moonwells across Teldrassil. The tree was planted without the blessings of the Great Aspects, Alexstrasza and Nozdormu, leaving its boughs open to corruption, strange beasts, and crazed furbolg tribes. Corithras Moonrage gathers the phials in Dolanaar and pours them into the Filled Vessel for the journey to the capital. Together, the waters offer a vital sample of Teldrassil’s vitality. Arch Druid Fandral Staghelm studies them in the Cenarion Enclave, seeking a remedy for the Great Tree’s flaws.

item:final-clue-to-sanders-treasure.text: Final Clue to Sanders' Treasure. Along Westfall's coast, Captain Sanders' last directions point out to sea. A note in an old jug sends scavengers west toward his buried treasure. Captain Sanders left his final directions in an old whiskey jug on the Westfall coast. The pirate had scattered cryptic notes along the shoreline, and this one completes the trail. From the jug, the directions lead due west into the ocean. Follow them through the surf to a lonely offshore rock, where his ironbound sea chest lies.

item:fine-crab-chunks.text: Fine Crab Chunks. Fine Crab Chunks come from the Reef Crawlers and Encrusted Tide Crawlers along Darkshore's coast. Gubber Blump seeks them for his cooking. Reef Crawlers and Encrusted Tide Crawlers roam Darkshore's shores. Travelers may see them as pests or dangers by the water, while cooks prize their meat. The chunks can be boiled, broiled, fried, or added to stews.

item:fine-moonstalker-pelt.text: Fine Moonstalker Pelt. In southern Darkshore, mature moonstalkers carry the hides Terenthis needs. Their Fine Moonstalker Pelt is thick and healthy enough for an enchanted cloak that helps searchers pass the region’s hostile beasts unnoticed. Moonstalker sires and matriarchs have coats dense and healthy enough to yield a fine pelt. They hold territories along the Wildbend River and farther south toward Ashenvale’s borders, where they hunt with patience. Common moonstalkers prowl across Darkshore’s forests, but their hides are not fine enough.

item:fire-tar.text: Fire Tar. Across the eastern Barrens, Razormane spellcasters carry Fire Tar. Horde shamans use it to brew the Fire Sapta, which lets them commune with fire spirits. Razormane geomancers, mystics, and thornweavers carry Fire Tar. The quilboar use the flame-tuned substance in their harsh magic and rituals. Shamanic instructors prize it as a worldly reagent that helps mortal senses reach the raw fury of the elements. Young orc and troll shamans travel to Telf Joolam, high among Durotar's crags, to forge their fire totems. Telf asks them for a reagent pouch taken from Burning Blade cultists and Fire Tar gathered from the Razormane. He brews the two ingredients into a fire sapta. Drinking it lets a shaman perceive the fire spirits waiting atop the nearby peaks.

item:fizzle-s-claw.text: Fizzle's Claw. In Thunder Ridge, Fizzle Darkstorm’s claw is carried to Razor Hill as proof of his death. The goblin warlock was a dangerous Burning Blade conspirator. Orgnil Soulscar sent forces to root out shadow cults threatening the orcish homeland. He identified Fizzle Darkstorm as an instigator spreading corruption in Thunder Ridge. The claw gives Horde commanders proof that the warlock, who operated under the Burning Blade’s banner, has been slain. Thunder Ridge lies just northwest of Razor Hill, close enough to threaten the surrounding lands. Horde scouts took Fizzle’s claw back to Razor Hill, confirming that his rituals and attempt to establish a Burning Blade foothold had been stopped.

item:flagongut-s-fossil.text: Flagongut's Fossil. At the Wetlands dig, Flagongut seeks answers in an ancient fossil. The Explorers' League keeps the specimen, and Flagongut believes the Stone of Relu can help him decipher its secrets. Prospector Whelgar keeps the fossil at his excavation site in the southern hills of the Wetlands. Dwarven expeditions across Khaz Modan unearthed it, and Archaeologist Flagongut believes its ancient stone holds forgotten powers. He sees a kinship with artifacts found across the sea in Darkshore.

item:flatland-cougar-femur.text: Flatland Cougar Femur. A Flatland Cougar Femur is a dense thigh bone taken from the predatory cougars that prowl the golden grasses of Mulgore. It serves as a vital component in a traditional tauren folk remedy used to counter lethal, venomous infections. The flatland cougar is one of Mulgore's most dangerous native stalkers, blending seamlessly with the dry brush until it springs upon unsuspecting prey. While hunters often harvest cougar pelts and claws for leatherworking and trophies, their heavy marrow-rich bones possess practical value in regional medicine. When Maur Raincaller, a tauren of Bloodhoof Village, suffered a venomous wound from the monstrous pink strider Mazzranache, he urgently requested a cougar femur alongside parts from other local beasts. The bone is crushed or boiled to extract its potent properties, forming an antitoxin poultice capable of drawing fever and necrotic venom out of a festering bite.

item:flatland-prowler-claw.text: Flatland Prowler Claw. A Flatland Prowler Claw is taken from the dangerous feline predators that stalk the grassy plains of Mulgore. For aspiring hunters, gathering these claws serves as a traditional rite of passage, demonstrating cunning and martial resolve to the elders of Thunder Bluff. Flatland prowlers are among the most cunning and territorial predators roaming the wind-swept plains of Mulgore. Quick on their feet and adept at ambushing prey in the tall grass, they present a genuine threat to travelers and a worthy test for young hunters. Collecting their sharp claws is not merely a task of survival, but a recognized tradition. Skorn Whitecloud advises promising wanderers to harvest these trophies to present to Melor Stonehoof atop Thunder Bluff's Hunter Rise, proving they possess the resolve and fieldcraft necessary to pursue the hunter's way.

item:foreman-s-blackjack.text: Foreman's Blackjack. Foreman's Blackjack keeps peons at work in Durotar's Valley of Trials. Foremen use the leather-wrapped cosh to wake laborers who fall asleep during the Horde's early construction. Durotar's rugged desert needs stockpiles of lumber for the Horde's new home. In the Valley of Trials, the work falls to the peons, and Foreman Thazz'ril keeps the crews moving with Foreman's Blackjack. The weighted bludgeon delivers a jarring wake-up call to laborers caught napping beneath the valley's shade trees, rather than a lethal blow. Peon life in the new Horde means grueling, unglamorous work under an iron fist.

item:forged-steel-bars.text: Forged Steel Bars. In the northern Barrens, Thun'grim Firegaze's steel bars are missing. Recovering them will prove a warrior's resolve to reclaim stolen property. Thun'grim Firegaze, a visually impaired orc smith, keeps a camp in the northern Barrens. Razormane quilboar took his iron chest during a night raid, distracting him with grunts and snorts while thieves slipped away. Unable to work fine steel, the quilboar left the unopened chest near a ruined wagon in their encampment to the northwest. The bars remain intact for warriors willing to recover them.

item:fragments-of-rok-alim.text: Fragments of Rok'Alim. Fragments of Rok'Alim are the shattered stone remains of a primeval earth elemental roaming the canyons of Thousand Needles. Brought to Dorn Plainstalker at the Weathered Nook, they serve as undeniable physical proof that a warrior has bested an ancient terror in single combat. While most elementals faded from Azeroth following the banishment of the Old Gods, a handful possessed enough raw power to endure on the surface without being summoned by mortal magic. Rok'Alim the Pounder is one such survivor, wandering the canyon flats south of the main thoroughfare. Local centaur know him by the thunderous crashes of his stony fists pulverizing anything foolish enough to wander into his path. Striking down this living remnant of the primordial world yields jagged pieces of dense, animated rock—a trophy fit to prove unmatched physical prowess. For the tauren hermit Dorn Plainstalker, recovering the fragments is the decisive component of the Test of Strength. As part of a series of spiritual and martial rites conducted high within the Weathered Nook, the trial demands that an initiate face an entity of unyielding brute force. Delivering the battered rubble of Rok'Alim proves that an adventurer possesses the bravery and physical might required to survive the harshest perils of Kalimdor.

item:frostwolf-banner.text: Frostwolf Banner. The Frostwolf Banner is a tribal standard cached deep within Wildpaw Cavern in Alterac Valley. Horde initiates are sent to recover it as an ancestral rite of passage to awaken their battle spirit and earn their first clan insignia. For warriors of the Horde arriving in Alterac Valley, claiming true standing among the Frostwolf clan begins with a trial of grit. Warmaster Laggrond sends new recruits south into the damp, hostile corridors of Wildpaw Cavern, a den swarming with territorial gnolls. Reaching the banner hidden within their depths and returning it unbroken demonstrates courage, proving the warrior's battle rage has awakened and earning them the Frostwolf initiate's insignia.

item:full-leaden-collection-phial.text: Full Leaden Collection Phial. A heavy, lead-lined flask filled with irradiated radioactive fallout gathered from the troggs infesting Gnomeregan. The inventor Ozzie Togglevolt requested this hazardous sample in hopes of synthesizing a cure for irradiated leper gnomes—or perhaps concocting a dangerously potent rum. The lead lining of this collection phial is essential to shield the carrier from the volatile green fallout saturating Gnomeregan. The fallout originated when High Tinker Mekkatorque's advisors flooded the lower corridors with toxic radiation to halt the invading troggs, a catastrophe that instead corrupted both troggs and surviving gnomes into maddened, irradiated horrors. By collecting fluid residue directly from Irradiated Invaders and Pillagers, daring adventurers furnish refugee tinkerers like Ozzie Togglevolt and Razzle Sprysprocket in Kharanos with raw materials needed to experiment on remedies.

item:fungal-spores.text: Fungal Spores. Around the Barrens' oases, Fungal Spores gather in swollen mushrooms. The waters quicken the life around them, and the Royal Apothecary Society seeks the spores for its alchemy. The Barrens' oases bring unusual life to the dry plains. At the Forgotten Pools, the Lushwater Oasis, and the Stagnant Oasis, the water does more than ease thirst. It quickens and changes the plants and wildlife nearby. Mushrooms along the damp shores swell with spores, carrying the waters' concentrated power to spur growth. Naturalists study this change, while the Royal Apothecary Society gathers the mushrooms for its alchemy. Apothecaries abroad gather unusual local ingredients for their laboratories and colleagues. At the Crossroads, Apothecary Helbrim sends such reagents onward, including to Apothecary Zamah in Thunder Bluff. The spores are valuable for brewing potent chemical mixtures. Their natural properties have already been altered by the mysterious forces beneath Kalimdor's soil, making them useful to the Forsaken.

item:furen-s-instructions.text: Furen's Instructions. In Stormwind, Furen's Instructions name the materials needed for fire-hardened mail. Furen Longbeard gives the parchment to Alliance warriors he has tested. Furen Longbeard offers to forge a resilient suit of mail for a warrior who has proved himself through simpler smithing work. The dwarven armorer asks the warrior to fetch the rare components himself. His parchment records what is needed and sends the warrior across continents to gather it. The parchment calls for a dangerous journey through the Eastern Kingdoms and Kalimdor. The hardened links need dozens of scorched spider fangs from damp caves in the Wetlands, along with horns from fire-breathing chimaeras in the crags of Stonetalon Mountains. The list also calls for a galvanized horn from the chimaera matriarch and a vial of volatile phlogiston held deep within Razorfen Kraul, a quilboar bastion.

item:furen-s-notes.text: Furen's Notes. Furen's Notes carry his discoveries in metallurgy and armorsmithing from Stormwind to Alliance craftsmen. After forging protective gear for veteran warriors, Furen Longbeard sends copies to help fellow smiths refine their work. In Stormwind's Dwarven District, Furen Longbeard forges specialized armaments for warriors and records the methods and discoveries he makes along the way. Dwarven metalworking keeps changing, so he makes several copies for other smiths to use and build upon. His notes describe practical ways to temper, reinforce, and shape armor against deadly blows. Furen sends copies to trusted contacts in the Alliance's crafting networks. Grimand Elmore may scoff at a fellow smith he claims to have taught, but the notes still hold useful insights. Copies cross the Great Sea to night elven craftsmen, including Mathiel on Darnassus's Warrior's Terrace. Shared needs in battle bring their different traditions into contact.

item:furlbrow-s-deed.text: Furlbrow's Deed. The Furlbrows are stranded near Westfall's border, and their land deed is in Defias hands. The paper bears Theodore and Verna Furlbrow's claim to their family farm, while the couple waits by their broken wagon. The deed bears Theodore Furlbrow's signature and Verna's as well, securing their family farm in Westfall. When the Defias Brotherhood overran the region, bandits drove the couple from their home and carried the paper into Elwynn Forest. Notes on its back show they meant to copy it when forging claims to other properties. The Furlbrows lost their home and livelihood, then took to the road. Their wagon broke near the border, leaving them stranded.

item:furlbrow-s-pocket-watch.text: Furlbrow's Pocket Watch. In Westfall, Farmer Furlbrow has lost a keepsake from his wedding day. His pocket watch came from Verna’s father, and it was left behind when Defias bandits seized the family’s pumpkin farm. Farmer Furlbrow and Verna fled their home in the night when Defias bandits swarmed the Furlbrow Pumpkin Patch. In the rush, he left a pocket watch from Verna’s father behind. The watch remains in a wardrobe in the overrun farmhouse, where Benny Blaanco and his cutthroats keep watch. The displaced couple now camps along the road, and the watch is one of the few pieces of their former life the outlaws have not ruined.

item:gaea-seed.text: Gaea Seed. Gaea Seeds are hardy plant kernels found along the water's edge of Mirkfallon Lake in the Stonetalon Mountains. Treasured by tauren shamans, they are imbued with elemental blessings to help replenish areas ravaged by war and industry. Gaea Seeds are native to Stonetalon Mountains, naturally washing up or growing around the shores of Mirkfallon Lake. While modest in appearance—resembling small, fibrous coconuts—they carry an inherent resilience. As industrial exploitation and conflict scar Stonetalon, shamanic practitioners view these seeds as vital conduits for healing the wounded earth.

item:gaffer-jack.text: Gaffer Jack. Off Auberdine, Gaffer Jack parts lie beneath Darkshore's waves. Wizbang Cranktoggle lost a crate of them during his voyage across the sea. Gnome tinkerer Wizbang Cranktoggle booked passage to Auberdine, seeking quiet away from Ironforge's forge-works and taverns. During the voyage, he drank too much and fumbled an entire container of gaffer jacks over the railing. The small fasteners sank into Darkshore's coastal waters, leaving Wizbang without the parts he needed to tune his stintle pegs. The gaffer jacks sank in the surf along Darkshore's shore, where patient fishermen sometimes snag them on their hooks. Recovering the parts lets Wizbang assemble his strange contraptions. Finding tiny metal hardware in the open sea takes patience and luck.

item:gallywix-s-head.text: Gallywix's Head. In Orgrimmar, Gallywix's Head proves that a Venture Company overseer was executed. The Shattered Hand demands the trophy as proof of the killing. Grand Foreman Puzik Gallywix directed the Venture Company's work from its tower north of the Sludge Fen. When word arrived that the Venture Co. planned something on a grand scale, the Shattered Hand sent operatives to dismantle the facility. Bringing Gallywix's head to Shenthul in Orgrimmar proves the overseer was executed and secures the rogue's standing within the guild.

item:galvanized-horn.text: Galvanized Horn. In the Charred Vale, chimaera matriarchs bear horns that Stormwind and Thunder Bluff armorers seek. These hardened growths go into specialized armor for warriors. Chimaera matriarchs prowl the Charred Vale in the Stonetalon Mountains. Their horns grow unusually hard through ash, flame, and survival. Lesser fledgling chimaeras yield brittle, blackened horns, but a matriarch's horn has strength like treated metal. Furen Longbeard in Stormwind and Orm Stonehoof in Thunder Bluff both seek one as a test of martial valor and a key ingredient for exceptional mail armor.

item:gargantuan-tumor.text: Gargantuan Tumor. In Teldrassil, a great growth was torn from Oakenscowl, the corrupted timberling by Lake Al'Ameth. The tumor bears witness to sickness spreading among the creatures there. Oakenscowl lurks in a cavern near Lake Al'Ameth's southern bank. Once a noble timberling elder, the creature has fallen to a vile affliction. A huge growth poisoned Oakenscowl, warped its behavior, and spread taint through the surrounding wildlife. The tumor was severed to end the beast's rampage and give local researchers a chance to examine the blight. They hope to learn how the malady took root in the boughs of the newly grown World Tree.

item:garrick-s-head.text: Garrick's Head. At Northshire's vineyards, Garrick Padfoot's severed head proves the cutthroat is dead. The authorities at Northshire Abbey require it to pay the bounty. Garrick Padfoot and his gang harassed Northshire Valley's farmers and merchants for weeks. With Stormwind's defenses stretched thin, Garrick made his hideout in a shack near the vineyards and raided passing trade. Local guards were occupied by kobolds and Defias bandits, so Deputy Willem offered a bounty for the outlaw's death. He sought someone willing to kill Garrick and bring back proof.

item:gazlowe-s-ledger.text: Gazlowe's Ledger. In Ratchet, Gazlowe checks his trade records against the harbor manifest when a shipment from Booty Bay goes missing. Gazlowe tracks trade goods in Ratchet with a personal ledger. It records imported crates, outbound cargo, and warehouse stores. When a shipment from Booty Bay is missing, Gazlowe compares his expected inventory with the dock records kept by Wharfmaster Dizzywig.

item:gem-of-anacondra.text: Gem of Anacondra. The Gem of Anacondra is one of four dream gems held by the corrupted serpent leaders within the Wailing Caverns. Carried by Lady Anacondra, it serves as tangible proof of her defeat and the curbing of the Nightmare's spread over the Barrens. When Naralex entered his deep slumber to bring water and life back to the arid Barrens, the Emerald Nightmare invaded his thoughts and warped his closest disciples. Lady Anacondra and her fellow conspirators abandoned their traditional ways to become the Druids of the Fang, twisting their noble restorative purpose into a toxic delusion. The Gem of Anacondra is one of the four dream gems carried by these serpentine leaders, focusing their corrupted bond with the Emerald Dream and anchoring the nightmare within the cave system.

item:gem-of-cobrahn.text: Gem of Cobrahn. The Gem of Cobrahn is a dream gem carried by Lord Cobrahn, one of the corrupt leaders of the Druids of the Fang within the Wailing Caverns. It serves as both a focus of his corrupted reverie and physical proof needed by Nara Wildmane to confirm his defeat. When the night elf druid Naralex entered the Emerald Dream to restore the barren plains of Kalimdor, his nightmare twisted both the Wailing Caverns and his disciples. Among them was Cobrahn, who abandoned the peaceful ways of the Cenarion Circle to take the shape of the serpent. Lord Cobrahn carries one of the four dream gems that anchor the leaders' hold over the subterranean waterways, using it to channel the twisted dreams that threaten to transform the Barrens into a venomous marsh.

item:gem-of-pythas.text: Gem of Pythas. The Gem of Pythas is one of four corrupted dream gems carried by the leaders of the Druids of the Fang within the Wailing Caverns. Held by Lord Pythas, it fuels the nightmare twisting the subterranean oasis and threatening the Barrens. When Naralex entered the Emerald Dream to restore the arid Barrens, his noble vision was twisted into a living nightmare. His foremost followers fell with him, styling themselves the Druids of the Fang and seeking to remake the surface world into a venomous jungle. Lord Pythas carries this resonant stone, one of four dream gems anchoring the corruption within the caverns. The gem serves as a conduit of their dark design and proof to the druids of Thunder Bluff that Pythas's twisted trance has finally been broken.

item:gem-of-serpentis.text: Gem of Serpentis. The Gem of Serpentis is a dream gem carried by Lord Serpentis, one of the four leaders of the Druids of the Fang in the Wailing Caverns. It acts as a focal conduit for the twisted nightmare reshaping the cave network and threatening the Barrens. When Naralex's slumber inside the Wailing Caverns succumbed to the Emerald Nightmare, his most devoted followers were warped into the fanatical Druids of the Fang. Lord Serpentis is one of the cabal's four leaders. Like the other three, Serpentis carries an enchanted dream gem that anchors their collective will to the corrupted vision. Recovering this gem breaks Serpentis's hold over the cavern's ecosystem, striking directly at the leadership directing the corruption spreading across the Barrens.

item:gerenzo-s-mechanical-arm.text: Gerenzo's Mechanical Arm. Gerenzo's Mechanical Arm is the grafted prosthetic limb taken from the rogue engineer Gerenzo Wrenchwhistle in the Stonetalon Mountains. It serves as unmistakable proof of his demise for goblin operatives seeking to clear out competition. Gerenzo Wrenchwhistle took self-modification to a grotesque extreme, grafting whirring gears and metal directly onto his failing body. Perched above Cragpool Lake, the renegade gnome replaced natural limbs with intricate machinery. When the goblin tinker Ziz Fizziks seeks Gerenzo's elimination to impress his superiors, this distinctive mechanical arm is the only trophy unique enough to serve as indisputable evidence of the engineer's death.

item:ghost-hair-comb.text: Ghost Hair Comb. The Ghost Hair Comb is an eerie grooming tool entangled with the spectral strands of the spirit Blind Mary. Sent to the ghost by Madame Eva, the comb becomes an instrument of tragic realization before its gathered hair is spun into uncanny thread. Madame Eva of Darkshire sends the comb to the haunted spirit Blind Mary, who resides in a lonely dilapidated dwelling on the outskirts of Duskwood. When presented with the comb, the ghost recoils in sheer horror, suddenly confronted with the harrowing reality that she is no longer the lovely living woman she once was. In her grief and distress, Mary thrusts the comb away, leaving it tangled with strands of her own ghostly hair.

item:ghost-hair-thread.text: Ghost Hair Thread. Ghost Hair Thread is a rare, supernatural material spun by Madame Eva in Darkshire. Infused with potent occult properties, it is said to bind spiritual energies and even sew life into inanimate things. The hermit Abercrombie requests it to ward his dilapidated shack against restless ghosts. Spun by the fortune teller Madame Eva in Darkshire, Ghost Hair Thread is far more than an ordinary tailoring supply. According to Eva, the spectral thread possesses versatile occult properties, ranging from binding malevolent spirits to stitching vitality into inanimate objects. Its ethereal nature makes it a valuable asset for rituals and wards in the cursed realm of Duskwood.

item:ghoul-fang.text: Ghoul Fang. Ghoul Fangs are gruesome trophies harvested from the undead prowling the blighted groves and cemeteries of Duskwood. In Darkshire, the seer Madame Eva uses them as essential components in crafting defensive talismans for travelers facing the encroaching darkness. The shadowed forest of Duskwood crawls with ravenous undead, from flesh eaters lurking near the graves to rotted corpses roaming the woods. Taking a fang from these monstrous creatures is both grim work and proof of survival against the ravenous dead that threaten Darkshire's borders. Madame Eva, the resident fortune teller and mystic in Darkshire, sees terrible omens swirling around travelers who dare step through Duskwood. She binds the latent necrotic essence of ghoul fangs alongside skeletal fingers and arachnid venom to enchant the Totem of Infliction, turning the dark forces of the forest into a protective charm against violent assault.

item:ghoul-rib.text: Ghoul Rib. Ghoul Ribs are harvested from the undead prowling the haunted groves and cemeteries of Duskwood. The hermit Abercrombie claims to need them as materials to construct a grotesque effigy to ward off the flesh-eating horrors near his shack. The cursed forest of Duskwood crawls with violent undead, including ravenous ghouls such as Flesh Eaters, Bone Chewers, Brain Eaters, Rotted Ones, and Plague Spreaders. Abercrombie, an eccentric recluse living isolated in a shack north of Raven Hill Cemetery, requests these sturdy, rotted bones from passing travelers. He claims that living outside the protection of the Night Watch in Darkshire leaves him vulnerable, and that assembling a terrifying effigy from ghoul ribs will serve as a scarecrow to frighten off prowling packs of the dead.

item:giant-crocolisk-skin.text: Giant Crocolisk Skin. Giant Crocolisk Skins are thick hides taken from the massive reptiles native to the marshes of the Wetlands. Prized by Menethil Harbor tradesmen for leatherworking, harvesting them is perilous work that has maimed more than one unwary hunter. The bogs and waterways of the Wetlands are home to enormous crocolisks whose hides are dense enough to resist the damp rot of the marshes. In Menethil Harbor, artisans like James Halloran rely on steady shipments of skins to craft rugged leather goods. However, taking a hide from a fully grown giant crocolisk requires braving deep waters and outmatching ferocious swamp predators, making every gathered pelt hard-won.

item:gloom-weed.text: Gloom Weed. Gloom Weed is a sickly plant native to the blighted soil of Tirisfal Glades, commonly growing in the fields between Deathknell and Brill. It is best known as the wrong plant collected by Gordo, a lumbering Forsaken abomination who confuses it with the alchemy reagent doom weed. Sprouting amid the gloom and decay of Tirisfal Glades, Gloom Weed thrives in the fallow earth west of Brill and east of the Solliden Farmstead. Despite its morbid name, the plant is relatively harmless and lacks the potent alchemical kick prized by the Royal Apothecary Society. Its primary notoriety stems from the abomination Gordo, who wanders the roadway attempting to pull weeds with his massive, clumsy hands. Having misunderstood his master's commands, Gordo constantly gathers Gloom Weed and enlists gullible travelers to carry bunches of it back to Master Holland in the Brill graveyard, much to the apothecary's supreme annoyance.

item:glowing-ember.text: Glowing Ember. At the Shrine of Eternal Flame, a Glowing Ember kindles the brazier for a shaman's trial. It comes from a Minor Manifestation of Fire on Durotar's crags. A rising shaman drinks fire sapta to see the fiery spirits on the ridge near Telf Joolam. There, the initiate faces a Minor Manifestation of Fire. When the elemental falls, only a smoldering ember remains of its physical form. Raw elemental heat still pulses within it, carrying the living spark needed to awaken the sacred brazier at the Shrine of Eternal Flame.

item:glowing-fruit.text: Glowing Fruit. On Teldrassil, a strange fruit glows beneath unusual fronds. Denalan at Lake Al'Ameth studies its strange reaction to the World Tree's soil. The Glowing Fruit hangs beneath unusual fronds on Teldrassil, bright and round. Botanist Denalan at Lake Al'Ameth recognizes it as foreign to the World Tree. He thinks its seeds came from distant lands across the sea. Its reaction to Teldrassil's rich, enchanted soil shows how foreign plants can affect the young World Tree.

item:glowing-gem.text: Glowing Gem. The Glowing Gem is an enchanted stone recovered from the murloc camps along the waters of Ashenvale. Originally sought by the fallen scout Teronis, the stone is a vital component needed to reconstruct the magical rod crafted by Dartol. Discovered in the possession of the aggressive murlocs dwelling near Lake Falathim, the Glowing Gem is imbued with latent magical energy. The young night elf Teronis ventured out from Astranaar to track it down, aiming to piece together a tool capable of driving back the corruption seeping through Ashenvale's forests. Though Teronis met an untimely end at the lake, the stone itself survived intact among the shoreline scavengers.

item:glowing-soul-gem.text: Glowing Soul Gem. In Ordil'Aran, the Glowing Soul Gem serves the Cult of the Dark Strand's work in northern Ashenvale. Shadow sorcery fills the stone, which holds the spirit of an unwitting victim. Northeast of Maestra's Post, the ruins of Ordil'Aran shelter members of the Cult of the Dark Strand and their shadowy masters. The cult's operatives carry Glowing Soul Gems, enchanted vessels that trap and torment the souls of the dead. These stones channel magical energy and bind spirits to the cult's ends.

item:glutton-shackle.text: Glutton Shackle. Glutton Shackles are enchanted restraints worn by Moonrage Glutton worgen in Silverpine Forest. Crafted by the mad archmage Arugal, these bands channel magic to bolster his otherwise flawed sorcery and sustain his cursed lupine creations. To the trained mages of the Forsaken, the feral worgen infesting Silverpine are not merely savage monstrosities—they are evidence of gross arcane ineptitude. Dalar Dawnweaver, an accomplished arcanist stationed at the Sepulcher, holds nothing but contempt for Archmage Arugal, deeming him an incompetent hack unworthy of the Kirin Tor. Dawnweaver discovered that Arugal relied on enchanted relics to compensate for his fragile spells. The Glutton Shackles, worn by the heavy Moonrage Gluttons wandering northern Silverpine, act as magical anchors that reinforce the curse binding the beasts.

item:glyph-of-azora.text: Glyph of Azora. From the Tower of Azora, Theocritus uses Glyphs of Azora to watch distant threats. The inscribed stones extend the Eye of Azora's reach, letting him read enemies' thoughts and plans. Theocritus watches hostile powers from his tower in Elwynn Forest. His crystal relic, the Eye of Azora, lets him see across great distances, but cannot reach into the minds or plans of his adversaries. He places small focuses called Glyphs of Azora on surfaces far away to carry his magic farther. Each glyph anchors his power, letting him read enemy intentions and project his voice across miles to speak with field agents.

item:glyphic-letter.text: Glyphic Letter. At Northshire Abbey, Glyphic Letter calls promising novitiates to arcane study. After early service to the garrison, they are summoned upstairs to Khelden Bremen, the resident mage trainer. Khelden Bremen seals the Glyphic Letter with his personal insignia. Apprentice spellcasters receive it after proving their discipline in Northshire Valley. The summons calls them away from basic field duties and into dedicated magical instruction within the abbey. Bremen tests each student's resolve before they take up the arcane, with its dangerous forces, unyielding scrutiny, and burdens.

item:glyphic-memorandum.text: Glyphic Memorandum. The Glyphic Memorandum is a written notice delivered to novice mages arriving in Coldridge Valley. Penned on behalf of the mage trainer Marryk Nurribit, it directs fledgling spellcasters indoors to begin their formal arcane instruction. Novice spellcasters setting out into the bitter frost of Coldridge Valley receive this brief missive after completing their initial tasks. Authored by the local mage trainer Marryk Nurribit, the memorandum summons young practitioners into the warmth of Anvilmar. Rather than stern academic dogma, Marryk's guidance is informal and blunt: learn your incantations, set aside coin for training and tavern ale, and steer well clear of the irradiated ruin of Gnomeregan.

item:glyphic-scroll.text: Glyphic Scroll. The Glyphic Scroll is a summons delivered to newly raised Forsaken magi in Deathknell. Bearing the seal of Isabella, the local arcane trainer, it calls fledgling spellcasters to the desecrated church to refine their craft in undeath. When a freshly awakened Forsaken mage returns from culling mindless Scourge in the graveyard of Deathknell, this sealed missive awaits them. Written under the mark of Isabella, the settlement's resident mage trainer, the scroll calls the recipient into the ruined parish sanctuary. For newly risen magi, it serves as an initial orientation into the discipline of the arcane under the Forsaken banner—reminding them that while death may have unburdened them of mortal weakness, the corrupting temptations of magical power remain as persistent as ever.

item:glyphic-tablet.text: Glyphic Tablet. In the Valley of Trials, Gornek gives the Glyphic Tablet to novice Darkspear troll mages. Its summons sends them to Mai'ah for instruction in arcane magic. New Darkspear initiates with an affinity for arcane power receive the Glyphic Tablet in the Valley of Trials. Gornek passes it to young recruits as they handle early tasks around the red canyons. On the slate, Mai'ah, a seasoned troll mage outside the Den, invites them to meet her. The Darkspear follow arcane traditions unlike the scholarly academies of humans or high elves. Mai'ah offers instruction and a solemn warning: raw magic corrupts and deceives, and its dangers to a mage's mind exceed those of any enemy soldier.

item:glyphs-of-summoning.text: Glyphs of Summoning. In Orgrimmar, apprentice warlocks use the Glyphs of Summoning to call a voidwalker. Transcribed from the ancient Tablet of Verga, the inscriptions draw one from the Nether into a summoning circle and bind it to the warlock’s service. In the Cleft of Shadow, warlocks study the dark arts far from the prying eyes of the Warchief’s guards. For an aspiring warlock learning from Gan'rul Bloodeye, commanding a voidwalker marks an important step. The Glyphs of Summoning come from knowledge inscribed on the Tablet of Verga, and bridge Azeroth and the Nether. In Neeru Fireblade's tent, the warlock lays them within a summoning circle. They open a threshold and draw a creature of the Void into the mortal realm. Before Gan'rul teaches the final methods of binding, the warlock must defeat the summoned creature in combat.

item:gnoam-sprecklesprocket.text: Gnoam Sprecklesprocket. The Gnoam Sprecklesprocket is a sophisticated power supply salvaged from Sneed's shredder deep within the Deadmines. Gnomish engineers seek this component to supercharge specialized drilling machines in an ambitious bid to reclaim their fallen home of Gnomeregan. Found in a goblin shredder operated within the Defias stronghold, the Gnoam Sprecklesprocket represents an exceptional feat of compact mechanical energy. Operating deep in the lumbering machine piloted by the goblin taskmaster Sneed, this specialized core delivers enough sustained energy to drive heavy industrial logging and cutting blades. Its stability and potent output make it an invaluable piece of salvage amidst the subterranean tunnels of Westfall. In Stormwind City, the gnomish inventor Shoni the Shilent singled out the Deadmines shredder as the key to a larger offensive. Gnomish forces seek to reclaim Gnomeregan from the trogg hordes that overran it, but the sealed underground approaches present a formidable barrier. By harnessing the Sprecklesprocket, Shoni intends to power heavy gyrodrillmatic excavationators capable of boring directly through the solid bedrock surrounding the lost techno-city, establishing an unexpected underground assault route.

item:gnoll-paw.text: Gnoll Paw. Gnoll Paws reach Sentinel Hill as proof of a patrol against Westfall’s Riverpaw packs. The People's Militia offers bounties to help protect local farmsteads. The People's Militia defends Westfall from Sentinel Hill. With the royal army absent and the crown seemingly blind to rural troubles, ordinary citizens and volunteers face outlaws, rogue mechanoids, and Riverpaw gnolls. Captain Danuvin offers bounties for proof that gnolls have been slain. Bringing back their paws shows that patrols have searched the scrublands instead of resting beneath the watchtower.

item:gnomeregan-gumdrop.text: Gnomeregan Gumdrop. During Hallow's End, Gnomeregan Gumdrops reach travelers from the exiled gnomes. One sweet helps sick Jesper celebrate at the Stormwind orphanage. At Ironforge's Mystic Ward, Talvash del Kissel hands out Gnomeregan Gumdrops to travelers who play along with his Hallow's End tricks. Innkeepers across the Alliance offer regional treats, but the exiled gnomes have no capital inn of their own. The radioactive disaster drove them from their underground kingdom, yet they still share their distinct sweets with the Alliance. Sick Jesper is confined to the Stormwind orphanage in Cathedral Square and cannot travel the continents to trick-or-treat. Travelers gather four regional sweets from Alliance capitals to bring the holiday to him: Gnomeregan Gumdrop, Stormwind Nougat, Ironforge Mint, and Darnassus Marzipan.

item:gnomish-tools.text: Gnomish Tools. Along Durotar's coast, Gnomish Tools lie among the wrecks of Proudmoore's fleet. The Horde seeks the salvaged devices to study Alliance engineering and adapt its innovations for survival. Grand Admiral Daelin Proudmoore's fleet brought vast supplies of modern equipment to Durotar. Proudmoore led Kul Tiras and Alliance forces to its shores, with sophisticated gear made by their gnomish allies aboard. After the fleet was destroyed along the Scuttle Coast, east of Tiragarde Keep, the delicate mechanical kits sank beneath the waves. Waterproof toolboxes still lie among the rotting timbers and barnacle-encrusted hulls in the shallows. Gar'Thok, who oversees Razor Hill, sent Horde scouts to recover tools from the watery grave of Proudmoore's navy. The orcs know humans and gnomes are skilled in engineering, especially siege engines, shipwrighting, and clockwork mechanics. They send the kits by caravan to craftsmen and scholars in Orgrimmar. There, the Horde means to study Alliance contraptions, learn to counter enemy war machines, and adapt foreign innovations for its own survival.

item:gold-dust.text: Gold Dust. In Elwynn Forest, kobolds gather and hoard flecks of gold in the mines. Local buyers pay for the dust, while miners seek whole veins of ore. Kobolds dig through the Fargodeep and Jasperlode mines beneath Elwynn Forest. They keep the gold dust they find in pockets and pouches instead of refining it. Local peddlers and fences want these scraps, hoping to profit without paying official smelting tariffs.

item:golm-fragment.text: Golm Fragment. The Golm Fragment is one of four missing pieces chipped from the Goaz Stone, an ancient relic uncovered at the Wetlands excavation site. Recovered by adventurers dodging ferocious raptors, it helps dwarven archaeologists piece together mysterious Titan inscriptions. Discovered at the excavation site in the southern Wetlands, the Golm Fragment is part of a monumental slab known as the Goaz Stone. Prospector Whelgar discovered the stone shortly before raptors drove the Explorers' League back, but found its inscription severed in four critical places. The Golm Fragment was abandoned amid the dirt and overturned crates when the dig was overrun, hidden away inside an ancient relic box until brave explorers could retrieve it.

item:gordon-s-crate.text: Gordon's Crate. Gordon's Crate is a heavy shipment of weapons packed in the Undercity for the Forsaken forces stationed in Silverpine Forest. It serves as an essential supply consignment meant to be ferried directly to the remote garrison at the Sepulcher. Maintaining the Forsaken grip on Silverpine Forest requires a steady logistical flow from the Undercity. Gordon's Crate holds armaments intended to bolster Deathguard Podrig's defenders at the Sepulcher, ensuring outpost sentries are not caught off guard by the worgen, wild beasts, or human remnants lurking in the woods. Because overland roads out of the capital are dangerous and slow, valuable shipments rely on the Undercity's bat handlers. The crate is handed to Michael Garrett, the bat master perched above the city's trade quarter, who secures passage atop a trained flying bat back to Karos Razok's roost in the Sepulcher.

item:grape-manifest.text: Grape Manifest. At Northshire Abbey, the Grape Manifest records grapes recovered from Milly Osworth's vineyard after brigands seized the harvest. The fruit is bound for the abbey's cellars. Milly Osworth tends a vineyard in Northshire Valley, where local farms help feed Northshire Abbey. Defias bandits seized the harvest, putting the abbey's supply of fresh fruit and fermentable grapes at risk. The Grape Manifest records the grapes reclaimed from the fields and their quantity, so the abbey's quartermasters can account for their stores and prepare barrels for fermentation. Brother Neals oversees Northshire Abbey's food and drink, and he enjoys sampling its wine in the quiet of the bell tower. The manifest tells him the grapes are coming, helping ensure monks and visiting recruits have drink. For the abbey's brothers, each saved bushel is a victory for their stores and a blessing from the Holy Light.

item:gray-bear-tongue.text: Gray Bear Tongue. A gray bear tongue is a raw reagent harvested from the wild bears roaming the Hillsbrad Foothills. It is sought after by the Royal Apothecary Society in Tarren Mill to serve as a biological component in their experimental toxins. The untamed wilderness surrounding Tarren Mill is rich in native fauna, including several varieties of sturdy gray bears. While natural predators pose a constant threat to travelers, the Forsaken see them as a harvestable source of raw alchemy components. Apothecary Lydon studies local wildlife to isolate potent organic agents, using the heavy muscular tissue and fluids of gray bear tongues as a base ingredient for concocting lethal solutions such as the Elixir of Suffering.

item:gregor-s-remains.text: Gregor's Remains. Gregor's Remains are the physical bones recovered from the Scourge-enslaved Gregor Agamand. Once part of the wealthiest dynasty in Tirisfal Glades, his remains are sought by a former mill worker eager to settle an old score from beyond the grave. Before the Third War, the Agamand family held immense wealth and vast tracts of land across northern Tirisfal Glades. When the Scourge invaded Lordaeron, the patriarchs chose pride over flight, fortifying their family mills and persuading their loyal laborers to make a desperate stand against the undead. The defense failed entirely. The estate was overrun, and those who stood their ground were butchered and raised into undeath. Gregor Agamand became another mindless thrall in the service of the Lich King, haunting the very mills his family once ruled. For survivors who broke free from the Lich King's grip to join the Forsaken, the memory of that fateful defense remains a bitter wound. Coleman Farthing, a former mill worker stationed in Brill, blames the hubris of the Agamands for trapping his soul in eternal rot. Collecting Gregor's remains offers Farthing a measure of personal retribution, closing the chapter on a master who led his household straight into damnation.

item:grelin-s-report.text: Grelin's Report. Grelin's Report is a dispatch written by Grelin Whitebeard detailing the Frostmane troll situation in Coldridge Valley. Entrusted to an adventurer rather than a novice apprentice, it serves as the official link between the scouts guarding Anvilmar and Senir Whitebeard stationed in Kharanos. Written after observing the Frostmane trolls in Coldridge Valley, Grelin's Report concludes that they pose no large threat and can be dealt with by the Mountaineers already stationed there and mercenaries paid from Senate funds. Rather than trusting his fumbling apprentice with such vital intelligence, Grelin enlists a capable traveler to carry the document through the trogg-infested Coldridge Pass. The paper acts as an official pass through Mountaineer Thalos's blockade, proving the bearer travels on urgent business to the wider snowy expanse of Dun Morogh. When delivered to Senir Whitebeard at the Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos, the report provides critical field updates intended for Ironforge. Senir notes with amused resignation that his brother invoked King Magni Bronzebeard's name liberally throughout the text. Grelin claims the King's sanction for the action, and Senir expects that appeal to royal authority to ruffle some feathers in the Ironforge Senate.

item:grelin-whitebeard-s-journal.text: Grelin Whitebeard's Journal. Grelin Whitebeard's Journal is a personal field notebook kept by the dwarf scout Grelin Whitebeard in Coldridge Valley. Containing critical notes on local Frostmane troll activity, the journal was stolen by the Frostmane brute Grik'nir the Cold and dragged into the troll cave in Coldridge Valley. While observing the aggressive movements of the Frostmane trolls near Coldridge Valley, Grelin Whitebeard diligently recorded his findings in this leatherbound notebook. The document contains his raw field observations regarding the strength, organization, and threat level posed by the indigenous winter trolls. However, during a confrontation or ambush, the journal was snatched away by Grik'nir the Cold—a heavily marked troll brute—forcing Grelin to recruit passing adventurers to delve into the troll cave and wrest it back before his report could be finalized.

item:grell-earring.text: Grell Earring. In Bashal'Aran, Grell Earring carries traces of the seal binding Asterion. Wild Grells and Vile Sprites in Bashal'Aran gather scraps among the ruins and make earrings from them. Most mortals see only worthless trinkets. Asterion, an ancient night elf bound there as a tormented phantom, studies the magic lingering on the earrings. He hopes those traces will lead him to the ancient seal that imprisons him.

item:grenka-s-claw.text: Grenka's Claw. Grenka's Claw is a physical trophy taken from the formidable harpy Grenka Bloodscreech in the depths of Roguefeather Den. Presented to Dorn Plainstalker at the Weathered Nook, it serves as undeniable proof that an aspiring adventurer has endured a grueling physical trial in the canyon heights. Within the winding caverns of Roguefeather Den, west of Freewind Post, harpies cache food and violently defend their territory against outsiders. To test the physical resilience of young champions, Dorn Plainstalker tasks them with invading the deep roosts and destroying the flock's food reserves. Such brazen provocation inevitably draws the fury of Grenka Bloodscreech. Severing and returning her wicked talon proves that a warrior can withstand wave after wave of enraged harpies and survive the vicious onslaught of their matriarch.

item:grimtotem-satchel.text: Grimtotem Satchel. Deep beneath Orgrimmar, Grimtotem Satchel remains in Maur Grimtotem’s grasp. Troggs killed the tauren in Ragefire Chasm, but he shielded the pouch as he died. Its return to Thunder Bluff brings Magatha Grimtotem’s interest to light. Maur Grimtotem fell to troggs deep inside Ragefire Chasm, beneath Orgrimmar. The tauren still clutched the simple leather pack when his body was found.
