He had fought to protect it while the troggs surrounded him. What could it hold that made him guard it with his life?

item:grizzled-bear-heart.text: Grizzled Bear Heart. A Grizzled Bear Heart is a biological reagent harvested from the sturdy bears roaming Silverpine Forest. It serves as a vital component in the Royal Apothecary Society's grim research into the New Plague. The Royal Apothecary Society works ceaselessly to develop an engineered blight capable of exterminating both the Scourge and living humanity. In the woodlands of Silverpine Forest, Apothecary Renferrel discovered that a unique toxin derived from the heart of a grizzled bear, when combined with arachnid ichor, yields a remarkably lethal concoction. Couriers and Forsaken loyalists hunt down ferocious grizzled bears, giant grizzled bears, and the infamous beast Old Vicejaw to carve out these organs and deliver them directly to Master Apothecary Faranell deep within the Apothecarium of the Undercity.

item:grizzled-scalp.text: Grizzled Scalp. In southern Darkshore, grizzled thistle bears roam the forests south of Auberdine. Their thick, furred hides reach Wizbang Cranktoggle, a gnome tinkerer with a use for them.

item:gryshka-s-letter.text: Gryshka's Letter. Innkeeper Gryshka sends a note of thanks to Zargh at the Crossroads after receiving fresh meat. The letter also introduces young Horde couriers to the wind rider flight network. Innkeeper Gryshka thanks Zargh for the steaks he sends from the Barrens to Orgrimmar's central tavern. She recalls the time he lost a finger while preparing meat, then teases that he looks handsome even when bloodied by his trade. To return Gryshka's Letter to the Crossroads, you report to Doras, the wind rider master atop Orgrimmar's plateau. Show him that you have already checked in with Devrak at the Crossroads, and Doras introduces young couriers to the wyvern flight paths linking settlements in Durotar and the Barrens.

item:gunther-s-spellbook.text: Gunther's Spellbook. Gunther's Spellbook is a personal arcane tome belonging to Gunther Arcanus, a former Kirin Tor wizard dwelling in Tirisfal Glades. Imbued with an enchantment by Bethor Iceshard, the book serves as proof to Gunther that other mages have successfully broken free of the Lich King's control.

item:gyromechanic-gear.text: Gyromechanic Gear. A Gyromechanic Gear is a salvaged piece of precision engineering recovered from the fallout outside Gnomeregan. Gnomish inventors in Kharanos seek these specific gears to construct an experimental device capable of reversing leper gnome mutations. When radiation flooded Gnomeregan to purge the trogg invasion, it corrupted a vast portion of the surviving gnome population into mad, irradiated leper gnomes. Refusing to abandon their twisted kin, inventors Ozzie Togglevolt and Razzle Sprysprocket set to work drafting schematics for the Recombobulator—an ambitious contraption designed to undo the radiation's horrific effects. Building the prototype requires precision mechanisms capable of enduring volatile internal pressures, particularly Gyromechanic Gears and complementary Restabilization Cogs. Because local manufacturing collapsed with the fall of their capital, researchers are forced to scavenge these delicate parts directly from the hostile leper gnomes roaming Dun Morogh.

item:hallowed-letter.text: Hallowed Letter. Priestess Anetta calls young priests from Northshire Valley to Northshire Abbey. Her letter begins their study of the Holy Light. The Hallowed Letter bears Priestess Anetta’s personal mark and reaches fledgling priests after their first trials against the kobold camps of Northshire Valley. She sees the Holy Light’s spark within each novice and urges them to enter the abbey and dedicate themselves to its service. Dark forces still linger across Azeroth in the wake of the Third War. The priesthood gathers those able to heal, protect, and guide an empire struggling to keep order.

item:hallowed-rune.text: Hallowed Rune. The Hallowed Rune is an inscribed stone passed to novice priests beginning their training in Coldridge Valley. Sent by the dwarven priest trainer Branstock Khalder, it calls aspiring wielders of the Holy Light into Anvilmar to begin their formal tutelage. When a fledgling priest demonstrates their resolve aiding the mountaineers and defenders of Coldridge Valley, Branstock Khalder sends forth the Hallowed Rune. Inscribed with teachings of the Holy Light, the stone serves as both an introduction and an invitation. Dwarven novices are directed to step away from minor skirmishes in the snow and report to Anvilmar, where Branstock prepares them to mend wounds and harness holy power against the trogg infestation threatening Dun Morogh.

item:hallowed-scroll.text: Hallowed Scroll. The Hallowed Scroll is a formal summons delivered to newly awakened Forsaken priests in Deathknell. Bearing the personal seal of Dark Cleric Duesten, it directs fledglings to the ruined chapel to begin their re-education in faith, willpower, and shadow. Newly risen Forsaken priests find that their connection to the world has violently shifted. Delivered amidst the ongoing chaos of Deathknell's reclamation, the Hallowed Scroll directs nascent spellcasters to seek guidance within the settlement's ruined chapel. Marked with the seal of Dark Cleric Duesten, the parchment serves as both an introduction and an order to report for formal instruction, initiating the priest into the pragmatic philosophy that defines Forsaken priesthood. Upon answering the scroll's summons, priests are immediately disabused of old dogmas. Duesten makes it clear that traditional crutches—the veneration of the Holy Light, ancestral spirits, or demonic pacts—no longer serve the undead. Instead, the scroll marks the start of an inward discipline rooted strictly in individual willpower. The teachings initiated by this parchment emphasize surviving and ruling through sheer conviction, turning religious devotion into an instrument of self-determination and mastery.

item:hallowed-sigil.text: Hallowed Sigil. In Shadowglen, the Hallowed Sigil summons young night elf initiates to Aldrassil. Shanda sends it to call them into service to Elune. Young night elf priests in Shadowglen receive the Hallowed Sigil from a woodland messenger. Holy markings are engraved on the token, which carries a personal summons from Shanda, the priest trainer at Aldrassil. Read it, then go up to the great hollow of Aldrassil. There, the summons brings the acolyte to the Sisterhood of Elune and begins their service to the Kaldorei as new travelers arrive across Teldrassil.

item:hallowed-tablet.text: Hallowed Tablet. In the Valley of Trials, the Hallowed Tablet calls young Darkspear priests to Ken'jai. Its words begin their lessons in communing with the spirits. Gornek gives the Hallowed Tablet to a promising troll priest taking their first steps through the Valley of Trials. The words carry a personal invitation from Ken'jai, the priest trainer outside the Den. Ken'jai reads signs and hears the spirits' whispers, sensing when young Darkspear with spiritual potential arrive in Durotar. The tablet tells the initiate to read its message and seek Ken'jai's guidance in channeling spiritual authority.

item:hand-of-dextren-ward.text: Hand of Dextren Ward. The Hand of Dextren Ward is a severed trophy taken from a condemned grave robber imprisoned within the Stormwind Stockade. Delivered to Darkshire, it serves as proof that frontier justice has finally been carried out against a man who desecrated the town's dead. Dextren Ward earned a death sentence from Lord Ebonlocke after he was caught digging up bodies in the Duskwood cemeteries and selling them to the necromancer Morbent Fel. Before the town could execute him, Stormwind intervened, hauling the criminal away to the Stockade. For the grieving families of Darkshire, the Hand of Dextren Ward is physical proof that the defiler has met the execution he deserved, bypassing the House of Nobles' unwanted leniency.

item:handful-of-oats-classic.text: Handful of Oats (Classic). In Westfall, Old Blanchy needs oats after the Furlbrows' wagon breaks down. Westfall once fed the Kingdom of Stormwind, but its farms now lie overgrown or under the control of Defias bandits and rogue harvest golems. Sacks of grain and oats remain near barns, outbuildings, and overgrown fields. Travelers and refugees stranded by broken wagons along the dusty roads can gather the leftover oats to feed their weary draft horses.

item:handful-of-stardust.text: Handful of Stardust. Handfuls of Stardust are shimmering, frosted coatings gathered from sparkling bushes in the southern wilderness of Ashenvale. Sourced from the ancient Ruins of Stardust, this powder possesses cooling natural properties prized by night elven healers treating intense fevers. Found clinging to the leafy shrubs within the ancient Ruins of Stardust south of Astranaar, stardust appears as a fine, luminous frost. While the ruins themselves are haunted by lingering elemental spirits, the vegetation that thrives among the broken stones absorbs a rare ambient luminescence. Traditional night elven medicine makes use of this frosted residue, processing it into poultices to draw out persistent, dangerous fevers when ordinary salves and moonwell waters fail to bring complete relief.

item:hardened-tortoise-shell.text: Hardened Tortoise Shell. Hardened Tortoise Shells are remarkably durable carapaces harvested from the sparkleshell tortoises wandering the Shimmering Flats. Coveted by gnomish racers at the Mirage Raceway, these rugged organic plates offer unmatched resistance against volatile and corrosive experimental fuels. The sun-scorched expanse of the Shimmering Flats is home to various breeds of sparkleshell tortoises, including snappers and borers, whose carapaces have evolved into exceptionally tough defenses against the harsh desert salt and wandering predators. Out on the salt flats, standard metal alloy fuel tanks frequently corrode or rupture under the strain of gnomish experimental chemistry. Mechanics like Wizzle Brassbolts prize these shells not for armor or shields, but as organic raw material tough enough to be retrofitted into makeshift, acid-resistant fuel tanks capable of containing volatile rocket propellants.

item:hardened-tumor.text: Hardened Tumor. A Hardened Tumor is a rare biological anomaly harvested from the Vile Fin murlocs dwelling around Lake Lordamere. Noted originally in the research of Apothecary Berard, now a mindless servant of Arugal, this calcified growth serves as an unusual reagent in the Royal Apothecary Society's efforts to brew the New Plague. While studying the indigenous wildlife along the eastern borders of Silverpine Forest, Apothecary Berard cataloged an abnormal, calcified growth developing within the Vile Fin murlocs of Lake Lordamere. Such growths are exceedingly rare, appearing only in mature specimens along the shoreline and the Dawning Isles. What causes the Vile Fin murlocs to produce these hardened masses remains uncertain, but their dense, morbid tissue caught the immediate attention of the Royal Apothecary Society.

item:harpy-lieutenant-ring.text: Harpy Lieutenant Ring. In the Dry Hills, Harpy Lieutenant Rings mark the Witchwing Slayers who command the flock. Darsok Swiftdagger at the Crossroads asks for them as proof of death. Witchwing Slayers direct attacks on Horde travelers in the Barrens. Their rings mark their place among the flock’s leaders, above the ordinary raiders who fight with little coordination. At the Crossroads, Darsok Swiftdagger and the defenders need the rings taken from fallen slayers to confirm that this part of the harpies’ leadership has been broken.

item:head-of-arugal.text: Head of Arugal. The Head of Arugal is the grisly trophy taken from the mad archmage atop Shadowfang Keep. Brought to the Forsaken at the Sepulcher, it serves as undeniable proof that the master of the local worgen has fallen. Archmage Arugal has long cast a dark shadow across Silverpine Forest, commanding the lupine horrors from the ramparts of Shadowfang Keep. Claiming his severed head is the ultimate mandate given by Dalar Dawnweaver at the Sepulcher. To the Forsaken, the head is far more than a gruesome token; it signifies the removal of a potent spellcaster whose feral beasts impeded Lady Sylvanas's complete dominion over Silverpine. Presenting it to Dawnweaver confirms that the rogue archmage's foul sorcery has finally been severed from the land.

item:head-of-bazil-thredd.text: Head of Bazil Thredd. The severed head of Bazil Thredd serves as definitive proof that the leader behind the Stockade uprising has been eliminated. Demanded by Warden Thelwater, this grim trophy marks an end to the Defias Brotherhood's organized control over Stormwind's subterranean prison. When riots erupted throughout the Stockade beneath Stormwind City, Bazil Thredd quickly established himself as the rebellion's mastermind. Entrenched in his cell block among loyal Defias inmates, Thredd directed the chaos from deep within the dungeon walls. Distrustful of outsiders and struggling to maintain order, Warden Thelwater demanded Thredd's head as unambiguous evidence of his demise and as a test of the adventurer's true allegiance to Stormwind.

item:head-of-deepfury.text: Head of Deepfury. The severed head of Kam Deepfury serves as grim proof that the Dark Iron conspirator behind the sabotaged Thandol Span has met his end. Slain within the riots of the Stormwind Stockade, his death fulfills a personal vendetta for the dwarven defenders of Dun Modr. Kam Deepfury was arrested and locked away in the Stormwind Stockade for political reasons, spared from immediate execution by human diplomatic bureaucracy. To the Ironforge mountaineers stationed at Dun Modr, this restraint was unacceptable. Intelligence uncovered by Roggo revealed that Deepfury orchestrated the devastating attack on the Thandol Span—an assault that cost the lives of King Magni's soldiers and the kin of Longbraid the Grim. Bound by duty to remain at his post, Motley Garmason commissioned Alliance champions to infiltrate the rioting prison and claim Deepfury's head, ensuring true dwarven vengeance was delivered where human diplomacy faltered.

item:head-of-gath-ilzogg.text: Head of Gath'Ilzogg. The severed head of Gath'Ilzogg serves as indisputable proof that the Blackrock warlord has been slain. Claiming it breaks the leadership behind the siege of Stonewatch Keep and brings desperate relief to the town of Lakeshire. Gath'Ilzogg orchestrated the brutal Blackrock assault that overran Stonewatch Keep, driving out its defenders and subjecting the surrounding valley to relentless raiding. With Lakeshire on the verge of ruin and Stormwind offering virtually no military reinforcements, Magistrate Solomon posted a bounty upon the warlord's head. Slaying Gath'Ilzogg within the fortified upper levels of Stonewatch and claiming his head shatters the local Blackrock leadership, marking the first real step toward reclaiming the keep for the kingdom.

item:head-of-grimson.text: Head of Grimson. The Head of Grimson is the severed trophy taken from Grimson the Pale, the corrupted overseer of the Deep Elem Mine in Silverpine Forest. Brought to Dalar Dawnweaver at the Sepulcher, it serves as physical proof that the mine's leadership has been eliminated. Securing the mine allows the Forsaken to seize valuable mineral wealth to fuel Varimathras's military campaigns. While Dalar Dawnweaver studies Archmage Arugal's shadowy enchantments from the safety of the Sepulcher, Forsaken scouts known as Darkstalkers identified a strategic threat brewing in the southeastern hills. Arugal's dark magic had seeped into the Deep Elem Mine, corrupting its workers and driving its overseer, Grimson the Pale, into madness. To secure the subterranean riches for Varimathras's forces, Dawnweaver dispatched champions to cut down Grimson and return with his severed head as undeniable confirmation of the mine's liberation from rogue magics.

item:head-of-kelris.text: Head of Kelris. The severed head of Twilight Lord Kelris serves as undeniable proof that the leader of the Twilight's Hammer within Blackfathom Deeps has fallen. Carried out from the corrupted temple ruins, it is sought by representatives of the Argent Dawn to confirm the end of his profane ritual sacrifices. Within the submerged depths of the sunken Temple of Elune, Twilight Lord Kelris orchestrated dark sacrifices to Aku'mai, a monstrous servant of an Old God. Claiming his head marks the end of his tyrannical leadership over the Twilight's Hammer cultists and their naga allies in the cavern. The grisly trophy must be carried back to surface civilizations to assure leaders that Kelris's bloody ceremonies have finally ceased. For months, Kelris was presumed dead or lost by the Argent Dawn, only for his sinister influence to resurface alongside Kalimdor's encroaching shadows. When presented to agents in Darnassus or Thunder Bluff, the head settles lingering bounties and confirms that his attempts to plunge the world back into primeval chaos have been thwarted.

item:head-of-targorr.text: Head of Targorr. The Head of Targorr is the grim proof demanded by Guard Berton in Lakeshire to confirm the death of Targorr the Dread. Once the supreme executioner for the Blackrock warlord Gath'Ilzogg in the Redridge Mountains, the captured orc was sentenced to death in the Stormwind Stockade before suspicious political meddling halted his execution. Targorr the Dread gained infamy across Redridge as the brutal executioner serving under the Blackrock clan warlord Gath'Ilzogg. Responsible for torturing and slaughtering defenders of the Kingdom of Stormwind, Targorr was eventually captured and condemned to death within the Stormwind Stockade. However, bureaucratic intervention from Stormwind nobles mysteriously suspended the sentence, leading local guardsmen like Berton to suspect foul play and corruption in the capital. Fearing that Targorr might be used as a political pawn or somehow orchestrate an escape, Guard Berton commissioned an outside champion to breach the volatile prison and finish what the courts delayed. Severing Targorr's head bypassed the paralyzed legal system entirely, delivering closure to the grieving families and besieged defenders of Lakeshire who suffered under the executioner's blades.

item:head-of-vancleef.text: Head of VanCleef. The severed head of Edwin VanCleef serves as grim, irrefutable proof that the leader of the Defias Brotherhood has fallen. Brought back from the depths of the Deadmines to Sentinel Hill, it represents the hard-won vengeance of the People's Militia. For months, Edwin VanCleef directed the Defias Brotherhood's terror from the deepest sanctum of the Deadmines, shielded by heavily armed outlaws, goblin engineers, and a massive war juggernaut. Words alone could never convince the battered settlers of Westfall that their nightmare was over. Gryan Stoutmantle, leader of the People's Militia, demanded undeniable physical proof before declaring the countryside safe. Severing the ringleader's head and bringing it out into the daylight offers the exhausted defenders tangible assurance that the grand architect of their ruin will never threaten Westfall again.

item:heart-of-isha-awak.text: Heart of Isha Awak. Hunters seek Isha Awak’s heart along the Merchant Coast south of Ratchet. Mahren Skyseer wants it as proof that the Deep Doom has been overcome. Isha Awak prowls the sea off the Merchant Coast, south of Ratchet. Sailors and coastal folk revere and fear the massive thresher, known as the Deep Doom. It has killed many human trespassers along the shore. Mahren Skyseer, a tauren mystic, sees an honorable predator, not a mindless menace. She believes its fierce spirit dwells in its heart. Mahren charges brave hunters to plunge into the waves, defeat Isha Awak in its own domain, and claim the heart as both trophy and spiritual offering.

item:heartswood.text: Heartswood. Heartswood is timber harvested from a sacred tree rooted within the Ruins of Ordil'Aran in northwestern Ashenvale. Born from the final resting place of two ancient lovers, its resonance with undying devotion makes it an essential lure for summoning a succubus. The Heartswood grows among the elven stones of the Ruins of Ordil'Aran in northwestern Ashenvale. According to legend, two lovers named Anathera and Latherion fell side by side during the catastrophic War of the Ancients thousands of years ago. On the very earth where they breathed their last, a peculiar tree took root, blossoming as an eternal testament to their devotion. Even millennia later, the wood cut from this tree hums with the memory of undying passion, making it an object of great curiosity for those who study emotional and spiritual bonds.

item:heartswood-core.text: Heartswood Core. Warlocks in Stormwind City use the Heartswood Core to summon a succubus. Gakin the Darkbinder provides the enchanted ritual focus, crafted from an ancient tree’s wood, to pierce the Twisting Nether and draw the demon into an arcane summoning circle. Beneath the Slaughtered Lamb in Stormwind’s Mage Quarter, warlocks perform rites beyond the city watch’s gaze. The Heartswood Core channels the magic needed to begin a binding ritual. Crafted from the wood of an ancient tree, it holds enough lingering magic to pierce the veil between worlds. At a consecrated summoning circle, an initiate focuses dark arts through the core and opens a passage to the Twisting Nether, drawing a succubus across the divide.

item:heavy-leaden-collection-phial.text: Heavy Leaden Collection Phial. The Heavy Leaden Collection Phial is a shielded sampling vessel provided by Ozzie Togglevolt in Kharanos. It is designed to safely siphon and contain highly unstable irradiated discharge from the mutants deep inside Gnomeregan for ongoing decontamination research. The Heavy Leaden Collection Phial is a sampling vessel used to draw volatile residues from living, irradiated creatures in Gnomeregan. Containing this fallout is difficult, and collecting a suitable sample may take several attempts. Ozzie Togglevolt provides the phial as part of his research to reverse the horrific mutations afflicting leper gnomes. Earlier samples taken from surface troggs lacked the potency needed for effective chemical analysis. By using the leaden phial on virulent beasts like irradiated slimes and lurkers in the Hall of Gears, researchers hope to isolate the active elements of the city's toxic fallout and formulate an effective antidote.

item:hezrul-s-head.text: Hezrul's Head. At Lushwater Oasis, Hezrul Bloodmark leads the Kolkar centaur in the Barrens. His head is carried to Regthar Deathgate west of the Crossroads as proof their chieftain has fallen. Hezrul Bloodmark leads his Kolkar centaur clan from Lushwater Oasis, south of the Crossroads. The Kolkar hold the Barrens' oases and threaten Horde supply routes and young settlements. Regthar Deathgate, an orc veteran charged with securing the land west of the Crossroads, sees their fierce rage but little discipline. He demands Hezrul's severed head to break the clan's command and throw its surviving fighters into disarray, weakening their attacks on the Horde.

item:high-potency-radioactive-fallout.text: High Potency Radioactive Fallout. High Potency Radioactive Fallout is a concentrated, volatile sample of the irradiated sludge poisoning the lower depths of Gnomeregan. Gathered in heavy leaden containers by order of gnome researchers, it is sought in the hope of reverse-engineering a cure for the afflicted leper gnomes. While minor radiation samples can be scraped from contaminated surface scavengers outside, the true heart of Gnomeregan's catastrophe demands something far more concentrated. Researchers stationed outside the fallen capital require raw, unadulterated radioactive fallout taken directly from living irradiated horrors, lurkers, and slimes creeping across the lowest tiers of the Hall of Gears. Because this viscous sludge is constantly decaying, it must be contained in a specialized leaden phial and returned quickly before the sample destabilizes entirely. The desperate pursuit of such lethal materials serves an urgent purpose. Ozzie Togglevolt and his colleagues believe that unlocking the secrets of the irradiated sludge is the only viable path toward developing a cure for the leper gnomes. Driven mad and deformed by the toxic venting ordered during the trogg invasion, these tragic survivors remain trapped in a living nightmare, making even the most dangerous gathering expeditions inside the ruins worth the hazard.

item:highborne-relic-classic.text: Highborne Relic (Classic). In Darkshore, Highborne Relics remain in the hands of spirits haunting Ameth'Aran. Night elf scholars seek them for destruction before their dormant magic can cause more harm. Ten thousand years ago, the Highborne caste brought ruin upon ancient Kalimdor through reckless arcane magic. Their estates lie in shattered ruins across Darkshore. At Ameth'Aran, wailing apparitions wander among the crumbling columns, still clutching the implements of their old sorcery. The relics bind arcane taint to the spirits, who will not release the objects tied to their undoing. Night elf society largely renounced arcane magic after the Great Sundering, and scholars see these relics as a grave hazard. Acting on reports from the Sentinels, Thundris Windweaver in Auberdine sends travelers to wrest them from the cursed spirits. Once gathered, the relics are destroyed so the Highborne's ancient evils and catastrophic mistakes cannot be repeated.

item:highperch-venom-sac.text: Highperch Venom Sac. Highperch Venom Sacs are harvested from the wild wyverns nesting upon the towering spires of Highperch in Thousand Needles. While orcs prize wyverns as aerial mounts, select apothecaries and traders value their potent stingers even more than the living beasts. The high spires of Thousand Needles house thriving prides of wild wyverns, particularly around the elevated crags of Highperch. These winged predators rely on powerful venom delivered through their barbed tails to paralyze and kill prey. While the Horde often domesticates these creatures as loyal wind riders, their venom sacs command a remarkably high price among alchemists, hunters, and opportunistic merchants across Kalimdor. Though native to the deep canyons of central Kalimdor, this venom draws interest far beyond them. In the port town of Theramore, the high elf Fiora Longears pays handsomely for fresh sacs collected from Highperch's broods. She seeks samples swollen with venom—typically found only on young wyverns or fertile females—fueling trade in dangerous reagents far from the beasts' natural desert habitat.

item:highperch-wyvern-egg.text: Highperch Wyvern Egg. Highperch Wyvern Eggs are clutch eggs gathered from the nesting grounds atop the high mesas of Thousand Needles. They are sought after by aspiring Horde wind riders to raise and train new aerial mounts. The high plateau of Highperch in Thousand Needles provides a natural sanctuary for native wyverns to roost and raise their young. Accessible only via steep winding paths up the canyon walls, these nesting grounds are fiercely guarded by adult beasts. The eggs laid among these roosts are sturdy and warm, holding developing hatchlings capable of adapting to the harsh skies of Kalimdor. Across Kalimdor, the demand for trained wyverns continually outstrips supply as the Horde expands its courier and scouting networks. At Freewind Post, trainees like the tauren Elu seek out intact eggs directly from wild aeries. By raising the hatchlings from their shells, handlers hope to forge the deep bonds required to train trustworthy winged mounts for the Horde's wind riders.

item:hildelve-s-journal.text: Hildelve's Journal. Hildelve's Journal is the final record of dwarven pilot Hildelve, recovered from his remains in the frigid wilderness of Dun Morogh. Its bloodstained pages recount his fatal encounter with a ferocious bear and convey his dying wish for vengeance. When his steam tank broke down, dwarven pilot Hildelve left his partner Hammerfoot with the tanks and set out alone into the snow-swept crags of Dun Morogh in search of rumored chiron ore. According to the entries scrawled in his journal, he was stalked for days and then ambushed by a monstrous ice claw bear known as Mangeclaw. Though Hildelve fought bravely and managed to drive the beast off, he was left gravely mauled and stranded in the bitter cold. The journal details his agonizing final hours, concluding with a single, clear plea before the predator returned to finish him: that whoever discovered his body avenge his death by hunting down Mangeclaw.

item:hillsbrad-human-skull.text: Hillsbrad Human Skull. A gruesome war trophy harvested from slain human defenders and townsfolk across the Hillsbrad Foothills. These skulls are collected by Forsaken stationed at Tarren Mill as grim mementos of the relentless assault against the local human settlements. As conflict rages between the Forsaken of Tarren Mill and the human inhabitants of Southshore and surrounding settlements, severed skulls serve as physical proof of the slaughter. While Deathstalkers and soldiers carry out the systematic purge ordered by Darthalia during the Battle of Hillsbrad, other guards stuck on watch duty crave a piece of the carnage. Deathguard Samsa eagerly solicits these trophies from frontline fighters, taking twisted pleasure in amassing the remains of the very people the Forsaken once lived among in life.

item:hillsbrad-town-registry.text: Hillsbrad Town Registry. The Hillsbrad Town Registry is an official municipal ledger kept inside the town hall of the Hillsbrad Fields. It serves as an accounting of the settlement's surviving citizens, landowners, and civic records, making it a key strategic target during the Forsaken offensive against the human stronghold. Resting in the town hall near the podium of Magistrate Burnside, the Hillsbrad Town Registry documents the population, households, and administrative rights of Hillsbrad. As the Forsaken from Tarren Mill push to break human resistance in the foothills, Darthalia commands Horde champions to infiltrate the town hall, eliminate the council, and seize this ledger. Confiscating the registry strips Hillsbrad of its civic order and provides the Undercity with valuable intelligence on the surviving population and their assets.

item:hollow-vulture-bone.text: Hollow Vulture Bone. Hollow Vulture Bones are lightweight, durable skeletal remains harvested from the scavengers of the Shimmering Flats. At the Mirage Raceway, goblin mechanics prize them as specialized building materials to lighten their rocket cars without sacrificing structural integrity. Speed is everything out on the salt, and weight is the enemy of speed. While standard engineering leans heavily on iron and copper, the goblin pit crews at the Mirage Raceway turn to whatever the desert provides to gain an edge. Vulture bones are naturally hollow yet remarkably sturdy, providing the perfect strength-to-weight ratio for internal brackets, steering rigs, and minor structural supports. For chief tinkerers like Pozzik, harvesting bones from local scavengers is a practical and cheap shortcut to shaved seconds on the track.

item:honorary-picks.text: Honorary Picks. The Honorary Picks are a bundle of ceremonial tools crafted in Ironforge for young dwarven mining apprentices. Entrusted to travelers by way of the gryphon network, they are delivered to Brock Stoneseeker in Thelsamar to mark his students' readiness to work the rich ore veins of Loch Modan. In dwarven society, mining is far more than a trade; it is a cultural cornerstone that keeps the great forges burning and the kingdom supplied with iron and stone. The Honorary Picks represent formal recognition for novice prospectors learning under Brock Stoneseeker in Thelsamar. Sourced directly from Ironforge, these picks are presented to students who have proven their dedication and are ready to tackle the open ore deposits across Loch Modan. Transporting the picks serves a secondary purpose for the mountaineers and merchants of the Alliance: introducing couriers to the kingdom's gryphon network. Ferried from Ironforge's Great Forge directly to Gryth Thurden and flown across the mountains to Thorgrum Borrelson in Thelsamar, the shipment illustrates how closely tied the capital remains to its outlying outposts through swift aerial passage.

item:horn-of-arra-chea.text: Horn of Arra'chea. The Horn of Arra'chea is a hunting trophy taken from the legendary kodo Arra'chea, who wanders the plains of Mulgore. Claimed at the behest of High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof, the horn serves as definitive proof that an aspiring hunter has the discipline and tracking prowess to provide for the Shu'halo. Though passing the initial Rites of the Earthmother grants a youth their rightful place atop Thunder Bluff, High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof expects his people to continually prove their worth. For the tauren, identity is bound directly to the hunt and their enduring harmony with the land. Cairne tests young hunters by tasking them with tracking down Arra'chea, a massive, lone kodo bull roaming the grasslands below. Taking Arra'chea's horn proves mastery over the fundamental art of tracking prey across vast distances. Bringing the horn to the high rise of Thunder Bluff is more than a display of martial strength; it serves the survival of the entire community. In tauren culture, nothing of a slain beast is allowed to go to waste. Presenting the trophy alerts the High Chieftain to the fallen beast's location, allowing gathering parties to quickly depart down into the plains to harvest Arra'chea's thick hide and rich meat for the fledgling capital.

item:horn-of-awakening.text: Horn of Awakening. In southern Darkshore, Kerlonian Evershade keeps a horn close at hand. It rouses him whenever sleep overtakes him on the road to Ashenvale. Kerlonian Evershade has only recently awakened from centuries in the Emerald Dream, and wakefulness still weighs on him. The Druid of the Claw travels south toward Maestra's Post and entrusts the horn to travelers willing to escort him. When exhaustion takes him along the wilderness trail, a clear blast jolts him awake and gets him back on his feet before wild beasts or cultists can reach him.

item:horn-of-echeyakee.text: Horn of Echeyakee. At the Crossroads, Sergra Darkthorn gives hunters the Horn of Echeyakee. Sounded among the ancient kodo remains northeast of the settlement, it calls the legendary white predator of the Barrens. Hunters who are being tested in the hunt receive the horn. Its call summons Echeyakee, whose name means “Whitemist” in Taur-ahe. Taure n hunters revere the king of the savannah cats as both mercy and death. He strikes so swiftly that his quarry feels neither terror nor suffering. The horn belongs at the predator’s lair, among giant kodo bones behind the hills northeast of the Crossroads.

item:huge-gnoll-claw.text: Huge Gnoll Claw. In southwestern Elwynn, Hogger’s huge claw is sought as proof of his death. Stormwind’s authorities in Goldshire require it for the bounty. Hogger has terrorized the southern woodlands of Forest's Edge for months. Patrols have failed to stop the brute, and the local garrison cannot corral or subdue him. The Stormwind Army, stretched thin across Elwynn, posted an open bounty on his head. Marshal Dughan in Goldshire requires clear proof before paying it. Hogger's oversized claw leaves no doubt that the notorious marauder has fallen.

item:humbert-s-sword.text: Humbert's Sword. Humbert's Sword is the personal sidearm belonging to Deathguard Humbert of Tarren Mill. The weapon was looted from his camp by dwarven soldiers while he was scouting their stronghold at Dun Garok. Deathguard Humbert was dispatched by High Executor Darthalia to monitor the dwarven presence at Dun Garok from a concealed position. While he left his post unattended one morning to collect firewood to boil water, dwarven patrols stumbled across his campsite and plundered all of his gear, including his personal blade. With so many dwarves to search, Humbert relies on Horde agents to infiltrate the fortress and retrieve his lost weapon. Following the theft, Humbert's belongings were carried back behind the fortified barricades of Dun Garok. Because dwarven riflemen, mountaineers, and priests circulate supplies throughout the garrison, locating the specific thief requires searching among the defenders stationed within the stronghold's trenches and redoubts.

item:hyacinth-mushroom.text: Hyacinth Mushroom. In Shadowglen, Hyacinth Mushrooms grow at the roots of trees across Teldrassil. Night elf herbalists use them for medicine, and grell and grellkin forage for them. Hyacinth Mushrooms grow in Shadowglen among the trees and roots of Aldrassil. Forest healers use them in remedies for young night elf sentinels and trainees harmed by venomous creatures. The spiders of Shadowthread Cave are among the dangers they face, and the mushrooms go into soothing draughts and antivenoms. Corrupted grell also hoard them.

item:hypercapacitor-gizmo.text: Hypercapacitor Gizmo. The Hypercapacitor Gizmo is an eccentric piece of engineering recovered from the canyon floor of Thousand Needles. Once dangling from the neck of a caged beast in a ruined caravan, its true purpose remains a mystery even to the tinkerer who claims to own it. When centaur marauders ambushed a goblin caravan traveling through Thousand Needles, they plundered nearly everything in sight. The sole survivor, Wizlo Bearingshiner, managed to crawl his way to safety at Whitereach Post, leaving behind his best gizmo: the Hypercapacitor Gizmo. Strangely, the gadget wound up secured around the neck of a ferocious, enraged panther locked inside a transport cage. The raiding centaur feared the beast enough to leave the cage entirely alone amidst the burning wreckage, unwittingly preserving Wizlo's odd machine. While Wizlo proudly calls the device his best gizmo, he admits upon its recovery that he has no real idea what it actually does. Like many goblin contraptions, the Hypercapacitor Gizmo is a tangled mass of ambition and volatile parts, destined to keep its owner occupied with endless tinkering rather than serving any practical, understood function.

item:ignition-key.text: Ignition Key. At Sludge Fen, the Ignition Key is held by Supervisor Lugwizzle at the Venture Company drilling operation. Wizzlecrank needs it to unlock an advanced shredder's movement column and activate its controls. Sputtervalve of Ratchet sent an operative to steal a Venture Company shredder from Sludge Fen, but the plan stalled. The undercover pilot, Wizzlecrank, climbed into the cockpit and found the movement column locked. He pretended the machine had mechanical trouble so the foremen would not grow suspicious while he waited for someone to fetch the Ignition Key. Supervisor Lugwizzle keeps the key high atop the central oil derrick, where access to the shredder's arm, speed, and rotation controls is held.

item:ilkrud-magthrull-s-tome.text: Ilkrud Magthrull's Tome. At Fire Scar Shrine, Ilkrud Magthrull's Tome draws Delgren the Purifier's attention. Its pages connect the warlock to the cultists at the Tower of Althalaxx. Ilkrud Magthrull holds the Fire Scar Shrine in southwestern Ashenvale, where demonic influence has poisoned the site. The formidable orc warlock is surrounded by summoned minions. His personal tome records foul rituals and shadowy communications. The Argent Dawn paladin Delgren the Purifier has long known of Magthrull's presence, but the ties between the warlock and the dark cultists gathering at the Tower of Althalaxx make the book urgent to recover.

item:incantations-from-the-nether.text: Incantations from the Nether. Beneath Orgrimmar, Searing Blade cultists hold Incantations from the Nether, a grimoire of demonic magic. Sylvanas Windrunner and Varimathras seek its fel knowledge for the Forsaken. The Searing Blade is a subterranean sect tied to the Shadow Council, working in the fiery tunnels of Ragefire Chasm beneath Orgrimmar's red stone streets. Its cultists prize Incantations from the Nether, a spellbook of demonic rites given by agents of the Burning Legion. They use its secrets to plot treason in the Orcish capital. Word of the tome has reached the royal quarters of Undercity.

item:incendia-agave.text: Incendia Agave. Incendia Agave is a rare, spiky aquatic plant native to the Boiling Pool beneath Darkcloud Pinnacle in Thousand Needles. When enchanted by a skilled shaman, its unique properties allow it to kindle the sacred fire of life. Growing beneath and around the waters of the Boiling Pool in Thousand Needles, Incendia Agave thrives directly in the shadow of Darkcloud Pinnacle. Guarded naturally by wandering steam elementals, the plant is difficult to harvest and scarce across Kalimdor. Despite growing submerged in water, it contains potent natural elements that lend themselves directly to rituals of flame.

item:incendia-powder.text: Incendia Powder. Incendia Powder is an enchanted ritual catalyst refined to ignite sacred flames. Carried by Horde emissaries into Thousand Needles, the powder is specifically treated with shamanic incantations to invoke the slumbering spirit-beast Arikara atop Darkcloud Pinnacle. Incendia Powder is no mundane explosive or mundane flash powder; it is a purified, ritualistic substance carefully infused with shamanic magic. Enchanted and entrusted to travelers by Magatha Grimtotem on Thunder Bluff's Elder Rise, the mixture is designed to react solely with the dormant sacred fire of life atop the isolated spires of Darkcloud Pinnacle. Once scattered across the consecrated brazier where the dead are laid to rest, its alchemical and spiritual warding calls forth the vengeful winged serpent Arikara.

item:insane-scribbles.text: Insane Scribbles. In Darkshore, cultists carry Insane Scribbles torn from the Twilight Tome, a fragment of dark literature. The dancing text and distorted scrollwork cause dizziness and mental strain. Ancient forest protectors study the fragments to learn the Twilight's Hammer's motives. Reading the Twilight Tome can endanger a mortal's sanity. Its script writhes across the parchment, and graceful scrollwork warps into grotesque images before the reader's eyes. Tearing out even one sheet, called Insane Scribbles, leaves the bearer lightheaded and disoriented. Though the writing makes little sense, the parchment hums with primal, deeply ancient magic tied to dark powers long buried beneath Azeroth.

item:inscribed-bark.text: Inscribed Bark. In Teldrassil, Inscribed Bark carries word of the World Tree's state to Arch Druid Fandral Staghelm. The Oracle Tree entrusts it with news of the boughs and the threats troubling the woods. The Oracle Tree sends Inscribed Bark to the Cenarion Circle in Darnassus. After you drive the harpies from their nests, the ancient tree gives you its message, wary of sending ordinary couriers along Teldrassil's tainted paths. The report tells Arch Druid Fandral Staghelm of recent victories and the deeper blight still gripping the woods.

item:intact-raptor-horn.text: Intact Raptor Horn. Across the Barrens savannas, raptors are hunted for their intact horns. Mebok Mizzyrix of Ratchet wants them for a scheme built on rumors of raptor intelligence. Hunters prize raptor hides, talons, and trophies, but whole horns are harder to take in the field. Mebok Mizzyrix, an eccentric goblin alchemist in Ratchet, believes the Barrens raptors are more cunning than their kin elsewhere. He suspects their intellect lies in their horns. By grinding whole horns and brewing them into tonics, Mebok hopes to bottle that supposed genius in commercial drinks. A horn fit for brewing must come from a particularly vicious predator, not just any young raptor. Sunscale Scytheclaws prowl the southern plains and the northern borders near Ashenvale. Takk the Leaper and the elusive Ishamuhale are notable terrors of the veldt, and their stout horns can survive the clash of the hunt intact.

item:intrepid-strongbox-key.text: Intrepid Strongbox Key. The Intrepid Strongbox Key is a rusted iron key once guarded jealously by Captain Halyndor, commander of the doomed Alliance vessel Intrepid. Even in undeath, the captain clutches it, keeping locked away the cursed artifact that brought ruin to his crew off the coast of the Wetlands. During the wreck of the Third Fleet off the stormy shores of the Wetlands, the warship Intrepid was cast into ruin, its crew twisted into restless, cursed spirits. Captain Halyndor obsessively watched over a mysterious item stowed inside the vessel's heavy strongbox. In death, his spectral figure continues to prowl the waterlogged deck, refusing to relinquish the rusted key that unlocks the hold's deepest, darkest cargo.

item:invisibility-liquor.text: Invisibility Liquor. Invisibility Liquor gives Maybell Maclure a way to slip from her family's sight and meet Tommy Joe Stonefield. Their households are locked in a feud. Tommy Joe Stonefield seeks a quiet meeting with Maybell Maclure, though their families' feud keeps the households apart. Their kin watch closely, and ordinary secrecy is not enough. Invisibility Liquor lets the drinker pass unseen across the disputed farmland.

item:iron-pike.text: Iron Pike. Iron Pikes are sturdy construction materials originally shipped from Stormwind to aid in repairing the Everstill Bridge in Lakeshire. The shipment was ambushed and looted by Redridge gnolls, leaving the town short on essential rebuilding supplies. When Lakeshire faced recent attacks from the Blackrock orcs, the town's metal reserves were melted down to forge armor, blades, and ammunition for defense. In response to the shortage, local builders requested a resupply shipment of iron from Stormwind City. Before the materials could reach the town, a pack of Redridge gnolls hijacked the transport caravan along the road. The gnolls dragged crates of iron pikes and rivets north into the hills, halting critical repairs on the Everstill Bridge. Foreman Oslow, charged with overseeing the reconstruction of the Everstill Bridge, relies on adventurers to enter gnoll territory and reclaim the pilfered hardware. Without these heavy iron pikes to reinforce the stone and timber framework, Lakeshire remains partially severed from the northern roadway and vulnerable to further incursions.

item:iron-pommel.text: Iron Pommel. The Iron Pommel is the final missing fragment of Dartol's Rod, a rod created by the long-dead wizard Dartol and sought by the night elves of Astranaar to slow the furbolg attacks on their people. Entrusted to the druids of the Dor'Danil Barrow Den for safekeeping, it was lost when their sanctuary was slaughtered and overrun by oozes. Dartol's Rod was divided and scattered across Ashenvale to protect its mystic power. The Iron Pommel was placed into the care of the night elf druids dwelling near the road winding south toward the Barrens. Tragedy struck the secluded enclave at the Dor'Danil Barrow Den when the circle was massacred, their tranquil shelter falling into ruined silence. The pommel vanished into the aftermath, swallowed by the grotesque, bubbling oozes that now shamble through the defiled glade.

item:iron-rivet.text: Iron Rivet. Iron Rivets are sturdy construction fasteners manufactured in Stormwind to help rebuild the ruined Everstill Bridge in Lakeshire. After a supply caravan was ambushed and looted by Redridge gnolls, these heavy metal components ended up scattered across the gnoll camps in the northern hills. When Lakeshire faced repeated assaults from the Blackrock orcs, the town council was forced to melt down their structural iron reserves to forge urgent weapons, armor, and munitions. Once the immediate crisis subsided, Foreman Oslow requested fresh building supplies from Stormwind to mend the fractured Everstill Bridge. However, the supply caravan ferrying the shipment was ambushed by local Redridge gnolls before reaching the town. The pack beasts and wagons were dragged into the hills north of Lake Everstill, scattering essential construction materials like iron rivets and pikes among the gnoll packs. Without these heavy iron rivets, structural repairs on the Everstill Bridge cannot proceed safely. The stone and timber framework spanning the lake requires reinforced metal fasteners to withstand the weight of carts and travelers. Recovering the rivets directly from the gnoll camps is essential for restoring Lakeshire's vital link to the western valleys and securing the town's perimeter against further incursions.

item:iron-shaft.text: Iron Shaft. The Iron Shaft is a metallic segment of Dartol's Rod, a relic Raene Wolfrunner's friend Teronis sought in hopes of slowing the furbolg assaults on Ashenvale. Recovered from a locked chest near the border of Felwood, it serves as a crucial component in restoring the relic for the defenders of Ashenvale. Dartol's Rod was the creation of Dartol, and its pieces were scattered across Ashenvale; one was even given to the druids of Dor'Danil for safekeeping. The Iron Shaft represents the sturdy metal core of the instrument, secured away inside a locked chest in a secluded glade near the northern border of Ashenvale, not far from the tainted realm of Felwood.

item:ironband-s-progress-report.text: Ironband's Progress Report. Ironband's Progress Report is a written dispatch detailing the troubles facing Prospector Ironband's excavation site in eastern Loch Modan. It conveys both an account of slow digging hindered by aggressive troggs and an urgent plea for more blastpowder. Prospector Ironband's excavation in Loch Modan faces continuous disruption from local troggs. To keep the project moving forward, Ironband compiled this progress report to restate his desperate need for blastpowder. Carried first to Jern Hornhelm in Thelsamar and then forwarded to the Assembly of Explorers in Ironforge, the report documents the site's stalls while requesting heavy munitions. The dispatch quickly raises eyebrows among league leadership, as an ample supply of blastpowder was dispatched to Ironband weeks prior, leaving superiors wondering where the previous shipments vanished.

item:ishamuhale-s-fang.text: Ishamuhale's Fang. At Camp Taurajo, Jorn Skyseer awaits Ishamuhale's Fang from the feared sunscale raptor Speartooth of the Barrens. The tooth proves the hunter bested one of Kalimdor's deadliest natural predators. Across the central savanna, hunters fear Ishamuhale, the fiercest sunscale raptor alive. Some say the apex hunter kills from predatory passion, not hunger. Fresh zhevra meat draws the beast into the open beside a withered tree northwest of Ratchet, where it gives no quarter. Taking its massive fang proves to the Horde's hunting instructors that a traveler has overcome the savagery of the plains.

item:ivar-s-head.text: Ivar's Head. Ivar's Head is the gruesome proof of the destruction of the ravenous ghoul Ivar the Foul in Silverpine Forest. It is sought by the Deathstalker Rane Yorick to ensure safe recovery for her wounded brother Quinn. While scouting northern Silverpine Forest on the orders of High Executor Hadrec, the Forsaken Deathstalkers Rane and Quinn Yorick were ambushed at an abandoned farmstead by a feral ghoul known as Ivar the Foul. Though the siblings managed to fend off the fiend, Quinn was severely mauled in the confrontation. Stranded at the ruined farm while her brother recovered, Rane could not safely leave Quinn unattended to complete their mission. Severing Ivar's head provides definitive proof that the beast will never terrorize the estate again, granting Quinn the necessary time to recuperate under Rane's watchful eye.

item:iverron-s-antidote-item.text: Iverron's Antidote (item). In Shadowglen, Iverron's Antidote must reach a young night elf before it spoils. Dirania Silvershine brews it to counter the lethal venom of local Webwood spiders, but it lasts only five minutes. Dirania Silvershine brews the antidote in Aldrassil for Iverron, a young night elf bitten by Webwood spiders. Its volatile ingredients and herbal catalysts give the draught a shelf life of only five minutes. Couriers must hurry north to the Webwood cave and deliver it before it spoils.

item:jade-phial.text: Jade Phial. In Dolanaar, Corithras Moonrage entrusts the Jade Phial to young initiates. It carries sacred water from Teldrassil’s moonwells to replenish the druids’ central well in Darnassus. The Jade Phial gathers water from a moonwell near Starbreeze Village. Teldrassil’s many moonwells channel lunar and natural energies that matter to night elf society and druidic worship. From time to time, the druids replenish their central moonwell in Darnassus with water from wells across the great bough. Corithras Moonrage entrusts the phial to young initiates, who use it to collect pure water without disturbing the moonwell’s spiritual potency.

item:jennea-s-flask.text: Jennea's Flask. At the Wizard's Sanctum in Stormwind, Jennea Cannon sends apprentices to Mirror Lake for water. They bring the sample back for arcane analysis. After magical struggles across Azeroth, arcane currents have torn loose from their ancient channels. Jennea Cannon seeks to learn how these shifts have affected Elwynn Forest. She gives promising apprentices a glass flask and sends them southwest of Stormwind's gates to the base of Mirror Lake's waterfall. The flask protects the water sample on the journey back to the Wizard's Sanctum, where it can be examined for arcane disturbances. Jennea's flask lets Stormwind's mages check whether shifting ley lines have tainted Mirror Lake. If the water carries harmful magic, the surrounding life and anyone who drinks from it could suffer strange afflictions. A sample can reveal magical residue before tainted currents spread through the countryside.

item:jitters-completed-journal.text: Jitters' Completed Journal. Jitters' Completed Journal is a handwritten account detailing the grim tragedies of Duskwood, specifically the massacre at Sven Yorgen's farm. Fearing vengeance, the reclusive Jitters surrenders the finished text to clear his name and shed light on the sinister forces haunting the region.

item:johaan-s-findings.text: Johaan's Findings. Johaan's Findings is a bundle of research documents penned by Apothecary Johaan in Brill. Entrusted to a courier heading south, these notes convey recent alchemical developments in Tirisfal Glades to Apothecary Renferrel at the Sepulcher. The Royal Apothecary Society operates under relentless pressure from Lady Sylvanas Windrunner to engineer a New Plague capable of destroying both the living and the Scourge. Because researchers are scattered across Lordaeron's contested ruins, maintaining a flow of data between outposts is vital. Apothecary Johaan compiles his local testing notes in Brill and dispatches them southward to Apothecary Renferrel, who directs society efforts from the Sepulcher in Silverpine Forest. These records represent one small piece of the Society's collective effort to hone their lethal brews.

item:johaan-s-special-drink.text: Johaan's Special Drink. Johaan's Special Drink is a lethal concoction prepared by Apothecary Johaan in the village of Brill. Disguised as a common refreshment, the mixture serves as a field test for the Royal Apothecary Society's developing plague. Brewed in the brewing cauldrons of Brill, Johaan's Special Drink is far from a tavern beverage. Apothecary Johaan concocts the draft by refining various venomous components and local reagents into a single draught, tailored specifically to test virulence against living physiology. Handed over under the guise of slaking a captive's thirst, it represents the Forsaken apothecaries' ongoing ambition to engineer a weapon potent enough to fulfill Sylvanas Windrunner's designs for Azeroth.

item:jordan-s-ore-shipment.text: Jordan's Ore Shipment. Jordan's Ore Shipment is a crate of ore that Bailor Stonehand was to turn into his alloy for the smith Jordan Stilwell. Carried by caravan from the Wetlands, the delivery was intercepted and looted by Mo'grosh ogres in the northeastern hills of Loch Modan. Meant to be refined by the dwarf Bailor Stonehand into his special alloy, this ore was originally promised to Jordan Stilwell for his metalwork. While crossing south through the mountains from the Wetlands into Loch Modan, the supply caravan was violently ambushed by the Mo'grosh ogres. The shipment was dragged into the ogres' wilderness stronghold, leaving the surviving guards to perish from their wounds and halting Jordan's smithing project until an adventurer can pry it back from the brutes.

item:jordan-s-refined-ore-shipment.text: Jordan's Refined Ore Shipment. Jordan's Refined Ore Shipment is a crate of high-grade metal prepared specifically for the smith Jordan Stilwell. Acquired as part of a paladin's sacred trials, it provides the essential stock needed to forge a holy weapon of virtue. When Jordan Stilwell set out to forge a weapon worthy of a dedicated paladin, ordinary stock would not suffice. The blacksmith required an assortment of rare and exacting components: a Purified Kor Gem, sturdy Whitestone Oak lumber, his own lost smithing hammer, and a specialized shipment of refined ore. This consignment represents the metal foundation for that sacred labor, brought to Ironforge to complete the Test of Righteousness.

item:jordan-s-smithing-hammer.text: Jordan's Smithing Hammer. Jordan's Smithing Hammer is a cherished family heirloom passed down to the human blacksmith Jordan Stilwell by his father. Its recovery from the haunted halls of Shadowfang Keep is essential for forging a holy weapon consecrated to the Light. To an ordinary observer, Jordan's Smithing Hammer might seem like mere smith's iron, but to Jordan Stilwell, it represents both heritage and destiny. Inherited from his father, this tool is central to Jordan's identity as a forge master outside Ironforge. Having somehow wound up within the forsaken stone walls of Shadowfang Keep in Silverpine Forest, it must be reclaimed before Jordan can attempt his masterwork—a sacred weapon fit for a holy champion.

item:kadrak-s-flag.text: Kadrak's Flag. At the edge of the Barrens and Ashenvale, Kadrak gives the Horde a mark to carry into enemy ground. The flag is planted in the Talon Den after Keymaster Rynthariel is killed. Kadrak sends the Horde flag into the Talon Den on Stonetalon Peak. The dryad Rynthariel, Keymaster of the Den, has sent communications across the border, and Kadrak decides her death alone will not answer them. He gives you the crimson banner to plant deep inside the Den. The Horde colors there carry a warning to the night elves and dryads: incursions across the Barrens will meet retaliation on Alliance soil.

item:keg-of-shindigger-stout.text: Keg of Shindigger Stout. A Keg of Shindigger Stout is a barrel of potent dwarven ale brewed and guarded by the riflemen and soldiers garrisoned within Dun Garok. Desired by the Royal Apothecary Society in Tarren Mill, it serves not as an evening drink, but as a deceitful delivery vehicle for newly synthesized plagues. Dun Garok stands as a formidable dwarven bastion in the southeastern Hillsbrad Foothills, fiercely maintained by the dwarves of Ironforge. Within its entrenched barracks and mess halls, the stout-hearted defenders share barrels of Shindigger Stout to weather the cold and the grinding siege against regional enemies. The brew is robust and plentiful, making it a staple of the garrison's day-to-day survival.

item:ken-zigla-s-draught.text: Ken'zigla's Draught. Ken'zigla's Draught is a potent, foul-tasting medicinal tonic prepared by Ken'zigla in the Stonetalon Mountains. It is formulated to restore enough strength to critically wounded individuals so they can move without bleeding out. Prepared by Ken'zigla in the Stonetalon Mountains, this potent brew serves as an emergency restorative for those on the verge of death. The tonic is extremely strong and must be measured carefully; drinking more than half a dose at once risks causing the patient to bleed out as their circulation surges. Administering half provides enough raw vigor to move and flee imminent danger, while the remainder must wait until the body stabilizes after a full night's rest.

item:khazgorm-s-journal.text: Khazgorm's Journal. At Bael Modan, Prospector Khazgorm leads the Ironforge dwarven excavation in the southern Barrens. His field ledger records the Explorers' League's work on lands claimed by the Stonespire tauren. Prospector Khazgorm directs the heavy machinery and blasting that cut into the southern Barrens hillsides. His notes show an excavation far from the Explorers' League's promised search for knowledge: its work has displaced the Stonespire tribe. The tauren tried to settle matters peacefully, but the dwarves refused. Gann Stonespire wants the journal to understand the Ironforge presence in his homeland and find a way to break it.

item:klaven-mortwake-s-journal.text: Klaven Mortwake's Journal. Inside a chest from Duskwood, Klaven Mortwake's Journal records the Defias Brotherhood's search for a way to raise the dead. SI:7 operatives recovered it from the Defias tower in northeastern Westfall. Master Mathias Shaw leads Stormwind's intelligence service, SI:7, and sought Mortwake's journal to trace the Brotherhood's wider alliances. The notes confirm experiments in reanimation and illicit support linking Duskwood, the Venture Company, and the Defias. For rogues serving the crown, recovering the research marks a step toward mastering poisons.

item:kodo-horn.text: Kodo Horn. In the Barrens, Kodo Horns are gathered from the roaming kodos. Tonga Runetotem uses them in herbal remedies for poisoned wildlife. Across the Barrens, Tonga Runetotem uses intact kodo horns in his herbal remedies. He works from the Crossroads, where the horns help strengthen his salves. Chips and fragments lack the strength he needs, so he gathers whole horns from mature kodos wandering the plains.

item:kodo-liver.text: Kodo Liver. In Ratchet, Brewmaster Drohn needs Kodo Liver for a strange ale. He learned to brew trogg ale from the wandering brewmaster Chen Stormstout. Kodos roam the Barrens, where tauren and predators hunt them for their hides and meat. In Ratchet, Brewmaster Drohn uses a fresh Kodo Liver with thunderhawk saliva glands and lightning glands to make trogg ale. Chen Stormstout taught Drohn the recipe, and Drohn says the blend packs a potent kick for adventurous travelers. The ingredients come from the wilds of central Kalimdor.

item:kodobane-s-head.text: Kodobane's Head. Near the Forgotten Pools, Barak Kodobane's severed head proves the cunning chieftain's death. The orc warlord Regthar Deathgate receives it as proof that the centaur threat there has been broken. Kolkar bands in the Barrens have long been divided, but ambitious warlords now threaten to gather them into an army. Barak Kodobane made his camp by the lush waters of the Forgotten Pools, where the oasis offers vital resources and nearby paths lie open to raids. Regthar Deathgate, stationed in a bunker west of the Crossroads, demands Kodobane's severed head as proof that this commander can no longer rally his kin against the Horde.

item:kravel-s-crate.text: Kravel's Crate. Kravel's Crate is a heavy package dispatched by Kravel Koalbeard from the Mirage Raceway in the Shimmering Flats. Destined for the Nesingwary expedition in Stranglethorn Vale, it contains specialized hunting ammunition designed to bring down the jungle's deadliest game. Handed out by the shrewd entrepreneur Kravel Koalbeard at the Mirage Raceway, Kravel's Crate represents an unfinished business transaction across continents. Ordered weeks prior by a wealthy dwarven patron, the shipment was delayed long enough for its buyer to depart Kalimdor entirely. Rather than lose out on the favor of a wealthy customer who already paid for forwarding, Kravel entrusts passing adventurers to haul the crate all the way to northern Stranglethorn Vale. Despite its nondescript appearance and the crust of salt dust it gathers in the Shimmering Flats, the crate carries lethal cargo: heavy, special-gauge ammunition tailored specifically for hunting rifles. When received at the expedition camp north of Grom'gol, the recipient notes that the potent rounds are prized by big-game hunters and vital for survival against the predators roaming the jungle canopy.

item:kreenig-snarlsnout-s-tusk.text: Kreenig Snarlsnout's Tusk. At the Crossroads, Thork seeks proof that Kreenig Snarlsnout has fallen. His tusk marks the end of the Razormane leader's attacks on Horde caravans in the northern Barrens. Horde caravans traveling west from Durotar face constant attacks in the Barrens. Those raids grew bolder under Kreenig Snarlsnout, a fierce Razormane leader. Thork, commander of the Crossroads watch, ordered Kreenig killed to disrupt the quilboars' coordination. His tusk offers proof that the leader is dead and insults the Razormane, weakening their resolve and leaving their fighters without central direction.

item:kuz-s-skull.text: Kuz's Skull. In the southern Barrens, Kuz's Skull marks the end of a feared Razormane raider. Kuz came from Razorfen Kraul and helped lead attacks on Horde outposts before a captive former kin sought vengeance. Kuz, Nak, and their chieftain Lok Orcbane led Razormane attacks across the southern Barrens. Sent from Razorfen Kraul, the three raiders struck travelers and settlements such as the Crossroads. Their betrayal of Mangletooth, a fellow quilboar, turned one of their own against them. They left Mangletooth to rot in a cage at Camp Taurajo. From that cage, he revealed Kuz's location to Horde champions willing to kill the raider and take her head.

item:laced-pumpkin.text: Laced Pumpkin. A Laced Pumpkin is an ordinary gourd treated with a lethal concoction developed by Apothecary Johaan in Brill. Handed to a starving, imprisoned Scarlet Crusader under the guise of sustenance, it serves as a live field test for the Forsaken's growing arsenal of alchemical weapons. To the untrained eye, the laced pumpkin appears to be ordinary produce salvaged from the blighted soil of Tirisfal Glades. Under the supervision of Apothecary Johaan in Brill, however, the vegetable is treated with experimental toxins designed to realize the full potential of undeath. The Royal Apothecary Society constantly seeks new weapons to repel both the Scourge in the north and living human forces advancing from the south, turning even simple harvest goods into vectors for infection and chemical death.

item:laird-s-response.text: Laird's Response. Along Teldrassil's shores, Laird's Response carries a puzzle for Nessa Shadowsong. The fish there are larger and more plentiful than those along mainland Darkshore. Laird compares catches from across the Veiled Sea. Fish from Teldrassil's coast are larger and more plentiful than those from Darkshore's mainland beaches. In his reply to Nessa Shadowsong, Laird of Auberdine offers a theory: the newly planted World Tree's unusual presence and vitality may be changing the surrounding sea life. Travelers carry his letter across the water to Rut'theran Village, where the fisherfolk greet the news with wonder and quiet curiosity.

item:lake-creeper-moss.text: Lake Creeper Moss. Lake Creeper Moss is an organic compound harvested from the aquatic creepers dwelling among the Dawning Isles in Lake Lordamere. It serves as a vital reagent sought by the Royal Apothecary Society for their efforts to engineer a lethal new plague. Grown along the hides of the vicious freshwater beasts that prowl the southern Dawning Isles of Lake Lordamere, Lake Creeper Moss carries unique properties shaped by Lordaeron's blighted waters. Apothecary Berard, before Arugal's curse claimed his mind, documented it in his journal, noting that the moss resembled trace materials on the fossils of creatures killed by an ancient plague in the lake. When recovered by Forsaken agents, samples are dispatched directly to the Apothecarium in the Undercity to fuel Master Apothecary Faranell's dark research.

item:lake-skulker-moss.text: Lake Skulker Moss. Lake Skulker Moss is a biological reagent gathered from the bog beasts inhabiting the northern reaches of Lake Lordamere. It was identified by Apothecary Berard, before Arugal's curse claimed his mind, as a key organic component for the Royal Apothecary Society's research into brewing a New Plague. Harvested from the mossy bodies of Lake Skulkers and Elder Lake Skulkers on the Dawning Isles, this damp aquatic moss possesses properties prized by Forsaken alchemists. Before Arugal's curse claimed his mind, Apothecary Berard meticulously cataloged the flora and fauna of eastern Silverpine Forest, concluding in his journal that both Lake Skulker and Lake Creeper mosses could serve as stabilizing or reactive agents. After Berard became a mindless servant of Arugal, his journal was recovered from Pyrewood Village for Apothecary Renferrel, who instructed Forsaken champions to gather moss samples alongside a rare tumor from local Vile Fin murlocs, delivering them directly to Master Apothecary Faranell in the Undercity.

item:large-candle.text: Large Candle. In Elwynn's mines, kobolds carry Large Candles on their heads for light and wax. Their flames guide them through dark tunnels, and apothecaries value the wax. Kobolds use candle flame to find their way through the dark shafts beneath Elwynn Forest. They fasten the tapers to their heads, and Kobold Miners, Tunnelers, and Geomancers defend them fiercely from intruders. Though crudely made, the Large Candles carried in Fargodeep Mine and Jasperlode Mine hold valuable wax. Surface tradesmen cannot easily produce it in bulk, so the candles are both tools for the kobolds and a commodity for alchemists. William Pestle, an apothecary operative from Stormwind City, gathers Large Candles at the Lion's Pride Inn in Goldshire. His family runs an apothecary, and he needs rendered wax for its concoctions, balms, and ointments. Pestle hires passing adventurers to clear the infested mines and take candles from the kobolds.

item:large-soran-ruk-fragment.text: Large Soran'ruk Fragment. The Large Soran'ruk Fragment rests in Shadowfang Keep, far from the other shards. Its broken orb once held a disgraced demon of the Burning Legion. Disgraced demons of the Burning Legion may be condemned to imprisonment in enchanted orbs. Mages and warlocks aligned with the Legion receive these vessels and draw on the fel forces trapped within. Even when an orb is shattered, its bound fiend's lingering essence still radiates power. Each fragment draws ambitious practitioners of shadow magic. The orb of Soran'ruk was cracked into two halves long ago. Cultists elsewhere scattered one half into smaller pieces. A sorcerer in the cursed Shadowfang Keep claimed the larger half. The Shadowfang Darksouls carry the Large Soran'ruk Fragment, which holds the bound spirit until someone seeks to reforge the ancient vessel.

item:laughing-sister-s-hair.text: Laughing Sister's Hair. Laughing Sister's Hair consists of soft, magical locks harvested from dryads residing in the enchanted forests of Ashenvale. Highly sought after by skilled weavers, these strands possess innate mystical properties ideal for crafting fine robes. Harvested from the dryads known as laughing sisters near Raynewood Retreat in Ashenvale, this hair holds remarkable natural magic. While dryads are sacred woodland protectors linked to Cenarius and the night elves, craftsmen within the Horde value their hair purely as a potent crafting reagent. The troll tailor Kil'hala at the Crossroads spins these gathered locks into enchanted vestments for burgeoning practitioners of the arcane.

item:legacy-of-the-aspects.text: Legacy of the Aspects. Legacy of the Aspects is an ancient tome hidden deep within the Dor'Danil Barrow Den in southern Ashenvale. Retrieved during a Horde trial of the intellect, the volume contains essential lore concerning the Great Aspects that shaped ancient Azeroth. While earlier trials set forth by tauren elders test physical endurance and resolve, the pursuit of Legacy of the Aspects is designed to challenge the mind. Tasked by Braug Dimspirit at the entrance to the Talondeep Path in the Stonetalon Mountains, an aspirant must delve into the haunted barrow dens of Dor'Danil. Guarded by the restless spirits of fallen druids and the vicious creatures that slew them, the ancient text rests upon a stone pedestal. Claiming the volume is only the first step; the seeker must commit its contents to memory before relinquishing the book, as they are tested on its historical lessons.

item:letter-to-delgren.text: Letter to Delgren. Balthule Shadowstrike sends a warning from the Tower of Althalaxx in northern Darkshore. His letter to Delgren the Purifier describes the Dark Strand cult's demonic work and must reach Maestra's Post in Ashenvale. Balthule Shadowstrike watches the Dark Strand cult gather around the Tower of Althalaxx ruins. He cannot destroy the cult alone, so he writes to Delgren the Purifier, his tutor in the Holy Light, asking for aid. The cult's foul rites threaten more than Darkshore's coast. The letter must travel south through the region into western Ashenvale, where Delgren works with night elf Sentinels against demonic and undead threats.

item:letter-to-jin-zil.text: Letter to Jin'Zil. The Letter to Jin'Zil is a piece of correspondence penned by the orc Darsok Swiftdagger at the Crossroads. Entrusted to an adventurer after the defeat of Serena Bloodfeather, it bears word to the Darkspear witch doctor Jin'Zil in the Stonetalon Mountains that the northern Barrens have been purged of the Bloodfeather threat. Following the eradication of the harpy infestation at the Dry Hills and the slaying of Serena Bloodfeather, Darsok Swiftdagger drafts this missive to an old comrade. Recognizing that the harpies of the Barrens originally roosted within the peaks of Stonetalon Mountains, Darsok uses the dispatch to introduce a promising warrior to the wider frontier while notifying the witch doctor Jin'Zil that the harpy matron has fallen.

item:letter-to-jorgen.text: Letter to Jorgen. A sealed letter calls on Jorgen in Stormwind City to help with a missing diplomat. A diplomat bound for Theramore failed to arrive for talks with Lady Jaina Proudmoore, and royal investigators moved quickly to keep the matter quiet. While official agents searched the capital, other channels stirred. The letter bypasses military bureaucracy and seeks out Jorgen, a gruff veteran who fishes beneath the great statues in the Valley of Heroes. It invokes old obligations and draws him into a covert inquiry amid rumors of a Defias conspiracy.

item:lewis-note.text: Lewis' Note. At Sentinel Hill, Quartermaster Lewis sends an urgent supply requisition to a private armorer in Stormwind. A courier carries it by gryphon, asking for protective gear for the Westfall garrison. The People's Militia at Sentinel Hill gets little support from Stormwind's House of Nobles. Skirmishes with the Defias Brotherhood keep draining its meager stocks of gear. To keep the defenders outfitted, Quartermaster Lewis turns to private business instead of crown supplies. His requisition bypasses official military channels entirely. An Alliance courier must fly by gryphon to Old Town and present the order to Osric Strang, proprietor of Limited Immunity.

item:lightning-gland.text: Lightning Gland. In the Barrens, Lightning Glands are taken from stormhides roaming the plains. Brewmaster Drohn in Ratchet needs them for trogg ale, a fiery brew Chen Stormstout taught him to make. Stormhides roam the Barrens savannas among other predators touched by the elements. Their flesh holds lightning glands, organs charged with latent electricity. These glands are poor fare on their own, but brewers prize them for the sting they bring to a brew. Brewmaster Drohn keeps Chen Stormstout’s brewing traditions alive in Ratchet. To make trogg ale, a potent brew, Drohn needs five lightning glands, a thunderhawk saliva gland, and a fresh kodo liver. The finished drink has a sharp kick that adventurers find invigorating and potent.

item:logging-rope.text: Logging Rope. Logging Rope is heavy cordage vital to the Warsong clan's ongoing logging operations within Ashenvale. Shipments of this sturdy line were ambushed and stolen by local furbolg tribes who violently resist the Horde's expansion into the ancient forest. Maintaining the goblin-built machinery and lumber mills of the Warsong Lumber Camp requires massive quantities of durable logging line. Rather than reaching the loggers at their encampment, essential shipments were intercepted by the Foulweald and Thistlefur furbolg tribes. Driven mad by corruption and fiercely defensive of their ancestral woods, these furbolgs hoard the stolen ropes in their encampments across northern and central Ashenvale. Locke Okarr at Splintertree Post is tasked with recovering the misplaced logistical chain before the Warsong lumber camp grinds to a halt. Reclaiming the heavy rope directly from the furbolg den-mothers and warriors allows the Horde to secure fellable timber, bound logs, and rig saw machinery amidst constant guerrilla resistance from the native forest inhabitants.

item:lok-s-skull.text: Lok's Skull. In the southern Barrens, Lok's Skull marks the fall of a feared Razormane leader. Lok Orcbane led fierce quilboar raids against Horde supply routes, and the skull is his severed head. Lok Orcbane led aggressive Razormane assaults on Horde supply lines in the southern Barrens. He emerged from Razorfen Kraul with his lieutenants Nak and Kuz. After betraying Mangletooth and leaving him captive at Camp Taurajo, Lok became known to orcish defenders for ruthless raids they struggled to contain. Mangletooth directs Horde champions to Lok's camp, where claiming Lok's skull avenges the captive and strikes at the leadership driving the Razormane offensive.

item:lonebrow-s-journal.text: Lonebrow's Journal. Lonebrow's Journal is a weathered diary found clutched in the skeletal remains of the dwarven explorer Henrig Lonebrow at the base of the Great Lift. Its pages detail the final grim journey of Lonebrow through the Barrens and point toward dangers lurking within Razorfen Kraul. Henrig Lonebrow met an unfortunate end near the base of the Great Lift connecting the Barrens to Thousand Needles. Lying abandoned on a rocky ledge, his skeletal remains still grip this weathered journal. The diary serves as a testament to his final travels and directs whoever discovers it to bring word to the night elf druid Falfindel Waywarder at Thalanaar, the border outpost leading into Feralas. Lonebrow's notes shed critical light on the quilboar menace brewing in the southern barrens.

item:lorgalis-manuscript.text: Lorgalis Manuscript. The Lorgalis Manuscript is an ancient text tied to the worship and lore of the Old Gods, preserved from the fallen night elven ruins beneath Ashenvale. Hidden within the sunken temple complex of Blackfathom Deeps, it holds secrets coveted by dark scholars seeking to awaken ancient, slumbering powers. The Lorgalis Manuscript rests at the bottom of Blackfathom Deeps, the sunken ruins where long-dead elves once dwelt before their city fell. Written by one Lorgalis, it speaks of the Old Gods who raged across Azeroth when the world was new and now lie chained and sleeping, and it praises Aku'mai, a servant of the Old Gods who dwells in the Deeps.
