Its lore is said to open mystical doorways and stir ancient entities that sleep deep beneath the world. Stored away in a pitted iron chest amidst the flooded corridors, it has drawn the attention of cultists and shadow scholars alike.

item:lunar-fungus.text: Lunar Fungus. Lunar Fungus grows in Darkshore's caves, where druids gather it for healing. Mixed with Earthroot and water, it helps make a salve for sick deer. Lunar Fungus grows from Lunar Fungal Blooms in Darkshore's underground caverns. The Cenarion Circle values its amplifying effects. Mixed with soothing water and common Earthroot, it lends potency to a salve that counters debilitating afflictions. Damp caves where it grows are also frequented by territorial moonkin, so gathering it means navigating carefully. In Auberdine, Alanndarian Nightsong has young druids gather Lunar Fungus as part of their studies in nature's healing arts. They see how physical ingredients such as this fungus can counter poisons in local deer. By learning how herbal remedies work, initiates prepare to channel natural antidotes through shapeshifting and spiritual power.

item:lurker-venom.text: Lurker Venom. Lurker Venom is a potent natural toxin harvested from the predatory spiders that prowl the rocky hills and woods of Loch Modan. Dwarven defenders require this caustic venom as a key ingredient to prepare an alchemical neutralizing compound against Dark Iron sabotage. The hills and crags surrounding Loch Modan crawl with predatory arachnids—ranging from common wood lurkers to the infamous matriarch Shanda the Spinner. While their bites pose a constant hazard to mountaineers and travelers, the explosives expert Ashlan Stonesmirk named their virulent poison as one ingredient of a disarming mixture, which Chief Engineer Hinderweir prepares. Combined with rare minerals and tears harvested from the loch's crocolisks, Lurker Venom forms a reactive solvent capable of disarming complex Dark Iron explosives.

item:lydon-s-toxin.text: Lydon's Toxin. Lydon's Toxin is an alchemical concoction synthesized by Apothecary Lydon in Tarren Mill to disrupt the Venture Company's deforestation in the Stonetalon Mountains. Entrusted to Horde adventurers, it is delivered to Apothecary Zamah in Thunder Bluff so she can devise an effective delivery mechanism. Developed by Apothecary Lydon in the Hillsbrad Foothills, this virulent compound is designed to combat the invasive Venture Company loggers despoiling the Stonetalon Mountains. According to Lydon, the concoction produces lethal and potentially contagious results upon contact. However, before the substance can be unleashed against the goblins' operations around the Windshear Crag, it must be ferried across continents to Apothecary Zamah, the Royal Apothecary Society's representative in Thunder Bluff. Zamah requires the raw mixture to engineer a wide-dispersal apparatus—the Toxic Fogger—ensuring the brew wipes out the exploitative deforesters without needlessly endangering Horde assets.

item:macgrann-s-dried-meats.text: MacGrann's Dried Meats. MacGrann's Dried Meats are a month's worth of salted provisions prepared by the hunter Tundra MacGrann to survive the harsh Dun Morogh winter. Stored in a reinforced thorium meat locker, the entire cache was snatched by the ferocious yeti known as Old Icebeard. Life in the freezing crags of Dun Morogh demands careful planning. To prepare for the blizzards of the cold season, the dwarf hunter Tundra MacGrann spent weeks hunting game, salting the meat, and securing it inside a sturdy chest. Aware that scavenging bears and prowling predators routinely plague his homestead, MacGrann took no chances and locked his food supply away inside a thorium meat locker. Even with those precautions, he did not anticipate an intruder strong enough to carry away the entire chest rather than trying to pry it open on the spot. While MacGrann was away tracking deer, the notorious yeti Old Icebeard raided the hunter's camp and dragged the heavy chest back to his den in Chill Breeze Valley. Though the beast lacked the means to break through the solid thorium plating, MacGrann's injured leg left him unable to mount a swift rescue into the cavern. Without outside assistance to retrieve the cache before winter sets in, the stranded hunter faced starvation amidst the mountain snows.

item:mackreel-s-moonshine.text: MacKreel's Moonshine. MacKreel's Moonshine is a potent dwarven liquor brewed by Foggy MacKreel, stationed on the broken Thandol Span north of the Wetlands. Strong enough to knock out a sentry on duty, it is prized as far north as Southshore, where Brewmeister Bilger accepts it as payment for debts. Brewed by the guard Foggy MacKreel on the Thandol Span, this moonshine carries an infamous reputation for potency. Even hardened dwarven sentries find themselves laid low by a night with the brew, waking with headaches akin to a brigade of siege engines rolling overhead. Despite its punishing kick, it is highly valued for warming up travelers against the damp chills of Lordaeron and Khaz Modan. Foggy MacKreel ran up an unsettled debt with Brewmeister Bilger, the tavern keeper and master brewer of Southshore. In order to clear his tab, Foggy traded a batch of his moonshine instead of coin. Bilger gladly accepts the liquor in place of gold, eager to add MacKreel's potent brew to his stock for the chilly coastal days of the Hillsbrad Foothills.

item:maggot-eye-s-paw.text: Maggot Eye's Paw. Maggot Eye's Paw is the gruesome trophy taken from the gnoll chieftain Maggot Eye at Garren's Haunt. Carried back to Brill, it serves as physical proof of the beast's execution for grave-robbing on behalf of the Scourge. Maggot Eye earned the harsh wrath of the Forsaken by raiding graves and pillaging the countryside near Garren's Haunt, providing corpses to bolster the ranks of the Lich King's armies. In response, a formal death sentence and bounty were posted in the town of Brill. Because mere rumors of a death are never enough for military administrators like Executor Zygand, bounty hunters must sever the villain's paw and bring it back to town to collect their reward and close the bounty.

item:maggran-s-reserve-letter.text: Maggran's Reserve Letter. Maggran's Reserve Letter is an official dispatch written by Maggran Earthbinder at Sun Rock Retreat. Carried across Kalimdor to the Great Lift, it grants a stationed sentry long-awaited relief so he may return home to visit his family. Maintaining outposts across the rugged expanse of Kalimdor demands vigilance, but the leaders of the Horde recognize that prolonged watch duty takes a heavy toll on morale. Penned by Maggran Earthbinder in the high crags of Sun Rock Retreat, this simple missive serves as official orders notifying Grish Longrunner that a replacement warrior has been dispatched to take over his post at the Great Lift. For a lonely guard watching over the towering wooden winches far to the south, the letter promises something rare in troubled times: an honorable leave of absence to reunite with family.

item:mangy-claw.text: Mangy Claw. The Mangy Claw is a severed claw taken from the great ice claw bear Mangeclaw in Dun Morogh. It serves as grim proof that the deadly beast responsible for killing a stranded dwarven pilot has finally been slain. When Pilot Hildelve's steam tank broke down in the frozen hills of Dun Morogh, he continued his search for ore on foot, only to face the mountain wilderness alone. As recorded in his recovered journal, Hildelve managed to fight off an initial attack by a monstrous ice claw bear named Mangeclaw, though he was savagely mauled in the struggle. The beast later returned to finish off the weakened pilot. Hildelve's final written entry pleaded for vengeance against the predator, a task fulfilled by taking the Mangy Claw from the fallen bear.

item:marshal-haggard-s-badge.text: Marshal Haggard's Badge. At his farm in Elwynn, Marshal Haggard has lost the badge he carried in Stormwind's service. Dead-tooth Jack stole it by trickery, and the Defias may use it to impersonate city officials. Marshal Haggard retired to a small farmstead in the hills of Elwynn Forest, but his old Stormwind Marshal's badge still carries official weight. One night, Dead-tooth Jack, a Defias rogue, wore a Stormwind tabard and posed as Marshal Dughan, Goldshire's garrison commander. He tricked Haggard into believing his former peers needed the insignia for official business. The aging marshal handed it over without suspicion. Jack fled into the woods before Haggard saw through the ruse. In Defias hands, the emblem of Stormwind authority could let outlaws pass checkpoints or confuse local patrols.

item:mary-s-looking-glass.text: Mary's Looking Glass. Mary's Looking Glass is a discarded hand mirror once treasured by Blind Mary before tragedy claimed her sight and life. Abandoned in the haunted groves of Duskwood, it was scavenged by a roving ghoul before being sought out to complete Viktori Prism'Antras's telescope. Before her terrible fate, Blind Mary treasured this polished looking glass. After her death and the loss of her eyes, looking upon her reflection became an agonizing reminder of what she had lost. She cast the mirror away behind her barn, leaving it to the encroaching gloom of Duskwood. There it fell into the clutching claws of an Insane Ghoul that wandered the ruined outskirts, carrying the trinket south into the crypts of Tranquil Gardens Cemetery. In Darkshire, the eccentric stargazer Viktori Prism'Antras dreamed of peering through Duskwood's eternal twilight toward the pristine heavens above. Building his telescope required specialized optical lenses and reflective glass. Learning of his need, Mary directed adventurers to hunt down the feral undead prowling the cemetery's ruined chapel, reclaiming the looking glass to serve as an optical reflector in his grand star-viewing machine.

item:mathystra-relic.text: Mathystra Relic. Among Mathystra’s overgrown ruins in northern Darkshore, ancient night elven relics still hold traces of magic. The Twilight's Hammer cult has taken an interest in them. Mathystra once stood on the Kalimdor coast as a city and bastion of elven civilization. Before the Great Sundering, it was a proud place. Now toppled columns and cracked stones lie half-swallowed by brush and sea mist, with restless spirits and lurking beasts among them. Relics from that age are scattered through the ruins. Ten thousand years of neglect have worn them, but traces of elven arcane craft remain, and they are dangerous in careless hands.

item:melenas-head.text: Melenas' Head. At Fel Rock, Melenas' Head marks the end of a lingering demonic threat on Teldrassil. Taken as a bounty from Lord Melenas, the satyr commander encamped there, it is proof of his death. Satyrs on Teldrassil’s new World Tree shame the night elves who guard Shadowglen and the surrounding reaches. Lord Melenas made his lair in Fel Rock’s twisted caverns, just north of the elven settlements, and rallied aggressive grell warriors to his banner. The kaldorei prize discretion when dealing with corruption so close to their heartlands. Melenas' Head is private proof that his schemes have ended before his influence could spread.

item:menethil-statuette.text: Menethil Statuette. The Menethil Statuette is a rare silvery figurine portraying the late King Terenas Menethil II as a youthful paladin with an upraised warhammer. Lost in a shipwreck off the coast of the Wetlands, it is an exceptionally scarce memorial of Lordaeron's fallen sovereign. The statuette depicts King Terenas Menethil II in his early years, portrayed as a long-haired paladin lifting a hammer toward the heavens. Terenas was notoriously humble during his reign and disliked personal monuments, meaning few statues or likenesses were ever commissioned in his honor. Following the collapse of the Kingdom of Lordaeron to the Scourge, almost all such relics were obliterated, making this surviving effigy extraordinarily valuable to the Alliance. The statuette was cargo aboard the merchant vessel Blind Princess, bound for the Alliance harbor of Menethil. When the ship came under attack by aggressive Bluegill murlocs off the marshy coast, the cargo was scattered and the statuette ended up trapped in a half-buried barrel on the shore. With local threats like the Dragonmaw orcs hovering nearby, local defenders hurried to send the retrieved icon south to Stormwind City, where Highlord Bolvar Fordragon entrusted it to the Cathedral of Light.

item:merrin-s-letter.text: Merrin's Letter. Merrin's Letter is an urgent message written by Merrin Rockweaver, an archaeologist trapped at the dig site in the Wetlands. It recounts the catastrophic overrun of their archaeological expedition by vicious raptors and assures her loved ones of her immediate survival. While excavating enormous prehistoric fossils and relics at the Whelgar's Excavation site in the Wetlands, the dwarven expedition disturbed a nest of ferocious Mottled Raptors. The beasts swarmed the trenches, slaughtering several workers and cutting off the surviving researchers from escape. Penning this note amidst the chaos, Merrin Rockweaver wrote to inform her husband Tarrel back at Menethil Harbor that while the dig lies in ruins, she, Prospector Whelgar, and Ormer Ironbraid managed to survive behind barricaded shelter.

item:middle-of-gelkak-s-key.text: Middle of Gelkak's Key. Off Darkshore, Gelkak Gyromast’s key lies in three pieces after threshadons sank his ship. Greymist murlocs took the middle fragment from the shore. Gelkak Gyromast’s winding key broke when threshadons dragged his ship beneath the waves. The gnome pirate came ashore with his belongings shattered on the rocky shoals. The specialized key was made for his mechanical first mate, but the wreck split it into three pieces scattered along the strand. Coastal beasts carried off the top and bottom. Greymist murlocs prowling the Darkshore surf took the middle piece and kept it in their camps and among the wreckage they hold.

item:milly-s-harvest.text: Milly's Harvest. In the Northshire Vineyards, Milly's grapes lie abandoned after the Defias arrive. Crates and buckets of fruit remain at risk of theft or being crushed beneath the abbey guards' boots. Milly Osworth gathers grapes in the Northshire Vineyards, where the harvest matters to local vintners and the abbey community. When armed brigands in red masks push into the fields, Milly flees to the abbey grounds. Her fresh-picked grapes remain scattered between the rows. Stormwind guards watch the valley entrance, but too few soldiers leave Northshire vulnerable. The garrison promises to drive out the Defias, while Milly fears a drawn-out fight between guards and thieves will ruin her harvest. The crates may be trampled or carried off as provisions, costing Northshire one of its few peaceful harvests.

item:miners-gear.text: Miners' Gear. Miners' Gear consists of sturdy dwarven picks, shovels, and excavation tools stored within the Silver Stream Mine. Following an infestation of vermin, the Miners' League tasked adventurers with retrieving these valuable implements before local guards launched an assault. When the Silver Stream Mine in northern Loch Modan ran out of ore, the Miners' League repurposed the quiet tunnels into a subterranean storage depot for mining equipment. Unfortunately, tunnel-dwelling kobolds quickly overrun the complex, making off with the stored goods and nesting among the crates. Fearing the valuable dwarven gear would either be wrecked in an all-out assault by the Mountaineers or ruined by the scavengers, the league relies on bold adventurers to venture inside and haul the crates back to safety.

item:miners-union-card.text: Miners' Union Card. A Miners' Union Card is an identification credential once carried by laborers working the rich subterranean veins beneath Moonbrook. Following a catastrophic cave-in that sealed a wing of the tunnels, these tokens now remain on the restless skeletal corpses wandering the dark drifts. Long before the Defias Brotherhood took absolute control over Moonbrook, laborers toiled underground under the banner of the miners' guild, extracting valuable ore for the kingdom. That ended in disaster when a severe tunnel collapse crushed a major shaft, trapping and killing dozens of workers beneath tons of rock. Rather than finding a quiet grave, those who perished rose again as skeletal miners, excavators, and dynamiters. The union cards clutched in their bony pockets are the sole surviving proof of their identities, sought out by surviving colleagues in Stormwind hoping to bring closure to grieving families.

item:minshina-s-skull.text: Minshina's Skull. On the Echo Isles, Minshina's Skull holds the bound soul of Minshina, a Darkspear troll and brother of Master Gadrin. Zalazane trapped him there after driving the tribe from the isles, and uses the skull to fuel dark rituals. Minshina was captured and slain when Zalazane seized the Echo Isles and drove out the Darkspear. The traitorous witch doctor bound his victim's soul to Minshina's severed skull instead of letting him pass into death. The skull lies within a circle of power on the southernmost isle, tethering Minshina to Zalazane's magic. Tormented by dreams of his brother calling to him, Master Gadrin seeks brave travelers to enter the occupied islands, reclaim the skull, and break Zalazane's hold over Minshina's spirit.

item:mirror-lake-water-sample.text: Mirror Lake Water Sample. At Mirror Lake in Elwynn Forest, a flask of water is gathered for Jennea Cannon in Stormwind. The mages will test it for signs of altered arcane currents in local water. Jennea Cannon sends promising apprentices to collect water from Mirror Lake. The lake lies just southwest of the Stormwind Gate, and they fill a specially prepared flask at the base of its waterfall. The Wizard's Sanctum in Stormwind is concerned that the world's mystic channels remain unsettled after catastrophic conflicts. Its mages will examine the sample for stray magical taint in the waterways used by people nearby.

item:mist-veil-s-lockbox.text: Mist Veil's Lockbox. Off Darkshore, Mist Veil's Lockbox lies in the sunken night elven vessel. It holds the captain's log and personal effects, lost when coastal murlocs ambushed and sank the ship. The night elven vessel Mist Veil sank while sailing toward Auberdine. Coastal murlocs ambushed it alongside its sister ship, the Silver Dawning, and overwhelmed both vessels. The captain perished in the attack. Their logbook and personal belongings remain sealed in the lockbox in the flooded hold, surrounded by murlocs. Surviving sailors reached Auberdine, but the loss of their vessel and commander still grieves them. Gorbold Steelhand seeks Mist Veil's Lockbox so the captain's final effects can be honored and laid to rest. Recovering it from the flooded wreck may bring some solace to the survivors on the mainland.

item:mo-grosh-crystal.text: Mo'grosh Crystal. Mo'grosh Crystals are rare mineral formations mined and hoarded by the Mo'grosh ogres in northeastern Loch Modan. Prized for their unusual alchemical properties, they serve as a vital component in neutralizing Dark Iron demolition materials. Tucked away in the crags of northeastern Loch Modan, the Mo'grosh ogres excavate these distinctive crystals from their stronghold. Though the brute-strength ogres rarely specialize in delicate metallurgy, Mo'grosh Crystals are prized treasures among their clan, carried by common enforcers, mystic shamans, and their towering leaders alike. The crystals are relatively uncommon, making them a heavily guarded possession within the Mo'grosh Stronghold.

item:modr-fragment.text: Modr Fragment. The Modr Fragment is one of four missing pieces broken off from the ancient Goaz Stone, a relic unearthed in the Wetlands. Discovered amid relics and loose earth within the Whelgar Excavation Site, it bears ancient Titan script vital to assembling a forgotten prophecy. Before vicious raptors drove the Explorers' League from their dig in the Wetlands, Prospector Whelgar uncovered the Goaz Stone—a massive tablet inscribed with ancient Titan markings. Its translated text abruptly broke off across four distinct gaps, obscuring warnings of a divine plan and a doomed prophecy. The Modr Fragment is one of those four lost pieces, left behind among ancient relics and overturned soil when the diggers were forced to flee for their lives.

item:moldy-tome.text: Moldy Tome. The Moldy Tome is a water-damaged, salvaged remnant containing half of the original Tome of the Cabal. Lost in a shipwreck off the coast of Hillsbrad Foothills, it holds dark esoteric rituals coveted by warlocks seeking to master demonic summonings. The Tome of the Cabal was a singular, irreplaceable treatise on dark arts once held within the kingdom of Lordaeron. At some point in its murky history, the grimoire was ruthlessly vandalized and split in two. The portion now designated as the Moldy Tome was being transported south by ship toward Menethil Harbor and Ironforge. The vessel never reached its destination, succumbing to the treacherous waters west of Southshore. Swept ashore south of Azurelode Mine, the surviving half lay ruined by damp and surf amidst the scavenging murlocs that stalk the Hillsbrad coast.

item:moonpetal-lily.text: Moonpetal Lily. Moonpetal Lilies are large, luminous flora native to Teldrassil that flourish around freshwater pools. Renowned for their potent restorative qualities, their petals are prized as key ingredients in natural remedies and healing draughts. Moonpetal Lilies grow exclusively along the moist banks of freshwater pools and ponds, particularly favored along the northwestern side of Aldrassil in Shadowglen. Like much of the plant life flourishing atop the newly grown World Tree, they absorb the unique essence of Teldrassil's sheltered groves. Their broad petals are gentle and radiant, easily spotted hugging the tranquil water's edge where natural moisture allows them to thrive. Night elf healers and herbalists value the Moonpetal Lily for its extraordinary healing properties. When combined with other forest flora, such as Hyacinth Mushrooms, the lily acts as a powerful soothing and stabilizing agent. This restorative quality makes it an essential component when brewing antidotes to counteract lethal toxins, notably the virulent venom produced by the Webwood spiders lurking within Shadowthread Cave.

item:moonstalker-fang.text: Moonstalker Fang. Near Auberdine, travelers gather Moonstalker Fangs for Wizbang Cranktoggle's sampling devices. The teeth come from the moonstalkers of Darkshore. Moonstalker Fangs come from saber cats that hunt along Darkshore’s forest fringes. Their long teeth can shear flesh and bone. Wizbang Cranktoggle, an eccentric gnome tinkerer, uses them in a different way. North of Auberdine, near the bridge, Buzzbox 323 crushes the durable fangs to dust for his ecological surveys.

item:moonwell-water-tube.text: Moonwell Water Tube. At Auberdine, water from the moonwell carries purifying nature magic. The vial is used to test a mysterious red crystal set among Darkshore’s eastern ridges. Water from Auberdine’s moonwell fills the tube. The sacred pool is tied to Elune and holds restorative, purifying magic. Even a small amount can be used against corruption or to test strange mystical forces.

item:mossy-tumor.text: Mossy Tumor. Around Wellspring Lake, mossy tumors mark Teldrassil's spreading corruption. Carved from the bark and flesh of corrupted timberlings, these poisonous growths show the malevolence taking hold in the young World Tree. Teldrassil's timberlings were made to nurture and tend the great tree's boughs, but many have grown hostile and diseased. Mossy tumors are signs of that sickness made flesh. Thick with toxins, they spread across the Mire Beasts, Tramplers, and Elder Timberlings around Wellspring Lake. Rellian Greenspyre and the keepers in Darnassus send travelers to cut away the tumors and burn them thoroughly, so their poison cannot take deeper root in the island's soil.

item:mountain-lion-blood.text: Mountain Lion Blood. Mountain Lion Blood is a reagent collected from the prowling predators of the Hillsbrad Foothills and the snowy slopes of Alterac. Apothecary Lydon of Tarren Mill seeks this fresh blood to formulate the Royal Apothecary Society's dreaded Elixir of Pain. The highlands and foothills flanking Hillsbrad and Alterac are prowled by feral and starving mountain lions. While ordinary hunters seek these predators for their pelts and claws, the Forsaken of the Royal Apothecary Society find value in what pumps through their veins. Fresh mountain lion blood possesses specific biological properties that Apothecary Lydon in Tarren Mill believes will serve as the base for a potent new toxic brew designed to bring misery to the living. Apothecary Lydon's experiments in Tarren Mill contribute directly to the Royal Apothecary Society's overarching mandate: perfecting the Forsaken's New Plague. By harvesting the blood of vigorous wild beasts, Lydon seeks to refine a concoction he calls the Elixir of Pain, testing how potent local organic compounds can be weaponized against the enemies of the Dark Lady.

item:mudsnout-blossom.text: Mudsnout Blossom. Mudsnout Blossoms are pungent, toxic fungal growths found sprouting in Nethander Stead in the Hillsbrad Foothills. Guarded by local gnolls and harvested by the Royal Apothecary Society, these foul mushrooms are used in Apothecary Lydon's elixir research. Despite their floral name, Mudsnout Blossoms are actually large, foul-smelling mushrooms that flourish primarily in the soiled dirt of Nethander Stead, south of Tarren Mill. They grow amidst the camps of the local Mudsnout gnolls, who defend the territory fiercely. To living organisms, the spores and flesh of the mushroom act as a virulent poison, causing agony and rapid biological deterioration.

item:mudsnout-composite.text: Mudsnout Composite. Mudsnout Composite is an alchemical paste prepared by Apothecary Lydon in Tarren Mill from harvested Mudsnout Blossoms. It serves as an essential base ingredient carried to the Undercity for the Royal Apothecary Society's research into a new plague. Crafted in the field by Apothecary Lydon, this fine composite is derived directly from Mudsnout Blossoms gathered in the Hillsbrad Foothills. While noxious on its own, the mash requires a specialized colloid of decay—concocted by Master Apothecary Faranell himself—to activate its more lethal qualities. Once bound, the mixture forms a key chemical component in the development of the Dark Lady's Elixir of Agony.

item:mudsnout-mixture.text: Mudsnout Mixture. Mudsnout Mixture is a toxic alchemical base concocted by Master Apothecary Faranell in the Undercity. Created by blending a mudsnout composite with an alchemical colloid of decay, it serves as the foundation for the Royal Apothecary Society's deadly Elixir of Agony. When Apothecary Lydon in Tarren Mill seeks to craft a virulent new biological weapon, he sends a base composite of Mudsnout Blossoms, toxic mushrooms from the gnoll-held Nethander Stead, north to the Undercity. Impressed by the composite's potential, Master Apothecary Faranell introduces his own colloid of decay into the blend, producing the volatile Mudsnout Mixture. The solution stabilizes the mushroom compound while readying its virulent properties for further catalytic refinement back in the foothills.

item:murloc-head.text: Murloc Head. Murloc Heads are grim trophies severed from the amphibious creatures prowling the Western Strand in Hillsbrad Foothills. Lieutenant Farren Orinelle of Southshore requires them as physical proof of culled threats to satisfy his superior, Marshal Redpath. Southshore faces dangers from all directions, but the aggressive murlocs clustering along the Western Strand are an immediate menace to local fishermen and coastal travelers. Although Alliance adventurers frequently sweep the beaches to cull the creatures, Marshal Marcus Redpath demands undeniable verification before signing off on defensive reports. To humor the bureaucracy, Lieutenant Farren Orinelle relies on hired fighters to haul in cold, dripping murloc heads—an unpleasant task Farren himself finds entirely repulsive, especially given how thoroughly the sight has spoiled his appetite for Southshore's local seafood.

item:musquash-root.text: Musquash Root. Beneath the Stonewrought Dam, Musquash Root grows in the Wetlands. The rare root is hard to gather, and a hidden coven beneath Stormwind needs it for a brew. Musquash Root grows in the damp ground beneath the Stonewrought Dam's falls. The mist and secluded setting make it hard to gather. Few herbalists seek it, but practitioners of the darker arts prize its chemical and alchemical properties.

item:mysterious-fossil.text: Mysterious Fossil. Along Darkshore's coast, Prospector Remtravel uncovers the Mysterious Fossil. The Explorers' League sends it across the sea for study. Prospector Remtravel uncovers an unusual fossil while working along Darkshore's wild coast. He arranges for dwarven scholars to receive it instead of leaving it in the wilderness. In Darnassus, Chief Archaeologist Greywhisker sees an extraordinary find among the stones of Kalimdor.

item:nak-s-skull.text: Nak's Skull. In the southern Barrens, Nak leads Razormane warbands against the Horde. His skull proves his defeat and gives Mangletooth a means to avenge betrayal by his former kin. Nak, Kuz, and Lok Orcbane lead raids from Razorfen Kraul across the Barrens. Their warbands strike Horde settlements and roads, while defenders at the Crossroads do not know the three commanders are planning attacks beyond ordinary tribal skirmishing. At Camp Taurajo, the captive Razormane Mangletooth has been left to die in a cage by his own people. He now seeks revenge against those former brethren. Mangletooth demands proof that Nak and his companions are dead: their severed skulls, delivered by Horde adventurers. He means to use that proof to break the southern raiding parties.

item:nek-rosh-s-head.text: Nek'rosh's Head. Nek'rosh's Head is the gruesome proof of the downfall of Chieftain Nek'rosh, leader of the Dragonmaw clan in the Wetlands. Procured by Alliance adventurers, this trophy is delivered to Captain Stoutfist to confirm that the orcish threat menacing Menethil Harbor has been shattered. The Dragonmaw clan poses a persistent danger across the marshlands, massing forces and siege weapons against the Alliance port of Menethil Harbor. After burning their catapults, the defense of the port hinges on slaying Chieftain Nek'rosh himself. Severing his head provides undeniable proof to Captain Stoutfist and the Ironforge authorities that the warlord's grip over the Wetlands is broken.

item:neru-fragment.text: Neru Fragment. The Neru Fragment is one of four ancient carved stone pieces belonging to the Goaz Stone, a relic discovered in the Whelgar's Excavation site within the Wetlands. Unearthed from the disturbed earth, it holds a segment of ancient Titan script detailing the primeval history of Azeroth. Discovered by the dwarven archaeological expedition led by Prospector Whelgar, the Goaz Stone broke apart into four distinct remnants: the Ados, Modr, Golm, and Neru fragments. When raptors overrun the dig site, work ground to a halt, leaving the Neru Fragment buried beneath loose soil amid the aggressive beasts. Recovering this fragment is crucial for reassembling the tablet, allowing dwarven scholars to decipher a forgotten record whose surviving words mention a divine plan and a doomed prophecy.

item:nessa-s-collection.text: Nessa's Collection. At Rut'theran Village, fish bones and scales gathered from nearby waters are prepared for study by Laird in Auberdine. Nessa's Collection shows the great size of aquatic life around Teldrassil's roots. Nessa Shadowsong lives in Rut'theran Village at Teldrassil's base, where she gathered fish bones and scales to compare island sea life with that of mainland Kalimdor. Catches from the waters around the Great Tree grow to striking size. Nessa sent physical proof across the sea to Laird, a fish merchant along Auberdine's docks. The parcel travels through Vesprystus, Rut'theran's hippogryph master, and offers practical evidence of Teldrassil's growing vitality. In Darkshore, Laird finds that the specimens far outsize their mainland counterparts. The collection holds jawbones nearly twice the size of those from fish native to the Darkshore coast, and scales as large as a clenched fist. For coastal night elves, the package offers a clear look at how greatly the waters around Teldrassil differ from northern Kalimdor's somber shores.

item:nether-gem.text: Nether Gem. The Nether Gem is an enchanted arcane stone entrusted by the reclusive necromancer Gunther Arcanus. Imbued with magical power, it acts as a long-distance conduit allowing Gunther to manifest an arcane projection and communicate directly with his old associate, Bethor Iceshard, in the Undercity. Forged or enchanted by Gunther Arcanus on his solitary island in Brightwater Lake, the Nether Gem serves as a mystical link across Tirisfal Glades. Gunther, having broken free from the Lich King's control through his own sheer willpower, long avoided the fledgling Forsaken nation out of suspicion. After receiving his lost spellbook, he entrusts the gem to an emissary as a gesture of goodwill. Once brought to Bethor Iceshard atop the Magic Quarter in the Undercity, the stone channels Gunther's magical visage directly before the Mage Guild leader, opening the path for the solitary mage to align with Lady Sylvanas and the Forsaken.

item:ng-5.text: NG-5. NG-5 is the shorthand designation for Nitromirglyceronium, a notoriously volatile chemical compound. Procured for the gnome tinkerer Gaxim Rustfizzle in the Stonetalon Mountains, it serves as the essential catalyst for his explosive engineering schemes. Known formally as Nitromirglyceronium, NG-5 is an exceptionally hazardous chemical solution handled only with extreme caution—or reckless gnomish enthusiasm. Gaxim Rustfizzle, an operative stationed in the Stonetalon Mountains, requires the substance as a critical ignition compound. According to Gaxim, NG-5 provides the exact reaction necessary to detonate entire wagons loaded with dynamite, orchestrating a massive explosion meant to serve as a chaotic distraction against his adversaries in the region.

item:nida-s-necklace.text: Hilary's Necklace. Hilary's Necklace is a cherished childhood keepsake lost beneath the surface of Lake Everstill in the Redridge Mountains. Given to young Hilary by her father, the trinket slipped into the murky waters while the children of Lakeshire were out fishing along the docks. While fishing along the shoreline of Lakeshire with her friend Shawn, young Hilary accidentally dropped her treasured necklace into Lake Everstill. The heirloom holds immense sentimental value, having been a gift from her father. Fear of the fierce beasts and aggressive murlocs inhabiting the depths keeps the local children safely on the docks, leaving the necklace sunken and buried in the silt of the lakebed until an adventurer is willing to dive into the murky water to recover it.

item:nightmare-shard.text: Nightmare Shard. The Nightmare Shard is a crystalline relic handed to couriers by Falla Sagewind after she examines a tainted glowing shard recovered from the Wailing Caverns. Containing the pure, disturbed essence of the Emerald Dream, it carries a troubling vision that prompts immediate warning and secrecy among senior druids in Darnassus and Thunder Bluff. When Falla Sagewind inspects the mysterious glowing shard unearthed deep within the Wailing Caverns, she realizes its energy is far darker than anticipated. Rather than mirroring the serene vitality of the Emerald Dream, the fragment reflects a twisting, unnatural affliction—a waking nightmare. Fearful of what its presence implies, she binds this tainted essence into the Nightmare Shard and commands that it be ferried straight to elder leaders of the Cenarion Circle without delay.

item:nightsaber-fang.text: Nightsaber Fang. In Teldrassil, hunters take fangs from the nightsabers prowling the forest. Woodland residents also seek these teeth as reagents. Nightsabers hunt beneath Teldrassil’s canopy, among the deadliest natural predators of northern Kalimdor. Night elves revere them for their agility, ferocity, and deep spiritual bond with Elune. A hunter who kills one can take its sharp fangs as proof of skill. Some figures in the forest seek those fangs for darker rites.

item:nissa-s-remains.text: Nissa's Remains. Nissa's Remains are the recovered earthly remnants of Nissa Agamand, a noblewoman of the once-wealthy Agamand dynasty in northern Tirisfal Glades. Slain and raised as mindless servants of the Scourge during the Third War, she and her family are now hunted down by former laborers seeking vengeance. Before the Third War, the Agamand family stood as the wealthiest and most influential dynasty in Tirisfal Glades, operating prosperous mills across the northern hills. When the Plague of Undeath crept across Lordaeron, the family patriarchs stubbornly refused to evacuate. Instead, they fortified their estates and convinced their retainers and laborers to stand their ground. That arrogance cost everyone their lives. The Agamands fell to the Scourge, rising not with their proud independence intact, but as shambling, mindless thralls bound to the Lich King's will. In the town of Brill, survivors who later broke free under Queen Sylvanas Windrunner have not forgotten the family's fatal pride. Coleman Farthing, a former laborer in the Agamand mills, holds a bitter grudge against his former masters for luring their workers into the jaws of undeath. He charges adventurers with putting down the risen Agamands and retrieving their physical remains, such as Nissa's. For Farthing and others among the Forsaken, burning or destroying these relics offers a grim sense of final closure and spiteful revenge.

item:nitroglycerin.text: Nitroglycerin. At Bael Modan, Nitroglycerin helps the dwarves drive their excavation through tauren lands. Their soldiers and officers carry the volatile chemical, which can also be used against the fortress. Bael Modan's dwarves dig into the ancestral lands of the Stonespire tauren with heavy drillers and volatile chemicals. At the excavation site and its fortified keep, they keep nitroglycerin close to blast deep holes and break apart hills. Soldiers and officers, including Lord Cyrik Blackforge, carry vials of the fluid as the digging continues.

item:nondescript-letter.text: Nondescript Letter. The Nondescript Letter is a sealed, unmarked missive entrusted to newly awakened Forsaken leaving Deathknell. Handed over by Calvin Montague under the guise of an errand, it directs the bearer down the road to Innkeeper Renee at the Gallows' End Tavern in Brill. Newly arisen Forsaken looking to venture beyond Deathknell are approached by Calvin Montague, a shifty rogue lingering near the village perimeter. Claiming to be weary from fighting mindless zombies and arachnids, Calvin asks travelers to carry a plain, unmarked envelope along the eastward road to Brill. Addressed casually to an innkeeper named Renee, the letter serves as an excuse to push travelers out of the valley and toward the Gallows' End Tavern, though Calvin's promises of rich compensation ring hollow from the start.

item:nori-s-mug.text: Nori's Mug. Nori's Mug is the personal drinking vessel of Nori Pridedrift, used to deliver scalding mornbrew across the frigid drifts of Dun Morogh. After delivering a warm drink to stave off the biting alpine chill, travelers are tasked with returning the empty cup to its thrifty owner. In the freezing mountain passes of Dun Morogh, a piping hot tankard of mornbrew is one of the few comforts capable of cutting through the bitter cold. Nori Pridedrift entrusts his mug to travelers delivering a fresh, steaming pour to Durnan Furcutter in Anvilmar. Once drained, the sturdy vessel must make the trek back. As Nori notes, mugs do not grow on trees, and keeping track of hard-wearing dwarven dishware is essential business when hospitality meets snowy wilderness.

item:notched-rib.text: Notched Rib. A Notched Rib is a bone trophy harvested from the ranks of mindless undead wandering Tirisfal Glades. Deathguard Dillinger in Brill collects these scarred remains as proof of efforts to break the Scourge's foothold at the Agamand Mills. The Scourge forces massing across the northern fields of Tirisfal Glades consist of reanimated skeletons clad in ruined armor. Among their ranks, Cracked Skull Soldiers and Rattlecage Soldiers throw themselves against any living or free-willed being they encounter. Slicing through their brittle frames leaves their bone structure pitted and scored. To ensure that Forsaken scouts and volunteers actually cull these mindless intruders rather than merely observing them, the Deathguards demand tangible evidence. A notched, battle-marked rib serves as unmistakable proof that another of the Lich King's thralls has been shattered. The Agamand Mills represent a critical strategic position northwest of Brill. Should the Scourge firmly entrench themselves among the ruined farmsteads and windmills, they would possess a direct staging ground to launch assaults deep into the heart of Tirisfal. Deathguard Dillinger monitors the roads leading north, dispatching champions to crush the skeleton cohorts before they can consolidate. Piles of notched ribs returned to Brill demonstrate that the Forsaken lines are holding, slowly grinding down the Scourge vanguard bone by bone.

item:nugget-slug.text: Nugget Slug. Nugget slugs are specialized 17.5-gauge mechanical fasteners used in industrial engineering. Stockpiled in tool buckets by the Venture Company at the Sludge Fen, they are coveted by tinkerers attempting to repair volatile machinery. Nugget slugs are heavy-duty metallic fasteners manufactured for demanding industrial assemblies. Specifically sized at 17.5 gauge, these components are an essential part of the heavy equipment deployed across Venture Company extraction sites. While useless as ordinary trade goods, they are indispensable to tinkerers dealing with customized goblin hardware.

item:ogre-s-monocle.text: Ogre's Monocle. The Ogre's Monocle is an oversized eyeglass worn by Zzarc'Vul, an ogre dwelling in southern Duskwood's Vul'Gol Ogre Mound. Its immense glass lens provides the exact dimensions needed by Viktori Prism'Antras in Darkshire to assemble an elaborate stargazing telescope. While ogres are rarely renowned for refined scholarship, Zzarc'Vul somehow came into possession of an enormous monocle tailored to his massive stature. When the Darkshire resident Viktori Prism'Antras set out to build a stargazing instrument using blueprints drafted by the gnome engineer Cog, he found standard lenses far too small. Zzarc'Vul's eyewear proved to be the only piece of polished glass in the region with the curvature and size necessary to focus light through the completed device. Acquiring the monocle requires braving the Vul'Gol Ogre Mound in the shadow of southern Duskwood. Zzarc'Vul resides among his brute brethren, showing little inclination to voluntarily part with his distinctive accessory. Claiming the lens means defeating the brute on his own territory before returning the glass to Darkshire so Viktori can finally turn his gaze to the night skies.

item:okra.text: Okra. In Westfall, Okra grows in the plots at Saldean's Farm. Homesteaders prize the crop, and it thickens the stews that feed them. Saldean's Farm still yields vegetables while much of Westfall lies fallow under threat from Defias outlaws and rogue harvest golem attacks. Okra grows in the tilled plots around the farm. The crop persists through the harsh conditions, nourishing local homesteaders when trade and supplies from Stormwind run dry. Salma Saldean's famous Westfall Stew depends on okra. She combines sliced pods with whatever meat settlers can hunt across the dusty plains, including vulture flesh, goretusk snouts, and coastal murloc eyes. The pods break down in the heat, thickening thin broth into a filling, restorative meal. For settlers clinging to their homesteads, fresh okra turns sparse scavenging into a hot supper.

item:ordanus-head.text: Ordanus' Head. Ordanus' Head is the grisly trophy taken from Keeper Ordanus at Raynewood Retreat in Ashenvale. Claimed on behalf of the blood elf magi Braelyn Firehand, it serves as undeniable proof that one of Cenarius's eldest sons has fallen to arcane vengeance. Keeper Ordanus was an ancient keeper of the grove, one of the elder scions of the forest god Cenarius. When Braelyn Firehand climbed the heights of Stonetalon Mountains on orders from her master, she sought to end the druids' stifling of magic at the peak and exact vengeance on Ordanus. However, the keeper was spirited away to the heart of Ashenvale before she could strike. Using arcane scrying to peer through the forest canopy, Firehand located his sanctuary in the boughs of Raynewood Retreat, demanding his severed head as proof that the wild demigod's arrogance had finally been answered.

item:orendil-s-cure.text: Orendil's Cure. Orendil's Cure is a medicinal draught concocted by the herbalist Orendil Broadleaf in northern Ashenvale. Created using the rare herb Bathran's Hair, it is meant to treat the mysterious, deathly sickness afflicting Relara Whitemoon in Astranaar. When young Relara Whitemoon fell deathly ill in Astranaar, conventional remedies proved useless against her ailment. Her desperate father, Pelturas Whitemoon, turned to Orendil Broadleaf, a hermit and master of natural medicine dwelling along the northern reaches of Ashenvale. Utilizing bundles of the rare plant Bathran's Hair harvested from the haunted ruins of Bathran's Haunt, Orendil brewed this tailored concoction. The arrival of the vial gives Pelturas hope where before he had little, though the cure only slows the disease, and Pelturas must turn to the further remedies Orendil suggested.

item:oslow-s-toolbox.text: Oslow's Toolbox. Oslow's Toolbox contains the vital construction tools needed by Foreman Oslow in Lakeshire. En route from Goldshire, the supplies were ferried across Lake Everstill only to be sunk by an orcish catapult bombardment. Maintaining the defenses and infrastructure of Lakeshire is a grueling challenge, particularly with the Blackrock orcs besieging the Redridge Mountains. Foreman Oslow ordered a vital set of construction tools brought in from Goldshire. Because the main bridge leading into Lakeshire had been destroyed by enemy action, the shipment had to be loaded into a rowboat to cross Lake Everstill. The crossing was abruptly cut short when Blackrock forces struck the vessel with a catapult blast, plunging the boat and Oslow's heavy chest straight down into the murloc-infested depths.

item:osric-s-crate.text: Osric's Crate. At Sentinel Hill, Osric's Crate brings armor from Stormwind to the People's Militia. The defenders face the Defias Brotherhood and marauding gnolls without the Stormwind army. Westfall faces the Defias Brotherhood and marauding gnolls, while the Stormwind army remains absent. At Sentinel Hill, the People's Militia must make do without the crown's formal support. Osric's Crate holds freshly made armor from the capital, sent to Quartermaster Lewis to distribute among the volunteer fighters. Gryphons carry the crate from Dungar Longdrink's roost in Stormwind's Trade District to Thor at Sentinel Hill. The flight avoids the dangerous roads through Elwynn Forest and across the Westfall border, where bandits may ambush travelers. Gryphons help keep frontier garrisons supplied during wartime.

item:package-of-empty-ooze-containers.text: Package of Empty Ooze Containers. This package is a kit of specialized, empty specimen jars supplied by the gnome researcher Laris Geardawdle in Ironforge. Intended for dangerous field sampling in the blighted forests of Felwood, it contains jars designed to safely hold tainted and cursed ooze extracts without dissolving. Containing a dozen empty jars—split between containers meant for cursed and tainted oozes—this kit was assembled by Laris Geardawdle for intrepid travelers heading out to Felwood. Because raw ooze specimens are notoriously caustic and prone to digesting ordinary luggage, sturdy, sealed glass is essential for transporting the acidic residues across continents back to the tinker's workbench in Ironforge. Geardawdle's interest in ooze is far from a simple eccentric hobby. Noticing that Forsaken researchers from the Royal Apothecary Society routinely harvest these bizarre organisms across Azeroth, he suspects oozes may hold profound secrets about the world's origin. Geardawdle theorizes that slimes might be primordial secretions connected to the planet's very creation, and he relies on field agents using this kit to collect the evidence he needs to win acclaim within the Explorers' League.

item:painted-gnoll-armband.text: Painted Gnoll Armband. At Westbrook Garrison, Painted Gnoll Armbands prove that Riverpaw gnolls have been slain. The marked bands come from packs pressing against Elwynn Forest's western border. Riverpaw warriors and scavengers wear rough armbands painted with crude tribal patterns. The bands come from gnolls along Elwynn Forest's wilderness borders. For Stormwind's defenders, the packs pose a growing threat near Stone Cairn Lake and in the woods south of Westbrook Garrison. Stormwind's Army is stretched thin across the kingdom, leaving Westbrook Garrison hard pressed to secure the western border. Deputy Rainer offers a standing bounty for slaying Riverpaw outrunners and runts. Their painted armbands prove the kills, helping the deputies count the bounties and thin the packs near nearby farmlands.

item:panther-cage-key.text: Panther Cage Key. The Panther Cage Key is a small metal key held by Wizlo Bearingshiner at Whitereach Post. It unlocks a reinforced cage holding an enraged, captive predator within the wreckage of an ambushed caravan in Thousand Needles. When a traveling caravan was attacked and ransacked by centaur raiders north of Whitereach Post, the goblin tinker Wizlo Bearingshiner barely escaped with his life. Amid the ruins of wagons and plundered cargo, the marauders left one thing entirely untouched: a sturdy cage housing a ferocious, rare panther. Around the predator's neck hung Wizlo's prized invention, a hypercapacitor gizmo. Unwilling to approach the snarling beast, the centaur gave the cage a wide berth, leaving Wizlo's key as the only way to open the door and retrieve the device.

item:parker-s-lunch.text: Parker's Lunch. Parker's Lunch is a freshly prepared meal packed by Darcy in Lakeshire. Intended for Guard Parker on patrol, it offers a simple glimpse into the daily bonds and modest comforts of Redridge's defenders. While Redridge Mountains reels under attacks from gnolls and Blackrock orcs, the small gestures of daily life persist. Darcy, a waitress at the inn in Lakeshire, packs this wholesome meal for Guard Parker, who patrols the exposed road leading south toward Duskwood. Redridge's garrison is stretched thin and isolated from Stormwind's aid, leaving individual guards to maintain long, lonely watches. Delivering this bundle not only keeps a sentry fed, but also sparks an enduring, bashful courtship between the two townspeople.

item:partially-filled-vessel.text: Partially Filled Vessel. Tenaron Stormgrip gives young night elf initiates the Partially Filled Vessel in Aldrassil. It carries blessed moonwell water from Shadowglen toward Dolanaar. Young kaldorei initiates gather blessed water from Shadowglen’s secluded moonwell. In Aldrassil, Tenaron Stormgrip pours a sample into the vessel for its journey across Teldrassil. More water from the tree’s moonwells must be gathered to tend to the island’s health. Carry the vessel south through the valley gates, then follow the cobblestone roads west to Dolanaar. The journey takes a young adventurer beyond Shadowglen’s protected nursery and into Teldrassil’s wider wilds. At Dolanaar’s central moonwell, Corithras Moonrage takes the vessel and directs the next part of the ritual.

item:pendant-of-shadow.text: Pendant of Shadow. The Pendant of Shadow is a dark talisman worn by the renegade warlock Morganth atop the Tower of Ilgalar in the Redridge Mountains. Brought to the mage Theocritus at the Tower of Azora, it serves as undeniable proof that the rogue spellcaster has been eliminated before his sinister ambitions could bear fruit. Held by the rogue warlock Morganth within his perch at the Tower of Ilgalar, the Pendant of Shadow is steeped in dark sorcery. Morganth sought to unravel the mysteries of the Scythe of Elune, an ancient relic of immense and volatile power. Fearing the havoc the warlock could unleash upon the Redridge Mountains and the kingdom of Stormwind, the mage Theocritus tasked adventurers with infiltrating Ilgalar, ending Morganth's plotting, and wresting the talisman from his grasp as proof of his demise.

item:pendant-of-the-sea-lion.text: Pendant of the Sea Lion. The Pendant of the Sea Lion is a sacred druidic talisman representing the union of aquatic agility and endurance. Assembled at the Shrine of Remulos in Moonglade, it serves as proof that an initiate is ready to master their aquatic form. To claim the aquatic aspect of the sea lion, a druid must prove mastery over the water's greatest hazards. The pendant is created by recovering two distinct halves: one embodying the agility needed to slip past aquatic predators, and the other granting the endurance required to withstand prolonged submersion. Brought before the Shrine of Remulos in Moonglade, the two pieces are joined into a single whole. Once forged, the completed pendant is brought before elder mentors—such as Turak Runetotem on the towering rises of Thunder Bluff or Mathrengyl Bearwalker in Darnassus. The talisman provides undeniable proof of the initiate's trials under Dendrite Starblaze, permitting the elders to bestow the secrets of shifting into an aquatic form.

item:perenolde-tiara.text: Perenolde Tiara. In the ruins of Alterac, an emerald-studded heirloom of the Perenolde family has turned up again. Dwarven craftsmen of Ironforge made it, and collectors in Stormwind now seek it. The Perenolde family ruled Alterac before the kingdom fell during the Second War. Their treasures included a delicate tiara, made by master jewelers in Ironforge and set with brilliant emeralds. After King Aiden Perenolde’s treachery brought Alterac to ruin, the tiara vanished amid the devastation of the high crags. Grel'borg the Miser, an ogre mage, unearthed the tiara while searching Alterac’s ruins for abandoned wealth. Word of the surviving relic reached Count Remington Ridgewell, a wealthy noble in Stormwind who collects famous relics for his family museum. Now the count seeks to take the tiara from the ogre.

item:phial-of-scrying.text: Phial of Scrying. In Darkshore, scouts use the Phial of Scrying to reach Onu from afar. The ancient of lore provides the enchanted vessel, which calls forth a bowl for scrying across corrupted woodlands. The Phial of Scrying carries mystical waters that form a temporary bowl on the ground. Scouts investigating deep within Darkshore use it for long-distance divination. From perilous places such as the Master's Glaive, they can speak directly with Onu instead of returning to his grove.

item:piece-of-krom-zar-s-banner.text: Piece of Krom'zar's Banner. At Regthar Deathgate's bunker west of the Crossroads, a torn banner marks the broken assault. Warlord Krom'zar led the Kolkar retaliatory force from Desolace. Warlord Krom'zar led a warband east from Desolace to strike back. Kolkar chieftains across the Barrens had fallen, and the furious centaurs attacked the defensive bunkers west of the Crossroads. A strip cut from Krom'zar's fallen standard gives Regthar Deathgate proof that the assault was crushed and the southern trade routes were preserved for the Horde.

item:plainstrider-beak.text: Plainstrider Beak. Across the Barrens, hunters bring Plainstrider Beaks back to the Crossroads. Huntmasters use them as proof that birds threatening local provisions have been culled. Plainstriders forage around the Crossroads and threaten its supplies. Greater, fleeting, and ornery plainstriders roam the surrounding savannah. Sergra Darkthorn asks arriving hunters to bring back their beaks as proof that the flocks have been culled away from supply lines and storehouses.

item:plainstrider-feather.text: Plainstrider Feather. Plucked from the swift birds roaming the plains of Mulgore, Plainstrider Feathers are essential materials gathered by young hunters on Red Cloud Mesa. The tauren of Camp Narache use them primarily for crafting clothing and tribal adornments, while honoring the creatures that provide for the village. On Red Cloud Mesa, young tauren learn early that survival relies on keen tracking and hunting. Plainstriders run wild across the grassy plateau, offering both sustenance and practical materials. Plucking their sturdy feathers allows the camp to craft traditional garments and gear. Presenting these feathers alongside fresh meat to Grull Hawkwind demonstrates respect for the tribe's needs and serves as the very first test toward being recognized by Chief Hawkwind and welcomed in Thunder Bluff.

item:plainstrider-kidney.text: Plainstrider Kidney. Across the Barrens, hunters harvest Plainstrider Kidney for Kalimdor's unusual brewing traditions. The organ is unappetizing to most travelers, yet essential to an exotic brew. The vast, arid plains of the Barrens are home to tall, flightless plainstriders. Hunters often take their feathers and meat for tools and simple rations, while Brewmaster Drohn in Ratchet seeks their internal organs for another purpose. Drohn says plainstrider kidneys are needed to recreate Chen Stormstout's legendary potent ale. He claims the kidneys give the brew a unique kick, in a tradition passed down through an unconventional line of brewmasters.

item:plainstrider-meat.text: Plainstrider Meat. Plainstrider Meat is freshly harvested game taken from the flightless birds that wander the plains of Mulgore. For the young tauren coming of age on Red Cloud Mesa, gathering this sustenance serves as both vital winter provisions and a core rite of passage. Tauren life is inextricably bound to the land, balancing respect for nature with the practical necessity of survival. On Red Cloud Mesa, the settlement of Camp Narache depends heavily on game hunted from the surrounding grasslands. Plainstrider meat provides essential food reserves for the village when stocks run lean, while the birds' plumage offers material for clothing and ceremonial adornments. Hunting plainstriders is one of the initial tests given to youth seeking to earn the tribe's respect. Grull Hawkwind directs hopeful hunters to stalk the swift birds across the mesa, gathering meat and feathers to prove their tracking skills and self-reliance before appearing before his father, Chief Hawkwind.

item:plainstrider-scale.text: Plainstrider Scale. A tough scale harvested from the tallstriders roaming the sweeping plains of Mulgore. It serves as a vital component in a traditional remedy prepared by Maur Raincaller to counter a virulent infection. While plainstriders are best known for their soft feathers and lean meat, their powerful legs are covered in tough, protective scales. These scales are resilient against the harsh scrubland terrain and predator claws. Finding one intact and suitable for medicine requires patience, as only select plainstriders across Mulgore yield scales firm enough to be ground and prepared for folk remedies.

item:plainstrider-talon.text: Plainstrider Talon. A Plainstrider Talon is a sharp claw harvested from the large, flightless plainstriders native to Mulgore. Tauren shamans use these talons alongside other natural reagents to craft sacred cleansing totems when the land's water sources are corrupted. The large, flightless plainstriders roam the open grasses of Mulgore, relying on powerful legs and sharp claws to defend against predators and forage through the tough prairie earth. To the tauren of Bloodhoof Village, every part of a hunted beast carries spiritual resonance. When goblin ventures tainted sacred sources like the Winterhoof Water Well, shaman Mull Thunderhorn sought plainstrider talons alongside prairie wolf paws. In tauren ritual crafting, gathering reagents from native predators and foragers allows the spiritual essence of the land to be channeled into totems capable of purging unnatural poisons.

item:podrig-s-order.text: Podrig's Order. Podrig's Order is a written military requisition penned by Deathguard Podrig at the Sepulcher. It requests a fresh shipment of weapons from Undercity merchant Gordon Wendham to keep Silverpine's Forsaken garrison properly armed. Silverpine Forest is a precarious frontier for the Forsaken, caught between encroaching Scourge, feral beasts, and other lurking threats. After an equipment inventory conducted by Deathguard Podrig on the orders of Executor Hadrec, the Sepulcher's stores were found mostly adequate but desperately low on replacement weapons. This official dispatch details the needed blades and arms to sustain the Deathguards holding the outpost. Because weapons cannot be forged easily amidst the damp crypts of Silverpine, the request is directed to Gordon Wendham, a weapon dealer located in the bustling Trade Quarter of the Undercity. To expedite the order, couriers carry the document directly to bat master Karos Razok, taking advantage of Forsaken flight paths to secure a swift resupply from the capital.

item:pork-belly-pie.text: Pork Belly Pie. In Elwynn Forest, Billy Maclure wants a pie from the Stonefield farm before he speaks about a missing necklace. Auntie Bernice Stonefield bakes it despite the feud between their families. The Stonefield and Maclure families have quarreled over land and pride for years in Elwynn Forest. Young Billy Maclure has a weakness for Auntie Bernice's pork belly pie. When a valuable Stonefield family necklace goes missing, Billy refuses to share what he knows until an adventurer brings him a warm slice. Bernice bakes the pie reluctantly, wishing the greedy boy would choke on it.

item:powdered-azurite.text: Powdered Azurite. In Hillsbrad Foothills, Powdered Azurite is taken from the Azurelode Mine. Thun'grim Firegaze needs it to forge brutal armor for rising Horde warriors. Powdered Azurite comes from the mineral veins beneath Hillsbrad Foothills. Human workers dig the blue stone from Azurelode Mine, then grind and pack it for trade and metalworking. A skilled smith mixes the dust with dense metals to make armor more durable and resilient. Horde blacksmiths prize Powdered Azurite for its strength in metalworking, though it comes from human-held tunnels across the Great Sea. Thun'grim Firegaze, an aging orc armorer in the Barrens, asks for small amounts alongside refined iron and fiery reagents. Mixed into the smelt, the powder helps him hammer out the heavy plating of his Brutal Armor.

item:powers-of-the-void.text: Powers of the Void. A stolen tome draws Drusilla La Salle's attention in Northshire. Powers of the Void was kept in a restricted wing of Northshire Abbey's library until a novice took it while defecting to the Defias Brotherhood. Drusilla seeks its recovery for her own study of dark magic. Powers of the Void was kept behind guarded shelves in Northshire Abbey's library. The abbey archives hold holy scripture and clerical records, along with scholarly works on shadow and nether energies. The tome was presumably penned by the archmage Khadgar. Because its subject was dangerous, abbey authorities kept the book under guard and away from casual visitors. That barred Northshire's warlock mentor, Drusilla La Salle, from browsing it without drawing the priesthood's suspicion. A Northshire novice carried the tome away while abandoning his vows to join the Defias Brotherhood. As he fled into the neighboring vineyards, he took several valuable volumes from the abbey. Drusilla sends promising warlock initiates into the Defias bandit camp to recover the book from their tents. She wants the dark knowledge for her own study, and the effort tests whether an initiate has the nerve to bind otherworldly demons.

item:prairie-alpha-tooth.text: Prairie Alpha Tooth. A Prairie Alpha Tooth is taken from the fierce pack leaders roaming the plains around Thunder Bluff. In tauren tradition, these teeth serve as a potent offering to cleanse and honor the land's precious water sources. The water wells of Mulgore are vital lifelines for the tauren, and maintaining their spiritual purity demands rites of respect and sacrifice. To cleanse the Wildmane Well, Mull Thunderhorn of Bloodhoof Village requires teeth gathered from the prairie wolf alphas that stalk the shadow of Thunder Bluff. As apex predators of the rolling grassy plains, these alphas represent the raw strength of the wild. Offering their teeth honors the balance between hunter, prey, and the spirits of the earth.

item:prairie-wolf-heart.text: Prairie Wolf Heart. A Prairie Wolf Heart is a vital organ harvested from the wolves roaming the grasslands of Mulgore. It serves as an essential ingredient in an urgent folk remedy prepared by Maur Raincaller in Bloodhoof Village to counteract venomous infection. The wolves of the plains are fierce predators, hardy and persistent across the sweeping grasses of Mulgore. Their hearts are sought out by Maur Raincaller, a tauren residing in Bloodhoof Village who fell victim to the legendary plainstrider known as Mazzranache. Struck by the creature's virulent, fever-inducing venom, Maur relies on traditional plains medicine to halt the spreading poison. Alongside other potent reagents like cougar bone and bird gizzard, the vital essence of a freshly slain prairie wolf provides the cleansing properties needed to concoct a cure before delirium proves fatal.

item:prairie-wolf-paw.text: Prairie Wolf Paw. Prairie Wolf Paws are harvested from the predators roaming the plains of Mulgore. Shamanic practitioners, such as Mull Thunderhorn in Bloodhoof Village, use them as organic components to bind the natural power of the land into cleansing totems. Prairie wolves stalk the rolling grasses across Mulgore, hunting in packs alongside prairie stalkers and their pack alphas. While dangerous to young hunters and local livestock, the creatures are deeply intertwined with the spiritual balance of the plains. Tauren shamans view the wolf's paws not merely as trophies, but as vital conduits of the earth's innate vitality. When goblin ventures tainted Mulgore's sacred water reserves, shaman Mull Thunderhorn required the physical aid of the land itself to counteract the pollution. Bound together with plainstrider talons, the wolf paws provide the raw spiritual resonance necessary to fashion cleansing totems, beginning the vital work of purifying the Winterhoof Water Well.

item:pridewing-venom-sac.text: Pridewing Venom Sac. Pridewing Venom Sacs are harvested from the lethal wyverns nesting around Mirkfallon Lake in the Stonetalon Mountains. The night elves of Astranaar seek to stockpile and destroy these sacs after intelligence suggests Horde operatives harvest the potent poison for covert assassinations. The pridewings of Stonetalon are dangerous, airborne predators native to the peaks south of Ashenvale, particularly around Mirkfallon Lake. While wild wyverns are naturally venomous, Alliance intelligence out of Theramore suggests that Horde assassins have begun milking them for poison to coat blades used in covert raids against night elf settlements. To safeguard their kin and disrupt enemy supplies, the Sentinels in Astranaar hire scouts to hunt down the beasts and collect the venom glands before the Horde can secure them.

item:prismatic-punch-card.text: Prismatic Punch Card. The Prismatic Punch Card is the highest security clearance data card found within the fallen city of Gnomeregan. Upgraded sequentially through a series of Matrix Punchograph terminals, it holds data desperately sought by gnome refugees in Ironforge. When the gnomes fled the trogg invasion and toxic irradiation of Gnomeregan, massive troves of research and civic records were abandoned in the depths. To safeguard high-level systems, the gnomes utilized an escalating security protocol. Accessing the Matrix Punchograph 3005-D terminal in the lower Engineering Labs requires working through a progression of punch cards: starting from a basic White Punch Card and advancing through Yellow, Blue, and Red clearances at dedicated terminals before stamping the final Prismatic Punch Card. Its encoded clearance level is whimsically noted as pending the invention of an entirely new number.

item:pristine-spider-silk.text: Pristine Spider Silk. Stormwind mages seek Pristine Spider Silk for robes woven to endure enchantments. The fine thread comes from venomous spiders in Duskwood. Stormwind mages need silk strong enough to bear enchantments and the wear of an adept. Tailors use common spider silk, but the strands gathered from carrion recluses and black widow hatchlings in Duskwood are more resilient. Mages from the Wizard's Sanctum send rising adepts into those woods to collect the silk. Master tailor Wynne Larson then weaves it into a robe for an adept.

item:prowler-claws.text: Prowler Claws. Across the Barrens, Prowler Claws are carried back to Sergra Darkthorn at the Crossroads. They show that a hunter can track and defeat the prowlers stalking the plains. Savannah Prowlers hide in the Barrens’ tall grass, waiting to strike with patience and cunning. These large cats ambush creatures that enter their hunting grounds, unlike grazing plainstriders and zhevra. Taking their curved claws means facing predators that rely on stealth and defend their territory. For Horde warriors and scouts, the hunt tests whether they can track a stalker through its own ground and make it the prey. Sergra Darkthorn, the huntress at the Crossroads, asks initiates to bring back Prowler Claws before facing greater trials. The claws show that a hunter can follow tracks through the savannah grass and withstand a predator’s attack. Those who return with them have proved they can stay alert among the dangerous beasts of the plains.

item:pure-hearts.text: Pure Hearts. Pure Hearts are ritual reagents provided to Forsaken warlocks by Carendin Halgar in the Undercity. They are used to lure and manifest a succubus across the Twisting Nether so the practitioner can defeat and bind the demon. Demonology relies on exploiting base desires and spiritual vulnerabilities. To summon a succubus into the Magic Quarter of the Undercity, Carendin Halgar provides warlocks with Pure Hearts. When placed upon the summoning circle, these untainted spiritual essences act as potent bait, drawing the seductive demon across the Twisting Nether into the mortal realm. Once the demon manifests, the warlock must resist her enthralling mind-charms and strike her down in combat. Overcoming the succubus asserts mystical dominance, banishing her back to the Twisting Nether until Carendin teaches the warlock the spell to summon her forth at will.

item:purified-kor-gem.text: Purified Kor Gem. A Purified Kor Gem is a rare, consecrated crystal required by the weaponsmith Jordan Stilwell outside Ironforge. Once tainted by dark energies, it must be reclaimed from the depths of Kalimdor and cleansed by elven magic before it can be forged into a holy arm of the Light. The stone begins its journey as a Corrupted Kor Gem in the possession of the vile naga lurking within Blackfathom Deeps, deep beneath the coast of Ashenvale. To cleanse the stone of its aquatic, shadowy taint, a paladin must seek out the night elf Thundris Windweaver in Auberdine. Drawing upon arcane and natural arts, Thundris purges the corruption from the stone, transforming it into the radiant Purified Kor Gem. Only in this pristine state is it fit to serve as a conduit for holy power. Outside Ironforge in the snowy crags of Dun Morogh, the human weaponsmith Jordan Stilwell requires the gem as a key component for forging a masterwork weapon. Having long possessed designs for an armament worthy of the Silver Hand, Stilwell lacked the exotic materials to realize his plans. The Purified Kor Gem, alongside Whitestone Oak Lumber and rare ore, provides the spiritual core necessary to channel the paladin's righteous wrath.

item:putrid-claw.text: Putrid Claw. Putrid Claws are the decaying hands severed from mindless undead prowling the woods west of Brill. Deathguard Dillinger collects them as definitive proof that the encroaching Scourge threat near the old bridge is being held at bay. Even in their own homeland, the Forsaken are not entirely safe from the Lich King's reach. Pockets of mindless Scourge—rotting dead and ravaged corpses—regularly wander across the eastern borders into Tirisfal Glades, clustering along roads and near the old bridge west of Brill. To ensure the safety of travelers and garrison supply lines, the Deathguards place bounties on these wandering horrors. A severed putrid claw serves as unmistakable, physical evidence that one more shambling corpse has been put down for good.

item:pyrewood-shackle.text: Pyrewood Shackle. Pyrewood Shackles are enchanted restraints worn by the beleaguered inhabitants of Pyrewood Village in southern Silverpine Forest. Imbued with the strange magic of Archmage Arugal, these bands are linked to the eerie curse that transforms ordinary townsfolk into ravenous worgen once night falls. The cursed village of Pyrewood holds an unsettling secret: by day, its residents carry on ordinary lives appearing as typical humans, but the setting sun twists them into feral Moonrage worgen. Archmage Arugal bound these villagers in enchanted shackles as part of his twisted experiments with worgen sorcery. Dalar Dawnweaver, an arcane researcher stationed at the Sepulcher for the Forsaken, studies these shackles to decode the enchantments driving this dual existence. By gathering and analyzing the lingering energy on the bands, Dawnweaver seeks a deeper understanding of Arugal's magic in hopes of unraveling the mad archmage's hold over the region.

item:quinn-s-potion.text: Quinn's Potion. Quinn's Potion is a restorative draught concocted by Apothecary Renferrel in the Sepulcher. It is brewed to stabilize and revitalize the wounded Deathstalker Quinn Yorick following a disastrous scouting patrol in Silverpine Forest. After Deathstalker Quinn Yorick was severely battered and incapacitated near the Ivar Patch, word reached the Royal Apothecary Society at the Sepulcher. Apothecary Renferrel hastily compounded this specialized draught to facilitate Quinn's recovery. While Renferrel rarely lets minor field casualties distract him from his grander, more sinister research for Lady Sylvanas, he provided the restorative to get the injured scout back on his feet and capable of travel.

item:ran-bloodtooth-s-skull.text: Ran Bloodtooth's Skull. Ran Bloodtooth's Skull is a grisly trophy taken from the chieftain of the corrupted furbolgs in Ashenvale. Brought back to the night elves of Astranaar, it serves as tangible proof that a ferocious threat to the woodland realm has been ended. The forests of Ashenvale have suffered immensely from demonic taint and wilderness corruption, driving once-peaceful furbolg tribes into murderous madness. Among the fiercest of these hostile chieftains was Ran Bloodtooth. Recovering his skull provides the night elf Sentinels with definite proof that the brute has fallen, breaking his hold over the local furbolgs and offering a small measure of respite to the beleaguered town of Astranaar.

item:raptor-head.text: Raptor Head. Across the Barrens, Raptor Head trophies answer a bounty from Gazrog at the Crossroads. The guard payroll vanished from a watchtower, and a wild raptor was caught in the theft. A stolen chest of guard payroll has left the Crossroads watchtower without its silver. The defenders caught a wild raptor red-handed, to their disbelief. Gazrog has put a bounty on the cunning reptiles prowling the Barrens. Bring their severed heads to the outpost, and the predators will be culled before they can pilfer more Horde supplies.

item:rare-earth.text: Rare Earth. At Dolanaar, Rare Earth waits for delivery to Denalan's camp near Lake Al'Ameth. The mineral-rich soil came from Darnassus for his botanical experiments on Teldrassil. Rare Earth is late reaching Dolanaar from Darnassus. Denalan, an eccentric botanist on Lake Al'Ameth's eastern shore, requested the parcel to study plants in Teldrassil's young ecosystem. Herbalist Syral Bladeleaf now entrusts the soil to travelers heading south, hoping it reaches Denalan before its potency fades.

item:rattlecage-skull.text: Rattlecage Skull. Rattlecage Skulls are the shattered remnants of mindless undead roaming the ruined outskirts of Deathknell. Novice Forsaken warlocks must gather these calcified trophies for Venya Marthand to demonstrate their emerging will and qualify for the dark arts of summoning. Within the sunless bounds of Deathknell, newly raised Forsaken with an affinity for dark magic are guided by Venya Marthand. To prove that a fledgling practitioner has the fortitude to bend extraplanar creatures to their command, Venya tasks them with subduing the lingering Rattlecage Skeletons near the ruined smithy. Striking down these lesser undead and retrieving their severed skulls serves as both a practical test of discipline and a ritual foundation before learning to breach the void and enslave a first demonic minion.

item:raven-claw-talisman.text: Raven Claw Talisman. In Ban'ethil Barrow Den, the Raven Claw Talisman is kept among relics needed to awaken sleeping druids. The sacred night elf relic is one of four Relics of Wakening used to guide the Druids of the Talon safely back from the Emerald Dream. The Raven Claw Talisman rests in a designated chest inside Ban'ethil Barrow Den, where Teldrassil's Druids of the Talon entered deep meditative sleep. Their hibernation is a delicate spiritual threshold. Without the proper ceremonial focus, a druid whose link to the waking world is broken may remain stranded in the Emerald Dream. Athridas Bearmantle in Dolanaar needs this talisman, the Black Feather Quill, the Sapphire of Sky, and the Rune of Nesting to perform the awakening ritual and bring the sleepers back safely. Corrupted Gnarlpine furbolgs have overrun Ban'ethil Barrow Den, putting its sacred chests and sleeping druids in peril. Their desecration has cut the sanctuary off from outside aid, and the relics may be lost or destroyed. Athridas Bearmantle calls on Teldrassil's defenders to brave the den's winding earthen corridors and secure the Raven Claw Talisman before the displaced druids are lost to the Dream forever.

item:razorflank-s-medallion.text: Razorflank's Medallion. Razorflank's Medallion is a personal token carried by Charlga Razorflank, the crone ruling over Razorfen Kraul. Recovered from the heart of the quilboar stronghold, it serves as undeniable proof that the matriarch has been brought down. Carried by Charlga Razorflank herself, this medallion represents the authority of the crone who leads the Razorfen quilboar. When Falfindel Waywarder at Thalanaar learns of the fates of fallen explorers like Heralath and the dwarf Lonebrow, he tasks Alliance adventurers with striking directly at the quilboar leader.
