Presenting the crone's medallion confirms her death, reassuring the night elf sentinels guarding the borders of Feralas that the gathered forces within the Kraul have lost their leader.

item:reagent-pouch-shaman.text: Reagent Pouch (shaman). Burning Blade cultists in Durotar carry reagents for a shaman's first fire sapta. Telf Joolam uses them with fire tar from Razormane quilboar to make the draught that lets a young shaman see the realm of fire. Burning Blade cultists carry reagents for a young shaman's first fire sapta. The hermit Telf Joolam uses the powders and oils in their pouches with fire tar from Razormane quilboar. Together, these components make a draught that grants sight into the realm of fire and attunes the shaman to the spirits of flame. Burning Blade cultists turn flame toward destruction and fel sorcery, yet the elements in their pouches still belong to heat and combustion. Shaman teach that elemental forces exist in tension: fire creates as well as destroys. A shaman can take the cultists' tools and use those elements to awaken true communion with the spirits.

item:reconstructed-tome.text: Reconstructed Tome. In warlocks’ hands, the Reconstructed Tome gathers the scattered teachings of the cabal. Its pages hold the rites for summoning and binding a felhunter from the Twisting Nether. Warlocks of the Alliance and Horde search for the torn leaves of the Tome of the Cabal. They piece the grimoire back together and consult occult scholars, who are eager to glimpse its rare teachings before the finished book is surrendered.

item:recruitment-letter.text: Recruitment Letter. Takrin Pathseeker sends promising adventurers from Durotar west to serve in the Barrens. His letter directs able-bodied volunteers to the border outpost run by Kargal Battlescar. Takrin Pathseeker watches young warriors and scouts prove themselves around Razor Hill. He chooses those who seem strong enough for frontline service and gives them a letter for duty in the Barrens. Across the Southfury River bridge, recruits leave Durotar’s sheltered red dirt and join the Horde’s guard against quilboar, centaur, and Alliance scouts. Kargal Battlescar receives the recruits at the outpost just across the river. The grizzled veteran manages the post and evaluates each conscript before signing off on their enlistment. A signed recruit is soon sent farther west to the Crossroads, where the frontier outposts are stretched thin.

item:red-burlap-bandana.text: Red Burlap Bandana. In Northshire Valley, Deputy Willem gathers red bandanas from slain Defias thieves near the abbey vineyards. The cloth marks low-ranking highwaymen and cutpurses of the Brotherhood. Red burlap masks mark the Defias Brotherhood's rank-and-file. Cheap, rough cloth dyed red hides a thief's features and signals allegiance to the growing rebellion. In Northshire, young recruits and common thugs carry these scarves into the eastern orchards. The local guards recognize the striking red fabric as proof of thieves slain nearby.

item:red-leather-bandana.text: Red Leather Bandana. In Westfall, Red Leather Bandanas mark those who defy Stormwind’s Crown. The Defias Brotherhood wears them as face coverings and a sign of their cause.

item:red-linen-bandana.text: Red Linen Bandana. Across Elwynn Forest, Red Linen Bandana marks the Defias Brotherhood. Its cloth hides a wearer’s face and can be put to use by local settlers. Across Elwynn Forest, full Defias operatives wear woven red linen bandanas. In Northshire Valley, lower-ranking initiates and common thugs use coarse burlap masks instead. The crimson cloth hides a face and marks allegiance to Edwin VanCleef's rogue fraternity. It also signals their rebellion against Stormwind's crown. Sara Timberlain at the Eastvale Logging Camp asks travelers to gather bandanas from outlaw encampments. Though tied to bandits, the masks are made from respectable linen. After washing and needlework, settlers can turn the cloth into sturdy clothing and bandages for the forest's working folk.

item:red-wool-bandana.text: Red Wool Bandana. Red Wool Bandanas are makeshift symbols fashioned by imprisoned Defias cutthroats inside the Stormwind Stockade. Torn from jailhouse wool blankets, they serve as defiant emblems of brotherhood even behind bars. Even locked deep within the high stone walls of the Stormwind Stockade, members of the Defias Brotherhood refuse to surrender their identity. Using scraps torn from prison wool blankets, inmates secretly craft red bandanas to wear as identifying colors. To the guards, these scarves are contraband that spark fatal mutinies; to the prisoners, they are a statement that their brotherhood and rebellion endure, even in chains. The bandanas gained a bitter notoriety after fourteen-year-old prison guard Mac Raskol caught inmates shredding blankets to make them. When he attempted to discipline the prisoners, the Defias convicts stabbed him in the back. In the wake of his death, his grieving grandmother Nikova seeks out adventurers to venture into the rioting dungeon, cull the rioters, and retrieve the crimson cloth as proof of vengeance.

item:remaining-drops-of-purest-water.text: Remaining Drops of Purest Water. Across Kalimdor and Lordaeron, shaman gather what Brine needs for a draught. Its last drops wait for a perilous journey. Brine prepares a water draught in the Barrens from water gathered across Kalimdor and Lordaeron. Part of it gives shaman vision of distant elements. The remaining drops are kept for a harder purpose. Shaman carry them to the coast of Silverpine Forest, near the Sepulcher, where the Brazier of Everfount stands. There, the drops are burned with the bracers of a fallen, tainted elemental. The pure water cuts through the undead plague’s corruption, calling an untainted water spirit to commune with the shaman and complete their communion with the element.

item:remedy-of-arugal.text: Remedy of Arugal. The Remedy of Arugal is an incantation penned by the mage Arugal during his early experiments with worgen magic. Left behind in a dilapidated farmhouse in Silverpine Forest, the spell is sought by Dalar Dawnweaver to unravel the sorcerer's dark work. Before seizing Shadowfang Keep, Archmage Arugal took refuge at an abandoned wheat farm north of the river bridge in Silverpine Forest. There, amidst forgotten farm tools and rotting floorboards, he documented his strange arts in a set of dusty spellbooks. The scroll titled the Remedy of Arugal is among these notes, outlining early methods and magical formulations he devised while dabbling in the dangerous transmutations that cursed the local populace. Dalar Dawnweaver, an accomplished Forsaken spellcaster operating from the Sepulcher, holds little respect for Arugal's pedigree, dismissing the former Dalaran wizard's intellect as fragile and transparent. Even so, Dawnweaver recognizes the urgent need to understand the exact mechanics behind the worgen curse. By recovering the Remedy of Arugal, Forsaken agents provide Dawnweaver with the foundational arcana required to counter Arugal's spreading menace and secure Silverpine for Lady Sylvanas.

item:rendered-spores.text: Rendered Spores. Rendered Spores are a volatile emulsion prepared from fungal samples gathered across the Barrens. Created by Apothecary Helbrim at the Crossroads, the mixture decays rapidly unless swiftly delivered to Apothecary Zamah beneath Thunder Bluff for stabilizing. After acquiring strange fungal spores from mushrooms near the damp oases of the Barrens, Apothecary Helbrim processes them into an active chemical emulsion known as Rendered Spores. The delicate extraction suspends the potent compounds of the fungal growths in a liquid medium, but the solution is chemically unstable. It maintains its vital potency for only forty-five minutes before breaking down and becoming completely useless for scientific study. Because Helbrim lacks the necessary facilities or time at his remote outpost to complete the refining process, the emulsion must be rushed directly to his Forsaken colleague, Apothecary Zamah. Hidden away in the subterranean Pools of Vision beneath Spirit Rise in Thunder Bluff, Zamah possesses the specialized equipment and reagents needed to reseal and finish processing the spores for the Royal Apothecary Society.

item:renferrel-s-findings.text: Renferrel's Findings. Renferrel's Findings is a collection of research notes compiled by Apothecary Renferrel in Silverpine Forest. Entrusted to Horde couriers, these documents carry vital data southward to Apothecary Lydon in Tarren Mill to assist in brewing the Forsaken's New Plague. The Royal Apothecary Society labours tirelessly under direct orders from the Dark Lady, Lady Sylvanas Windrunner, to engineer a New Plague. Achieving this breakthrough requires constant collaboration among researchers scattered across Lordaeron. Stationed at the Sepulcher in Silverpine Forest, Apothecary Renferrel compiles these findings to document his progress and experiments, sending the gathered intelligence south to Tarren Mill so fellow researchers can build upon his results. Carrying these papers across the border from Silverpine into the Hillsbrad Foothills represents a vital link in the Forsaken's alchemical network. In Tarren Mill, Apothecary Lydon eagerly awaits Renferrel's notes to cross-reference and advance his own concoctions against the living and the Scourge. Without reliable couriers running the contested roads of Hillsbrad, the Society's decentralized research would quickly stall.

item:report-on-the-defias-brotherhood.text: Report on the Defias Brotherhood. At Stormwind Keep, a report on the Defias Brotherhood carries the findings of a long investigation to the royal court. City Architect Baros Alexston entrusts it to the adventurer who uncovered the conspiracy. City Architect Baros Alexston prepared a report for Stormwind's leaders after a long investigation into unrest in Westfall and nearby lands. He entrusted the document to the adventurer who unraveled the conspiracy. The report is carried to Stormwind Keep, where it is meant to accompany a personal audience about the conspirators' schemes and the danger they pose to the kingdom.

item:resonite-crystal.text: Resonite Crystal. Resonite Crystals are rare mineral samples mined by kobolds inside Boulderslide Cavern in the Stonetalon Mountains. Their frantic digging has drawn the concern of Mor'rogal at Sun Rock Retreat.

item:restabilization-cog.text: Restabilization Cog. Restabilization Cogs are precision mechanical components salvaged from the leper gnomes wandering outside the irradiated ruins of Gnomeregan. In Kharanos, gnomish tinkerers require these intact parts to construct the Recombobulator, an ambitious machine intended to reverse leper mutation. When radiation flooded Gnomeregan in a disastrous attempt to wipe out the invading troggs, countless gnomes were twisted into sick, hostile leper gnomes. Despite their madness, these afflicted exiles still carry intricate gnomish machinery and salvageable fittings. Tinkers Ozzie Togglevolt and Razzle Sprysprocket believe the horrific transformation can be systematically undone. To finish their prototype Recombobulation Device, they rely on adventurers to recover vital parts directly from the afflicted outside Gnomeregan's gates, including intact Restabilization Cogs to balance the machine's inner combustion systems.

item:ring-of-zoram.text: Ring of Zoram. The Ring of Zoram is an ancient Kaldorei heirloom dating back to the glory days of the sunken city of Zoram before the Great Sundering. Once worn by the city's rulers and the key to the ancient lock of a sunken statuette, it recently fell into the hands of the encroaching coastal naga. Before the Well of Eternity collapsed and the oceans swallowed the western reaches of Kalimdor, Zoram was a coastal jewel of the night elven empire. The Ring of Zoram belonged to the rulers of the city, and a strange code is written upon its inner band in the language of the night elves. When the Great Sundering shattered the continent ten thousand years ago, the ring sank along with the city, lost beneath the crashing tides of what is now the Zoram Strand. For millennia, the ring remained buried beneath silt and ruins until the naga began scouring the coastline of Ashenvale. Ruuzel, a naga leader dwelling on an islet off the northern strand, uncovered the artifact among the sunken debris. Scholars like the night elf Talen seek the ring not merely for its antiquity, but because it functions as the only key capable of unlocking other relics salvaged from the depths, including sealed ancient statuettes recovered from the sea floor.

item:robo-mechanical-guts.text: Robo-Mechanical Guts. Robo-Mechanical Guts are salvagable gearworks, conduits, and machine innards harvested from the malfunctioning constructs roaming the ruins of Gnomeregan. Gnomish engineers in Stormwind require these specific components to repair heavy tunneling vehicles meant to aid in the reclamation of Gnomeregan in Dun Morogh. When High Tinker Gelbin Mekkatorque and the surviving gnomes evacuated Gnomeregan, thousands of automated mechanisms, clockwork sentries, and industrial robots were abandoned inside. In the city's radioactive aftermath, these machines continue to roam the corridors autonomously. In Stormwind City, the tinker Shoni seeks to assemble a fleet of gyrodrillmatic excavationators to pierce the defenses of Gnomeregan and reclaim the lost city. Lacking fresh raw materials, she tasks bold adventurers with braving the contaminated halls of Gnomeregan to carve out functional robot viscera—springs, wires, and gyro-components—to refit the excavation machinery.

item:rocket-car-parts.text: Rocket Car Parts. Rocket Car Parts are the scattered, twisted metal remains of high-speed collisions across the Shimmering Flats in Thousand Needles. Constantly generated by reckless gnome and goblin racers pushing experimental speeders past their limits, these salvaged scraps are harvested by opportunists looking to turn racetrack accidents into quick coin. The Mirage Raceway in the Shimmering Flats is the staging ground for an unending, combustible rivalry between goblin and gnome engineering. In their pursuit of unmatched land speed, racers regularly suffer catastrophic breakdowns, explosive misfires, and high-velocity crashes that scatter metal across the salt flats. These discarded remnants—ranging from bent cylinders and burnt gears to crushed sheet metal—do not stay abandoned for long. Scavengers and merchants, most notably the opportunistic dwarf Kravel Koalbeard, hire passing adventurers to comb the blinding white expanse and collect the debris. Because both racing teams are perpetually desperate for spare machinery to patch together their next prototype, scavenged wreckage can easily be resold directly back to the very teams that wrecked it.

item:rod-of-channeling.text: Rod of Channeling. In the Wetlands, the Rod of Channeling is carried by Dragonmaw spellcasters. Warlocks seeking to summon a felhunter gather three for Strahad Farsan's acolytes to steady the ritual circle in Ratchet. Warlocks need more than willpower to bind a volatile felhunter. Strahad Farsan asks for three matched rods so his acolytes can channel magic together and steady the summoning circle while the warlock binds the beast. Dragonmaw darkcasters carry these rods for their own workings. Bonewarders and shadowwarders bear them at Angerfang Encampment and in the surrounding Wetlands ruins. Combat leaves the rods worn and nicked, but they still focus chaotic nether energy.

item:rot-blossom.text: Rot Blossom. Rot Blossoms are foul, necrotic flora found growing among the desecrated graves of Duskwood. Fed by the blighted soil and undead remains, they are sought after for their potent, unwholesome alchemical properties. Duskwood's unnatural corruption breeds bizarre and disturbing plant life, none more unsettling than the Rot Blossom. Rooted in the defiled earth of graveyards such as the Tranquil Gardens Cemetery, these morbid blooms thrive in proximity to death. Local rumors claim they can even take root within the cracked skulls of the walking dead, particularly Skeletal Horrors and Skeletal Fiends that stalk the barrows. To the locals in Darkshire, harvesting them is both a grim chore and a dangerous necessity, as disturbing their soil means braving the unrested dead. Despite their repulsive nature, Rot Blossoms serve a specialized purpose in local concoctions. The blooms contain dark essences required to brew Zombie Juice, a foul draft tied to Duskwood's macabre survival efforts. Those dispatched to gather the blossoms often find themselves inadvertently aiding the Night Watch, culling the restless skeletons that wander the haunted gravesites in the process.

item:rot-hide-ichor.text: Rot Hide Ichor. Rot Hide Ichor is a foul bodily fluid harvested from the undead Rot Hide gnolls infesting Fenris Isle in Lordamere Lake. Apothecary Renferrel collects samples of the substance at the Sepulcher to uncover the origin of the gnolls' corruption and devise a strategy against them. The Rot Hide gnolls of Fenris Isle are not ordinary wild beasts; they are visibly decomposed and twisted by unnatural blight. Rather than normal blood, their veins pump a noxious ichor that sustains their animated flesh. The Royal Apothecary Society suspects that this fluid holds the secret to how the pack was corrupted and who commands them from within the ruined keep of Fenris Isle. Apothecary Renferrel gathers vials of this ichor to analyze its properties at the Sepulcher. By isolating the chemical and magical components fueling the gnolls, the Forsaken hope to pinpoint vulnerabilities before committing troops to a full-scale assault across Lordamere Lake.

item:rough-quartz.text: Rough Quartz. In Durotar, a Rough Quartz comes from a Minor Manifestation of Earth. A shaman brings the stone to an elder, who binds it into the first Earth Totem. Rough Quartz is a gift from a Minor Manifestation of Earth to a shaman who communes with the spirits in Durotar or Mulgore. To the untrained eye, it looks like an ordinary desert pebble. The stone represents endurance, patience, and unwavering strength. At the Valley of Trials, Canaga Earthcaller binds it into carved wood to make an Earth Totem. The quartz becomes the spiritual focus joining a young shaman to Azeroth's living soil.

item:rumbleshot-s-ammo.text: Rumbleshot's Ammo. Rumbleshot's Ammo is a mislaid crate of munitions bound for the gunsmith Hegnar Rumbleshot in Dun Morogh. Lost when a frightened courier fled from hungry wendigos, the heavy crate sits abandoned in the snow near the Grizzled Den. Hegnar Rumbleshot operates a roadside arms shop along the mountain path leading down from Coldridge Pass toward Anvilmar. With Ironforge riflemen, mountaineers, and dwarven mortar teams constantly drilling in the snowy heights, his supplies burn away almost as fast as powder catches flame. This particular shipment of shot was dispatched by Loslor from Kharanos, but never reached the shelves. The courier tasked with transporting it pitched camp too close to the predatory wendigos of the Grizzled Den, panicked when attacked, and fled for his life, leaving the heavy supply crate sitting deep within the beast's hunting grounds.

item:rune-inscribed-parchment.text: Rune-Inscribed Parchment. In the Valley of Trials, Gornek hands aspiring orc shamans a message from Shikrik. It calls them to become spiritual leaders and conduits for elemental spirits. New orc shamans begin training under veteran overseers in the Valley of Trials. While an initiate performs initial trials for Gornek, he hands them a rune-covered document sent by Shikrik, the local shamanic instructor. The message summons them to deeper communion with the elements. Among the orcs, shamans mediate between the living and their ancestors. The writ marks a move from brute strength toward disciplined reverence for ancestors.

item:rune-inscribed-pendant.text: Rune-Inscribed Pendant. The Rune-Inscribed Pendant is a magical trinket recovered from Dalaran supply shipments destined for Ambermill. Prized by the Kirin Tor, these pendants serve as conduits for channeling potent arcane energies. Discovered among crates of cartographic supplies bound for the Dalaran enclave at Ambermill, this pendant bears intricate arcane inscriptions. High-ranking wizards of the Kirin Tor frequently employ such artifacts to focus and amplify their spellcasting. The presence of numerous channeled pendants moving into the region immediately draws the suspicion of the Forsaken at the Sepulcher, signaling an impending project of immense magical power.

item:rune-inscribed-tablet.text: Rune-Inscribed Tablet. In the Valley of Trials, Gornek gives young Darkspear troll shamans a stone message. It sends promising mystics to Shikrik to begin formal communion with the elements. Gornek gives the rune-carved stone to initiates who prove their mettle in the Valley of Trials. The troll shaman Ishi-yo sent it to direct them to Shikrik, the shaman trainer. For Darkspear trolls, the tablet begins a shared path with the orcs, joining their old spiritual traditions with the shamanic heritage Warchief Thrall has renewed.

item:rune-of-nesting.text: Rune of Nesting. At Ban'ethil Barrow Den, the Rune of Nesting lies among four sacred relics. It helps Athridas Bearmantle prepare the ritual that safely awakens the Druids of the Talon from the Emerald Dream. The Rune of Nesting lies in the Chest of Nesting, deep in the winding chambers of Ban'ethil Barrow Den. Night elf druids hibernate in underground barrow dens to commune with nature through the Emerald Dream. To return safely, the Druids of the Talon need a precise awakening ritual guided by sacred relics. The rune is one of four: the Raven Claw Talisman, the Black Feather Quill, the Sapphire of Sky, and the Rune of Nesting. Together, the relics help call the sleeping druids back to the waking world. Corrupted Gnarlpine furbolgs have overrun Ban'ethil Barrow Den, putting its sleeping defenders in peril. Without the relics, the druids risk remaining trapped in the Emerald Dream while invaders desecrate their sanctuary. Recovering the Rune of Nesting and its companion artifacts allows Athridas Bearmantle in Dolanaar to prepare the ritual that can safely awaken them.

item:runes-of-summoning.text: Runes of Summoning. The Runes of Summoning are a ritual item provided by the warlock trainer Carendin Halgar in the Magic Quarter of the Undercity. They are used to call forth an unbound voidwalker into a summoning circle so that an aspiring warlock may bend it to their will. Within the dark recesses of the Undercity's Magic Quarter, Forsaken practitioners of the dark arts study the manipulation of the Nether. Carendin Halgar entrusts the Runes of Summoning only to warlocks who have prepared themselves to take command of a voidwalker. By casting the runes within the active summoning circle below Halgar's station, the practitioner tears through the fabric of the Void, drawing forth a creature that must be overpowered and bound into servitude.

item:sack-of-murloc-heads.text: Sack of Murloc Heads. The Sack of Murloc Heads is a gruesome bundle collected along the beaches of the Hillsbrad Foothills. Assembled as proof of military action against local shore pests, it is pawned off by Lieutenant Farren Orinelle onto passing adventurers for delivery to Marshal Redpath in Southshore. Southshore stands under constant siege from Syndicate outlaws, Forsaken skirmishers, and wild murlocs crowding the coast. To secure funding and favor from town leadership, local officers must demonstrate that coastal threats are actively being culled. Lieutenant Farren Orinelle gathers proof in the form of severed heads, but the distasteful nature of the cargo—and his own squeamishness—prompts him to hand the dripping sack off to travelers rather than deliver the grisly evidence to Marshal Redpath himself.

item:sack-of-supplies.text: Sack of Supplies. A caravan shipment bound for Rezlak lies scattered among the harpy roosts of Razorwind Canyon. Dustwind harpies intercepted the goods as they crossed Durotar. Rezlak needs steady supplies for his work outside Orgrimmar. The goblin engineer, contracted from Ratchet by Gazlowe, builds for the Horde. A caravan carrying a promised shipment passed near the canyon road south of Orgrimmar, where Dustwind harpies ambushed it. They dragged the cargo into their roosts in Razorwind Canyon, scattering sacks among dirt and scree beside their nesting sites.

item:salty-scorpid-venom.text: Salty Scorpid Venom. Salty Scorpid Venom is a caustic fluid harvested from the scorpids stalking the Shimmering Flats in Thousand Needles. Packed with natural salts from the desert floor, it is prized by gnomish rocket racers attempting to engineer volatile, ultra-hot fuel. The scorpids crawling the arid expanse of the Shimmering Flats have adapted to an intensely mineral-rich environment. Over generations, the venom of beasts like the Scorpid Reavers and Scorpid Terrors has absorbed enormous quantities of local salt. Rather than brewing antidotes or standard poisons, gnomish tinkers like Fizzle Brassbolts prize this caustic compound as a prospective additive for high-combustion engine fuel. Out at the Mirage Raceway, the engineering competition between gnomes and goblins drives inventors to test increasingly dangerous materials in their rocket cars. Fizzle Brassbolts believes boiling down the salted venom, treating it with specialized catalysts, and mixing it into propellant tanks will deliver the blazing heat necessary to outrun goblin racers on the salt pans.

item:samophlange-item.text: Samophlange (item). In the Barrens, Samophlange is hidden inside an automated control console. Goblin mechanics cannot explain what the strange component does. Samophlange lies inside a control console in the Barrens, behind a maze of wiring and hollow tubes. It takes careful searching to free the component from its housing. It looks like a vital part of clockwork and steam machinery, but goblin tinkerers cannot make sense of its purpose. They mean to send it to the Tinkers' Union in Undermine, though the fragile piece may not survive rough handling.

item:samophlange-manual.text: Samophlange Manual. In Orgrimmar, Rilli Greasygob seeks the scattered pages of the Samophlange Manual. The handbook holds instructions for repairing and operating the Venture Company's samophlange. Boss Copperplug guarded the Venture Company's knowledge of the samophlange. The ambitious overseer kept the manual's pages from most workers, giving scattered leaves only to his most loyal subordinates. When the device slipped from company hands, no one could repair it without gathering the torn documentation from Copperplug and his crew at the Boulder Lode Mine. Rilli Greasygob left the Venture Company and settled in Orgrimmar to learn how the samophlange was built. Copperplug had never favored him, so Rilli depends on enterprising travelers to retrieve the manual's cover and loose leaves. Reassembled, the handbook gives goblin tinkerers working alongside the Horde a rare look at Venture Company engineering.

item:sample-ichor.text: Sample Ichor. This vial contains a refined extract of the foul fluid that sustains the rot hide gnolls of Silverpine Forest. Distilled down to its base components by Apothecary Renferrel, the substance carries lingering traces of both necromancy and warlock sorcery. The Rot Hide gnolls that prowl Silverpine Forest are no ordinary beasts. After recovering samples from the creatures and their lingering remnants, Apothecary Renferrel of the Royal Apothecary Society reduced the vile liquid into its constituent elements. His chemical breakdown revealed that the ichor was artificially manufactured through a convergence of dark schools: necromantic rites woven together with warlock magics. Because the craft behind it borders on arcane disciplines outside simple alchemy, Renferrel packaged this sample and dispatched it to the Undercity for Bethor Iceshard to examine with divination.

item:sample-of-zanzil-s-altered-mixture.text: Sample of Zanzil's Altered Mixture. A courier carries Sample of Zanzil's Altered Mixture across the sea to Tarren Mill. The brew came from the witch doctor Zanzil and leaves its carrier weakened. Serge Hinott may find a cure and uncover the poison's workings. An operative carries the mixture after infiltrating the Venture Company's tower near the Sludge Fen in the Barrens. The sample came from a cache in Gallywix's lockbox, and Zanzil's brew has left the agent afflicted. Shenthul sends the stricken operative across the Great Sea with the sample. At Tarren Mill in the Hillsbrad Foothills, apothecary Serge Hinott has the rare skill to isolate the toxin and learn its components.

item:sample-snapjaw-shell.text: Sample Snapjaw Shell. Across the Barrens, Sample Snapjaw Shells carry lingering vitality from freshwater oases. Tauren druids send them across the Great Sea to help heal Silverpine Forest. Snapjaws thrive in the lush, strange oases of the Barrens. Their durable shells keep a faint inner glow and pulse with energy long after separation from the creature. Tauren druids watching the land's swift changes see in these carapaces the resilient spark of Kalimdor's wilderness. Their vigor shows how life can flourish even in harsh, arid surroundings. Tauren naturalists send couriers across the sea with shells for Mura Runetotem at the Sepulcher. Stationed in Silverpine Forest's blighted expanses, Mura seeks ways to help the Forsaken heal the northlands. She studies the life-force preserved in the snapjaw's armor, hoping to find what can renew an ailing forest and bring growth back to dying soil.

item:samuel-s-remains.text: Samuel's Remains. Samuel's Remains are the recovered earthly remnants of Samuel Fipps, a former resident of Tirisfal Glades who fell to the Scourge. Gathered by adventurers near Deathknell, they are laid to rest beside his wife Marla to fulfill her dying wish. Before the plague of undeath swept across Lordaeron, Samuel Fipps lived peacefully with his wife, Marla. When the contagion struck, Samuel succumbed and was bound into mindless service to the Scourge. Marla escaped undeath only to be struck down by the very husband she loved. Despite this brutal end, her final wish was not vengeance, but eternity together: she pleaded to be interred beside Samuel once his cursed form was put to rest. Novice Elreth in Deathknell enlists newly awoken Forsaken to track down Samuel's wandering form northeast of the settlement, recover his bones, and bury them in the front row of the local cemetery.

item:sapphire-of-aku-mai.text: Sapphire of Aku'Mai. Sapphires of Aku'Mai are glowing, water-infused mineral clusters growing along the subterranean tunnels of Blackfathom Deeps. The encroaching naga have begun harvesting these gems, prompting the Earthen Ring to seek them out before their potent arcane power can be exploited. Discovered within the watery cavern entrances of Blackfathom Deeps along Ashenvale's Zoram Strand, Sapphires of Aku'Mai are crystalline formations rich in elemental energy. The spirits of water cling tightly to them, making them exceptional catalysts for magical workings. When scouts reported that the subterranean naga had begun actively quarrying these clusters from the cavern walls, the Shaman Je'neu Sancrea sought adventuring assistance to confiscate them. Left in the serpent peoples' clutches, the stones could easily fuel devastating arcane rites.

item:sapphire-of-sky.text: Sapphire of Sky. In Ban'ethil Barrow Den, Sapphire of Sky helps call sleeping Druids of the Talon back from the Emerald Dream. It is one of four sacred Relics of Wakening kept by the night elves. Druids of the Talon sleep in hibernation within Ban'ethil Barrow Den, deep among Teldrassil's roots, while they commune with the wilds. Waking from that deep trance is perilous. Four sacred relics protect the passage: the Black Feather Quill, the Raven Claw Talisman, the Rune of Nesting, and the Sapphire of Sky. The gem completes the harmony needed to call the sleeping spirits back from the Emerald Dream. Without it, they risk being trapped there forever. Corrupted Gnarlpine furbolgs have overrun Ban'ethil Barrow Den, leaving the sacred relics in their repositories. The Sapphire of Sky is secured inside the Chest of the Sky, along the winding underground corridors. The druids still sleep as the furbolgs rampage around them. Athridas Bearmantle in Dolanaar needs the sapphire and its companion relics to wake the sleepers before they are lost forever.

item:sara-balloo-s-plea.text: Sara Balloo's Plea. Sara Balloo's Plea is a handwritten missive penned by a grieving widow in Ironforge. Unable to face the monarch directly in her sorrow, she entrusts this letter to a trusted champion of the Alliance to carry before King Magni Bronzebeard. Written in the shadow of deep personal tragedy, Sara Balloo's Plea represents a humble appeal directly to Ironforge's throne. Rather than braving the High Seat herself in her grief-stricken condition, Sara seeks an adventurer who has demonstrated loyalty and valor to the Alliance to deliver her words. The message asks for the attention of King Magni Bronzebeard, drawing the sovereign's gaze toward the private mourning and sacrifices made by ordinary dwarven families serving the kingdom.

item:sarilus-foulborne-s-head.text: Sarilus Foulborne's Head. Sarilus Foulborne's Head is a gruesome trophy claimed from an undead sorcerer who defiled the waters of northern Kalimdor. Carried back across the border from the Barrens into Ashenvale, it serves as undeniable proof that the meddling mage has met his end at the hands of the Sentinels. Perched high atop Dreadmist Peak in the northern Barrens, the Forsaken spellcaster Sarilus Foulborne drew the wrath of the night elves by corrupting and binding swarms of water elementals. From her post at Silverwind Refuge, Sentinel Velene Starstrike recognized his foul handiwork and dispatched champions across the frontier into Horde territory to end his reckless experiments. Severing the mage's head was the only proof Starstrike would accept to verify that his mocking grin was wiped away forever, securing a measure of peace for the troubled waters of Ashenvale.

item:sarkoth-s-mangled-claw.text: Sarkoth's Mangled Claw. Across the southern bluffs of the Valley of Trials, Sarkoth's Mangled Claw bears the mark of a wounded hunter. Hana'zua's crushing blow scarred the scorpid's pincer before its venomous sting struck him down. Hana'zua, a young Darkspear troll, met Sarkoth while hunting in the Valley of Trials. The massive scorpid's venomous stinger pierced his chest, leaving him bleeding beneath a nearby tree. Before the blow landed, Hana'zua crushed the beast's pincer. Its severed, battered claw proves Sarkoth has been slain. For the wounded hunter, that scar on the beast is proof his desperate strike left its mark, and a last hold on his warrior's honor as venom courses through his veins.

item:sarltooth-s-talon.text: Sarltooth's Talon. Sarltooth's Talon is a severed claw taken from the alpha raptor lurking above Whelgar's Excavation Site in the Wetlands. It serves as tangible proof for the dwarf Ormer Ironbraid that the vicious beast responsible for overrunning the archaeological dig has been slain. When raptors overran Whelgar's Excavation Site and butchered the dwarven expedition, Ormer Ironbraid watched from the ridge above, unable to prevent the slaughter. He singled out one massive, menacing raptor—Sarltooth—as the likely pack leader behind the assault. Seeking retribution for his fallen kin, Ormer demanded the beast's death and requested one of its vicious talons as proof of the deed. Severing this claw marks the end of Sarltooth's reign of terror over the ancient dwarven ruins.

item:sathrah-s-sacrifice.text: Sathrah's Sacrifice. At the Temple of the Moon, Sathrah's Sacrifice offers Lady Sathrah's spirit a chance at peace. Her silvery spinnerets come from the mighty spider who dwells in Teldrassil. Lady Sathrah was a venerable creature of Teldrassil, until creeping madness and corruption spread through the great tree's boughs and took hold of her. The Sisterhood of Elune asks you to bring back her silvery spinnerets as a consecrated offering, not a trophy. At the fountain in the Temple of the Moon, the remains are bathed in holy water. The rite washes away the taint that poisoned Sathrah's mind and frees her troubled soul. Her spirit then appears peacefully within the sanctuary, with the promise of rebirth under Elune's grace.

item:satyr-horns.text: Satyr Horns. Satyr Horns are grim trophies harvested from the corrupted satyrs that plague the ancient woods of Ashenvale. Coveted both by grieving forest dwellers seeking retribution and opportunistic merchants trading out of Ratchet, they serve as undeniable proof that another servant of the Burning Legion has fallen. The curled horns of Ashenvale's satyrs are stark symbols of demonic corruption taken root in the sacred forest. For the dryad Illiyana at the Shrine of Aessina, gathering these severed horns is a matter of grief and vengeance for her lost sister Anilia. To outside traders like the traveling goblin Pixel resting at Splintertree Post, however, the horns represent raw opportunity. Demand for satyr horns has surged in the neutral port of Ratchet, transforming these macabre remnants of slain demons into lucrative trade goods for anyone daring enough to hunt their bearers. Satyr Horns cannot be bought from ordinary suppliers; they must be cut directly from the beasts lurking in the dark corners of the woodland. The satyrs maintain strongholds across Ashenvale, most notoriously in the corrupted groves of Xavian, the shadowed hollows of Satyrnaar, and the ruins of Night Run. Clearing these enclaves rids the land of lingering demonic taint while keeping both grieving guardians and eager merchants supplied with proof of the cull.

item:savannah-lion-tusk.text: Savannah Lion Tusk. In the Barrens, Savannah Lion Tusks go from hunting trophies to ingredients in Chen Stormstout's legendary potent ale. The great cats roaming the Barrens carry sharp, heavy tusks. Prowlers, huntresses, prides ruled by patriarchs, and beasts like Humar the Pridelord all bear them. Travelers often take the teeth as proof of a successful hunt. Brewmaster Drohn in Ratchet uses the tusks with plainstrider kidneys and thunder lizard horns to recreate Chen Stormstout's famous namesake brew, a potent ale with a legendary kick few mortal gullets can withstand.

item:scaber-stalk.text: Scaber Stalk. In Darkshore, Barithras Moonshade seeks Scaber Stalks from a hidden cavern behind Cliffspring Falls. Scaber Stalks grow in a subterranean cave behind Cliffspring Falls, among the northeastern mountains of Darkshore. The pale mushrooms thrive in the damp, secluded cave network, far from ordinary forest growth. Their remote, hazardous home makes them rare to gather, and Barithras Moonshade in Auberdine commissions scouts to brave its darkness.

item:scale-of-old-murk-eye.text: Scale of Old Murk-Eye. On Westfall's coast, Old Murk-Eye terrorizes the shore. Captain Grayson, the ghost at Westfall Lighthouse, needs a scale from the murloc as proof of his death. Old Murk-Eye turned Westfall's coast into a killing ground. Captain Grayson, the ghost bound to Westfall Lighthouse, says the cunning murloc rallied weaker-minded murlocs to raid the shore. Murk-Eye drove away the keeper's family, leaving the beacon dark when Grayson's ship struck the rocks. When the family returned to relight the flame, Murk-Eye attacked again and slaughtered them. Grayson seeks a scale from the creature as proof that the shore is clear of its fiercest predator.

item:scarlet-armband.text: Scarlet Armband. Scarlet Armbands are insignia worn by members of the Scarlet Crusade, marking their fanatic allegiance to the eradication of all undead. In Deathknell, Executor Arren demands them as proof that fledgling Forsaken have struck back against the zealots encroaching on their territory. Worn on the sleeves of Scarlet Initiates and fresh converts alike, the Scarlet Armband is the unmistakable mark of the Scarlet Crusade. To the newly risen Forsaken emerging from Deathknell, these strips of red cloth represent a lethal threat right on their doorstep. The Crusade makes no distinction between the mindless minions of the Scourge and the free-willed subjects of the Dark Lady; in their eyes, any walking corpse must be put to the torch. Executor Arren uses the collection of these armbands as a grim rite of passage, confirming the deaths of enemy scouts southeast of the settlement and proving that new Forsaken can defend their fledgling nation.

item:scarlet-crusade-documents.text: Scarlet Crusade Documents. These intercepted papers were carried by a Scarlet Crusade messenger at the Crusade's camp near Deathknell. Containing orders for the Crusade's field commanders across Tirisfal Glades, they provide the Forsaken with the exact military intelligence needed to target the Crusade's regional leadership. The courier Meven Korgal carried these documents at the Crusade's encampment southeast of Deathknell. Issued by order of the Highlord, the directives are addressed to the captains of the Crusade's Tirisfal Regional Command: Captain Perrine is to further fortify the southwest tower and gather information on the undead in Brill, Captain Vachon to crush undead movement near the northern tower, and Captain Melrose to watch the borders of the Plaguelands. The documents reveal the names, posts, and orders of Scarlet field officers stationed across Tirisfal Glades, turning an otherwise routine courier run into a catastrophic intelligence breach for the zealots. Executor Arren swiftly recognized that local forces in Deathknell could not exploit the full breadth of the intelligence. Instead, the captured dossier serves as a newly awakened Forsaken's passport out of Deathknell. Carried northeast past Cold Hearth Manor into Brill, the documents are handed directly to Executor Zygand outside the Brill Town Hall. With these orders in hand, the Forsaken military leadership plans swift decapitation strikes against Scarlet commanders entrenched across the Glades.

item:scarlet-insignia-ring.text: Scarlet Insignia Ring. A Scarlet Insignia Ring is a signet band worn by members of the Scarlet Crusade garrisoned throughout Tirisfal Glades. For the Forsaken defenders of Brill, these rings serve as gruesome proof that another zealot has been eliminated from Lordaeron's soil. Every fighting member of the Scarlet Crusade in Tirisfal Glades—from fresh neophytes and zealous friars to seasoned captains like Melrache and Perrine—carries an insignia ring. Marked with the Crusade's fiery sigil, the rings identify brother and sister within an organization consumed by paranoia. To outsiders and enemies, however, these trinkets serve entirely different purposes: they are unmistakable identifiers of Lordaeron's most fanatical human remnant. Under the direct mandate of Varimathras, Lady Sylvanas's dreadlord lieutenant, Deathguard Burgess in Brill actively collects these rings. The Forsaken consider the Scarlet Crusade an intolerable pestilence crawling across their newly claimed homeland. For Forsaken recruits, bringing stacks of these rings back to Brill is treated as undeniable proof of demise and a direct affirmation of loyalty to the throne of the Undercity.

item:scavenged-goods.text: Scavenged Goods. Scavenged Goods are miscellaneous pieces of discarded gear and supplies packed into equipment boxes around Deathknell. Newly risen Forsaken recover them to ensure the endless stream of fresh recruits can be armed and clothed. When new Forsaken pull themselves out of the earth in Deathknell's graveyard, they awaken with little more than rotting burial shrouds. Surrounding settlements and kingdoms offer no aid to the undead, leaving them entirely dependent on what they can salvage. Deathguard Saltain coordinates the collection of discarded weapons, tools, and garments cached in supply crates across the village, distributing them directly to the next batch of risen recruits.

item:scavenger-paw.text: Scavenger Paw. Scavenger Paws are severed limbs gathered from the young and ragged wolves roaming the hills of Deathknell. Newly awakened Forsaken collect them for local caretakers to stitch together into crude, protective gear. Resources are scarce for the newly returned in Deathknell. With the Scourge and the Scarlet Crusade pressing against Tirisfal, every scrap of hide and bone is put to practical use. Novice Elreth, assistant to Shadow Priest Sarvis, collects paws from the local scavenger wolves alongside bat wings to fashion serviceable garments and armor for disoriented Forsaken stepping fresh from their graves.

item:scorched-spider-fang.text: Scorched Spider Fang. Across the Wetlands, Scorched Spider Fangs are taken from Cave Stalkers and Leech Stalkers. Furen Longbeard in Stormwind needs fifty to strengthen mail for Alliance warriors. In Stormwind, blacksmith Furen Longbeard uses unusual methods to strengthen mail. He calls for fifty scorched fangs from the giant spiders of the Wetlands. Their dense, venomous, toughened substance reinforces the mail links as he tempers them. Cave Stalkers and Leech Stalkers bear the fangs Furen needs. They live in the Wetlands' sunken valleys and burrows, where damp and rot surround their hardened, scorched mandibles. Gathering fifty means venturing into deep hollows and facing the spiders in their swarms.

item:scroll-of-messaging.text: Scroll of Messaging. The Scroll of Messaging is an enchanted parchment carrying a specific magical sending spell. Acquired for the gnome engineer Gaxim Rustfizzle in the Stonetalon Mountains, it serves an unusual purpose: providing the magical trigger needed to detonate remote explosives. While ostensibly an arcane script meant for long-distance communication, Gaxim Rustfizzle has a far more disruptive application in mind for the Scroll of Messaging. By combining its transmission incantation with volatile NG-5 charges, the gnome plans to create a remotely detonated explosive. The resulting blast is intended to trigger a massive distraction at the Venture Company's logging operation in Stonetalon, granting operatives a window to slip past guards and pilfer proprietary engineering schematics and confidential correspondence.

item:sea-creature-bones.text: Sea Creature Bones. On Darkshore, Sea Creature Bones come from massive marine carcasses washed ashore. Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde gathers skeletal samples for the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus, where the cause of the strandings is under investigation. Massive sea creatures have begun flinging themselves onto Darkshore’s shallows, where they perish. Among them are giant threshers far larger than those native to the local waters. Night elves see the sudden increase as an ominous portent. Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde, sent by the Temple of the Moon to Auberdine, gathers bones from the beached creatures. Hippogryphs carry the specimens to Darnassus for close examination. The immense carcasses attract local scavengers. Greymist murlocs gather around the dead and dying creatures, feeding on their remains and fiercely defending the feeding grounds. The murlocs are too weak to hunt beasts of this size, but investigators and adventurers must fight through their packs along Mist's Edge to recover bone fragments for study.

item:sea-turtle-remains.text: Sea Turtle Remains. Along Darkshore, giant sea turtles lie dead on the coast and beneath the waves. Their remains go to researchers in Auberdine, who study the growing number of strandings. Giant sea creatures are washing ashore along Darkshore, while others lie beneath the water near sunken wrecks. In Auberdine, Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde oversees the collection of bone fragments and tissue from the bodies. The Temple of the Moon in Darnassus urgently requests these samples. Its scholars and priestesses fear the creatures may be fleeing an unnatural disturbance in the waters around Teldrassil. Recovering the remains is dangerous. Murloc tribes along the coast routinely gather around the huge carcasses, picking bones clean and nesting beside them. Scholars need fresh bone fragments and tissue before the scavengers destroy evidence that could explain the creatures' fatal migration.

item:sealed-description-of-thredd-s-visi.text: Sealed Description of Thredd's Visitor. Warden Thelwater seals a report about a visitor to Bazil Thredd in the Stormwind Stockade. The confidential account helps track a covert operative moving through Stormwind's political and criminal spheres. Prisoner Bazil Thredd spent years in the Stockade without a visitor. Then a quiet man began coming once or twice each week, carrying valid identification papers under the name Maelik. Warden Thelwater took note of the unusual visits and wrote down the man's appearance. He sealed the description so no meddling eyes could read it before proper investigators acted.

item:sealed-envelope.text: Sealed Envelope. This tightly sealed packet contains confidential Venture Company technical documents and stolen schematics. Assembled by the exiled goblin engineer Fizziks, it holds proprietary designs meant for delivery to Sputtervalve in Ratchet. When the goblin engineer Fizziks was abruptly ejected from the Venture Company's logging operations in the Stonetalon Mountains, he did not leave empty-handed. Stuffing internal manuals, operating procedures, and technical specifications into this envelope, he managed to smuggle out company secrets under the noses of his former overseers. Most prized among these stolen records are the technical schematics for the Super Reaper 6000, a devastating piece of industrial clear-cutting machinery. Rather than keeping the dangerous trade secrets buried, Fizziks sends the packet south to Sputtervalve, an engineer residing in the neutral goblin port of Ratchet. While business rivals in the Steamwheedle Cartel have little personal love or trust for Fizziks, the engineering value of the designs inside the envelope is undeniable. The documents provide a clear window into Venture Company mechanical ingenuity and give independent engineers a chance to exploit the Venture Company's advanced logging technologies.

item:sealed-note-to-elling.text: Sealed Note to Elling. Jorgen sends a sealed dispatch through Stormwind to Elling Trias, the proprietor of Trias' Cheese. The fisherman’s message draws Trias into a quiet inquiry about a vanished diplomat. Jorgen gives a strict charge for the sealed note in Stormwind: place it in Elling Trias's hands and keep silent. The stakes leave no room for careless talk. Trias runs a cheese shop in the Trade District, where Jorgen's message brings the inquiry into the diplomat's disappearance to his counter.

item:sealed-note-to-watcher-backus.text: Sealed Note to Watcher Backus. In Stormwind, Elling Trias sends a sealed note to Watcher Backus in Duskwood. He asks the Night Watch guard to report Defias activity near Darkshire. Elling Trias agrees to use his contacts to help search for the missing diplomat. He seals a note for Watcher Backus, a Night Watch guard stationed in Duskwood. Trias sends a traveler south through the forest to deliver it by hand. He hopes Backus will report any Defias seen near Darkshire.

item:searing-collar.text: Searing Collar. At Skull Rock in Durotar, Burning Blade cultists wear Searing Collars in their rites. The heated torcs burn their flesh as the cultists attune themselves to demonic power. The Burning Blade gathers for dark rites in Skull Rock, just east of Orgrimmar. Cultists, neophytes, and thugs wear Searing Collars around their necks, enduring heat that brands and sears their skin. Margoz, a hermit, studies the cruel devices. He suspects the burning and the enchantments bound to the metal attune the wearers to demonic energies. What part do these collars play in the corruption spreading through orc society under the Horde’s nose?

item:searing-coral.text: Searing Coral. Searing Coral is a rare, resilient mineral substance harvested from living iron corals off the coast of the Wetlands. Prized by tinkerers and smiths, it possesses remarkable thermal properties that allow it to be smelted and forged into protective armor. Searing Coral grows exclusively in the chilly ocean waters along the coast south of Menethil Harbor in the Wetlands. Despite thriving in cold saltwater, this unique marine organism yields a mineral-rich material capable of enduring extreme heat. Harvesters brave the Wetlands' treacherous surf and coastal predators to pry the hardened formations loose. While traditionally outside standard dwarven metallurgy, Searing Coral caught the attention of inquisitive minds in Ironforge. Gnome craftsmen such as Klockmort Spannerspan adapt the techniques of veteran armorsmith Furen Longbeard, smelting and hammering the coral directly into metal alloys to produce lightweight, exceptionally durable armor for aspiring warriors.

item:secure-crate.text: Secure Crate. In the Barrens, a Secure Crate waits for a traveler to carry it to Ratchet. Potions and alchemical goods inside are bound for the Eastern Kingdoms. Couriers, caravans, and goblin ships carry trade between Kalimdor and the Eastern Kingdoms. When a Barrens caravan misses its departure, travelers take fragile cargo like this Secure Crate down to the coast. It holds potions, alchemical goods, and reagents for associates across the Great Sea. The crate is sealed against the Barrens trails and the sea spray on its voyage. The crate’s land journey ends at the Ratchet docks, where Wharfmaster Dizzywig oversees shipping. Ratchet is a neutral port for goods crossing the sea, including cargo bound for Blackwater Cove. Dizzywig works under the Steamwheedle Cartel’s ledger, recording parcels and freight before loading them onto the next departing vessel. Ratchet links the Old World with the frontier.

item:senir-s-report.text: Senir's Report. Senir's Report is a dispatched document penned by Mountaineer Senir Whitebeard detailing the Frostmane troll threat in Dun Morogh. It carries findings commissioned under royal directive and is destined for Senator Barin Redstone in Ironforge. Drafted after scouting missions against the Frostmane trolls nestled in the crags of Dun Morogh, this field report contains mountaineer observations intended for the dwarf Senate. Senir Whitebeard, stationed out in the cold foothills, penned the document and enclosed his brother Grelin's report on Coldridge Valley, which states that Grelin acted under a sanction from King Magni Bronzebeard. Senir tasks adventurers with hauling the findings straight to Senator Barin Redstone in the High Seat of Ironforge—cautiously advising couriers to omit just how much outside help he required to compile it.

item:serena-s-head.text: Serena's Head. At the Dry Hills in the northern Barrens, Serena Bloodfeather's head is sought as proof of her death. Darsok Swiftdagger plans to display it on a Horde supply wagon as a warning against further harpy raids.

item:serpentbloom.text: Serpentbloom. Serpentbloom is a rare, subterranean herb found growing only in the dark depths of the Wailing Caverns. Its potent natural properties have drawn the keen interest of the Forsaken's Royal Apothecary Society. Serpentbloom grows exclusively within the damp, shadowy tunnels of the Wailing Caverns beneath the Barrens. Rooted in an ecosystem warped by unrestrained Emerald Dream energies, the plant thrives far from sunlight and often harbors venomous serpents nesting among its stems. Because the cave system is overrun with hostile beasts and corrupted druids, few who venture inside ever return with viable specimens. Operating from the Pools of Vision beneath Thunder Bluff, Apothecary Zamah collects Serpentbloom on behalf of the Royal Apothecary Society of Undercity. The Forsaken continuously seek out virulent, strange, and chemically potent vegetation across Kalimdor to fuel their research for the Dark Lady. Zamah believes that harvesting Serpentbloom in significant quantities could yield valuable breakthroughs for Forsaken alchemy.

item:sethir-s-journal.text: Sethir's Journal. On Teldrassil, Sethir's Journal was recovered through stealth. Its pages confirm that corruption from mainland Kalimdor has reached the World Tree.

item:sevren-s-orders.text: Sevren's Orders. Sevren's Orders are written dispatches penned by Magistrate Sevren of Brill. They direct a proven Forsaken agent to report to Bethor Iceshard, a formidable mage stationed in the Undercity's Magic Quarter. As the Forsaken solidify their grip on the ruins of Lordaeron, skilled agents who have proven their worth against the Scourge in Tirisfal Glades are summoned south to the capital. Issued by Magistrate Sevren, these written orders serve as official introduction and credentials to Bethor Iceshard, one of the Dark Lady's foremost practitioners of the arcane in the Magic Quarter. While Sevren knows little beyond the fact that the assignment involves reaching out to an errant lich, the summons carries the absolute authority of the Undercity's high mages.

item:shadowhide-pendant.text: Shadowhide Pendant. Shadowhide Pendants are crude ornamental charms carried by the Shadowhide gnolls roaming the Redridge Mountains. Collected as legal proof of bounty enforcement, they signify that local defenders have enacted Lakeshire's law against gnolls collaborating with the rogue mage Morganth. Carried by warriors, brutes, and spellcasters of the Shadowhide clan, these pendants serve as crude personal totems or rank insignias. Deep in the hills of Redridge, the clan has rallied under Lieutenant Fangore and fallen under the sway of Morganth, a rogue wielder of the Arcane. To the townspeople of Lakeshire, these charms are not mere primitive jewelry; they are identifying marks of an organized menace harassing settlements across the region on behalf of an enemy of the Crown. Under the authority of Magistrate Solomon and the laws of Stormwind, actively aiding a known criminal of the realm carries a sentence of death. Lacking sufficient royal reinforcements, Bailiff Conacher in the Lakeshire Town Hall relies on independent adventurers to uphold the peace. Presenting ten Shadowhide Pendants provides tangible proof that gnolls obeying Morganth's orders have faced frontier justice.

item:shaman-voodoo-charm.text: Shaman Voodoo Charm. In Ban'ethil Barrow Den, Gnarlpine shamans wield the Shaman Voodoo Charm. Its vile magic can sever a sleeping druid's spirit from the body. The Gnarlpine tribe has fallen into madness and corruption on Teldrassil. Within Ban'ethil Barrow Den, its shamans wield magic beyond ordinary wilderness sorcery. Their voodoo charms let them tear a sleeping druid's consciousness from the mortal realm and trap it in the Emerald Dream. The furbolgs then animate the empty body. Night elf protectors become mindless guardians, killing anyone who enters the barrows.

item:shard-of-water.text: Shard of Water. Along the Barrens coast, Islen Waterseer receives the Shard of Water from a shaman who has faced corruption. Shamans must understand balance, life, and preservation to master water. In the Call of Water, they travel to corrupted springs, even crossing the sea to blighted Silverpine Forest. After purifying the tainted waters, a shaman receives the Shard of Water. Returning the crystal token to Islen Waterseer on the rocky Barrens shore proves the initiate's worth and provides the final key to forge a Water Totem.

item:shaw-s-report.text: Shaw's Report. In Westfall, Shaw's Report carries confidential intelligence from SI:7 to Gryan Stoutmantle. Written by Master Mathias Shaw, it describes the Stonemasons Guild, Edwin VanCleef, and their grievance with the crown after Stormwind was rebuilt.

item:shimmering-frond.text: Shimmering Frond. In the Oracle Glade, a strange plant casts a twisting, shimmering aura. Its fronds come from a species native to the Swamp of Sorrows, far across the Great Sea. A radiant plant grows among the trees near the Oracle Glade. Its aura pulses, and its fronds shimmer in the woodland light. Denalan, who tends planters beside Lake Al'Ameth, recognizes the leaves as belonging to a species from the Swamp of Sorrows in the Eastern Kingdoms. How seeds from that distant marsh crossed the Great Sea and took root on Teldrassil remains a mystery. Denalan is growing specimens in his own soil to study them.

item:shimmerweed.text: Shimmerweed. Shimmerweed is a distinct herb cultivated by the Frostmane trolls on Shimmer Ridge in the snowy heights of Dun Morogh. While the trolls harvest it for their own tribal rituals, local dwarven brewers covet its sharp, unique flavor for experimental ales. High above the lowlands of Dun Morogh, the Frostmane trolls tend patches of shimmerweed along the icy crags of Shimmer Ridge. The trolls harvest and store the plant in woven baskets scattered throughout their camps, relying on it to fuel their sacred and enigmatic rituals. Outside of troll society, few mountaineers pay the weed much mind, though its potent properties have drawn the gaze of inventive outsiders. In nearby Brewnall Village, brewmaster Rejold Barleybrew has taken a keen interest in the herb. Believing that brewing is in his blood, Rejold seeks to craft the ultimate dwarven stout and suspects that the pungent, unmistakable flavor of shimmerweed might be the missing piece. He frequently hires adventurous travelers to slip into the Frostmane encampments, dodge the hostile trolls, and haul back bushels to dump into his fermenting vats.

item:shindrell-s-note.text: Shindrell's Note. Shindrell's Note is a written missive detailing recent observations of corruption around Astranaar and the Ashenvale coastline. Penned by the night elf Sentinel Shindrell Swiftfire, it serves as an intelligence report dispatched east across the forest to the druid Kayneth Stillwind. As unrest spreads throughout Ashenvale, night elf sentinels and druids coordinate to monitor the woodland's borders. Penned by Sentinel Shindrell Swiftfire in Astranaar, this report details troubling disturbances spotted along the western coast and through the central canopies. It is addressed to Kayneth Stillwind, a druid stationed at the shrine of Forest Song within the Nightsong Woods to the east. By dispatching couriers with her firsthand observations, Shindrell aids Kayneth's investigation into the subtle corruption creeping through the sacred groves.

item:shipment-of-boots.text: Shipment of Boots. Off the Barrens coast, Shipment of Boots lies in a Southsea encampment south of Ratchet. Drizzlik sent the crate from Booty Bay for Gazlowe's trade network, but the pirates seized it before it reached port. Gazlowe arranged for Drizzlik, a clothing merchant in Booty Bay, to send boots to Ratchet. Southsea Freebooters patrolling the Merchant Coast ambushed the ship and carried the crates to their beach encampments south of the harbor. They scattered the stolen goods among their tents and shanties, and the shipment remains there, far from Ratchet's docks.

item:shipment-of-iron.text: Shipment of Iron. A crate of raw metal stored at the human smithy in Hillsbrad Fields. It serves as vital stock for local armament production, making it a priority target for Forsaken forces seeking to cut off the supply lines arming the Hillsbrad townsfolk. In the ongoing struggle across the Hillsbrad Foothills, the human peasantry has mounted surprisingly stiff resistance against Tarren Mill. Much of this fighting capability stems directly from the smithy at the southwestern edge of the Hillsbrad Fields, where Blacksmith Verringtan and his apprentices work round the clock churning out weapons and armor from heavy shipments of iron. To break the farmers' resolve, Forsaken commanders ordered the forge extinguished, its smiths eliminated, and its stockpiled metal seized for the Horde war effort.

item:shipping-schedule.text: Shipping Schedule. At Jerod's Landing, the Defias Brotherhood moves contraband along Elwynn's waterways. Its dockmaster guards a schedule that maps shipments between Redridge and Westfall, and SI:7 wants it. South of Goldshire, Jerod's Landing sits on the Elwynn bank of the Nazferiti River. The Defias Brotherhood seized the landing as a hub for river traffic. From there, they move contraband between Redridge and Westfall along waterways beyond the Stormwind Guard's notice. Their dockmaster keeps the Shipping Schedule close, recording these shipments. Master Mathias Shaw leads SI:7, Stormwind's intelligence agency, and ordered the schedule stolen. It can map Defias supply lines, while taking it tests new operatives. The theft must be made inside the dock house, from the dockmaster's pockets. If the operative is caught, SI:7 denies any connection, leaving no trail to its barracks in Stormwind.

item:sida-s-bag.text: Sida's Bag. Sida's Bag is the personal satchel of Sida, a resident of Menethil Harbor. Swallowed whole by a creeping ooze during her excursion to Ironbeard's Tomb, the bag and its mysterious contents require a thorough hunt through the acidic slimes of the Wetlands to recover. While paying her regular weekly visit to Ironbeard's Tomb near Dun Modr, Sida found herself ambushed by the dreadful, dripping oozes that infest the area. Panicking in the face of the encroaching sludge, she flung her personal satchel directly at one of the creatures. Rather than driving the beast off, the ooze simply absorbed the bag into its gelatinous body. The distraction bought Sida enough precious moments to flee with her life back to the safety of Menethil Harbor, leaving her possessions trapped inside an unknown slime. Because the undulating oozes prowling Ironbeard's Tomb—ranging from crimson to monstrous varieties—look largely identical, finding the bag requires cutting down the marsh slimes until the swallowed satchel emerges intact. Despite soaking within acidic digestive muck, the durable sack preserves its contents. Once returned to Sida, she eagerly reclaims her belongings and discards the ruined, slime-coated exterior, offering the washed-out container to whoever braved the marsh on her behalf.

item:signed-recruitment-letter.text: Signed Recruitment Letter. Kargal Battlescar sends the Signed Recruitment Letter west from the Far Watch Post. His mark directs new recruits to report for duty at the Crossroads. At the Far Watch Post, Kargal Battlescar prepares recruits for service in the Barrens. The post stands east of the Southfury River, where newcomers cross from Durotar. When a conscript proves ready to Kargal, he stamps and signs a letter of introduction. The orders send recruits west along the road to the Crossroads. There, Sergra Darkthorn coordinates supplies and the defense of the dry plains. Kargal's orders carry his personal contempt for the officer who awaits the recruit. He calls Sergra Darkthorn an abrasive shaman who talks in circles around soldiers. Kargal openly questions Warchief Thrall's high opinion of her. Even so, the dispatch must reach Sergra's hands before any further assignments at the Crossroads are granted.

item:silithid-egg-the-barrens.text: Silithid Egg (The Barrens). Across the Field of Giants, silithid eggs lie buried beneath the soil. Horde researchers gather them to learn about the swarm spreading through the southern Barrens. Silithid mounds rise from the Field of Giants as strange insect-like creatures churn the earth. Their eggs lie beneath the hardened soil, guarded by territorial silithid. The Horde knows little about these creatures, but scouts at the Crossroads have seen signs of coordination and intelligence beyond that of ordinary wild beasts. Unhatched eggs may help scholars in Orgrimmar learn about the silithid’s life cycle and nature. Silithid eggs must be dug from the mounds with an adapted digging claw. The creatures defend their underground nurseries fiercely, swarming anyone who threatens their unhatched young. Korran, a troll researcher, needs intact specimens for study before the swarm spreads farther across Kalimdor.

item:silixiz-s-tower-key.text: Silixiz's Tower Key. Foreman Silixiz carries the key to the Venture Company tower near the Sludge Fen. Shattered Hand operatives must take it from his pocket as part of an undercover sabotage assignment. North of the Sludge Fen, the Venture Company keeps its tower under tight security. Grand Foreman Puzik Gallywix oversees the isolated lookout, while goblin mercenaries patrol the compound. Outside, Foreman Silixiz carries the tower key. A Shattered Hand operative from Orgrimmar must steal it and keep it. Force will not do: the operative must enter unseen and pick Silixiz's pocket, proving their stealth before climbing into the tower's toxic upper levels.

item:silver-dawning-s-lockbox.text: Silver Dawning's Lockbox. Off the Darkshore coast, Silver Dawning's Lockbox lies in the wreck of a ship lost to coastal murlocs. Inside are the fallen captain's personal effects and ship log. The Silver Dawning sailed across the sea toward Auberdine when coastal murlocs attacked. They drove the ship beneath the waves north of the harbor, and the captain died in the assault. The flooded hull still holds the captain's personal lockbox, with the ship's log and private belongings inside. Recovering them could bring a final measure of peace to the surviving crew ashore.

item:silvery-spinnerets.text: Silvery Spinnerets. Near Wellspring Lake, Silvery Spinnerets are harvested from Lady Sathrah in northern Teldrassil. Her silver webs once gathered healing evening dew for the Temple of the Moon. The Sisterhood of Elune seeks the spinnerets for a sacred rite honoring her soul. Lady Sathrah once spun shimmering webs by moonlight near Wellspring Lake. Her silver silk gathered evening mist into healing dew prized by the Sisterhood of Elune in Darnassus. But corruption reached her in Teldrassil, driving her into violent madness. Sathrah threatened her brood and the surrounding forest. Priestess A'moora asks travelers to end her suffering and recover her spinnerets, bringing mercy to a once-revered creature of the great boughs.

item:simple-memorandum.text: Simple Memorandum. The Simple Memorandum is an official notice delivered to novice gnome warriors training in Coldridge Valley. A terse gnomish directive, it instructs fledglings to report to the warrior trainer Thran Khorman in Anvilmar to prepare for the war to take back Gnomeregan. Novice adventurers in Coldridge Valley frequently find themselves entrusted with letters of introduction as they demonstrate their mettle against the local wildlife and trogg threats. For young gnome fighters, this memorandum serves as a formal order to report to Thran Khorman, the resident warrior trainer within Anvilmar. Dwarven veterans recognize that while gnomes may rely on intellect and contraptions, retaking Gnomeregan will demand pure physical resolve and martial discipline. The memorandum directs the bearer to put aside preliminary tasks and seek personalized instruction in the art of war.

item:simple-rune.text: Simple Rune. A Simple Rune is an inscribed stone token passed to fledgling dwarven warriors training in Coldridge Valley. It serves as a summons from the warrior trainer Thran Khorman, directing recruits to seek instruction inside Anvilmar. Carved with basic martial marks, the Simple Rune is handed to promising recruits who have begun clearing out the threats around Coldridge Valley. Rather than a magical charm, it acts as a formal calling stone from Thran Khorman, the resident warrior trainer at Anvilmar. Upon reading its inscribed guidance, a young fighter is expected to report directly to Thran to learn basic combat techniques and hear practical advice on surviving Dun Morogh's hostile wilds.

item:simple-sigil.text: Simple Sigil. In Shadowglen, a Simple Sigil calls novice night elf warriors to training with Alyissia. It marks their first step into Teldrassil’s defense. In Shadowglen, Conservator Ilthalaine guides young night elves as they seek their calling. A runner brings a Simple Sigil from the warrior trainer Alyissia, and Ilthalaine gives it to fledgling warriors. Its inscription tells each recruit to report for instruction. The token marks the start of their martial training as troubling times come to the World Tree. Alyissia uses the sigil to speak with recruits about the kaldorei’s pressing needs. Teldrassil’s recent growth, corruption spreading among forest beasts, and the rediscovery of distant lands such as Feralas have stretched night elven protectors thin. The sigil holds no power. It welcomes a recruit among the guardians charged with shielding their people from emerging threats.

item:simple-tablet.text: Simple Tablet. At the Valley of Trials, Gornek gives new troll warriors a message to take to Frang. Gornek gives new troll warriors a message from Tar'sere, addressed to Frang, the warrior trainer near the Den. It introduces the recruit to combat training in Durotar and asks them to present themselves to Frang. The message calls on them to take up weapons for the Horde.

item:singed-scale.text: Singed Scale. In Durotar, Singed Scale comes from the charred plates of electrified thunder lizards. Horde warriors bring the scales to prove their endurance and learn defensive combat. Horde veterans judge a warrior by the blows they can bear while shielding allies. In Thunder Ridge, a canyon in western Durotar, lightning hides and thunder lizards crackle with storm energy. Hunting these beasts means enduring relentless electrical shocks and crushing blows. Their blackened scales show that a fighter can withstand punishing assaults and hold firm under pressure. At the Far Watch Post, on the border between Durotar and the Barrens, the veteran warrior Uzzek asks initiates for five scales before teaching them. He believes they need physical toughness before they can learn stances and tactical defense. Bringing the scales proves they have the fortitude to join thick hide, heavy armor, and careful footwork into a firm defense against the Horde’s enemies.

item:skeleton-finger.text: Skeleton Finger. A severed, bony digit scavenged from the walking dead prowling the cursed groves and cemeteries of Duskwood. Madame Eva of Darkshire collects these macabre remnants alongside ghoul fangs and spider venom to craft protective talismans. The cursed woods of Duskwood are overrun by the restless remains of the dead, ranging from skeletal raiders and warriors to necrotic mages and fiends. While ordinary travelers avoid touching the foul remains of the risen dead, fortune tellers and mystics value their cold essence. Madame Eva, the resident seer of Darkshire, gathers these bony fingers to bind their lingering necrotic energies into a ward of retaliatory magic known as the Totem of Infliction.

item:skin-of-sweet-rum.text: Skin of Sweet Rum. A Skin of Sweet Rum is a specialized liquor sourced from the Lion's Pride Inn in Goldshire. It is sought after by Barkeep Daniels in Lakeshire, who is desperate to keep his tavern stocked while Blackrock orcs cut off Redridge from regular trade routes. In the war-weary town of Lakeshire, tavern supplies are running dangerously low. The Blackrock orc invasion has choked the supply roads leading into the Redridge Mountains, leaving Barkeep Daniels scrambling to quench the thirst of beleaguered town guards and refugees. To restock his depleted shelves, Daniels sends travelers across the kingdom to gather regional specialties, including a waterskin filled with the distinctive sweet rum brewed and served in Goldshire's Lion's Pride Inn.

item:skittering-blood.text: Skittering Blood. Skittering Blood is an alchemical reagent harvested from the arachnids dwelling within the Skittering Dark of Silverpine Forest. It serves as a vital toxic ingredient for the Royal Apothecary Society's research into a New Plague designed to eradicate both Scourge and humanity. Harvested from Skitterweb lurkers, strikers, and their broodmother Krethis the Shadowspinner, this venomous hemolymph possesses virulent properties prized by Forsaken alchemists. Apothecary Renferrel discovered that when refined alongside toxins extracted from grizzled bear hearts, the blood forms the base of an exceptionally lethal elixir. The compounds within the fluid demonstrate severe contaminating agents, making it an ideal biological catalyst for the Apothecarium's chemical experiments. Under the direction of Master Apothecary Faranell in the Undercity, the Royal Apothecary Society gathers reagents like Skittering Blood to engineer a devastating New Plague. Faced with overwhelming Scourge hordes and hostile human remnants, the Forsaken pursue biological warfare as an equalizer. Faranell analyzes the blood's toxic potency to devise a contagion potent enough to snuff out unlife and living flesh alike.

item:sleepers-key.text: Sleepers' Key. The Sleepers' Key is one of three enchanted keys crafted by night elf druids to seal their sacred vault within the Talon Den atop Stonetalon Peak. Kept safe inside a hidden cache opened with the Gatekeeper's Key, it is one of the three keys needed to open the druids' hoard. Carved into the heights of Stonetalon Peak, the Talon Den serves as a redoubt and sanctum for the druids of Kalimdor. Aware that their sacred relics and potent treasures might draw unwanted attention, the night elf keepers devised an intricate system of locks and hidden caches to protect their hoard. The Sleepers' Key is one third of that protective ward. Placed within a secluded cache in the den's depths, it can only be retrieved using the Gatekeeper's Key hidden near the threshold. Alongside the Claw Key and the Barrow Key, the Sleepers' Key must be set into the stone locks of the Talon Den Hoard to disperse the ward and reveal the ancient items held within.

item:smoky-iron-ingot.text: Smoky Iron Ingot. At the Windshear dig sites, kobolds smelt Smoky Iron Ingots from ore they pull from the Stonetalon Mountains. Orcish armorers prize the bars as raw material for sturdy mail gear for Horde warriors. Kobolds smelt Smoky Iron Ingots in the Windshear Crag tunnels of the Stonetalon Mountains. They dig ore from the rocky slopes and heat it over crude, smoking fires. Residue and charcoal cling to the bars, but the metal remains dense and strong. Thun'grim Firegaze, a near-blind orc armorer, works from a rugged camp overlooking the Barrens. He asks for these ingots to make armor for proven Horde warriors. Alongside refined iron bars, powdered azurite, and volatile phlogiston, the smoky metal forms a resilient core for Brutal Hauberks.

item:smoldering-embers.text: Smoldering Embers. Smoldering Embers are the glowing, heat-baked remnants retrieved from the raging fire elementals of the Charred Vale. Night elf Sentinels track these cinders as physical proof that the fiery terrors overrunning the devastated woodland are being subdued. The Venture Company's relentless clear-cutting and industrial devastation tore through the Charred Vale, setting the forest ablaze and unleashing destructive fury from deep within the earth. In their wake, elementals of living fire—Burning Ravagers, Burning Destroyers, and wandering Rogue Flame Spirits—surged across the scorched basin. These Smoldering Embers are the lingering, ash-covered cores left behind when an elemental is extinguished, serving as proof that the rampant fires of the vale are being systematically suppressed.
