item:snellig-s-snuffbox.text: Snellig's Snuffbox. Snellig's Snuffbox is a personal keepsake recovered from the restless undead First Mate Snellig among the wreckage of the Lost Fleet. Bringing this trinket back to First Mate Fitzsimmons in Menethil Harbor serves as proof that his cursed former crewmate has finally been put to rest. When the Third Fleet of Kul Tiras ran aground along the northern shores of the Wetlands, its sailors and officers did not find peaceful deaths. Bound by a mysterious and dark power tied to a hidden treasure aboard the ships, the drowned crew rose again as tortured spirits and skeletal undead. Among them was First Mate Snellig, who still haunts the rotting hold of the wreck closest to the coastline. Even in death, he clung to his snuffbox—a small, mundane reminder of his mortal life at sea. For the sole living survivor of the disaster, First Mate Fitzsimmons, recovering this small possession provides tangible proof that at least one of his lost shipmates has been released from an eternity of torment.

item:snufflenose-command-stick.text: Snufflenose Command Stick. The Snufflenose Command Stick is a training rod provided by the goblin entrepreneur Mebok Mizzyrix in Ratchet. It is used to direct trained snufflenose gophers to locate and unearth valuable blueleaf tubers buried deep within Razorfen Kraul. Blueleaf tubers are coveted delicacies across Azeroth, but finding them is nearly impossible without specialized help. Buried in the thorny underground depths of Razorfen Kraul, the roots are entirely hidden from sight. To exploit this lucrative market without braving the quilboar dens himself, the Ratchet merchant Mebok Mizzyrix conditioned keen-scented snufflenose gophers to dig up the tubers. The Snufflenose Command Stick is the tool adventurers use to direct these trained critters, prodding them to sniff out and expose root nodes from up to fifty paces away.

item:snufflenose-owner-s-manual.text: Snufflenose Owner's Manual. The Snufflenose Owner's Manual is an instructional booklet from Marwig Rustbolt of Snuff Inc., kept beside the goblin entrepreneur Mebok Mizzyrix in Ratchet. It outlines how to deploy and direct a trained Snufflenose Gopher to locate rare Blueleaf Tubers buried in Razorfen Kraul. Written by Marwig Rustbolt, owner of Snuff Inc., this short guide details how to work with the company's trained snufflenose gophers. These beasts possess a keen sense of smell capable of detecting subterranean Blueleaf Tubers from fifty paces away. The manual instructs prospectors to release a gopher using a ventilated crate and guide its rooting instincts with a command stick, directing the creature through the hostile thorns and quilboar tunnels of Razorfen Kraul to secure the prized culinary delicacies.

item:sodium-nitrate.text: Sodium Nitrate. At Bael Modan, Sodium Nitrate helps the dwarves blast through the southern Barrens’ stone. Gann Stonespire seeks the chemical for charges against the fortress. Dwarven excavators at Bael Modan use Sodium Nitrate to break through the southern Barrens’ rock. The Bael'dun expedition entered the Stonespire tribe’s ancestral lands with earthmovers and blasting reagents. Riflemen, soldiers, and officers carry the chemical inside the excavation works and nearby fortress.

item:solomon-s-plea-to-darkshire.text: Solomon's Plea to Darkshire. Solomon's Plea to Darkshire is an urgent missive penned by Magistrate Solomon of Lakeshire addressed to Lord Ello Ebonlocke. In the face of mounting Blackrock orc and gnoll threats, the letter begs the leadership of Darkshire to send their elite militia, the Night Watch, to bolster Lakeshire's strained defenses. Lakeshire stands on the brink of being overwhelmed by invading Blackrock orcs, gnolls, and murlocs, with virtually no official reinforcements arriving from Stormwind. In desperation, Magistrate Solomon drafted this formal plea to Mayor Ello Ebonlocke of Darkshire, petitioning him to dispatch members of the Night Watch northward into Redridge. The document reflects the severe breakdown of central military support across southern Azeroth, forcing individual human settlements to look to one another for mutual survival.

item:solomon-s-plea-to-westfall.text: Solomon's Plea to Westfall. Solomon's Plea to Westfall is an urgent written appeal penned by Magistrate Solomon of Lakeshire. Desperate for reinforcements against the Blackrock orcs and gnolls, Solomon sends this dispatch to Gryan Stoutmantle in Westfall hoping the newly formed People's Militia can lend aid while Stormwind's royal army fails to respond. As the threat of the Blackrock clan and hostile gnolls looms large over Redridge, Magistrate Solomon finds himself dangerously isolated in Lakeshire. The royal army from Stormwind has inexplicably failed to arrive in force to defend the region's borders. Unable to wait for official support from the kingdom's capital, Solomon pens this plea in a desperate bid to recruit assistance from outside the regular military structure. Having caught word of a volunteer defense force coalescing across Elwynn to the west, he turns directly to the People's Militia. The message is addressed directly to Gryan Stoutmantle, a veteran warrior organizing the frontier defense of Westfall. Solomon hopes Stoutmantle can spare fighters to reinforce Lakeshire until Stormwind's crown finally sends regular reserves. Entrusted to an adventurer acting as courier, the document reflects the fracturing administrative coordination across Stormwind's outlying territories, where local magistrates are left to negotiate mutual aid agreements on their own initiative.

item:soran-ruk-fragment.text: Soran'ruk Fragment. In Blackfathom Deeps, cultists hold shards of Soran'ruk, a shattered prison orb. The pieces still carry fel energy from the demon once bound inside. Soran'ruk's prison orb was broken apart after the demon fell from favor with the Burning Legion. Demons who displease their masters may have their spirits sealed in orbs, then given to fel spellcasters as sources of power. The Twilight's Hammer cultists in the submerged ruins of Blackfathom Deeps possess smaller shards from one half of the orb. They draw on the lingering demonic essence for their own workings.

item:southsea-treasure.text: Southsea Treasure. The Southsea Treasure is a valuable hoard kept deep within the hold of the Southsea Freebooter vessel, the Tide Razor. Sought by Wrenix the Wretched in Ratchet, retrieving it tests the lockpicking and infiltration skills of fledgling thieves. Anchored along the Merchant Coast south of Ratchet, the pirate vessel Tide Razor serves as a forward base and training ground for the Southsea Freebooters. Stashed deep in its lowest hold lies a coveted stash of plunder known as the Southsea Treasure. Wrenix the Wretched, a goblin scoundrel operating out of Ratchet, considers it the ultimate test for aspiring pickpockets. According to Wrenix, the last five operatives sent to filch the chest returned in pieces, owing to the alert pirates aboard and a surprisingly ferocious guardian guarding the hold.

item:spectral-comb.text: Spectral Comb. The Spectral Comb is an ethereal grooming tool used to interact with the restless dead of Duskwood. Fashioned to pass through intangible forms, it is brought to the sorrowful spirit Blind Mary to harvest strands of ghost hair. Normal implements cannot touch or groom a spirit, making gathering ethereal materials nearly impossible for mortal craftsmen. The Spectral Comb is specially suited to interact with ghostly forms, gliding through otherwise intangible tresses. It is carried south of Darkshire to the ruined farmstead where the weeping ghost Blind Mary wails in isolation. Finding solace in the familiar act of grooming her ruined hair, Mary willingly uses the comb, leaving behind the spectral fibers needed to weave Ghost Hair Thread.

item:spells-of-shadow.text: Spells of Shadow. Beneath Orgrimmar, Spells of Shadow rests in the hands of Searing Blade cultists. The Forsaken leadership in the Undercity wants the grimoire recovered. Searing Blade cultists keep Spells of Shadow among their guarded treasures in Ragefire Chasm. The splinter cult is tied to the Shadow Council, and its members wield dark rites granted by demon masters of the Burning Legion. The book holds shadow and fel sorcery. Cultists and warlocks keep it close as they plot beneath the Horde in Durotar. Word of the Searing Blade's demonic gifts reached the Undercity's royal quarters. Lady Sylvanas Windrunner and her dreadlord lieutenant, Varimathras, decided the relics were wasted on cultists with lesser vision. Varimathras sends Horde adventurers into Ragefire Chasm to seize Spells of Shadow and its companion tome, Incantations from the Nether. Their power is meant to serve the Forsaken cause against the Scourge and the Lich King.

item:spotted-sunfish.text: Spotted Sunfish. Spotted Sunfish are freshwater fish native to Lake Everstill in the Redridge Mountains. Renowned locally for their flavor, they are a staple commodity for Lakeshire's docks, though the growing murloc infestation makes procuring them hazardous. Lake Everstill has long been celebrated for its spotted sunfish, which fetch a dependable price among local merchants and visitors alike. Dockmaster Baren keeps a steady trade in them at the Lakeshire piers, supplying food and commerce to a town under strain. However, the aggressive murloc tribes prowling the shallows have disrupted routine fishing, often stockpiling catches of their own that adventurers must recover by force.

item:stalker-claws.text: Stalker Claws. Stalker Claws are the talons harvested from the prairie stalkers roaming the rolling plains of Mulgore. Tauren shamans use them as vital components in carving traditional cleansing totems to purify tainted water wells. The grassy steppes of Mulgore are home to deadly natural predators, among them the stealthy prairie stalkers. These beasts survive through raw instinct and lethal precision, an essential balance within the Earth Mother's design. Mull Thunderhorn, seeking to heal the blighted land, requires these claws not out of malice toward the animals, but because the pure, natural ferocity with which they hunt holds the spiritual resonance necessary to counteract artificial corruption. When goblin ventures began drilling and mining across central Kalimdor, chemical poisons seeped deep into the subterranean waters feeding the ancestral tauren wells. The Thunderhorn Water Well in particular fell prey to vile taint. By binding Stalker Claws and Cougar Claws into a Thunderhorn Cleansing Totem, tribal shamans create a spiritual conduit capable of scouring the muck and unnatural sludge out of the earth's natural springs.

item:steelgrill-s-tools.text: Steelgrill's Tools. Steelgrill's Tools are a specialized set of mechanic implements requisitioned for Beldin Steelgrill, the master technician of Steelgrill's Depot. Renowned for pushing siege engines—and his own equipment—to their limits, Beldin frequently breaks gear and relies on shipments from nearby Kharanos to keep his workshop running. Beldin Steelgrill is widely regarded as one of the finest siege engine technicians in Dun Morogh, but his aggressive repair style is infamous among local merchants. Working tirelessly on armored tanks and mechanical contraptions, Beldin tends to destroy delicate equipment almost as fast as it can be forged. Between snapping arclight spanners and stripping fang-ratchets, the mechanic is constantly placing fresh orders in Kharanos to keep his repair benches stocked. This particular delivery of tools is vital for keeping Ironforge's war machines operational. At his depot northeast of Kharanos, Beldin is actively servicing combat vehicles for seasoned drivers like Pilot Stonegear. Without freshly supplied wrenches and ratchets, critical siege engines would sit half-assembled in the snow, leaving both the depot and local defenses stalled.

item:steelsnap-s-rib.text: Steelsnap's Rib. Steelsnap's Rib is a grim trophy taken from the carcass of the ferocious hyena Steelsnap in Thousand Needles. Brought back to Thunder Bluff, it serves as physical proof that a creature deemed outside the Earthmother's blessing has been put down. Most tauren hunts are undertaken for sustenance, for honor, or to seek harmony with nature. Steelsnap, however, represents a different kind of quarry. Roaming the canyon floor of Thousand Needles south of Camp E'thok, this vicious alpha hyena terrorizes peaceful wildlife and rallies packs of lesser predators to senseless bloodshed. When the hunt master Melor Stonehoof on Hunter Rise marks Steelsnap for death, he demands a heavy bone—Steelsnap's rib—as undeniable confirmation that the tyrant has been slain and the canyon cleansed of its blight.

item:stolen-silver.text: Stolen Silver. At the Crossroads, a strongbox of Horde silver has gone missing from the guard tower. Sunscale raptors carried the coins to their nests at the Raptor Grounds south of Ratchet. Sunscale raptors carried a strongbox of silver from the Crossroads guard tower. The coins were meant as pay for the garrison guards. The raptors dragged the lockbox to their communal nests at the Raptor Grounds, south of Ratchet. Gazrog and the other overseers cannot explain why the predators took it. The theft leaves them wondering whether the raptors prize shiny things or possess a cunning beyond that of ordinary wild beasts.

item:stone-of-relu.text: Stone of Relu. In the Wetlands, the Stone of Relu is lost to a raptor after an ambush. Archaeologist Flagongut believes it can unlock secrets within ancient fossils. Explorers' League work uncovered the Stone of Relu. Archaeologist Flagongut believes it can decipher prehistoric fossils gathered from Kalimdor and the Eastern Kingdoms. He means to use it on his Wetlands specimens and on the fossil Prospector Remtravel unearthed in Darkshore. Archaeologist Flagongut was traveling along the Wetlands roads to meet Prospector Whelgar when mottled raptors ambushed him. In the scramble, the relic was lost and swallowed by one of the beasts. The League now seeks the marsh raptors so the ancient stone can be cut from their gullets.

item:stonetalon-sap.text: Stonetalon Sap. Stonetalon Sap is a sticky, potent substance harvested directly from the lumbering sap beasts that roam the craggy heights of the Stonetalon Mountains. It serves as a key reagent for the Darkspear witch doctor Jin'Zil, who uses its raw woodland properties to concoct a spiteful brew.

item:stormpike-banner.text: Stormpike Banner. The Stormpike Banner is a military standard hidden deep within the treacherous Icewing Cavern in Alterac Valley. Alliance recruits must brave wild harpies to recover it as an initiation trial, proving they are worthy to wear the Stormpike insignia. To officially join the ranks of the Stormpike expedition in Alterac Valley, prospective recruits must prove their mettle before they ever clash with the Frostwolf orcs. Lieutenant Haggerdin sends newly arrived Alliance soldiers into the Icewing Caverns, situated southwest of Dun Baldar. Planted deep inside this frozen subterranean den, the Stormpike Banner serves as a testing ground: anyone brave enough to brave the native harpies, seize the standard, and bring it back alive earns the rank and insignia of an initiate in the Stormpike Guard.

item:stormpike-s-request.text: Stormpike's Request. Mountaineer Stormpike sends a written commission from Loch Modan to Stormwind City. He asks Furen Longbeard to craft him a shield of exceptional dwarven quality. Mountaineer Stormpike needs a sturdy shield while stationed in Loch Modan. He trusts no ordinary smith with the work and asks Furen Longbeard, whose craft he greatly admires. Furen now lives among the humans in Stormwind's Dwarven District, having left Ironforge. Stormpike assumes a king's ransom drew him south, so traveling adventurers carry the commission across the kingdoms. Furen Longbeard receives Stormpike's letter in Stormwind's Dwarven District and agrees to make the shield. A proud and established member of the Stormpike clan, known across Khaz Modan for its martial grit and wealth, Furen welcomes word and business from his northern homeland. He sets to work on the mountaineer's order.

item:stormwind-armor-marker.text: Stormwind Armor Marker. Stormwind Armor Marker lets those who aid the realm claim crafted gear from sanctioned artisans. Sara Timberlain accepts one at the Eastvale Logging Camp. Stormwind's commanders issue armor markers to those who serve the realm. Keeping law and order across Elwynn Forest stretches Stormwind's resources thin, so commanders sometimes use these official requisition slips instead of handing out standard gear at military outposts. A marker confirms the bearer's service and authorizes local craftsmen under contract to provide tailored armor. At the Eastvale Logging Camp, Sara Timberlain and other artisans work under commission from the Stormwind Army. The camp lies on Elwynn's eastern frontier, where they use local materials to make protective cloth and leather garments. Present a marker there to receive custom-fitted defense for guarding the surrounding woodlands.

item:stoutmantle-s-response-to-solomon.text: Stoutmantle's Response to Solomon. Gryan Stoutmantle sends a hard answer from Sentinel Hill to Lakeshire. His dispatch tells Magistrate Solomon that the People's Militia cannot spare a single soldier for Redridge Mountains. Magistrate Solomon of Lakeshire asks Sentinel Hill for reinforcements as Blackrock orcs and gnolls press his town. Gryan Stoutmantle replies in writing with sorrow for Lakeshire's losses, but Westfall faces a war of its own. The People's Militia formed from desperation after the Crown withdrew its garrison. Farmers and volunteers now fight the Defias Brotherhood alone. Stoutmantle's forces are already bleeding and stretched thin, with no men to spare for another abandoned frontier.

item:strange-smelling-powder.text: Strange Smelling Powder. Strange Smelling Powder is an enigmatic residue uncovered during investigations into suspicious sabotage around Loch Modan. Feared to be an unstable demolition agent, it prompts Chief Engineer Hinderweir to send an urgent courier north to seek out a demolition expert. Discovered amid signs of sabotage threatening Loch Modan's infrastructure, this peculiar powder immediately raised alarm for Chief Engineer Hinderweir. Its pungent odor and fine consistency suggest an engineered demolition compound rather than standard mining blast powder. Unsure of the mixture's chemical nature or origin, Hinderweir refuses to tamper with it himself, knowing that even a slight spark could trigger disaster.

item:strangely-marked-box.text: Strangely Marked Box. Along Darkshore, a Strangely Marked Box is found among cargo on dead sea turtles. Its runes point to the naga and show that the turtles did not come ashore by chance. Dead sea turtles and other sea creatures wash up on Darkshore's beaches. Some carry broken harnesses and carriages strapped to their shells. Sealed boxes marked with foreign, winding runes lie among the wreckage. Greymist murlocs often shelter in the hollow ribs and broken wagons, feeding on the carcasses and guarding what remains.

item:strigid-owl-feather.text: Strigid Owl Feather. Strigid Owl Feathers are gathered from the owls in Teldrassil's boughs. Zenn Foulhoof seeks them for his covert dealings.

item:sturdy-dragonmaw-shinbone.text: Sturdy Dragonmaw Shinbone. Sturdy Dragonmaw Shinbones are durable skeletal trophies gathered from the renegade Dragonmaw orcs in the Wetlands. Required by armor crafter Velora Nitely in the Undercity, they serve as reinforcement struts for bespoke warrior armor. When forging brutal leg guards for frontline warriors, smiths require raw components that can endure severe punishment. In the Undercity, Velora Nitely prizes the skeletal density of the renegade Dragonmaw orcs entrenched at the Angerfang Encampment in the central Wetlands. Dragonmaw orcs are known for their thick, sturdy frames, making their shins well suited to serve as structural bracers. However, not every collected bone can withstand the strain; warriors must test each piece with their bare hands, discarding those that snap under pressure.

item:sully-balloo-s-letter.text: Sully Balloo's Letter. Sully Balloo's Letter is a waterlogged, tender missive recovered from the sunken remains of a dwarven soldier beneath the Thandol Span. Addressed to his wife Sara in Ironforge, it represents the quiet personal tragedies lingering beneath the grand conflicts of Khaz Modan. Beneath the massive stone pillars of the Thandol Span, connecting the Wetlands to the Arathi Highlands, lies the skeletal remains of a dwarf pinned deep under the rushing water. Clutched in his grasp is a fragile, waterlogged envelope containing this letter. Written with painstaking care in his final days or hours, it begins with the poignant words, 'My dear Sara....' Though the parchment has suffered from prolonged submersion, the ink still holds the enduring love of a dwarven defender who never made it back home to the city of Ironforge.

item:sunscorched-shell.text: Sunscorched Shell. Beneath Highperch, wyvern eggs leave shells hardened by Thousand Needles' desert heat. Armorer Mathiel in Darnassus uses them to make lacquer for mail links. Highperch wyverns lay eggs on the mesa needles of southern Kalimdor. Beneath their roosts, discarded shell fragments bake in the desert sun and searing winds. Their brittle remains hold a natural resilience that draws the attention of skilled artisans. In Darnassus, armorer Mathiel studies methods pioneered by his colleague, the dwarf smith Furen Longbeard. Mathiel processes the shells into a fine lacquer for mail armor. Applied to the metal links, the coating strengthens them without burdening the wearer.

item:super-reaper-6000-blueprints.text: Super Reaper 6000 Blueprints. The Super Reaper 6000 Blueprints are the technical schematics for an enormous mechanized woodcutter deployed by the Venture Company in Stonetalon Mountains. Designed under the supervision of the gnome engineer Gerenzo Wrenchwhistle, the plans are heavily coveted by his disgruntled goblin rivals. The Venture Company's relentless clear-cutting operation in Windshear Crag relies on massive mechanized lumber harvesters known as Super Reapers. To the utter dismay of traditional goblin engineers, the company placed a gnome named Gerenzo in charge of designing the Super Reaper 6000 model. These blueprints contain the schematics for the contraption, carried by Venture Co. operators working the machinery across the crag. When the goblin engineer Ziz Fizziks was ousted from the operation, he was quickly hired by Sputtervalve to steal the designs. However, deciphering Gerenzo's dense, eccentric gnomish technical notations proves to be almost as difficult as taking the blueprints by force.

item:supplies-for-sven.text: Supplies for Sven. Supplies for Sven is a bundle of vital provisions packaged in Darkshire and destined for Sven Yorgen's secluded camp. Surrounded by the horrors of Duskwood, Sven and his small band rely on sympathetic townspeople like the Carevin family to sustain their vigil against the shadows. Carrying survival gear and basic necessities through Duskwood is no simple chore. Sven Yorgen and his handful of followers camp in the northwestern wilderness of the woods, far from the safety of Darkshire. Their numbers are so depleted and their watch so demanding that they cannot spare a single fighter to make the trek into town. This parcel represents a lifeline sent by the Carevin family, ensuring that the isolated camp has the food, bandages, and materials needed to hold their ground.

item:surena-s-choker.text: Surena's Choker. In Stormwind, Gakin the Darkbinder seeks the choker he gave his former apprentice, Surena Caledon. After Surena fled to join the Defias Brotherhood, Gakin sent aspiring acolytes to take it back by force. Gakin the Darkbinder works quietly beneath the Slaughtered Lamb in Stormwind, where he took Surena Caledon on as a promising student of the dark arts. Drawn to her youthful charm and magical aptitude, he gave her a valuable bloodstone choker to aid her studies. Surena abandoned her training and fled with Erlan Drudgemoor, a rogue aligned with the Defias Brotherhood. Gakin will not leave a potent artifact in a traitor’s hands. He sends initiates seeking mastery over the void to find Surena at the Brackwell Pumpkin Patch and reclaim the necklace by force. Their deed will show where true loyalty lies.

item:swoop-gizzard.text: Swoop Gizzard. A swoop gizzard is an organ harvested from the predatory birds soaring over Mulgore. Highly sought after for traditional folk remedies, it serves as a crucial ingredient for cleansing deadly toxins. Swoops are predatory avian hunters native to the plains and mesas of Mulgore, known for their keen eyesight and scavenging nature. While their feathers and meat serve everyday uses for the tauren, their internal organs—particularly the gizzard—are prized by herbalists and healers. When combined with other potent animal remnants like cougar bones and wolf hearts, the dense muscular organ aids in neutralizing venomous animal bites and halting festering systemic infections. In Bloodhoof Village, the medicine worker Maur Raincaller fell prey to the legendary plainstrider Mazzranache, suffering a vicious, venomous wound to his shoulder. Falling into delirium from the creeping poison, Maur relies on a swoop gizzard alongside a prairie wolf heart, a flatland cougar femur, and a plainstrider scale to concoct a curative poultice capable of expelling the beast's lethal venom.

item:tablet-of-verga.text: Tablet of Verga. In Skull Rock, the Tablet of Verga lies in Burning Blade hands, its demonic runes sought by warlocks in Orgrimmar. The Tablet of Verga bears ritual runes for summoning creatures of the Nether and bending them to a master's will. The Burning Blade cult stole the stone and hid it in a chest inside Skull Rock, just east of Orgrimmar. Warlocks in the Cleft of Shadow seek it to study the markings and learn to summon a voidwalker. Recovering it also keeps the cult from gaining that same advantage.

item:tainted-heart.text: Tainted Heart. In Teldrassil, Denalan gives adventurers a heart still troubled by corruption. Though its outer foul moss is gone, lingering energies remain, and he seeks to cleanse them with rich soil. Teldrassil's natural balance is troubled by a malady that warps its plants and beasts. After foul moss is stripped from a blighted growth, Denalan gives adventurers the Tainted Heart within. Darkness still clings to its tissue. Denalan hopes specially prepared, nutrient-rich earth can counter the taint and restore what was corrupted.

item:tainted-keg.text: Tainted Keg. The Tainted Keg is a barrel of stolen dwarven stout laced with a lethal Forsaken brew concocted by Apothecary Lydon. Delivered under the guise of refreshments to imprisoned human farmers in Tarren Mill, it serves as a gruesome field test for the Royal Apothecary Society's developing poisons. The keg began its existence as a barrel of Shindigger Stout, plundered from the dwarven riflemen entrenched at Dun Garok. Rather than drinking it, Apothecary Lydon contaminated the hearty ale with his newly refined Elixir of Agony. By lacing an ordinary beverage, the Forsaken crafted an insidious vector designed to slip past suspicion, turning a familiar comforts of the living into a swift death sentence.

item:tainted-letter.text: Tainted Letter. Drusilla La Salle sends the Tainted Letter to human warlock initiates near Northshire Abbey. It bears her seal and directs them to seek her tutelage discreetly. The Tainted Letter bears Drusilla La Salle’s insignia and reaches initiates returning from nearby kobold camps. While priests, paladins, and soldiers train openly across Northshire Abbey’s lawns, fel practitioners must keep their path quiet. The letter directs novice warlocks to find their mentor near the abbey grounds without drawing the notice of town guards or clerics. Drusilla La Salle meets her pupils on the fringes, where sentries are less likely to pry. Elwynn’s ordinary folk distrust warlocks, so the letter begins a lesson in discipline. Arcane and nether magic bring the risk of corruption. Those who commune with denizens of the Twisting Nether must temper ambition with patient self-control.

item:tainted-memorandum.text: Tainted Memorandum. The Tainted Memorandum is a discreet note handed to novice gnome warlocks starting out in Coldridge Valley. Penned by the warlock trainer Alamar Grimm, it urges the reader to cast aside traditional paths and seek out the true power offered by the dark arts. In the chilly dwarven outpost of Anvilmar, practitioners of fel magic are neither celebrated nor widely trusted. For young gnomes dabbling in forbidden arts, the Tainted Memorandum serves as an invitation from Alamar Grimm. The message rejects reliance on the Holy Light or mundane martial steel, pointing instead to the fall of Gnomeregan as proof that conventional methods and tinkering have failed their people. To Grimm, relying on dwarven charity is a dead end; gnomes must seize undeniable power and summon unquestioning minions if they ever hope to secure their own future.

item:talisman-of-corruption.text: Talisman of Corruption. In Darkshore, Xabraxxis uses the Talisman of Corruption to turn the Blackwood furbolgs against their former allies. The satyr keeps it in his personal pouch, where its magic binds the tribe to fel madness. Auberdine's night elves have long sought the cause of the Blackwood furbolgs' turn against their former allies. Thundris Windweaver found that satyrs had brought about the tribe's fall. With talismans like this, demonic agents spread corrupting sorcery through the wilderness, tainting food and twisting peaceful forest spirits into frenzied beasts. The devices channel fel magic that grips the minds and wills of local tribes.

item:tallonkai-s-jewel.text: Tallonkai's Jewel. On Teldrassil, Tallonkai's Jewel is lost from its druidic talisman. Ferocitas the Dream Eater prizes the emerald, which is needed to mend the Emerald Dreamcatcher. Tallonkai Swiftroot received the Emerald Dreamcatcher from Gaerolas Talvethen, warden of the druids in the Ban'ethil Barrow Den. The talisman is a powerful focus that draws energy from the Emerald Dream. When it was damaged, someone pried its radiant central emerald free and carried it into eastern Teldrassil. Ferocitas the Dream Eater, a corrupted Gnarlpine leader, took the jewel and made it into a necklace. Its green light glimmered in the forest gloom, but its harmony with the Emerald Dream meant nothing to the furbolg. To Ferocitas, it was only a trophy until it could be recovered.

item:taming-rod.text: Taming Rod. In Durotar, Taming Rods help novice hunters learn to command beasts. Trainers give them to students so they can practice before forming lasting bonds with animal companions. In Razor Hill, trainers such as Thotar give Taming Rods to aspiring orc and troll hunters. These enchanted tools help novices who cannot yet bind a wild creature permanently. A rod pacifies a regional predator, such as a dire mottled boar or an armored scorpid, so the hunter can practice giving commands and fighting beside an animal companion. The bond lasts only briefly, leaving the student free to learn without forming a lasting tie to the beast. Each Taming Rod's magic fades after a short while, and each is attuned to specific kinds of wild beasts. Novices face successive trials against different temperaments, from docile foragers to aggressive venomous hunters. When a student has shown they can command them, the rod goes back to the trainer. The trainer then teaches the student to tame, call, and dismiss lifelong companions without an artifact.

item:tattered-manuscript.text: Tattered Manuscript. The Tattered Manuscript consists of loose, vandalized pages torn from the singular copy of the Tome of the Cabal. Hidden away in the dusty depths of southern Kalimdor, this battered portion of the text holds arcane secrets vital to warlocks seeking mastery over felhunters. The Tome of the Cabal was once an intact, unique volume safeguarded within the fallen kingdom of Lordaeron. At some point, an unknown defiler ripped almost half of the treatise directly from its binding. While the surviving spine and remainder of the book—now known as the Moldy Tome—were shipped south toward Khaz Modan and lost at sea, these torn parchment leaves drifted far across the Great Sea into Kalimdor, ultimately falling into the hands of the Galak centaur inside Splithoof Hold. Kept within a battered chest deep within the labyrinthine caverns of Splithoof Hold, the manuscript survived the harsh arid winds of Thousand Needles. Despite its fragile, tattered state, practitioners of the dark arts—both Alliance warlocks working with Krom Stoutarm in Ironforge and Horde practitioners aiding Jorah Annison in the Undercity—brave the aggressive centaur to reunite these lost leaves with the Moldy Tome. Once combined, the completed treatise contains the dark rituals necessary to summon and bind a demonic felhunter.

item:tazan-s-satchel.text: Tazan's Satchel. Near Ratchet, Tazan carries a locked satchel as he deals with pirates along the coast. The Shattered Hand wants the secret information inside. Tazan deals with pirates camped along the Barrens coast near Ratchet. Therzok, a guild master of the Shattered Hand beneath Orgrimmar in the Cleft of Shadow, takes notice. The guild seeks covert power beyond Warchief Thrall's cautious diplomacy, and marks Tazan for elimination to seize the intelligence in his satchel.

item:tear-of-the-moons.text: Tear of the Moons. At Bael Modan in the southern Barrens, dwarven excavators have unearthed the Tear of the Moons. Its strange power draws Feegly into obsession, while General Twinbraid fears what the crystal can do. Dwarven excavators unearthed the Tear of the Moons during the first digging at Bael Modan. The crystal's strange radiance captivated the miners, especially Feegly. He claimed it gave him great strength, then grew unstable and turned against his comrades. General Twinbraid, commander of the expedition, feared the relic's influence and declared it cursed. He took the crystal and locked it in his personal strongbox at Bael'dun Keep. Then he cast Feegly out into the Barrens.

item:tear-of-tilloa.text: Tear of Tilloa. In Duskwood, the Tear of Tilloa grows on the Mistmantle estate near Darkshire. Its alchemical use draws interest from those seeking rare reagents. The Tear of Tilloa grows on the grounds of Stalvan Mistmantle’s estate outside Darkshire. Duskwood’s soil has turned hostile to wholesome vegetation, yet the small white flower persists among the shadowed plots. It grows rarely and in a secluded place, drawing those who seek uncommon reagents beyond lawful markets.

item:techbot-s-memory-core.text: Techbot's Memory Core. Techbot's Memory Core is the polarized central repository of Tinkmaster Overspark's mechanical assistant, Techbot. Recovered from the malfunctioning automaton within the corrupted depths of Gnomeregan, it contains the critical data Overspark hopes to use to reverse the machine's reversed, negatronic behavior. Before the catastrophe that forced the gnomes into exile, Techbot served Tinkmaster Overspark and his fellow inventors as an indispensable assistant, packed with gizmos and encyclopedic data. When Gnomeregan fell, an errant electrical discharge jolted the automaton, inverting its positronic brain into a hostile negatronic state. Driven mad by the reversal, Techbot now wanders the tainted halls of the city attacking anyone in sight. Recovering its memory core is Overspark's only hope for analyzing the malfunction and restoring his prized creation to its senses.

item:telescopic-lens.text: Telescopic Lens. Gazlowe needs the Telescopic Lens to finish the observatory telescope above Ratchet’s harbor. Southsea pirates took it from a ship, and the lens remains in their camp south of town. Ratchet is known chiefly for ruthless commerce, but its overseer and chief engineer, Gazlowe, has greater mechanical ambitions. His observatory rises above the harbor to house a telescope for watching maritime traffic and the stars. The larger lens came safely overland from Durotar. The smaller, vital lens traveled by sea, where Southsea Freebooters prey on merchant lanes off the Barrens coast. The Southsea Freebooters took anything of value when they raided the transport ship, including the delicate optics. The pirates may have left the lens among the clutter of their beachside camp south of Ratchet because they could not appreciate its craft or did not know how to pawn it. Gazlowe needs the unblemished glass brought back so his observation deck can come into focus.

item:teronis-journal.text: Teronis' Journal. Teronis' Journal is a field notebook recovered from the remains of a night elf scout in Ashenvale. Found alongside the slain investigator, it documents his search for a mysterious gem and serves as vital evidence for the Sentinels in Astranaar. A longtime friend of Raene Wolfrunner aiding the Sentinels, Teronis ventured into the wilds of Ashenvale seeking a gem for a rod he believed could slow the furbolg attacks on his people. His mission ended abruptly when he fell in the field, surrounded by aggressive creatures near the shore. Recovered from his personal effects, this journal remains in remarkably good condition despite the violence of his demise. It outlines his findings regarding a radiant gem that once formed part of that rod, providing Astranaar's defenders with the vital trail needed to see his unfinished mission through.

item:tharil-zun-s-head.text: Tharil'zun's Head. This grizzly trophy is the severed head of Tharil'zun, leader of the Blackrock orc Outrunners occupying Stonewatch. Marshal Marris demands it as irrefutable proof that the commander terrorizing the Redridge approaches has been slain. The Blackrock orcs entrenched within Stonewatch Keep have exerted ruthless pressure on Lakeshire, raiding farms and ambushing travelers along the roads. At the vanguard of these raiding parties were the Blackrock Outrunners, orchestrated by Tharil'zun. Because the garrison in Lakeshire cannot afford to act on rumors or partial victories, Marshal Marris demands concrete proof of the leader's demise. Bringing him Tharil'zun's severed head demonstrates that the coordinated ambushes from the keep have suffered a major blow.

item:tharnariun-s-hope.text: Tharnariun's Hope. In Darkshore, Tharnariun Treetender seeks a way to study the sick thistle bears and find a cure. His trap calms them long enough to bring them to his camp. Tharnariun Treetender made a calming trap to study the sick thistle bears. Across Darkshore, a mysterious affliction has left the animals increasingly frenzied and violent. Tharnariun hopes to cure them rather than see them killed. Set on the ground, Tharnariun's Hope casts a soothing light. A rabid thistle bear that crosses it grows calm for a time and can follow a traveler back to Tharnariun's camp for treatment.

item:the-book-of-ur.text: The Book of Ur. The Book of Ur is a scholarly magical treatise penned by the late Dalaran wizard Ur, detailing his research into strange extradimensional entities. Left behind in Shadowfang Keep, it fell into the hands of Archmage Arugal before drawing the keen interest of Forsaken researchers in the Undercity. Before Dalaran fell to the Scourge, Ur was renowned among the Kirin Tor for his esoteric investigations into other planes of existence and otherworldly creatures. Despite his fascination with extraplanar magic, Ur was guided by caution and ethical restraint, choosing to record his discoveries rather than recklessly breach the veil between worlds. Tragically, when the Scourge assaulted the violet city, his magical prowess and moral hesitations were not enough to save him.

item:the-collector-s-schedule.text: The Collector's Schedule. Near the Brackwell Pumpkin Patch, The Collector's Schedule marks when illicit gold shipments move through Elwynn Forest. Gnolls carry the handwritten itinerary, and Marshal Dughan recognizes the name it records. The Collector's Schedule marks dates and times for gold shipments from Elwynn's mines. Stormwind has not officially worked the mines for months, driven off by banditry and creature incursions, yet ore still leaves in an orderly flow. The itinerary names the days and hours when a figure called The Collector receives each shipment. The trail points to a camp near the Brackwell Pumpkin Patch in eastern Elwynn Forest. When Marshal Dughan sees the schedule, he recognizes the Collector's name. Who pays for the stolen gold remains unknown.

item:the-embalmer-s-heart.text: The Embalmer's Heart. The Embalmer's Heart is an unholy relic beating within the undead corpse of Eliza, buried deep in Duskwood. Once belonging to a grief-stricken alchemist known as the Embalmer, it was transplanted through dark magic to revive his deceased wife, becoming the primary anchor of his twisted power. According to the folklore of Darkshire, the Embalmer was once a gentle alchemist whose mind shattered upon the passing of his beloved wife, Eliza. Desperate to reclaim her from the grave, he turned to foul sorceries and cut out his own heart, placing it inside Eliza's lifeless chest. While the unholy transfusion successfully stirred her corpse back to unlife, the resurrection twisted her into a ravenous creature consumed by an insatiable hunger for living human flesh, forcing the horror-stricken alchemist to inter her once more within the earth.

item:the-general-s-response.text: The General's Response. General Marcus Jonathan sends word to Lakeshire while Redridge waits for aid. His dispatch acknowledges Magistrate Solomon's plea against the Blackrock orcs and gnolls, but offers no immediate reinforcements from Stormwind. Magistrate Solomon sends an urgent plea to Stormwind City for troops to defend Redridge from the gathering Blackrock orc clans and Gnoll warbands. General Marcus Jonathan replies that the plea has been forwarded to the throne, but no soldiers are being sent now. He orders the letter returned to Lakeshire. Solomon is left troubled by Stormwind's delay and suspicious that something is wrong with its leaders.

item:the-lich-s-spellbook.text: The Lich's Spellbook. The Lich's Spellbook is a volume of necromantic lore kept within a chest on the island in Brightwater Lake. Recovered for Bethor Iceshard in the Undercity, the tome reveals the true identity and immense magical power of a reclusive undead lich dwelling just north of the Forsaken capital. On an isolated island in Brightwater Lake stands an enigmatic lich surrounded by skeletal guardians. Though free-willed, this sorcerer distrusts the outside world, mistaking all other undead for thralls of the Scourge and ordering his minions to destroy any who approach. Bethor Iceshard, seeking gifted necromancers to bolster the Forsaken ranks beneath Queen Sylvanas Windrunner, tasked an emissary with infiltrating the island camp to retrieve the lich's spellbook. Through its study, Bethor hoped to discern the master's magical aptitude and uncover who he was before death took Lordaeron.

item:the-state-of-lakeshire.text: The State of Lakeshire. The State of Lakeshire is an urgent written report penned by Magistrate Solomon detailing the desperate military crisis gripping the town of Lakeshire. Intended directly for General Marcus Jonathan in Stormwind, the document pleads for the capital to deploy royal army reinforcements before the Redridge settlement falls. Penned by Magistrate Solomon amid relentless attacks on Redridge, 'The State of Lakeshire' outlines the dire circumstances threatening the township. Besieged by hostile Blackrock orcs and gnolls, Lakeshire lacks the local manpower to hold its borders indefinitely. Entrusted to trusted couriers traveling the road west to Elwynn Forest, this dispatch carries Solomon's formal request for the Stormwind Army to intervene and preserve the eastern reach of the kingdom. Upon delivery to General Marcus Jonathan at Stormwind's gates, the general acknowledges Solomon's noble standing and the gravity of the report. However, Jonathan cannot mobilize the army unilaterally. Military deployments require the explicit consent of the crown, forcing Lakeshire's urgent plea to wait upon high-level council with the young King and the regent Bolvar Fordragon.

item:theramore-medal.text: Theramore Medal. At Northwatch Hold, Theramore Medal marks service among the marines and officers defending the outpost along the Merchant Coast. The insignia bears Theramore’s mark and identifies the Alliance garrison. Marines, marksmen, commandos, and officers serving from Northwatch Hold carry stamped medals bearing Theramore’s mark. The soldiers are loyal to Lady Jaina Proudmoore’s realm. For the human troops on the cliffs above the Barrens, the medals show that their service is legitimate and their authority comes from Theramore. Others see the tokens as trophies from an overzealous foreign garrison, one that treats every vessel approaching the coast as a mortal threat. Northwatch Hold’s gun batteries menace ships along the Merchant Coast, often bombarding privateers and merchantmen alike. After losing ships to the guns, Ratchet privateer Captain Thalo'thas Brightsun seeks the medals. He wants proof that Northwatch’s trigger-happy ranks have paid in blood for sinking his ships, and that the soldiers responsible have been slain in retribution.

item:thick-bear-fur.text: Thick Bear Fur. Thick Bear Fur is a prized pelt gathered from the cold-hardened bears roaming the snowdrifts of Dun Morogh. Coveted for its heat retention, it is commonly used by traveling scouts and soldiers to craft insulation and warm bedding against the bitter alpine freeze. The bears prowling the ridges of Dun Morogh endure some of the harshest snowfields in the Eastern Kingdoms. Their thick, resilient coats provide vital protection from blizzards, making the pelt an invaluable resource for locals and travelers alike. Rather than being discarded as scrap, these heavy pelts are regularly harvested by hunters and used to line clothes, insulate drafty outposts, and pad cold sleeping rolls. When Pilot Bellowfiz began outfitting his siege tank, Jetsteam, at Steelgrill's Depot, he faced the harsh prospect of spending a full month in the field on a long mission for the Siege Brigade. Because cold iron offers little comfort in high-altitude snowbanks, he commissioned local scouts to gather thick bear furs from the snow fields south of the Grizzled Den to fashion warm bedding for his cabin quarters.

item:thistlenettle-s-badge.text: Thistlenettle's Badge. Thistlenettle's Badge is an official insignia of the dwarven Explorers' League, once carried proudly by Foreman Thistlenettle into the depths of the Deadmines. Following a catastrophic cave-in and an invasion of thieves, the token is all that remains to confirm the foreman's tragic fate to his surviving brother in Stormwind. Before the Defias Brotherhood locked down Moonbrook and the cavernous tunnels beneath it, dwarven prospectors affiliated with Ironforge's Explorers' League delved into the old gold mines of Westfall. Foreman Thistlenettle and his crew worked deep underground until a sudden tunnel collapse separated the team. While his brother Wilder managed to escape to Stormwind City, the foreman and several laborers remained trapped in the subterranean dark.

item:thresher-eye.text: Thresher Eye. Along Darkshore, Wizbang Cranktoggle wants Thresher Eyes for his Buzzboxes. He uses them to repair Buzzbox 411 on the beach north of Auberdine. Darkshore Threshers hunt the surf and outer shallows off Darkshore. They threaten local fishermen and travelers, and their large eyes have caught the interest of Wizbang Cranktoggle. The gnome engineer is stationed nearby and fond of crawler wine. He needs the eyes to repair Buzzbox 411, a far-speaking communication machine on the beach north of Auberdine. Wizbang does not explain how the slimy eyes repair delicate machinery. They might serve as crude lenses, chemical agents, or biological gears. Whatever the method, three eyes placed in Buzzbox 411's maintenance hatch restore its communication link, and Wizbang sends supplies through static-choked transmissions.

item:thule-s-head.text: Thule's Head. Thule's Head is the grisly proof demanded by the Forsaken to confirm the demise of Thule Ravenclaw, commander of the Scourge forces on Fenris Isle. Bringing this macabre trophy back to High Executor Hadrec at the Sepulcher solidifies the Forsaken's hold on Silverpine Forest. Fenris Isle serves as the primary bastion of the Lich King's Scourge within Silverpine Forest. From deep inside Fenris Keep, the necromancer Thule Ravenclaw directs his legions of rot hides and undead minions, directly threatening Forsaken outposts like the Sepulcher. High Executor Hadrec requires absolute certainty that this dark commander has fallen, refusing to accept any testimony short of Thule's severed head. The violent release of dark magic upon Ravenclaw's death was felt across the woods, but his head remains the physical proof Hadrec requires to declare Fenris Isle broken.

item:thunder-lizard-blood.text: Thunder Lizard Blood. In the southern Barrens, hunters bring back Thunder Lizard Blood as proof of survival. The blood comes from the great beasts that roam the plains. Thunder lizards go by the names Stormsnouts, Stormhides, and Thunderheads across the plains. Their heavy steps shake the earth, and their crushing weight can flatten unwary hunters. Bringing back their blood shows the skill to hunt them and the endurance to survive beneath their thundering feet.

item:thunder-lizard-horn.text: Thunder Lizard Horn. In the Barrens, Brewmaster Drohn seeks a Thunder Lizard Horn for Chen Stormstout's legendary brew. Thunder lizards roam the Barrens, their crested bodies crackling with lightning. Brewmaster Drohn in Ratchet values their horns as an ingredient for Stormstout ale. His mentor learned the recipe from the wandering pandaren Brewmaster Chen Stormstout and passed it down to Drohn. The horn gives the drink its potent kick.

item:thunderhawk-saliva-gland.text: Thunderhawk Saliva Gland. Across the Barrens, greater thunderhawks yield a gland prized by Brewmaster Drohn. He needs it to recreate Chen Stormstout's fiery Trogg Ale. Greater thunderhawks hunt across the Barrens' arid savannas. These winged serpents are known for harnessing storms, and the older, more dangerous ones produce a saliva gland charged with natural potency. Travelers keep clear of the deadly beasts, but brewmasters value the gland as a rare base for exotic drinks. Brewmaster Drohn settled outside Ratchet after Chen Stormstout traveled through Kalimdor. Drohn studies the wandering brewmaster's fermentation methods and needs a fresh thunderhawk saliva gland, stormhide lightning glands, and kodo liver to brew Trogg Ale. The fiery spirit has an unmistakable kick and is meant to fortify hardy adventurers.

item:thunderhawk-wings.text: Thunderhawk Wings. Across the central and southern Barrens, hunters claim Thunderhawk Wings from the wind serpents that soar overhead. At Camp Taurajo, Jorn Skyseer receives them as proof of a hunter’s strength, cunning, and endurance. Hunters stationed at Camp Taurajo prize a pair of intact Thunderhawk Wings. Wind serpents, whom local hunters call thunderhawks, are fierce winged reptiles that strike swiftly from above. Tracking them across the open plains and claiming their wings in combat tests a hunter’s skill. For an initiate, bringing back the wings proves readiness to follow the lifelong path of an accomplished hunter.

item:thunderhorn-cleansing-totem.text: Thunderhorn Cleansing Totem. The Thunderhorn Cleansing Totem is a consecrated ritual implement crafted by Mull Thunderhorn in Bloodhoof Village. It is imbued with ancestral magic to purify the corrupted waters of the Thunderhorn Water Well. Across the rolling plains of Mulgore, the lifeblood of the earth is being fouled by unseen corruption. The ancestral wells dug by the tauren tribes provide vital nourishment to the herds and hunting grounds, but foul agents have tainted the water. Entrusted by the elder Mull Thunderhorn, adventurers carry this prepared totem north of Bloodhoof Village to drive out the pollution settling over the Thunderhorn clan's sacred spring. Through ritual invocation, the totem calms the disturbed spirits of the water and cleanses the ancestral site.

item:thurman-s-remains.text: Thurman's Remains. Thurman's Remains are the corporeal remnants of Thurman Agamand, recovered from the family's ruined mills in northern Tirisfal Glades. Once a wealthy mill owner who persuaded his workers to stand against the Scourge, Thurman succumbed to the Plague and wanders his former estate as an undead thrall. Before the Third War, the Agamand family stood as the most prosperous landowners in Tirisfal Glades, operating extensive mills and employing dozens of local workers. When the Scourge swept across Lordaeron, Thurman Agamand and his kin fortified their estate rather than fleeing. Convinced that their wealth and fortified mills could weather the onslaught, they persuaded their loyal laborers to take up arms beside them. The defense failed utterly. The Agamands and their workers were slaughtered and transformed into mindless servants of the Lich King. Today, Coleman Farthing—a former employee risen as Forsaken—demands the destruction of his former masters, seeking Thurman's remains as proof that the foolish patriarch has paid for dooming his household.

item:thurman-s-sewing-kit.text: Thurman's Sewing Kit. At Larson Clothiers, Thurman's Sewing Kit is needed for his tailoring work. The tools belong to young apprentice Thurman Schneider, who left them behind at his family's canal home to avoid a long day of stitching. Thurman's Sewing Kit holds the everyday tools of an apprentice tailor: needles, shears, and thread. Young Thurman Schneider studies tailoring at Larson Clothiers, deep in Stormwind's Mage Quarter near the Mage Tower. His mother, Rema Schneider, knows he cannot do his work without the kit, so she asks passersby along the Canals to carry it to the shop. When Thurman gets the tools, his reaction shows he left them behind on purpose, hoping to trade a day of stitching garments for leisure.

item:timberling-seed.text: Timberling Seed. Across Teldrassil, Timberling Seeds are gathered from plant spirits that have grown hostile. Naturalists and druids study them to learn why the forest's plant life has turned aggressive. Timberlings are nature elementals of Teldrassil, and their temper reflects the World Tree's balance. Lately they have grown hostile and angry, troubling the night elves who tend the boughs. Herbalists such as Denalan at Lake Al'Ameth suspect trouble in the soil. They gather seeds from wild timberlings, hoping that purified, carefully tended soil might let docile offspring sprout.

item:timberling-sprout.text: Timberling Sprout. Along Lake Al'Ameth, Timberling Sprouts take root already touched by corruption. Night elf wardens pull them before they grow into aggressive timberlings. Timberlings are plant spirits bound to Teldrassil's natural vitality. Along Lake Al'Ameth, the night elves find seedlings that sprout tainted and aggressive instead of healthy and in harmony with the wild. The young sprouts seem beyond cleansing or natural healing, so the caretakers gather and destroy them. They hope to stop hostile timberlings from spreading across the fragile boughs of the newly planted World Tree.

item:tirisfal-pumpkin.text: Tirisfal Pumpkin. Tirisfal Pumpkins grow in the tilled plots of the Solliden Farmstead, tended by surviving living humans struggling to survive in the blighted glades. The Forsaken routinely raid these fields to supply the Royal Apothecary Society with organic matter for their ongoing chemical concoctions. Despite the corruption settling over Lordaeron, crops still somehow sprout in the fields west of Brill. At the Solliden Farmstead, living human farmers cling to their soil, cultivating massive orange squash under the watchful guard of the nearby Scarlet Crusade. For these mortals, the harvest is vital sustenance. For the nearby Forsaken of Brill, however, the pumpkins represent both a spiteful target of sabotage and a bounty of raw organic reagents needed by Apothecary Johaan. Deathguard Simmer directs young Forsaken out into the contested fields to pilfer the pumpkins directly from beneath the farmers' noses. Rather than feeding the dead, these vegetables find their way into the boiling cauldrons of the Royal Apothecary Society. The apothecaries frequently test how natural flora reacts to their plagues and experimental mixtures, turning Lordaeron's remaining agriculture against the living.

item:token-of-thievery.text: Token of Thievery. The Token of Thievery is a proof of skill recovered by novice rogues during their training in the Redridge Mountains. Placed inside a locked footlocker at the orc-threatened Alther's Mill, it serves as the final test set by the seasoned thief Lucius to demonstrate mastery over lockpicking. Not every scoundrel possesses an innate knack for working tumblers and slipping catches unnoticed. In Lakeshire, the roguish instructor Lucius puts promising operatives through their paces by testing their wits and tools in the field. Rather than keeping his trials confined to quiet alleys, Lucius stashes the Token of Thievery inside a sturdy lockbox hidden among the ruins of Alther's Mill, directly in the path of encroaching Blackrock orcs. Retrieving the token proves that an initiate can pick a secure mechanism under the pressure of mortal danger, earning them their formal Certificate of Thievery.

item:tome-of-the-cabal-quest-item.text: Tome of the Cabal (quest item). Warlocks in Ratchet receive the Tome of the Cabal from Strahad Farsan after gathering dangerous components. Its pages hold the incantations for drawing a felhunter across the Twisting Nether and binding it. A felhunter is a vicious beast from the chaotic Twisting Nether, feared for devouring mana. Subduing one marks a passage for seasoned warlocks. The Tome of the Cabal holds the rites for opening a path to such a demon. Strahad Farsan, an experienced conjurer in Ratchet, gives the tome to an aspirant only after they gather the rare and dangerous components its magic requires. Strahad Farsan establishes the primary summoning circle in his sanctum, while his acolytes use rods of channeling to form a greater protective boundary. The warlock recites the tome's exact incantations and drags the felhunter into our world. The demon must be battled at once and subdued, binding it to the warlock's will.

item:top-of-gelkak-s-key.text: Top of Gelkak's Key. A giant foreststrider carries the Top of Gelkak's Key into the woods near Darkshore. It is one of three broken pieces of a mechanical key belonging to the shipwrecked gnome Gelkak Gyromast. Threshadons attacked Gelkak Gyromast's ship off Darkshore and sent it beneath the waves. The gnome washed ashore with the winding key for his mechanical first mate. The impact against the coastal rocks broke it into three pieces. Before the dizzy pirate could gather his wits, beasts scavenged the wreckage. A giant foreststrider carried the ornate upper piece into the woods.

item:torch-of-the-dormant-flame.text: Torch of the Dormant Flame. At the Shrine of the Dormant Flame, a shaman prepares to kindle the Torch of the Dormant Flame. The unlit torch waits for a fire spirit's ember, earned on a mountaintop in Durotar. A shaman seeking fire's favor carries the unlit Torch of the Dormant Flame up the peaks above Durotar. Fire sapta lets the shaman see a Minor Manifestation of Fire on the mountaintop and challenge it. When the spirit falls, its glowing ember goes into the weathered brazier at the Shrine of the Dormant Flame. The shaman touches the torch's head to the white-hot blaze, and the wood awakens as a burning emblem of elemental mastery.

item:torn-fin-eye.text: Torn Fin Eye. Torn Fin Eyes are ocular organs harvested from the Torn Fin murlocs prowling the shores of Hillsbrad Foothills. They serve as a crucial reactive ingredient for the Royal Apothecary Society's grim alchemical research into new plagues. The Royal Apothecary Society rarely lets any vile biological component go to waste in their quest to develop the Forsaken's New Plague. Torn Fin Eyes, harvested from the salt-crusted murlocs prowling the Western Strand of Hillsbrad Foothills, possess specialized organic properties needed to activate volatile alchemical compounds. When combined with Daggerspine naga scales, restorative troll elixirs, and gnoll-derived sludge, the optic tissues help stabilize and trigger toxic mixtures formulated to sow death across enemy territories.

item:torn-murloc-fin.text: Torn Murloc Fin. In eastern Elwynn, Torn Murloc Fins show the Stormwind Army's bounty is being answered. Taken from foragers and lurkers along the riverbanks, they show that local waterways are being systematically cleared. Murlocs have grown numerous along eastern Elwynn's streams and lakes, and the Stormwind Army offers a bounty to reduce their numbers. Guard Thomas, who watches the bridge over the eastern river, collects the severed fins as proof of kills. Stormwind's soldiers are stretched thin by unrest at home and threats nearby, so local authorities depend on travelers to bring proof that murloc camps have been cleared.

item:totem-of-hawkwind.text: Totem of Hawkwind. The Totem of Hawkwind is a carved token carried by young tauren departing Camp Narache. Presented to Baine Bloodhoof in Bloodhoof Village, it serves as proof that the bearer has completed their initial trials and is prepared to undergo the remainder of the Rites of the Earthmother. Carved by the hand of Chief Hawkwind atop the Red Cloud Mesa, this wooden totem acts as an introduction and proof of passage for youth coming of age. In tauren tradition, formal writ is rarely used; instead, meaningful symbols and familiar tribal craft carry a leader's intent. When an aspiring youth completes their preliminary trials at Camp Narache, Hawkwind crafts this icon to send them forward along the road into the wider expanse of Mulgore. The distinctive carvings identify the bearer to Baine Bloodhoof, signaling that they possess the spirit and strength required to face the next trials and seek the eventual blessing of Thunder Bluff.

item:tough-wolf-meat.text: Tough Wolf Meat. Northshire and Coldridge wolves prowl their valleys, leaving raw Tough Wolf Meat for hungry locals. Coarse and stringy, it feeds people in Elwynn Forest and supplies dwarven outfitters in Dun Morogh. Wolves prowl near Northshire Valley and Dun Morogh, threatening nearby settlements and providing a hard-won source of food. Their meat is coarse, stringy, and chewy, but resource-strapped frontiersmen prize it. Outside Northshire Abbey, Eagan Peltskinner hates the vicious beasts yet cooks their meat into steaks. He trades basic supplies and gear to those willing to cull the packs.

item:tourmaline-phial.text: Tourmaline Phial. At the Pools of Arlithrien, the Tourmaline Phial gathers blessed moonwell water for Teldrassil's rituals. Corithras Moonrage gives the Tourmaline Phial to travelers for rituals that tend the World Tree. Druids in Dolanaar use gemstone vials to collect pure moonwell water across Teldrassil. This phial is meant for the moonwell beside the Pools of Arlithrien, southeast of the road to Darnassus, where hostile Gnarlpine furbolgs are growing more troublesome.

item:toxic-fogger.text: Toxic Fogger. The Toxic Fogger is a specialized dispersal device filled with lethal poison, concocted by the Forsaken Royal Apothecary Society. It is designed to contaminate the Venture Company's air transit operations in the Stonetalon Mountains. Carrying a toxin brewed by Apothecary Lydon in Tarren Mill and dispatched by Apothecary Zamah in Thunder Bluff, the Toxic Fogger serves as biological sabotage aimed directly at the Venture Company's strip-mining efforts. Suspecting that the goblins rely on courier flying machines to shuttle messages and light cargo between Stonetalon and their headquarters, Zamah sends the fogger to release its poison right where machines land and refuel. Rather than engaging in prolonged skirmishes with endless mercenary crews, the Forsaken method strikes at the logistical spine of the operation, ensuring that the poison travels directly back to corporate leadership.

item:treshala-s-pendant.text: Treshala's Pendant. Treshala's Pendant is an intimate heirloom of bonding belonging to Treshala Fallowbrook, a night elf dwelling in Darnassus. Carried into southern Kalimdor by her husband, Heralath, it was ripped away by the quilboar in Razorfen Kraul as he lay dying. The pendant serves as a symbol of deep marital devotion between Treshala and Heralath Fallowbrook. Before embarking on perilous journeys away from Teldrassil, Heralath carried the bonding necklace close as a reminder of his home and his beloved.

item:trogg-stone-tooth.text: Trogg Stone Tooth. A Trogg Stone Tooth is a rugged, mineralized tooth taken from the Stonesplinter troggs infesting the hills of Loch Modan. Dwarven defenders use these teeth as physical proof that wandering adventurers are thinning the trogg numbers around the southern frontier. With the Ironforge Reserve committed to the Alliance Front, local dwarven garrisons are stretched thin across Khaz Modan. At the southern gate guard tower in Loch Modan, Captain Rugelfuss cannot spare his soldiers from their posts to mount offensive patrols against the lurking Stonesplinter troggs. Instead, he issues a standing call for volunteers to hunt the creatures in the nearby hills. To confirm that the menace is being driven back, Rugelfuss demands Trogg Stone Teeth as crude, undeniable evidence of every beast slain.

item:troll-charm.text: Troll Charm. Troll Charms are sacred spiritual amulets carried by the Darkspear trolls. A collection of them was recently looted by hostile Thistlefur furbolgs after an ambush along the northern reaches of Ashenvale. To the trolls of the Horde, spiritual charms are far more than mere ornamentation. As the scout Mitsuwa explains, a troll without their charm is considered as diminished as an orc without battle scars. When a party of Darkspear kin journeyed toward Zoram'gar Outpost through the dense canopy of Ashenvale, they were ambushed and slaughtered by the corrupted Thistlefur furbolgs. While their spirits were commended to the afterlife, the furbolgs looted the dead and carried off their sacred charms as trophies, stashing them in chests deep within Thistlefur Hold.

item:trophy-swoop-quill.text: Trophy Swoop Quill. A Trophy Swoop Quill is a prized hunting token plucked from the large birds of prey that circle over the plains of Mulgore. Among the tauren, gathering these feathers demonstrates keen eyesight, patience, and hunting skill. Swoops are cunning avian predators indigenous to Mulgore, known for riding high thermals and remaining difficult to track across the grasslands. For young tauren hunters and travelers striving to prove themselves in Bloodhoof Village, claiming a trophy quill from these birds is a traditional rite of cleverness and determination. Presenting these quills to elders such as Harken Windtotem honors the hunter's clan and signifies that one possesses the sharp senses needed to thrive upon the plains.

item:twilight-pendant.text: Twilight Pendant. A Twilight Pendant is an insignia worn by cultists of the Twilight's Hammer deep within Blackfathom Deeps. To the Argent Dawn, these dark talismans serve as definitive proof of the cult's subversive operations on the coast of Ashenvale. Within the drowned ruins of Blackfathom Deeps, members of the Twilight's Hammer gather alongside the naga to conduct foul rites in veneration of the chaotic Old Gods. Cultists—ranging from shadowmages and aquamancers to reavers and loreseekers—wear these pendants as emblems of devotion to their shadowy patrons. Because the cult operates in secrecy beneath the former night elf temple, retrieving these ornaments is one of the few ways outside observers can gauge the cult's numbers and thwart their machinations. Argent Guard Manados in Darnassus actively seeks these pendants as evidence of a successful purge against the encroaching darkness. Blackfathom Deeps once housed a pristine moonwell, and its desecration by malevolent void-worshipers poses a severe threat to Kalimdor. Gathering the pendants confirms that the cultists' foothold in Ashenvale is being dismantled before their dark patrons can unleash greater terror.

item:twilight-whisker.text: Twilight Whisker. Twilight Whiskers are harvested from twilight runners prowling the northern heights of the Stonetalon Mountains. In the settlement of Malaka'jin, Witch Doctor Jin'Zil covets them as an ingredient in a cruel, venomous concoction he mockingly names forest magic. The high crags near Stonetalon Peak are home to twilight runners, predatory felines attuned to the deep shadows of the ancient groves. While hunters prize their pelts, Witch Doctor Jin'Zil of Malaka'jin seeks their stiff whiskers for a far darker purpose. Seeking vengeance upon captured night elves who once defended these woodlands, Jin'Zil gathers components of the forest—resinous sap, countless eyes, fey dragon scales, and twilight whiskers—to brew a lethal draught intended to mock and poison his captives.

item:twitching-antenna.text: Twitching Antenna. In the southern Barrens, silithid antennae still twitch after they are cut free. Ruga Ragetotem at Camp Taurajo seeks them as proof of a young warrior’s speed and skill in combat before the nerves go still. Silithid Grubs, Swarmers, Harvesters, and Creepers carry antennae that twitch after they are cut from the head. The spasms fade soon after the insects are slain. A young warrior must hunt silithid in the southern wastes and hurry back across the scrublands while the antennae still twitch. Bringing them back in time tests both speed and skill, making the hunt a rite of passage for Horde warriors. The silithid antennae also point to a threat that troubles Camp Taurajo’s hunters. Silithid are not native to the Barrens, and their new burrowing mounds at the Field of Giants unsettle the camp. Ruga Ragetotem wants the specimens to study the danger and prepare Horde warriors for the alien menace moving into the plains.

item:ukor-s-burden.text: Ukor's Burden. At the Valley of Trials, Ukor's food is turned away, and he needs help bringing it back to Razor Hill. Ukor, an orc peon, rarely acts on his own, but he carried provisions from the inn in Razor Hill to help young recruits in the Valley of Trials. The journey led him through Durotar's red dust and dangerous wildlife. The overseers and instructors refused the food, believing hardship and hunger make true warriors. Now Ukor waits outside the canyon's mouth, afraid of the beasts along the trail back. He has entrusted the sack to passing travelers, asking them to return it to Innkeeper Grosk.

item:uncloven-satyr-hoof.text: Uncloven Satyr Hoof. In Ashenvale, satyrs gorge themselves on the ancient forest’s magic. Their swollen hooves hold the power they steal, and Ula'elek uses it to forge armor in Sen'jin Village. Satyrs haunt the corrupted groves of northeastern Ashenvale, feeding on the ancient forest’s magical purity. The more they consume, the more corruption distorts their demonic bodies. Their hooves swell and lose their natural cleft, becoming dense stores of absorbed energy. Skilled shamans and leatherworkers can harvest that volatile power. At Sen'jin Village on Durotar’s coast, the troll armorer Ula'elek turns demonic corruption into strength for Horde champions. He takes hooves from satyrs that have fed on the forest and draws out their trapped magic. Then he channels that stolen power into brutal gauntlets, armor for young warriors facing the rigors of Kalimdor.

item:underbelly-whelp-scale.text: Underbelly Whelp Scale. Underbelly Whelp Scales are harvested from the younger broods of the Black Dragonflight found roaming the Redridge Mountains. Valued by craftsmen for their resilient yet pliable texture, they serve as precious barter material among local artisans. Dragonhide and scales possess legendary durability, but full-grown black dragons are lethal beyond measure to ordinary folk. Instead, resourceful frontiersmen and craftsmen look toward the skies south of Lake Everstill, where young black dragon whelps nest among the crags. While the dorsal plating of a whelp is brittle or coarse, the scales running along its softer underbelly strike an ideal balance between flexibility and protection. As a result, these underbelly scales command substantial value in regional trade, functioning as high-end crafting material and dependable collateral for debts. In Lakeshire, the magistrate's craftsmen must often rely on barter when coin is scarce or trade routes are strained. Verner Osgood, the local blacksmith, found himself heavily indebted to the blacksmith Argus over a shipment of shoes brought in from Goldshire. Knowing Argus's fondness for rare trade goods, Verner relies on passing adventurers to harvest underbelly whelp scales to satisfy the debt and keep his workshop in good standing.

item:unidentified-ore.text: Unidentified Ore. Unidentified Ore is a peculiar mineral sample unearthed by Venture Company operations in the crags of the Stonetalon Mountains. Recovered by the disgruntled laborer Piznik, it was smuggled away to be analyzed by goblin tinker Ziz Fizziks and forwarded to engineers in Undermine. The Venture Company's relentless clear-cutting and strip mining in Windshear Crag tore deep into the crags of the Stonetalon Mountains, exposing unusual mineral strata. The site's new boss, Gerenzo Wrenchwhistle, ordered large amounts of a strange gold-green ore mined, and the demoted goblin worker Piznik, still loyal to his fired former boss Ziz Fizziks, secured a sample of it while plotting his exit from the outfit. Handed off to a traveler bound for the western ridge of the crag, the sample made its way into the hands of Ziz Fizziks, who planned to ship the prize back to Undermine for study, keeping a pocket-sized cut for personal profit.

item:unrefined-ore-sample.text: Unrefined Ore Sample. In Thousand Needles, an unusual ore draws the Horde's attention. Tatternack Steelforge seeks a sample to judge whether the raw mineral can strengthen the weapons of Warchief Thrall's armies. South of the Barrens, Gravelsnout kobolds dig through the stone beneath the canyon walls of Thousand Needles. Travelers returning north found a curious mineral among slain vermin, unlike the usual veins of Kalimdor. They refused to surrender their prize to the Horde. The kobolds who dig and survey the depths carry raw chunks of the ore from their excavations. At Camp Taurajo, weaponsmith Tatternack Steelforge works under orders from Warchief Thrall to improve the Horde's arms. Travelers who kept knowledge of the deposit angered him; he saw their refusal as an insult to the Horde's war effort. With a raw sample, Tatternack plans to test the mineral's strength and temper, then smelt it and forge a prototype blade for Orgrimmar's approval.

item:ur-s-treatise-on-shadow-magic.text: Ur's Treatise on Shadow Magic. Stormwind's mages once guarded Ur's Treatise on Shadow Magic, but Morganth stole the perilous tome and hid it in the Tower of Ilgalar. Ur of Dalaran wrote a treatise on shadow magic and its subtle, corruptive nature. The mages of the Wizard's Sanctum in Stormwind feared that such arts could bring doom and ruin to the unwary, so they sealed the volume against readers. After Morganth surrendered to dark arts and Stormwind's magical circle exiled him, he took the tome east into the Redridge Mountains, to his stronghold at the Tower of Ilgalar.

item:urgent-message.text: Urgent Message. The Urgent Message is a sealed dispatch penned by Brave Moonhorn warning Freewind Post of escalating centaur violence across Thousand Needles. Carried by travelers descending into the canyon, the letter alerts the tauren garrison that their supply lines and scouting parties are under immediate threat. Penned by Brave Moonhorn near the great lift that descends from the Barrens into Thousand Needles, the Urgent Message represents the first line of defense for travelers crossing the border. Moonhorn monitors the jagged canyons below, where aggressive centaur tribes have renewed their relentless raids against Horde travel. Addressed to Cliffwatcher Longhorn atop Freewind Post, the missive sounds the alarm about emboldened attackers striking dangerously close to crucial roadways, urging the local garrison to brace for sustained conflict and guard against secondary threats like the unpredictable Grimtotem clan.

item:valdred-s-hands.text: Valdred's Hands. Valdred's Hands are the severed limbs of Valdred Moray, claimed after his death in southern Silverpine Forest. They are sought by Raleigh Andrean in the Undercity as a morbid trophy and proof of vengeance for the murder of his wife. Before the plague consumed Lordaeron, Valdred Moray and Raleigh Andrean were close friends. That bond was shattered when Valdred murdered Raleigh's wife, Deliah. Though Raleigh succumbed to death and arose as one of the Forsaken—professing an inability to genuinely grieve—the lingering hunger for retribution never left him. When Valdred attempted to flee southward past the Greymane Wall into Gilneas, Raleigh dispatched an emissary to end his former friend's flight, demanding his severed hands as definitive proof that the deed was done.

item:velinde-s-journal.text: Velinde's Journal. Velinde Starsong's personal journal records her duties and the mystery of her departure from Darnassus. The Night Elf priestess's journal is stored in the Sentinel bunkhouse. When Night Elf priestess Velinde Starsong left Darnassus, her belongings were locked in a footlocker at the Sentinels' bunkhouse in the Tradesmen's Terrace. Among them was her personal journal, a record of her responsibilities and duties. The Sentinels respected Velinde and believed she had left to attend to private matters. Her journal's contents suggest her unexplained absence is more troubling than they first believed.

item:velinde-s-key.text: Velinde's Key. In Darnassus, Velinde's Key guards the writings of a vanished priestess. Thyn'tel Bladeweaver entrusts it to those who bring proof of their interest in Velinde Starsong's fate. Thyn'tel Bladeweaver keeps Velinde's Key in Darnassus. The simple key secures Priestess Velinde Starsong's personal belongings in a footlocker in the Sentinel bunkhouse above the Tradesmen's Terrace. Velinde left night elf lands without warning, and her possessions were set aside. Bladeweaver gives the key only to those who bring genuine evidence of their interest in learning her fate, such as revelations found in the Tome of Mel'Thandris.

item:venomtail-antidote.text: Venomtail Antidote. In Durotar, Venomtail Antidote is urgently needed to save a scout from scorpid poison. Kor'ghan brews the remedy in Orgrimmar for Rhinag, who lies stricken near Durotar's northwestern border. Durotar's venomtail scorpids can kill a warrior within an hour of a deep sting.
