Rhinag, a troll scout, was envenomed near the northwestern border, far from aid. His only chance is a remedy from Kor'ghan, an apothecary in Orgrimmar's Cleft of Shadow. Finding Kor'ghan means making your way beneath Orgrimmar. He knows desert toxins and harsh remedies, and prepares a vial to purge the venom before it turns fatal. The draught stops the poison and spares Rhinag a humiliating death in the wilderness. Kor'ghan still demands further trials and hunts from the scout to atone for his carelessness.

item:venomtail-poison-sac.text: Venomtail Poison Sac. In Durotar, a scorpion’s venom can bring a hunter near death, while its poison sac holds what alchemists need to make a cure. Scorpids roam Durotar’s red rocks, including Venomtail Scorpids, Corrupted Scorpids, and the Death Flayer. Their tail sacs hold a fast-acting venom that can overwhelm even seasoned warriors if left untreated. The same sacs contain the primary compounds alchemists need to make an antidote. When a scorpion stung the hunter Rhinag outside Orgrimmar, local alchemists needed four fresh poison sacs to make a remedy and neutralize the venom in his veins.

item:venture-co-documents.text: Venture Co. Documents. These tightly bound papers were recovered from a crate amidst a ruined caravan in eastern Mulgore. They detail the operations of the Venture Company, confirming the predatory cartel's illegal strip-mining ventures within the tauren homeland. Discovered packed atop mined ore and minerals in the remnants of a ransacked wagon, these documents expose the scale of the Venture Company's intrusion into Mulgore. Known across Kalimdor for ruthless deforestation and uncontrolled excavation, the goblin-led cartel has quietly set up drilling and mining outposts in the eastern foothills. Morin Cloudstalker and the tauren Outrunners rely on these seized ledgers to gauge the threat to their sacred ancestral plains and rally hunters to drive the trespassers out.

item:venture-co-engineering-plans.text: Venture Co. Engineering Plans. The Venture Co. Engineering Plans are mechanical schematics kept inside the goblin logging mill in Windshear Crag. Recovered by Alliance operatives, they detail the inner workings of the heavy machinery devastating the Stonetalon Mountains. Windshear Crag is choked with smoke and logging machinery as the Venture Company strips the forests of Stonetalon. Hidden inside their lumber mill south of Cragpool Lake, these engineering blueprints lay out the exact construction, strengths, and flaws of their specialized timber-harvesting contraptions.

item:venture-co-letters.text: Venture Co. Letters. The Venture Co. Letters are internal correspondence recovered from Windshear Mine in Stonetalon Mountains. Stolen under the cover of explosive distractions, they provide the night elf Sentinels with crucial intelligence on goblin industrial operations in the region. Windshear Crag has been overrun by the Venture Company, whose logging machines and strip-mining operations tear through the ancient woodland. To uncover the full scope of the cartel's ambitions, Alliance operatives deployed covert sabotage to create distractions and infiltrate Windshear Mine. These retrieved letters contain private communications and logistical records detailing the company's local activities, giving Sentinel leadership insight into how the defilers organize their workforce and supply lines.

item:verdant-note.text: Verdant Note. The Verdant Note is a summons delivered to novice tauren druids in Camp Narache. Sent on behalf of the druid mentor Gart Mistrunner, it instructs young initiates to report for training and begin learning the rites of the Earthmother. Young tauren who demonstrate a spiritual affinity for nature receive the Verdant Note shortly after beginning their trials in the Red Cloud Mesa. Carried by a messenger sent by Gart Mistrunner, the brief missive directs the initiate to present themselves to the mentor at Camp Narache. Restless spirits and shifting elements have begun troubling Mulgore, making the instruction of new druids an urgent duty for the elders. Upon answering the note, initiates are inducted into the deeper mysteries of nature communion. Gart Mistrunner cautions young druids that although night elves share a common bond with the wild, their ancient pride keeps them distant and unwelcoming. Tauren druidism focuses strictly on reverence for the Earthmother, guiding initiates to listen to the land's restless ancestral voices and serve as her living instruments.

item:verdant-sigil.text: Verdant Sigil. In Shadowglen, Conservator Ilthalaine gives young night elf druids the Verdant Sigil as a summons to begin training. Young night elves in Shadowglen who feel the call of the wild receive the Verdant Sigil from Conservator Ilthalaine. A messenger brings it from Mardant Strongoak, the druid trainer, and it directs novices to climb into Aldrassil's boughs. The token invites them to leave basic chores behind and begin serious study of communion with nature spirits and the mysteries of the Emerald Dream. Presenting the Verdant Sigil to Mardant Strongoak begins a young druid's lifelong craft. Novices are not yet ready to walk the sleeping trance of the Emerald Dream, but the token marks the start of their mentorship. Under Mardant's instruction, they learn to read the wilderness's whispers and practice early shapeshifting and healing arts in service of Teldrassil.

item:verna-s-westfall-stew-recipe.text: Verna's Westfall Stew Recipe. Verna's Westfall Stew Recipe travels to Salma Saldean as the Furlbrows prepare to leave their farm. Her handwritten formula carries a familiar comfort for those who remain. Verna and Farmer Furlbrow have homesteaded in Westfall for years, but the Defias Brotherhood and rogue harvest golems now run rampant across the countryside. They wait for their wagon to be repaired so they can escape toward Stormwind. While they wait, Verna writes down her beloved formula for Westfall Stew. She entrusts the recipe to travelers bound for her neighboring friend, Salma Saldean, so the familiar comfort of the stew can endure for those left behind.

item:verner-s-note.text: Verner's Note. Verner's Note is a written requisition penned by Lakeshire's blacksmith, Verner Osgood, and carried to Smith Argus in Goldshire. It details a critical shortage of iron in Redridge, asking the Elwynn smith for emergency horseshoes. Maintaining the defense of Lakeshire demands a heavy toll in worked metal. With the Stormwind Guard stationed in town stretched thin against invading gnolls and local perils, Verner Osgood has consumed nearly all his iron reserves keeping soldiers armed and armored. As a result, Lakeshire's stables have fallen into neglect, lacking even basic horseshoes for their mounts. This letter represents Verner swallowing his pride to ask Smith Argus in Goldshire for an external shipment of prepared shoes to keep the town's horses mobile.

item:verog-s-head.text: Verog's Head. Regthar Deathgate seeks Verog's Head as proof of the Kolkar leader's death. The chieftain commands forces around the Stagnant Oasis, and his defeat is meant to weaken the tribes threatening the Barrens. The Kolkar centaur threaten Horde travelers and supply routes across the northern Barrens. Verog the Dervish roams the arid scrubland, leaving his command tent at the Stagnant Oasis vulnerable. Horde operatives attack his forces around the pavilion until an alarm sounds. Verog rushes back to defend his camp, where he is slain and decapitated. Regthar Deathgate receives his head as proof that another dangerous Kolkar chieftain has fallen. Barak Kodobane's head is already on display beside it.

item:vial-of-innocent-blood.text: Vial of Innocent Blood. A Vial of Innocent Blood is a grim alchemical reagent gathered by Syndicate shadow mages lurking in the ruins of Durnholde Keep. Sought after by the Royal Apothecary Society in Tarren Mill, it serves as a key catalyst in brewing experimental toxins. Within the crumbled walls of Durnholde Keep, the fallen human nobles of the Syndicate practice dark and unsavory arts. Among them are shadow mages who systematically harvest the blood of innocents for their own occult rituals. This macabre practice has drawn the keen attention of Apothecary Lydon in Tarren Mill. Needing untainted blood to brew an experimental pacifying agent meant to neutralize the Venture Company in Stonetalon Mountains, the Forsaken apothecary sees the Syndicate's grim stores as a convenient shortcut for his work.

item:vial-of-phlogiston.text: Vial of Phlogiston. A Vial of Phlogiston is an alchemical substance used by master armorers to temper extraordinarily resilient mail. Guarded within the quilboar stronghold of Razorfen Kraul, it is coveted by both Alliance and Horde smiths forging specialized battle armor for promising warriors. Phlogiston is an intensely volatile, fire-bearing substance prized in esoteric metallurgy. Both the dwarven smith Furen Longbeard in Stormwind and the near-blind orc armorer Thun'grim Firegaze in the Barrens consider it an indispensable component for hardening warrior armor beyond ordinary physical limits. Without this alchemical agent, the specialized forging techniques required for Fire Hardened Mail or the Horde's Brutal Armor cannot be completed. Obtaining a Vial of Phlogiston requires venturing into the tangled thickets of Razorfen Kraul, located at the southern tip of the Barrens. The phlogiston is held deep within the bristling redoubt by the geomancer Roogug. Whether recovered for Furen in Stormwind or carried across the dust to Thun'grim's anvil, the substance demands a perilous descent into hostile quilboar territory.

item:vial-of-purest-water.text: Vial of Purest Water. In the southern Barrens, Brine blesses a vial of pure water for a shaman initiate. Its contents help Islen Waterseer prepare a water sapta for seeing elemental spirits. Brine guides the initiate through trials of patience and cleansing before sealing the water in the vial. The water holds an uncorrupted elemental purity. Carry it across the Barrens to Islen Waterseer, who keeps watch on a solitary shore. She needs it to brew a water sapta. Without such pure water, a shaman cannot commune with spiritual guardians in places far from the sunbaked flats.

item:vial-of-spider-venom.text: Vial of Spider Venom. A Vial of Spider Venom contains the potent, necrotic poison harvested from the arachnids that infest the darkened woods of Duskwood. Madame Eva of Darkshire uses this dangerous extract alongside undead remains to craft protective wards against incoming harm. The shadowed thickets of Duskwood harbor monstrous arachnids—from skittering pygmy venom webs and green recluses to black widows and the notorious Naraxis. These creatures pump a foul, potent poison through their fangs, potent enough to paralyze travelers and decay flesh. Adventurers brave enough to slay these horrors can extract intact vials of the viscous fluid. In Darkshire, the fortune teller Madame Eva perceives ominous portents for travelers stepping out into the dark world. To craft a ward of retribution, she requires five vials of this raw venom, combined with ghoul fangs and skeleton fingers. Channeled through her craft, the venom’s predatory, biting nature is inverted into the Totem of Infliction, turning harm back upon anyone who attacks its bearer.

item:vicious-night-web-spider-venom.text: Vicious Night Web Spider Venom. Vicious Night Web Spider Venom is a potent natural toxin gathered from the arachnids haunting eastern Tirisfal Glades. The Royal Apothecary Society prizes it for its peculiar ability to carry and preserve historical disease strains, making it a critical reagent in the development of the Forsaken's New Plague. According to research conducted by Apothecary Johaan in Brill, ancient texts chronicle a devastating historical plague that wiped out thousands of innocent victims. Curiously, the contagious agent behind that forgotten outbreak managed to endure over centuries by embedding itself within the venom of the local Night Web spiders. By hunting down the vicious breed lurking in Venomweb Vale south of the Scarlet Monastery, the apothecaries extract this preserved virulence to serve as a vital catalyst in their ongoing alchemical experiments.

item:vile-familiar-head.text: Vile Familiar Head. Near the Burning Blade Coven, Vile Familiar Heads mark a grim test for young Horde warlocks. Under Ruzan's guidance, they gather the gruesome trophies as proof of readiness to bind their first demonic minions. The test demands discipline and respect for the lethality of the beings they mean to summon. In the sun-baked canyon of the Valley of Trials, Ruzan asks novices seeking to learn summoning to bring him six Vile Familiar Heads. Vile familiars are fiery imps with dangerous elemental cunning, found outside the Burning Blade Coven. Novices must face and defeat them, proving they can subdue demonic life rather than be overcome by it. Warlocks are barely tolerated within Thrall's Horde, so their training calls for care. A novice slain by a conjured creature only deepens the dishonor and suspicion cast upon practitioners of the dark arts.

item:vile-fin-scale.text: Vile Fin Scale. Vile Fin Scales are harvested from the murloc tribes prowling the waterways and northern coasts of Tirisfal Glades. In Brill, the Royal Apothecary Society utilizes these resilient biological samples in their ongoing research to engineer a devastating new plague. The Royal Apothecary Society works relentlessly to craft a virulent blight capable of decimating both the living and the Scourge. Simple toxins are easy enough to brew, but creating an infectious disease that spreads effortlessly across populations requires specialized alchemical properties. Apothecary Johaan in Brill studies Vile Fin scales specifically to understand how their natural resilience and mucous coatings can aid in stabilizing and transmitting his experimental contagions. The Vile Fin tribe infests the northern shores and western shallows of Tirisfal Glades, threatening travelers and encroaching upon Forsaken territory. Gathering their scales serves a dual purpose for the Undercity: keeping the feral murloc populations in check while providing Johaan's laboratory with fresh organic components for biochemical warfare tests.

item:voodoo-charm.text: Voodoo Charm. In Teldrassil’s barrows, the Voodoo Charm can break the Gnarlpine enchantment holding Oben Rageclaw’s body.

item:wailing-essence.text: Wailing Essence. Wailing Essence is a strange, concentrated substance found within the ectoplasms roaming deep inside the Wailing Caverns. Suspected of fueling the bizarre mutations spreading through the flora and fauna of the Barrens, it has drawn the attention of opportunistic alchemists eager to bottle its potent properties. The subterranean caverns beneath the central Barrens have grown thick with unnatural energy, warping beasts and giving rise to gelatinous ectoplasms. These oozing creatures concentrate a viscous substance known as Wailing Essence. While local druids observe these waters with growing dread, goblin entrepreneurs see only raw commercial opportunity. In the port town of Ratchet, an eccentric alchemist named Mebok Mizzyrix believes this essence is the missing active ingredient for a line of lucrative 'smart drinks' meant to enhance consumer intellect, utterly unconcerned with the nightmarish corruption it might actually harbor.

item:warsong-axe-shipment.text: Warsong Axe Shipment. The Warsong Axe Shipment is a heavy crate of newly forged axes waiting on the docks of Booty Bay in Stranglethorn Vale. Ordered by the Warsong Outriders to sustain their harvesting operations in Ashenvale, it serves as a crucial link in the Horde's overseas supply chain. Maintaining the logging operations at the Warsong Lumber Camp requires a continuous flow of durable tools that cannot always be forged on the front lines. To keep woodcutters supplied, orders are sent across the Great Sea to the neutral goblin port of Booty Bay. Stored near Wharfmaster Lozgil, this crate contains sharpened axes intended for shipment back to Splintertree Post, highlighting the logistical hurdles the Horde faces in keeping its distant frontier camps armed and functional.

item:warsong-oil.text: Warsong Oil. Warsong Oil is a crucial industrial lubricant intended for the machinery at the Warsong Lumber Camp in Ashenvale. A vital supply shipment was intercepted en route by local satyrs, who took the oil to their corrupted woodland sanctuaries for foul rituals. The Warsong Clan's logging efforts in Ashenvale rely heavily on heavy machinery, goblin-engineered shredders, and massive sawmills. Keeping this industrial equipment running requires a steady supply of specialized oil. Without it, the clan's timber harvest risks grinding to an abrupt halt, stalling the flow of lumber desperately needed to build Orgrimmar and fortify Horde settlements across Durotar and the Barrens. Rather than reaching Splintertree Post and the logging camps, a recent shipment of Warsong Oil was ambushed by the satyrs infesting the forest. Instead of discarding the refined fluid, the demonic servants carried the containers into their corrupted enclaves—including Night Run, Satyrnaar, and Xavian—to use the flammable lubricant in their dark, detestable rituals.

item:warsong-outrider-update.text: Warsong Outrider Update. Along Ashenvale’s eastern border, a Warsong Outrider prepares a dispatch for the Horde. Stationed there, the outrider records frontline intelligence for couriers serving the Horde to carry, helping secure the crossing toward Azshara and strengthen the orcish foothold against night elf resistance. Beyond Splintertree Post, the eastern road runs toward the ancient ruins of Azshara through Ashenvale’s volatile borderlands. Mounted orcish vanguards patrol this frontier and record tactical sightings, patrol movements, and resource evaluations. They send their field notes to Kadrak at the northern watchtower, which guards the Barrens border. The reports give Horde commanders a clear view of enemy troop concentrations and territorial threats beneath the forest canopy.

item:warsong-runner-update.text: Warsong Runner Update. At Zoram'gar Outpost, Warsong Runner Update carries reports from western Ashenvale to Kadrak. The Warsong runner at Zoram'gar Outpost watches the coast and nearby threats in western Ashenvale. The dispatch records observations gathered by scouts at the outpost and reports on local activity. It travels to Kadrak's watchtower on the Barrens border, helping Horde leaders strengthen their position and plan their movements into the elves' ancestral woods.

item:warsong-saw-blades.text: Warsong Saw Blades. Warsong Saw Blades are specialized industrial cutting tools ordered to supply the Horde's clear-cutting operations in Ashenvale. Delivered through goblin logistical networks, they are vital for keeping the Warsong Lumber Camp's timber machinery running. The Warsong Clan's logging efforts in Ashenvale rely heavily on heavy-duty machinery provided and maintained with goblin engineering. Standard axes alone cannot feed the Horde's massive appetite for Kalimdor lumber, requiring steam engines and circular saws that continually chew through raw timber. Because Ashenvale's ancient hardwood rapidly dulls and snaps ordinary blades, constant shipments of replacement saw blades are vital to keep the mills running at the Warsong Lumber Camp. Procuring mechanical parts deep in disputed territory is an ongoing logistical headache. While other logging supplies are frequently intercepted by hostile furbolgs or satyrs, shipments of saw blades are handled through goblin contacts like Pixel at Splintertree Post. Gathering these blades alongside rope, oil, and axes allows lumber master Locke Okarr to keep the camp operational despite constant sabotage from the native defenders.

item:warsong-scout-update.text: Warsong Scout Update. At Splintertree Post, a Warsong scout records what the Horde needs to know about Ashenvale. Warsong scouts watch the woods as the Horde seeks timber and supply routes through Ashenvale. From Splintertree Post, a fortified encampment, they track night elf sentinels and movements across the territory. Their observations reach Kadrak at the Barrens-Ashenvale border among routine orders. He uses them to judge troop readiness and coordinate supplies and travel through the contested woods.

item:water-of-the-seers.text: Water of the Seers. Water of the Seers is a sacred draught given to young tauren undertaking their tribal trials in Bloodhoof Village. Drinking the holy water near the tribal fire opens the mind to the spirit world, summoning an ethereal Plains Vision to guide the pilgrim on their spiritual journey. Prepared by tribal mystics, the Water of the Seers is an essential element of the ancient Rite of Vision. To pierce the veil between physical reality and ancestral guidance, the petitioner must drink the holy water before the central tribal fire in Bloodhoof Village. Once consumed, the potent draught grants spiritual sight, causing a ghostly guide known as the Plains Vision to materialize from the embers and lead the way toward Seer Wiserunner.

item:water-pitcher.text: Water Pitcher. A simple vessel used to carry fresh spring water from the local well in the Red Cloud Mesa. Greatmother Hawkwind directs young tauren to haul it back to Camp Narache to instill the values of humility, service, and respect for tribal elders. Though modest in design, the water pitcher serves as an essential teaching tool for the youth of Camp Narache. Resting beside the water well on the plains southeast of the camp, it represents the daily labor required to sustain the community. By asking a novice to fill and carry the heavy vessel to Chief Hawkwind, Greatmother Hawkwind tests their character. The chore demonstrates that no duty is beneath a tribal protector, reminding young braves that tending to the everyday needs of their kin is just as vital as wielding a weapon on the hunt.

item:webwood-egg.text: Webwood Egg. In Shadowthread Cave, Webwood Eggs lie in brooding nests in Shadowglen. Naturalists seek viable eggs to study the young spiders in secure laboratory conditions. Researchers cannot safely tame or subdue a fully grown, venomous Webwood spider alone. Scholars like Gilshalan Windwalker instead collect unhatched eggs from clutches hidden in Shadowthread Cave. An egg can be carried safely, and the spiderlings contained when they hatch, giving naturalists live subjects to study without facing adult spiders’ deadly fangs. Teldrassil’s native wildlife has grown unnaturally aggressive and corrupted, alarming scholars across the boughs. Eggs and gathered venoms secured at Aldrassil are bound for Darnassus. Researchers hope that raising and examining the spiders in controlled settings will reveal more about the dark affliction spreading through the World Tree’s boughs.

item:webwood-ichor.text: Webwood Ichor. In Shadowglen, Webwood spiders carry venom that has left Iverron gravely ill. Dirania Silvershine needs their ichor, hyacinth mushrooms, and moonpetal lilies to brew an antidote. Webwood spiders in Shadowglen carry venom that has left Iverron gravely ill. Dirania Silvershine asks for their ichor, hyacinth mushrooms, and moonpetal lilies to prepare an antidote.

item:webwood-spider-silk.text: Webwood Spider Silk. Webwood Spider Silk is gathered from Webwood Lurkers in the woods of Teldrassil. Crafters use spider silk in many ways, but these swatches draw the interest of suspicious figures among the World Tree’s boughs. Webwood Lurkers around Dolanaar spin a fine, strong thread that is dangerous to gather. Zenn Foulhoof, a satyr along the forest road, asks young adventurers to collect the silk with nightsaber fangs and strigid owl feathers. He says these rare reagents are needed for his forest business, and newcomers gather them without asking about his corrupt nature or true motives.

item:webwood-venom-sac.text: Webwood Venom Sac. In Shadowglen, Webwood Venom Sacs draw the attention of naturalists studying Teldrassil's growth. The sacs come from overgrown spiders, and their venom may show how the new World Tree has changed local wildlife. Webwood spiders live around and within Shadowthread Cave, and they are cousins to a much smaller breed found elsewhere. Their sudden growth and predatory aggression worry night elf researchers. Naturalists such as Gilshalan Windwalker study the venom in their sacs, examining its strength and composition. They hope to learn how Teldrassil's rapid, unblessed growth is changing the creatures that live on its boughs.

item:well-stone.text: Well Stone. Well Stones are small mineral rocks gathered from the banks and surroundings of Mulgore's water wells. Rich in subtle earthen energies, they serve as a vital component in brewing the Water of the Seers during the traditional tauren rites of passage. Resting naturally in the soft earth bordering the wells of Mulgore, Well Stones absorb the spiritual resonance of the plains and the waters beneath them. Shaman and seers such as Zarlman Two-Moons recognize these stones not as mundane river pebbles, but as receptacles of vital magic. When combined with grounded Ambercorn beneath the plains' mighty trees, their mineral properties temper the brew needed to awaken visionary trance states in young tauren undergoing the sacred Rite of Vision.

item:wendigo-mane.text: Wendigo Mane. Wendigo Manes are the thick, shaggy coats harvested from the savage wendigos roaming the frozen crags of Dun Morogh. Coveted for their heavy insulation against the biting mountain chill, these coarse pelts are tough enough to line cabin floors or the iron cabins of dwarven warmachines. The mountains of Dun Morogh are harsh and unyielding, prompting locals to make good use of the apex beasts stalking the snowdrifts. The coarse fur of a wendigo offers dense protection against bitter sub-zero drafts. Pilot Stonegear, stationed outside Kharanos, sends adventurers into the nearby Grizzled Den to gather these heavy manes. Rather than fashioning winter coats or cloaks, the eccentric pilot intends to weave them into a plush, insulating floor rug for the interior deck of his prized dwarven siege engine, Trollplow.

item:whitestone-oak-lumber.text: Whitestone Oak Lumber. Whitestone Oak Lumber is a sturdy crafting timber sourced from the subterranean shipyards beneath Moonbrook. Prized for its strength, it serves as a critical shaft material for sacred armaments forged by Alliance master smiths. Found deep inside the labyrinthine Deadmines of Westfall, Whitestone Oak is shaped by Goblin Woodcarvers constructing the Defias Brotherhood's clandestine war fleet. Its dense, resilient grain makes it ideally suited to bear structural strain and high-impact wear, drawing the interest of seasoned armorers who require more than common ash or pine for ceremonial and martial craft.

item:wildmane-cleansing-totem.text: Wildmane Cleansing Totem. The Wildmane Cleansing Totem is a consecrated ritual implement crafted to purify the northern water well of Mulgore. Entrusted to young defenders of the land, it serves as the final instrument in driving out the toxic corruption left by encroaching goblin ventures. When goblin ventures began poisoning the land and fouling Mulgore's scarce water supplies, the tauren turned to sacred ritual to reverse the blight. After cleansing both the Winterhoof and Thunderhorn water wells, Mull Thunderhorn crafts this final totem to purge the remaining corruption at the Wildmane Water Well north of Thunder Bluff. Infused with natural spirits, the totem cleanses the fetid waters so pure life can nourish the plains once more.

item:wiley-s-note.text: Wiley's Note. Wiley's Note is a confidential missive penned by the Lakeshire rogue Wiley the Black, paid as a debt to Gryan Stoutmantle. Its contents reveal alarming alliances formed by the Defias Brotherhood and draw Stormwind's intelligence service into the investigation. Penned in Redridge by the shady rogue Wiley the Black, this scribbled dispatch is handed over to settle an old favor owed to Gryan Stoutmantle. Within, Wiley exposes what he knows about the Defias Brotherhood's clandestine ambitions. His intelligence reveals that the brotherhood is not operating alone: they have brokered alliances with regional gnolls, kobolds, and goblin operatives to further their operations across the kingdom.

item:william-s-shipment.text: William's Shipment. In Goldshire, William Pestle packs candles from Elwynn's kobolds for his brother Morgan in Stormwind. William Pestle keeps trade moving between Goldshire and the capital. He gathers materials in Elwynn Forest, while his brother Morgan runs Pestle's Apothecary in Stormwind's Trade District. William cannot leave his duties to travel north, so he depends on couriers to carry the parcel of wax and candles into the city. Kobold candles from Elwynn's mines fill the shipment. William gathers the large candles for their wax and packs them for Morgan at Pestle's Apothecary. The wax joins the stock used in the capital's alchemical trade.

item:wine-ticket.text: Wine Ticket. In Stormwind, Renato Gallina hands out Wine Tickets to bring customers to his family's shop. Present one to Suzetta Gallina for a complimentary bottle of Pinot Noir. Renato Gallina promotes the Gallina Winery with printed tickets near Stormwind's Trade District. The winery is a boutique vintage shop along the nearby canals. Each ticket promises a complimentary sample of Pinot Noir, drawing curious passersby and newly arrived adventurers toward the family business in hopes they become loyal customers.

item:winterhoof-cleansing-totem.text: Winterhoof Cleansing Totem. The Winterhoof Cleansing Totem is a consecrated ritual implement crafted by Mull Thunderhorn in Bloodhoof Village. Carved to undo the toxic blight spread by Venture Company intruders, it channels the Earth Mother's power to purify the polluted Winterhoof Water Well. When the goblin engineers of the Venture Company encroached upon the plains of Mulgore, their industrial operations quickly tainted the land's precious subterranean water tables. In response, Mull Thunderhorn prepared the Winterhoof Cleansing Totem, imbuing the carved wood with protective magic intended to wash out the foreign poisons. Carried past hostile goblin guards to the edge of the Winterhoof Water Well, the totem disperses the contamination through a focused ritual, restoring pure drinking water to the wandering herds and native tribes of the plains.

item:witchwing-talon.text: Witchwing Talon. In the northwestern Barrens, Witchwing Talons mark dead harpy raiders. Horde scouts at the Crossroads seek them as proof while they work to secure vital caravan routes. Witchwing harpies raid Horde supply caravans from their roosts northwest of the Crossroads. Scout Darsok Swiftdagger coordinates strikes against the flock's hierarchy. Darsok requires physical proof of each dead scavenger, and the talons provide it. With proof that raiders have fallen, the scouts can weaken the flock's ranks before striking higher in its command.

item:wolf-heart-sample.text: Wolf Heart Sample. Wolf Heart Sample is bound for the Crossroads, carrying diseased wolf tissue from Lordaeron to Kalimdor. The Royal Apothecary Society seeks to learn what northern toxins do to the Barrens’ native beasts. Wolf Heart Sample began with plagued wolves in Lordaeron’s ruins. Apothecary Renferrel gathered the hearts, and they were packed for the journey across the Great Sea. The Forsaken’s Royal Apothecary Society seeks greater knowledge of venom, blights, and biological reagents. A courier carries the parcel to the Crossroads in the Barrens, linking Undercity’s experiments in the scarred Eastern Kingdoms with Kalimdor’s frontier outposts. At the Crossroads, Apothecary Helbrim receives Wolf Heart Sample. Helbrim studies how toxins from Lordaeron’s Scourge-ravaged lands affect the native wildlife of Kalimdor. The toxicity preserved in the wolf hearts may reveal properties that can improve Forsaken poisons and elixirs far from home.

item:wolf-heart-samples.text: Wolf Heart Samples. Wolf Heart Samples are peculiar organic specimens gathered from corrupted wolves in Silverpine Forest. Despite their lethal toxicity, the hearts beat within the living creatures without killing them, drawing the intense scientific interest of the Royal Apothecary Society. While examining carcasses in Silverpine Forest, Apothecary Renferrel discovered that certain wolf hearts harbor a deadly compound. Strangely, the level of poison present within the tissue should easily be fatal to the wolves themselves. Recognizing the unique value of a physiology that thrives while saturated in lethal toxicity, Renferrel set aside tissue samples to be dispatched directly to Undercity. For the Forsaken, studying naturally resilient or toxic organisms is a critical step in mastering biological warfare and compounding new reagents. Entrusted to couriers heading deep beneath the ruins of Lordaeron, the samples are delivered to Apothecary Zinge within the Royal Apothecary Society's headquarters in the Apothecarium. Zinge and her colleagues prize novel toxins above almost all else. By dissecting and experimenting on these tainted tissues, the Society seeks to isolate the virulent compounds and unravel how the beasts survived them, hoping to apply the principles to their own alchemical projects.

item:wood-pulp.text: Wood Pulp. At Bael Modan, Wood Pulp helps the dwarves prepare their blasting charges. The dwarven personnel stationed in the southern Barrens carry it as an absorbent base for stabilizing liquid explosives. At Bael Modan, Ironforge dwarves use earth-moving equipment and chemical explosives to tear into ancestral tauren hunting grounds. Liquid nitroglycerin is unstable on its own, so dwarven engineers soak it into porous wood pulp with sodium nitrate to make stable charges for excavation and combat. Riflemen, soldiers, and officers carry bundles for sapping and field munitions.

item:wooden-key.text: Wooden Key. The Wooden Key is a simple carved key carried by the maddened ancients roaming northern Ashenvale near the border of Felwood. It unlocks a concealed chest holding a remnant of Dartol's Rod, an ancient night elven relic. The Wooden Key is held by the Crazed and Withered Ancients wandering the shaded trails north of Raynewood Retreat. Shael'dryn once knew the local treants, but now describes their nature as twisted by corruption. One of them carries the key to a chest holding a piece of Dartol's Rod.

item:worn-parchment.text: Worn Parchment. At the Tower of Althalaxx in northern Darkshore, Worn Parchment scraps offer clues to the cultists gathered there. North along Darkshore’s mist-shrouded coast, dark spellcasters and their followers have seized the ruined Tower of Althalaxx. Dark Strand Fanatics patrol the grounds outside and carry scraps of worn parchment among their belongings. One scrap holds only scattered writing and strange symbols. Gathered together, the fragments reveal a previously unknown organization called the Cult of the Dark Strand.

item:worn-stone-token.text: Worn Stone Token. Worn Stone Tokens are small magical talismans carried by personnel and mages associated with Dalaran in the Alterac Mountains. Though their ambient magic has largely faded, they were crafted to help the Kirin Tor bind and command elemental servants. The magi of Dalaran have long possessed a formidable command over elemental entities, using specialized talismans to bend these extradimensional beings to their will. Worn Stone Tokens represent depleted or exhausted versions of these implements. Carried not only by theurgists and summoners but even by Dalaran laborers and guards stationed around the ruins and internment camps of Alterac, they demonstrate how deeply elemental binding is integrated into Dalaran's everyday operations. From their outpost in Tarren Mill, the Forsaken keep a watchful eye on the nearby wizards. Magus Voidglare sought specimens of these tokens to decipher Dalaran's methods of elemental enslavement. Keeper Bel'varil directs agents to collect worn, inert tokens first, allowing the Magus to safely analyze the foundational enchanting techniques before experimenting with more potent, volatile conduits.

item:woven-wand.text: Woven Wand. The Woven Wand is a unique enchanted relic crafted long ago by three Dalaran apprentice magi as a pledge of brotherhood. Following the fall of Lordaeron and bitter betrayals among its creators, the wand was hidden away in Fenris Keep before resurfacing in the hands of the Forsaken. In the days when Dalaran still trained the young magi of the north, three aspiring wizards—Bethor Iceshard, Gunther Arcanus, and Thule Ravenclaw—intertwined their individual apprentice wands into a single talisman. This Woven Wand served as both a conduit of combined magical power and a symbol of their enduring friendship. That fellowship shattered irrevocably when the Scourge swept through Lordaeron. Thule Ravenclaw chose to swear fealty to the Lich King, turning to foul necromancy. Meanwhile, the Plague of Undeath claimed both Bethor and Gunther, eventually cutting their ties to Dalaran entirely.

item:xavian-water-sample.text: Xavian Water Sample. A vial of pristine, magically infused water drawn from the base of the highest waterfall in the ancient elven ruins of Xavian. Horde mages in Orgrimmar seek it out to unravel the latent arcane powers preserved in Ashenvale's oldest sacred sites. Xavian is a fabled ancient elven city, and tales of its ancient knowledge are well known among the learned. Even in ruin, its waters are said to hold vast magical powers. Deino, an arcane instructor in Orgrimmar, tasks rising mages with trekking deep into Ashenvale to collect a fresh sample straight from the pool below Xavian's tallest waterfall. Securing it requires braving dangerous territory, as the ruins are now fiercely guarded by corrupt satyrs hostile to any meddling spellcasters.

item:young-crocolisk-skin.text: Young Crocolisk Skin. Young Crocolisk Skin is a pliable reptile pelt harvested from juvenile crocolisks throughout the Wetlands. Prized by local tanners like James Halloran of Menethil Harbor, these softer hides are cured and exported to ports across Azeroth. Menethil Harbor serves as a bustling hub of commerce along the western coast of Khaz Modan, exporting marshland goods to distant ports. Among the town's most lucrative exports are the cured hides processed by the harbor's resident tanner, James Halloran. While full-grown crocolisks yield thick, tough scales, their young provide softer, far more workable leather. Because these juvenile skins are delicate and in high demand, Halloran relies on local hunters and passing travelers to scour the boggy marshes just outside town to keep his curing racks stocked.

item:yowler-s-paw.text: Yowler's Paw. Yowler's Paw is the grisly trophy taken from Yowler, the ferocious pack leader of the gnolls menacing the hills above Lakeshire. Brought to the town artisan Verner Osgood, it serves as undeniable proof that the beast leading the local gnoll packs has been put down. The Redridge gnolls have long terrorized the heights surrounding Lake Everstill, their bloodcurdling howls echoing down into the settlement of Lakeshire. Among them, none is more feared than Yowler, the ruthless alpha driving their expansion. Because gnoll ears and paws are customary proof of bounties across the human territories, Verner Osgood asks brave adventurers to bring back Yowler's paw. Severing it marks not just the demise of an unusually cunning predator, but a deliberate move to shatter the chain of command among his disorganized followers. Bringing back Yowler's paw underscores the dire situation in Lakeshire. The Stormwind Army is completely consumed by the Blackrock orc threat entrenched around Stonewatch Keep, leaving civil authorities and townspeople to hire passing mercenaries for defense. In the absence of regular royal garrisons, securing proof like Yowler's paw is the only way settlers like Verner Osgood can ensure the local roads remain even marginally safe for trade and travel.

item:zalazane-s-head.text: Zalazane's Head. Master Gadrin awaits proof that Zalazane has fallen. The Darkspear seek relief from the witch doctor who drove them from the Echo Isles. Master Gadrin asks for proof that Zalazane is dead. The witch doctor betrayed the Darkspear and seized control of their island home with mind-enslaving hexes. His magic drove Vol'jin's people to the shores of Durotar. From the Echo Isles, Zalazane still sends hexed thralls across the water to seize more victims. Sen'jin Village needs proof that his rule has ended. Returning Zalazane's severed head confirms his defeat and gives the displaced tribe a measure of peace, with hope of reclaiming their stolen islands one day.

item:zamah-s-note.text: Zamah's Note. Zamah's Note is a written dispatch sent from Zamah in Thunder Bluff across the Great Sea to Apothecary Lydon in Tarren Mill. It outlines an urgent request for an alchemical concoction capable of dealing with the Venture Company in the Stonetalon Mountains without relying on direct bloodshed. The goblin operations of the Venture Company have entrenched themselves deeply within the Stonetalon Mountains, deforesting and tearing up the sacred land. Zamah, seeking a specialized solution to dislodge them without inciting outright slaughter, turns to the expertise of the Forsaken Royal Apothecary Society. The note serves as formal correspondence detailing Stonetalon's dire situation to her colleague, Apothecary Lydon, stationed far away in Tarren Mill within the Hillsbrad Foothills of Lordaeron. Carrying the sealed message requires a long trek across continents, guiding Kalimdor travelers aboard zeppelins to the Undercity and down through Silverpine Forest into Hillsbrad. Upon receiving Zamah's dispatch, Lydon is immediately intrigued by her specific requirements, taking pride that word reached him from across the ocean and preparing to craft an alchemical answer to the goblin problem.

item:zargh-s-meats.text: Zargh's Meats. At the Crossroads, Zargh prepares fresh meat for Gryshka in Orgrimmar. The parcel gives young Horde travelers a reason to learn the wind rider route. Zargh, an orc butcher and hunter at the Crossroads in the Barrens, prepares fresh cuts for Gryshka, the innkeeper in Orgrimmar's Valley of Strength. The heat across the savannas can spoil fresh game quickly, so the parcel goes with couriers bound for the Crossroads roost. Wind Rider Master Devrak arranges a wyvern flight to Orgrimmar's Skytower, sparing travelers the long overland journey through Durotar. Zargh's delivery carries a personal sentiment along with its provisions. When Gryshka receives the meat, she recognizes Zargh's knack for winning a lady's favor with quality game. She is eager to prepare the cuts for the inn's patrons and guests. For newly arrived orc and troll travelers, the delivery offers an introduction to long-distance flight between Kalimdor's Horde settlements.

item:zhevra-hooves.text: Zhevra Hooves. Across the Barrens, zhevras graze in the open savannah. Their hooves prove a hunter can face swift, powerful prey. Zhevras graze across the Barrens, but their compact, muscular legs can strike hard. Sergra Darkthorn, the orc shaman in charge of the Crossroads, sends aspiring Horde scouts to gather hooves from zhevra runners. The hunt sharpens a fledgling hunter's instincts and resilience. A panicked runner can kick even a sturdy tauren flat. Intact hooves show a hunter can handle swift, kicking quarry before taking on Kalimdor's deadliest predators.
